```toml id="df-lake-cargo"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros"] }
futures = "0.3"
```

Agent rule:

```text id="df-cargo-rule"
Application:
  datafusion crate.

Custom UDF/optimizer/table-provider library:
  narrow datafusion-* crates where possible.

Arrow-only kernel library:
  no DataFusion dependency.
```

---

## 8.2 Imports

```rust id="df-imports"
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::{ArrayRef, Int32Array, RecordBatch, StringArray};
use arrow_schema::{DataType, Field, Schema};

use datafusion::prelude::*;
use datafusion::logical_expr::{col, lit, Expr, JoinType};
use datafusion_common::{DataFusionError, Result, ScalarValue};
use datafusion_physical_plan::SendableRecordBatchStream;
```

`DataFrame` methods such as `select`, `filter`, `aggregate`, and `limit` build a logical plan; computation is lazy until execution methods such as `collect` or stream execution are called. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 8.3 Decision matrix: `arrow::compute` vs DataFusion

| Requirement                                | Use                    | Reason                             |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Add two `Int32Array`s                      | Arrow kernel           | no plan needed                     |
| Filter one `RecordBatch` by `BooleanArray` | Arrow kernel           | local batch operation              |
| Cast one `ArrayRef`                        | Arrow kernel           | direct datatype conversion         |
| Sort one batch by one column               | Arrow kernels          | `sort_to_indices` + `take`         |
| Select/project expressions over file scan  | DataFusion             | projection pushdown / lazy plan    |
| Filter Parquet dataset                     | DataFusion             | predicate pushdown / scan planning |
| Derived columns over DataFrame             | DataFusion             | expression planning                |
| Group by / aggregate                       | DataFusion             | relational aggregation             |
| Join tables                                | DataFusion             | join planning/execution            |
| Window functions                           | DataFusion             | window relational operator         |
| SQL                                        | DataFusion             | parser/planner                     |
| UDF in SQL/DataFrame                       | DataFusion             | function registry                  |
| Table-valued function                      | DataFusion             | table function registry            |
| Query plan serialization                   | DataFusion / Substrait | logical/portable plan layer        |

```text id="decision-rule"
If operation is array-local:
  arrow::compute / arrow-*.

If operation requires relation semantics:
  DataFusion Expr / DataFrame / SQL.

If operation requires optimizer/source pushdown:
  DataFusion.

If operation is a custom per-row vectorized function inside SQL:
  DataFusion UDF wrapping Arrow kernels.
```

---

## 8.4 Core `Expr` construction

### Column references and literals

```rust id="expr-col-lit"
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let c1 = col("c1");
let constant_i64 = lit(42_i64);
let constant_str = lit("hello");
let typed_null = Expr::Literal(ScalarValue::Int64(None), None);
let untyped_null = lit(ScalarValue::Null);
```

DataFusion `Expr::Column` references columns and is commonly created with `col("name")`; `Expr::Literal` stores typed literal values and is commonly created with `lit(...)`, while typed nulls use `ScalarValue::<type>(None)` and untyped nulls use `ScalarValue::Null`. ([Docs.rs][3])

### Binary expressions

```rust id="expr-binary"
let arithmetic = col("price") + col("tax");
let predicate = col("amount").gt(lit(0_i64));
let compound = col("a").gt(lit(6)).and(col("b").lt(lit(7)));
```

Expression methods and operator overloads build logical expressions, not immediate arrays; for example `col("c1") + col("c2")` builds a binary expression, and `col("c1").eq(lit(42_i32))` builds an equality predicate. ([Docs.rs][3])

### Boolean operators

```rust id="expr-boolean"
let p = col("country").eq(lit("US"))
    .and(col("amount").gt(lit(100_i64)));

let q = col("status").eq(lit("paid"))
    .or(col("status").eq(lit("settled")));

let not_deleted = col("deleted").not();
```

DataFusion’s expression API uses `.and(...)`, `.or(...)`, `not(...)`, or `!x`; Rust’s `&&` and `||` cannot be overloaded and are not available for DataFusion `Expr`. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

---

## 8.5 DataFrame lifecycle

```rust id="df-lifecycle"
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion_common::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let df = ctx
        .read_csv("events.csv", CsvReadOptions::new())
        .await?;

    let planned = df
        .filter(col("amount").gt(lit(0_i64)))?
        .select(vec![
            col("user_id"),
            (col("amount") + col("tax")).alias("gross"),
        ])?
        .limit(0, Some(100))?;

    let batches = planned.collect().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

A DataFrame represents a logical set of rows and is a wrapper around a `LogicalPlan` plus `SessionState`; most DataFrame methods build plans lazily, while `collect` executes the plan and buffers all output `RecordBatch`es into memory. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Stream execution

```rust id="df-execute-stream"
use futures::StreamExt;

let stream: SendableRecordBatchStream = df.execute_stream().await?;

futures::pin_mut!(stream);
while let Some(batch) = stream.next().await {
    let batch = batch?;
    // process RecordBatch
}
```

`execute_stream` executes a DataFrame and returns a single-partition stream without buffering all batches in memory; dropping the stream aborts execution and frees resources. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 8.6 Projection

### Select columns

```rust id="df-select-columns"
let df = df.select_columns(&["user_id", "amount"])?;
```

### Select arbitrary expressions

```rust id="df-select-exprs"
let df = df.select(vec![
    col("user_id"),
    col("amount"),
    (col("amount") + col("tax")).alias("gross"),
    lit("USD").alias("currency"),
])?;
```

`DataFrame::select` projects arbitrary expressions into a new DataFrame; the output has one column per expression. ([Docs.rs][2])

### SQL-like expression strings

```rust id="df-select-exprs-sql"
let df = df.select_exprs(&[
    "user_id",
    "amount + tax AS gross",
    "'USD' AS currency",
])?;
```

`select_exprs` parses string expressions and is available with the `sql` feature; use typed `Expr` construction for generated Rust code when possible. ([Docs.rs][2])

Agent rule:

```text id="projection-rule"
Generated Rust:
  prefer select(vec![Expr...])

Human-authored config/DSL:
  select_exprs acceptable if SQL feature enabled

Avoid:
  manual RecordBatch column replacement when the source is a DataFrame
```

---

## 8.7 Filtering

```rust id="df-filter"
let df = df.filter(
    col("country").eq(lit("US"))
        .and(col("amount").gt(lit(100_i64)))
)?;
```

`DataFrame::filter` returns rows for which the predicate evaluates to `true`; rows where the predicate evaluates to `false` or `null` are filtered out. ([Docs.rs][2])

### PyArrow dataset expression equivalent

PyArrow dataset expressions are created from `pyarrow.compute.field()` references and `pyarrow.compute.scalar()` values, then combined with comparisons and boolean logic for table/dataset filters. ([Apache Arrow][5])

```python id="pyarrow-filter"
import pyarrow.compute as pc

expr = (
    (pc.field("country") == pc.scalar("US")) &
    (pc.field("amount") > pc.scalar(100))
)
```

```rust id="df-filter-equivalent"
let expr = col("country").eq(lit("US"))
    .and(col("amount").gt(lit(100_i64)));

let df = df.filter(expr)?;
```

Mapping:

| PyArrow expression | DataFusion `Expr`           |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- |
| `pc.field("x")`    | `col("x")`                  |
| `pc.scalar(5)`     | `lit(5)`                    |
| `field == scalar`  | `col("x").eq(lit(...))`     |
| `field != scalar`  | `col("x").not_eq(lit(...))` |
| `field < scalar`   | `col("x").lt(lit(...))`     |
| `field <= scalar`  | `col("x").lt_eq(lit(...))`  |
| `field > scalar`   | `col("x").gt(lit(...))`     |
| `field >= scalar`  | `col("x").gt_eq(lit(...))`  |
| `expr1 & expr2`    | `expr1.and(expr2)`          |
| `expr1 \| expr2`   | `expr1.or(expr2)`           |
| `~expr`            | `expr.not()`                |

---

## 8.8 Derived columns

### Projection-based derived column

```rust id="derived-select"
let df = df.select(vec![
    col("order_id"),
    col("amount"),
    col("tax"),
    (col("amount") + col("tax")).alias("gross"),
])?;
```

### `with_column`

```rust id="with-column"
let df = df.with_column(
    "gross",
    col("amount") + col("tax"),
)?;
```

`union_by_name` examples in current DataFrame docs use `with_column("d", lit("77"))`, and the DataFrame API includes `with_column`, `with_column_renamed`, `fill_null`, and schema/plan accessors for plan manipulation. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Rename

```rust id="rename-column"
let df = df.with_column_renamed("gross", "total")?;
```

### Fill nulls

```rust id="fill-nulls"
let df = df.fill_null(
    ScalarValue::Int64(Some(0)),
    vec!["amount".to_string()],
)?;
```

`fill_null` fills null values in specified columns with a scalar value and only fills when the scalar can be cast to the column type. ([Docs.rs][2])

Agent rule:

```text id="derived-rule"
Use DataFusion expressions for derived columns over DataFrames.
Use Arrow kernels only when you already have one RecordBatch/Array and no plan/source is involved.
```

---

## 8.9 Aggregation

### Grouped aggregation

```rust id="df-aggregate"
let df = df.aggregate(
    vec![col("country")],
    vec![
        sum(col("amount")).alias("total_amount"),
        count(col("order_id")).alias("orders"),
        avg(col("amount")).alias("avg_amount"),
        min(col("amount")).alias("min_amount"),
        max(col("amount")).alias("max_amount"),
    ],
)?;
```

`DataFrame::aggregate(group_expr, aggr_expr)` returns a new DataFrame that aggregates rows, optionally grouping by the provided expressions. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Global aggregation

```rust id="df-global-aggregate"
let df = df.aggregate(
    vec![],
    vec![sum(col("amount")).alias("total_amount")],
)?;
```

### PyArrow-style mapping

| PyArrow-ish task                     | Arrow kernel                          | DataFusion                                          |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `pc.sum(array)`                      | `arrow_arith::aggregate::sum(&array)` | not needed                                          |
| `table.group_by("k").aggregate(...)` | not raw Arrow-level                   | `df.aggregate(vec![col("k")], vec![sum(col("v"))])` |
| dataset grouped scan                 | not raw Arrow-level                   | DataFusion query                                    |
| SQL aggregate                        | not raw Arrow-level                   | `ctx.sql("SELECT k, SUM(v) FROM t GROUP BY k")`     |

Agent rule:

```text id="aggregate-rule"
Single array aggregate:
  Arrow aggregate kernel.

Grouped aggregate:
  DataFusion aggregate.

Multi-file aggregate:
  DataFusion.

Streaming aggregate:
  DataFusion physical execution.
```

---

## 8.10 Joins

### Equi-join by column lists

```rust id="df-join-equi"
let joined = left.join(
    right,
    JoinType::Inner,
    &["customer_id"],
    &["id"],
    None,
)?;
```

`DataFrame::join` joins two DataFrames using explicitly specified left/right columns and an optional filter expression; DataFusion can identify and optimize equality predicates, and `join_on` is a more concise expression-based form. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Join with additional filter

```rust id="df-join-filter"
let joined = left.join(
    right,
    JoinType::Inner,
    &["customer_id"],
    &["id"],
    Some(col("amount").gt(lit(0_i64))),
)?;
```

### Expression join

```rust id="df-join-on"
let joined = left.join_on(
    right,
    JoinType::Inner,
    [
        col("a").not_eq(col("a2")),
        col("b").not_eq(col("b2")),
    ],
)?;
```

### Aliased join

```rust id="df-join-alias"
let orders = orders.alias("o")?;
let customers = customers.alias("c")?;

let joined = orders.join(
    customers,
    JoinType::Inner,
    &["customer_id"],
    &["id"],
    None,
)?;
```

Agent rule:

```text id="join-rule"
Use DataFusion for joins.
Do not implement joins with Arrow take/filter loops unless:
  data is tiny,
  algorithm is specialized,
  or building a custom physical operator.
```

---

## 8.11 Windows

### Window DataFrame operator

```rust id="df-window-placeholder"
let df = df.window(vec![
    // window Expr values, e.g. rank/sum-over expressions depending on imported function builders
])?;
```

`DataFrame::window` adds results of evaluating one or more `Expr::WindowFunction` expressions to the existing columns. ([Docs.rs][2])

### SQL window escape hatch

```rust id="df-window-sql"
let df = ctx.sql(r#"
    SELECT
      user_id,
      ts,
      amount,
      SUM(amount) OVER (
        PARTITION BY user_id
        ORDER BY ts
        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
      ) AS running_amount
    FROM events
"#).await?;
```

DataFusion’s SQL window function docs define window functions as calculations over related rows that preserve row identity instead of grouping rows into one output row. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

Agent rule:

```text id="window-rule"
For generated Rust:
  use DataFusion window expressions if function-builder API is known.

For robust agent output:
  SQL window syntax is often safer and clearer.

Do not use Arrow kernels for windows unless implementing a custom physical operator.
```

---

## 8.12 Set operations, distinct, limits

```rust id="df-set-ops"
let u = df1.clone().union(df2.clone())?;
let u_name = df1.clone().union_by_name(df2.clone())?;
let u_distinct = df1.clone().union_distinct(df2.clone())?;

let d = df1.clone().distinct()?;
let d_on = df1.clone().distinct_on(
    vec![col("user_id")],
    vec![col("user_id"), col("ts")],
    None,
)?;

let limited = df1.limit(0, Some(100))?;
```

DataFrame set operations include `union`, `union_by_name`, `union_distinct`, `union_by_name_distinct`, `distinct`, and `distinct_on`; union requires identical schemas unless using name-based union, where missing columns are filled with null. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 8.13 SQL API

```rust id="df-sql-basic"
let df = ctx.sql(r#"
    SELECT country, SUM(amount) AS total_amount
    FROM events
    WHERE amount > 0
    GROUP BY country
    ORDER BY total_amount DESC
    LIMIT 10
"#).await?;

let batches = df.collect().await?;
```

DataFusion’s main entry point is `SessionContext`; it can create DataFrames from sources such as CSV, and `Expr` represents expressions such as `a + b`. ([Docs.rs][1])

### SQL vs DataFrame selection

```text id="sql-vs-dataframe"
Use SQL when:
  user-authored queries
  complex windows/CTEs/subqueries
  compatibility with SQL clients
  concise expression syntax

Use DataFrame API when:
  generated Rust code
  typed DSL/compiler output
  programmatic plan construction
  controlled expression generation
```

---

## 8.14 Execution output modes

| Method                               | Behavior                                | Use                        |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `collect().await`                    | executes and buffers all output batches | bounded results / tests    |
| `show().await`                       | executes and prints                     | debugging / CLI            |
| `show_limit(n).await`                | prints first `n` rows                   | previews                   |
| `execute_stream().await`             | single stream, no full buffering        | service / large output     |
| `collect_partitioned().await`        | buffers by partition                    | testing partitioned output |
| `execute_stream_partitioned().await` | stream per partition                    | custom executors/services  |

`collect` executes and buffers output in memory; `execute_stream` returns a stream without buffering; partitioned execution APIs preserve partitioning. ([Docs.rs][2])

Agent rule:

```text id="execution-rule"
Default for services:
  execute_stream

Default for tests:
  collect

Default for CLI preview:
  show_limit

Never collect unbounded user query output without row/byte/time limits.
```

---

## 8.15 Logical plan inspection

```rust id="plan-inspection"
let plan = df.logical_plan();
println!("{plan:?}");

let optimized = df.clone().into_optimized_plan()?;
println!("{optimized:?}");

let explained = df.explain(false, false)?;
explained.show().await?;
```

`logical_plan` returns the unoptimized logical plan reference; `into_optimized_plan` returns an optimized plan and is marked as mainly appropriate for testing because it loses the attached state snapshot; `explain` returns a DataFrame containing the plan explanation, optionally with analysis/metrics. ([Docs.rs][2])

Agent rule:

```text id="plan-inspection-rule"
Use explain/analyze in:
  performance debugging
  optimizer regression tests
  generated-query validation

Avoid using into_unoptimized_plan in production flow unless state handling is explicit.
```

---

## 8.16 Function registry and built-in SQL functions

### Registry access

```rust id="function-registry-access"
let registry = df.registry();

let scalar_udf = registry.udf("my_func")?;
let aggregate_udf = registry.udaf("my_agg")?;
let window_udf = registry.udwf("my_window")?;
```

A DataFrame can expose its `FunctionRegistry`, and the registry can look up scalar UDFs, aggregate UDFs, window UDFs, and expression planners. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Registration via `SessionContext`

```rust id="function-register"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::execution::FunctionRegistry;

// ctx implements FunctionRegistry
ctx.register_udf(Arc::new(my_scalar_udf))?;
ctx.register_udaf(Arc::new(my_aggregate_udf))?;
ctx.register_udwf(Arc::new(my_window_udf))?;
```

`FunctionRegistry` provides `register_udf`, `register_udaf`, `register_udwf`, deregistration methods, function rewrites, and custom expression planner registration; `SessionContext`, `SessionState`, `TaskContext`, and `MemoryFunctionRegistry` implement it. ([Docs.rs][7])

---

## 8.17 UDF taxonomy

| UDF type         | DataFusion meaning                                        | Use                           |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Scalar UDF       | row-wise function, vectorized over Arrow arrays           | custom expression function    |
| Aggregate UDF    | group of rows → one value                                 | custom aggregate              |
| Window UDF       | row-wise output with access to neighboring/partition rows | custom window                 |
| Table function   | parameters → `TableProvider`                              | dynamic table source          |
| Async scalar UDF | scalar function doing async IO/network work               | external lookup / remote call |

DataFusion’s UDF guide covers scalar, window, aggregate, table, and async scalar UDFs; scalar UDFs are vectorized by receiving one or more Arrow arrays and producing an Arrow array with the same row count. ([Apache DataFusion][8])

### Scalar UDF design rule

```text id="udf-design-rule"
Scalar UDF:
  input = ColumnarValue / Arrow arrays
  output = ColumnarValue / Arrow array
  preserve row count
  preserve null semantics
  avoid per-row Python/object allocation
  reuse Arrow kernels internally
```

---

## 8.18 PyArrow dataset expression mapping

PyArrow datasets support larger-than-memory, multi-file datasets with discovery, partition handling, schema normalization, and local/cloud file systems; dataset/table filtering can use boolean `Expression` objects built from fields, scalars, comparisons, and compute transformations. ([Apache Arrow][9])

| PyArrow dataset / compute expression           | DataFusion equivalent                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ds.dataset(path, format="parquet")`           | `ctx.read_parquet(path, ParquetReadOptions::default()).await?` or table registration |
| `dataset.to_table(columns=[...], filter=expr)` | `df.filter(expr)?.select(vec![...])?.collect().await?`                               |
| `dataset.scanner(columns=[...], filter=expr)`  | lazy `DataFrame` chain, `execute_stream()` for scanner-like streaming                |
| `pc.field("a")`                                | `col("a")`                                                                           |
| `pc.scalar(3)`                                 | `lit(3)`                                                                             |
| `(field("a") < 3) & (field("b") > 1)`          | `col("a").lt(lit(3)).and(col("b").gt(lit(1)))`                                       |
| `pc.add(field("a"), field("b"))`               | `col("a") + col("b")`                                                                |
| `pc.cast(field("a"), pa.int64())`              | `cast(col("a"), DataType::Int64)` / SQL `CAST(a AS BIGINT)`                          |
| `columns={"x": expr}`                          | `select(vec![expr.alias("x")])`                                                      |
| filter null behavior                           | DataFusion filter also drops false/null rows                                         |

### Example

```python id="pyarrow-dataset-example"
import pyarrow.compute as pc

expr = (
    (pc.field("event_type") == pc.scalar("click")) &
    (pc.field("amount") > pc.scalar(0))
)
```

```rust id="datafusion-dataset-equivalent"
let df = ctx
    .read_parquet("s3://bucket/events/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
    .await?
    .filter(
        col("event_type").eq(lit("click"))
            .and(col("amount").gt(lit(0_i64)))
    )?
    .select(vec![
        col("user_id"),
        col("event_type"),
        col("amount"),
        (col("amount") * lit(100_i64)).alias("amount_cents"),
    ])?;

let stream = df.execute_stream().await?;
```

---

## 8.19 Function syntax cheat sheet

| Intent              | Rust DataFusion expression                   |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| column              | `col("x")`                                   |
| literal             | `lit(42_i64)`                                |
| alias               | `expr.alias("name")`                         |
| equality            | `col("x").eq(lit(1))`                        |
| inequality          | `col("x").not_eq(lit(1))`                    |
| less than           | `col("x").lt(lit(1))`                        |
| less/equal          | `col("x").lt_eq(lit(1))`                     |
| greater than        | `col("x").gt(lit(1))`                        |
| greater/equal       | `col("x").gt_eq(lit(1))`                     |
| AND                 | `a.and(b)`                                   |
| OR                  | `a.or(b)`                                    |
| NOT                 | `a.not()` or `!a`                            |
| arithmetic add      | `col("a") + col("b")`                        |
| arithmetic multiply | `col("a") * lit(2_i64)`                      |
| aggregate sum       | `sum(col("x"))`                              |
| aggregate min       | `min(col("x"))`                              |
| aggregate max       | `max(col("x"))`                              |
| aggregate avg       | `avg(col("x"))`                              |
| aggregate count     | `count(col("x"))`                            |
| sort                | `df.sort(vec![col("x").sort(true, false)])?` |
| limit               | `df.limit(skip, Some(fetch))?`               |
| projection          | `df.select(vec![...])?`                      |
| filter              | `df.filter(predicate)?`                      |
| aggregation         | `df.aggregate(group_exprs, aggr_exprs)?`     |
| SQL                 | `ctx.sql("SELECT ...").await?`               |

The expression API reference documents `col`, `lit`, chained boolean expressions, and many function builders; DataFrame methods such as `select` and `filter` accept logical expressions. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

---

## 8.20 End-to-end DataFrame pattern

```rust id="df-end-to-end"
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion_common::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let events = ctx
        .read_parquet("s3://bucket/events/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
        .await?
        .alias("e")?;

    let users = ctx
        .read_parquet("s3://bucket/users/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
        .await?
        .alias("u")?;

    let joined = events.join(
        users,
        JoinType::Inner,
        &["user_id"],
        &["id"],
        None,
    )?;

    let result = joined
        .filter(
            col("event_type").eq(lit("click"))
                .and(col("amount").gt(lit(0_i64))),
        )?
        .select(vec![
            col("user_id"),
            col("country"),
            (col("amount") + col("tax")).alias("gross"),
        ])?
        .aggregate(
            vec![col("country")],
            vec![
                count(col("user_id")).alias("events"),
                sum(col("gross")).alias("revenue"),
            ],
        )?
        .sort(vec![col("revenue").sort(false, false)])?
        .limit(0, Some(100))?;

    let stream = result.execute_stream().await?;
    // stream to Flight/HTTP/IPC sink

    Ok(())
}
```

---

## 8.21 Deployment guidance

### Use Arrow kernels when

```text id="arrow-kernel-use"
Inputs:
  ArrayRef
  RecordBatch
  small Vec<RecordBatch>
  Python extension function over one batch
  custom DataFusion UDF implementation internals

Operations:
  cast
  arithmetic
  comparison
  filter batch
  take batch
  sort one batch
  string kernel
  single-array aggregate
```

### Use DataFusion when

```text id="datafusion-use"
Inputs:
  files/directories
  object-store datasets
  table providers
  SQL
  user query
  many RecordBatch partitions
  relational operations

Operations:
  projection over scan
  predicate pushdown
  derived columns in plan
  grouped aggregation
  joins
  windows
  set operations
  subqueries
  UDFs in SQL/DataFrame
```

### Service profile

```text id="df-service-profile"
DO:
  keep SessionContext / SessionState at service boundary
  expose streaming output
  set row/byte/time limits for user queries
  use explain/analyze in observability paths
  register UDFs at context initialization
  use object_store-backed sources for cloud paths

DON'T:
  collect user query output by default
  build joins with Arrow kernels
  parse user SQL without resource limits
  expose raw DataFusionError over public RPC without normalization
```

---

## 8.22 Performance guidance

```text id="df-performance-guidance"
Fast path:
  push filter/projection before collect
  use DataFusion source readers for Parquet datasets
  stream output
  avoid materializing intermediate Vec<RecordBatch>
  inspect optimized plan for pushdown/joins
  use SQL/DataFrame expressions so optimizer can rewrite

Slow path:
  collect -> manual Arrow kernels -> re-register
  Python-like eager Table materialization
  unbounded collect
  string expression parsing in tight generated-code loops
  UDFs that allocate per row
```

Execution notes:

```text id="df-execution-notes"
collect:
  buffers all RecordBatch output in memory.

execute_stream:
  streams batches and supports abort by dropping stream.

collect_partitioned:
  preserves partitioning but still buffers.

execute_stream_partitioned:
  one stream per partition.
```

`collect` buffers output in memory, while `execute_stream` avoids full buffering; DataFrame docs explicitly point from `collect` to `execute_stream` for non-buffered execution. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 8.23 Error handling

```rust id="df-error-boundary"
fn normalize_df_error(e: DataFusionError) -> tonic::Status {
    match e {
        DataFusionError::Plan(msg) => tonic::Status::invalid_argument(msg),
        DataFusionError::SchemaError(err, _) => tonic::Status::invalid_argument(err.to_string()),
        DataFusionError::Execution(msg) => tonic::Status::internal(msg),
        other => tonic::Status::internal(other.to_string()),
    }
}
```

Agent rules:

```text id="df-error-rules"
Plan error:
  invalid expression/query/schema/function reference.

Execution error:
  runtime failure during physical execution.

Resource error:
  enforce limits and translate explicitly.

Public API:
  never leak internal plan/debug details unless verbose/debug mode is active.
```

---

## 8.24 Anti-pattern catalog

| Anti-pattern                                                 | Failure mode                            | Correct pattern                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Use Arrow kernels for joins                                  | incorrect/slow custom relational engine | DataFusion join                          |
| Use Arrow kernels for grouped aggregates                     | no grouping engine                      | DataFusion aggregate                     |
| `collect().await?` for user query                            | memory blowup                           | `execute_stream().await?`                |
| Convert DataFrame to `Vec<RecordBatch>` then filter manually | loses optimizer/pushdown                | `df.filter(...)`                         |
| Use SQL strings for generated simple projections             | parse overhead / quoting risk           | typed `Expr` API                         |
| Use typed Expr API for complex user SQL                      | reimplement parser                      | `ctx.sql(...)`                           |
| UDF allocates per row                                        | slow                                    | vectorized Arrow array operations        |
| Register UDF after queries are built                         | function not available in planning      | register at context init                 |
| Ignore `false/null` filter behavior                          | unexpected dropped rows                 | normalize predicate explicitly           |
| Use `into_unoptimized_plan` in production flow               | loses state snapshot                    | inspect plan by reference or use explain |

---

## 8.25 Golden test matrix

```rust id="df-golden-tests"
#[tokio::test]
async fn filter_drops_null_predicate_rows() -> datafusion_common::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
        ("a", Arc::new(Int32Array::from(vec![Some(1), None, Some(3)])) as ArrayRef),
    ])?;

    ctx.register_batch("t", batch)?;

    let df = ctx
        .table("t")
        .await?
        .filter(col("a").gt(lit(1_i32)))?;

    let batches = df.collect().await?;
    let rows: usize = batches.iter().map(RecordBatch::num_rows).sum();

    assert_eq!(rows, 1);
    Ok(())
}
```

Test categories:

```text id="df-test-categories"
Expression:
  col/lit typed null
  arithmetic
  comparison
  boolean
  alias

Filter:
  true rows kept
  false rows dropped
  null rows dropped

Projection:
  column order
  alias names
  derived datatypes

Aggregation:
  grouped
  global
  all-null group
  empty input

Join:
  inner
  left
  full
  expression join
  duplicate column handling

Execution:
  collect bounded
  execute_stream
  stream dropped/cancelled

Registry:
  UDF visible before planning
  missing UDF plan error
  deregistration behavior if used

Plan:
  explain snapshot
  optimized plan contains expected projection/filter pushdown where stable enough
```

---

## 8.26 Value case

```text id="df-value-case"
arrow::compute:
  value = direct vectorized batch-local kernels.

DataFusion Expr:
  value = composable logical expressions with type coercion and planning.

DataFrame:
  value = lazy relational pipeline over Arrow data.

SQL:
  value = user-facing query language and compact complex query representation.

Projection/filter in DataFusion:
  value = optimizer visibility and source pushdown.

Aggregation/join/window:
  value = relational execution operators unavailable in raw Arrow kernels.

FunctionRegistry:
  value = SQL/DataFrame-visible custom functions.

UDFs:
  value = reusable vectorized domain logic inside query plans.

execute_stream:
  value = lower memory, lower first-result latency, cancellation/backpressure compatibility.

explain/plan inspection:
  value = generated-query debugging and optimizer validation.
```

Final agent rule:

```text id="df-final-rule"
If the request says “array”, generate Arrow kernels.
If the request says “table”, “dataset”, “SQL”, “group by”, “join”, “window”, “query”, “scan”, or “pushdown”, generate DataFusion expressions/plans.
Keep DataFusion lazy until the final boundary.
Prefer execute_stream for services and large data.
Use collect only for bounded results and tests.
```

## 8.27 DataFusion 54 function additions: vector, nested, and metadata functions

New in DataFusion 54, at the query-engine level (SQL and `Expr` API). These are **not** arrow-rs compute kernels — they live in the `datafusion-functions-nested` and `datafusion-functions` crates and require a DataFusion session:

```text
datafusion-functions-nested (feature "nested_expressions", on by default):
  cosine_distance(a, b)    # cosine distance between two numeric arrays/vectors
  inner_product(a, b)      # inner (dot) product of two numeric arrays
  array_normalize(a)       # scale an array to unit norm
  array_compact(a)         # drop NULL elements from an array

datafusion-functions core:
  cast_to_type(v, t)       # cast honoring registered extension types
  try_cast_to_type(v, t)   # same, NULL on failure instead of error
  with_metadata(v, ...)    # attach field metadata to an expression's output field
```

```rust
// SQL surface
let df = ctx
    .sql("SELECT cosine_distance(embedding, [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]) AS d FROM items")
    .await?;
```

Rules:

```text
Vector similarity over List/FixedSizeList columns:
  use cosine_distance / inner_product / array_normalize in DataFusion
  do not hand-roll per-batch arrow_arith loops for query workloads

Array cleanup:
  array_compact drops NULL elements (query-level; no arrow-rs equivalent kernel)

Metadata-aware casts:
  cast_to_type / try_cast_to_type / with_metadata interact with the
  DataFusion 54 extension-type registry — see §26.22
```

The higher-order companions (`array_transform`, `array_filter`, `array_any_match`) take SQL lambdas and are covered with the higher-order-UDF surface in §18.28. Deep dive for the function catalog: `datafusion_rust.md` §12; UDF authoring: `datafusion_calculations_rust.md`.

---

# 9) CSV, JSON, and line-delimited ingestion

Style target: dense, syntax-first, agent-ready technical reference. Continues the uploaded advanced-reference format. 

---

## 9.0 Mental model

```text id="csv-json-mental-model"
CSV:
  row-oriented text
  explicit or inferred schema
  batched into RecordBatch
  reader implements Iterator<Item = Result<RecordBatch, ArrowError>>
  writer writes RecordBatch values

JSON:
  row-oriented JSON values
  line-delimited JSON is primary ingestion shape
  explicit or inferred schema
  Reader for sync BufRead
  Decoder for arbitrary byte streams / async integration
  serde-compatible Decoder::serialize for Rust structs -> RecordBatch
```

`arrow-csv` transfers data between Apache Arrow memory format and CSV and re-exports `Reader`, `ReaderBuilder`, `infer_schema_from_files`, `Writer`, and `WriterBuilder`; `arrow-json` readers load JSON records into batches and convert record-oriented JSON into Arrow’s columnar memory model. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 9.1 Cargo profiles

### Narrow ingestion profile

```toml id="csv-json-cargo-narrow"
[dependencies]
arrow-array = "58.4.0"
arrow-schema = "58.4.0"
arrow-csv = "58.4.0"
arrow-json = "58.4.0"
regex = "1"
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
```

### App/facade profile

```toml id="csv-json-cargo-facade"
[dependencies]
arrow = { version = "58.4.0", features = ["csv", "json", "prettyprint"] }
regex = "1"
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
```

### Async stream decoder profile

```toml id="csv-json-cargo-async"
[dependencies]
arrow-array = "58.4.0"
arrow-schema = "58.4.0"
arrow-csv = "58.4.0"
arrow-json = "58.4.0"
bytes = "1"
futures = "0.3"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros", "io-util", "fs"] }
```

### Compressed input profile

```toml id="csv-json-cargo-compressed"
[dependencies]
arrow-csv = "58.4.0"
arrow-json = "58.4.0"
flate2 = "1"
zstd = "0.13"
```

Rust Arrow CSV/JSON readers accept normal Rust `Read`/`BufRead`/byte-stream inputs; automatic file-extension decompression is a PyArrow convenience and is not the core Rust reader model, so wrap compressed streams explicitly with the appropriate decoder. PyArrow `read_csv` auto-decompresses paths ending in recognized compressed extensions, and PyArrow JSON docs also list filename-based automatic decompression. ([Apache Arrow][2])

## 9.2 Imports

```rust id="csv-json-imports"
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{BufReader, Cursor, Read, Seek, SeekFrom};
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::{ArrayRef, Int32Array, RecordBatch, StringArray};
use arrow_schema::{ArrowError, DataType, Field, Schema, SchemaRef};

use arrow_csv::reader::{Format as CsvFormat, ReaderBuilder as CsvReaderBuilder};
use arrow_csv::writer::{Writer as CsvWriter, WriterBuilder as CsvWriterBuilder};
use arrow_json::reader::{
    ReaderBuilder as JsonReaderBuilder,
    infer_json_schema,
    infer_json_schema_from_seekable,
};
use arrow_json::writer::{
    ArrayWriter as JsonArrayWriter,
    LineDelimitedWriter,
    WriterBuilder as JsonWriterBuilder,
    LineDelimited,
};

use regex::Regex;
```

---

## 9.3 CSV reader: explicit schema

### Sync file reader

```rust id="csv-explicit-schema-file"
use std::fs::File;
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_csv::ReaderBuilder;
use arrow_schema::{DataType, Field, Schema};

let schema = Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![
    Field::new("id", DataType::Int32, false),
    Field::new("name", DataType::Utf8, true),
    Field::new("active", DataType::Boolean, true),
]));

let file = File::open("users.csv")?;

let mut reader = ReaderBuilder::new(schema)
    .with_header(true)
    .with_batch_size(16_384)
    .build(file)?;

while let Some(batch) = reader.next() {
    let batch = batch?;
    // process RecordBatch
}
```

`ReaderBuilder::new(schema)` configures CSV parsing options; reader options include header handling, format override, delimiter, escape, quote, terminator, comment character, null regex, batch size, line bounds, projection, truncated-row handling, and sync/stream decoder construction. ([Docs.rs][3])

### Buffered reader path

```rust id="csv-buffered-reader"
let file = File::open("users.csv")?;
let buf = BufReader::new(file);

let mut reader = CsvReaderBuilder::new(schema)
    .with_header(true)
    .build_buffered(buf)?;
```

Use `build_buffered` when you already have a `BufRead`; `build` wraps non-buffered readers internally and docs recommend `build_buffered` to avoid unnecessary additional buffering when the input already implements `BufRead`. ([Docs.rs][3])

---

## 9.4 CSV reader: schema inference

### Infer from one seekable file

```rust id="csv-infer-seekable"
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{Seek, SeekFrom};
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_csv::reader::{Format, ReaderBuilder};

let mut file = File::open("users.csv")?;

let format = Format::default()
    .with_header(true)
    .with_delimiter(b',')
    .with_null_regex(Regex::new(r"^(|NULL|NA)$")?);

let (schema, records_read) = format.infer_schema(&mut file, Some(1_000))?;
file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(0))?;

let mut reader = ReaderBuilder::new(Arc::new(schema))
    .with_format(format)
    .with_batch_size(65_536)
    .build(file)?;
```

`Format::infer_schema` reads up to `max_records` when provided, or all records when `None`; if the CSV has no header, inferred names are generated with the `column_` prefix. `infer_schema_from_files` can infer across a list of files and merges discovered schemas. ([GitHub][4])

### Infer from multiple files

```rust id="csv-infer-many-files"
use arrow_csv::reader::infer_schema_from_files;

let files = vec![
    "part-000.csv".to_string(),
    "part-001.csv".to_string(),
];

let schema = infer_schema_from_files(
    &files,
    b',',
    Some(10_000), // total max records read across files
    true,         // has header
)?;
```

### Production rule

```text id="csv-infer-production-rule"
Prototype:
  infer_schema(..., Some(N))

Production:
  explicit schema preferred

Multi-file:
  infer only as bootstrap
  persist inferred schema
  validate every later file against persisted schema
```

---

## 9.5 CSV reader options map

| Option                | Rust API                       | Behavior                                      |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| header row            | `.with_header(true)`           | first row treated as header                   |
| delimiter             | `.with_delimiter(b'\t')`       | byte delimiter                                |
| escape                | `.with_escape(b'\\')`          | custom escape                                 |
| quote                 | `.with_quote(b'"')`            | custom quote, default double quote            |
| terminator            | `.with_terminator(b'\n')`      | custom terminator                             |
| comments              | `.with_comment(b'#')`          | lines starting with character ignored         |
| null tokens           | `.with_null_regex(regex)`      | regex; default `^$`                           |
| batch size            | `.with_batch_size(n)`          | records loaded per batch                      |
| line bounds           | `.with_bounds(start, end)`     | scan only line-number interval                |
| projection            | `.with_projection(vec![0, 2])` | load selected columns by zero-based index     |
| truncated rows        | `.with_truncated_rows(true)`   | short rows filled with nulls if schema allows |
| arbitrary byte stream | `.build_decoder()`             | push decoder for non-`Read` byte streams      |

`with_truncated_rows(false)` is the default and errors on rows of differing lengths; with `true`, shorter records are allowed and missing columns are filled with nulls, but non-nullable fields can still error. ([Docs.rs][3])

---

## 9.6 CSV null parsing

```rust id="csv-null-regex"
use regex::Regex;

let null_re = Regex::new(r"^(|NULL|null|NA|N/A)$")?;

let mut reader = CsvReaderBuilder::new(schema)
    .with_header(true)
    .with_null_regex(null_re)
    .build(file)?;
```

Rust CSV null parsing is regex-based, with the default null regex matching the empty string. Use anchored regexes; avoid broad patterns that accidentally null legitimate values. ([Docs.rs][3])

```text id="csv-null-rules"
Good:
  ^$
  ^(?:|NULL|NA|N/A)$

Bad:
  NULL
  N
  .*
```

---

## 9.7 CSV projection and bounded scans

### Projection

```rust id="csv-projection"
let mut reader = CsvReaderBuilder::new(schema)
    .with_header(true)
    .with_projection(vec![0, 3, 5])
    .build(file)?;
```

### Bounds

```rust id="csv-bounds"
let mut reader = CsvReaderBuilder::new(schema)
    .with_header(true)
    .with_bounds(1_000, 2_000)
    .build(file)?;
```

Use projections for ingestion-stage column pruning; use bounds for chunked file-splitting, batch jobs, sampling, and recovery workflows. `ReaderBuilder` exposes both `with_projection` and `with_bounds`, where bounds are line numbers. ([Docs.rs][3])

---

## 9.8 CSV streaming decoder for arbitrary byte streams

### Push-decoder skeleton

```rust id="csv-push-decoder"
use bytes::{Buf, Bytes};
use futures::{Stream, StreamExt};
use std::task::{Poll, ready};

fn decode_csv_stream<S>(
    mut decoder: arrow_csv::reader::Decoder,
    mut input: S,
) -> impl Stream<Item = Result<RecordBatch, ArrowError>>
where
    S: Stream<Item = Bytes> + Unpin,
{
    let mut buffered = Bytes::new();

    futures::stream::poll_fn(move |cx| {
        loop {
            if buffered.is_empty() {
                match ready!(input.poll_next_unpin(cx)) {
                    Some(bytes) => buffered = bytes,
                    None => break,
                }
            }

            let decoded = match decoder.decode(buffered.as_ref()) {
                Ok(n) => n,
                Err(e) => return Poll::Ready(Some(Err(e))),
            };

            buffered.advance(decoded);

            if decoded == 0 || decoder.capacity() == 0 {
                break;
            }
        }

        Poll::Ready(decoder.flush().transpose())
    })
}
```

`ReaderBuilder::build_decoder` produces a push-based CSV decoder for arbitrary byte streams; its `decode` method returns the number of bytes consumed, `flush` returns `Ok(None)` if no buffered data exists, and `flush` should be called after `decode` returns `Ok(0)` rather than in the middle of a partially decoded record. ([Docs.rs][3])

### Use cases

```text id="csv-decoder-use-cases"
Use CSV Decoder for:
  object_store ranged/streaming reads
  HTTP body chunks
  compressed stream after decompressor
  Tokio AsyncBufRead integration
  custom backpressure pipelines

Avoid Decoder when:
  std::fs::File + normal blocking reader is enough
  DataFusion table scan handles source already
```

---

## 9.9 CSV writer

### Basic write

```rust id="csv-writer-basic"
use arrow_csv::WriterBuilder;

let file = File::create("out.csv")?;

let mut writer = WriterBuilder::new()
    .with_header(true)
    .with_delimiter(b',')
    .build(file);

writer.write(&batch)?;
let file = writer.into_inner();
```

`arrow_csv::Writer` writes `RecordBatch` values to an underlying `Write`, exposes `write(batch)` and `into_inner`, and implements `RecordBatchWriter`. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Writer options

```rust id="csv-writer-options"
use arrow_csv::{QuoteStyle, WriterBuilder};
use csv::Terminator;

let mut writer = WriterBuilder::new()
    .with_header(true)
    .with_delimiter(b'\t')
    .with_quote(b'"')
    .with_double_quote(true)
    .with_escape(b'\\')
    .with_null("NULL".to_string())
    .with_quote_style(QuoteStyle::Necessary)
    .with_line_terminator(Terminator::LF)
    .with_timestamp_format("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%.f".to_string())
    .build(file);
```

CSV writer options include header, delimiter, quote, escape, double-quote behavior, date/datetime/time/timestamp/timestamp-with-timezone formats, null output string, whitespace trimming for string values, quote style, line terminator, and target writer construction. ([Docs.rs][6])

### Writer quote policy

```text id="csv-quote-policy"
QuoteStyle::Necessary:
  default, quote only when required

QuoteStyle::Always:
  Spark quoteAll-style output

double_quote = true:
  quote becomes ""

double_quote = false:
  quote escaped with escape character
```

## 9.10 JSON reader: explicit schema, object rows

### Sync line-delimited JSON

```rust id="json-explicit-schema"
use std::io::BufReader;
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_json::ReaderBuilder;
use arrow_schema::{DataType, Field, Schema};

let schema = Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![
    Field::new("id", DataType::Int32, false),
    Field::new("name", DataType::Utf8, true),
    Field::new("active", DataType::Boolean, true),
]));

let file = File::open("users.ndjson")?;
let mut reader = ReaderBuilder::new(schema)
    .with_batch_size(16_384)
    .with_strict_mode(true)
    .build(BufReader::new(file))?;

while let Some(batch) = reader.next() {
    let batch = batch?;
    // process RecordBatch
}
```

`arrow-json` reads JSON records into Arrow `RecordBatch` values; it ignores whitespace between JSON values, including newline and carriage return, so it can parse sequences of one or more arbitrarily formatted JSON values, including newline-delimited JSON. ([Apache Arrow][7])

### Strict mode / unknown fields

```rust id="json-strict-mode"
let reader = JsonReaderBuilder::new(schema)
    .with_strict_mode(true)
    .build(buf)?;
```

`ReaderBuilder::new(schema)` ignores JSON columns not present in the schema unless `strict_mode` is set, in which case unknown columns cause an error. ([Apache Arrow][8])

---

## 9.11 JSON reader: non-object root values

```rust id="json-new-with-field"
use std::sync::Arc;
use arrow_json::ReaderBuilder;
use arrow_schema::{DataType, Field};

let data = "1\n2\n3\n";
let field = Arc::new(Field::new("value", DataType::Int32, true));

let mut reader = ReaderBuilder::new_with_field(field)
    .with_batch_size(1024)
    .build(data.as_bytes())?;

let batch = reader.next().unwrap()?;
```

`ReaderBuilder::new_with_field(field)` parses JSON values whose root is not necessarily an object, allowing numeric/list/etc. top-level JSON values to be read into a single-column `RecordBatch`. ([Apache Arrow][8])

---

## 9.12 JSON reader options map

| Option                | Rust API                               | Behavior                                           |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| batch rows            | `.with_batch_size(n)`                  | rows per batch                                     |
| primitive → string    | `.with_coerce_primitive(true)`         | bool/number can coerce into Utf8/LargeUtf8 columns |
| strict fields         | `.with_strict_mode(true)`              | error on fields not present in schema              |
| struct decoding shape | `.with_struct_mode(mode)`              | objects/lists depending on mode                    |
| type conflicts        | `.with_ignore_type_conflicts(true)`    | incompatible value becomes null if nullable        |
| non-object root       | `ReaderBuilder::new_with_field(field)` | parse root JSON values as one field                |
| arbitrary stream      | `.build_decoder()?`                    | low-level streaming decoder                        |

`with_coerce_primitive` allows bool/number JSON values to become strings when the target column is `Utf8` or `LargeUtf8`; `with_ignore_type_conflicts(true)` makes incompatible values become null instead of errors, but nulls still error for non-nullable fields. ([Apache Arrow][8])

---

## 9.13 JSON schema inference

### Non-seekable inference

```rust id="json-infer-non-seekable"
use arrow_json::reader::infer_json_schema;

let file = File::open("events.ndjson")?;
let reader = BufReader::new(file);

let (schema, records_read) = infer_json_schema(reader, Some(10_000))?;
```

`infer_json_schema(reader, max_read_records)` reads up to the specified number of records, or the whole file if `None`; it returns the inferred schema and number of records read, but it does not seek back to the start of the reader, which matters for compressed/non-seekable streams. JSON cannot represent all Arrow types exactly, so inferred JSON schemas may differ from the original Arrow schema; for example, JSON integers infer as `Int64` and binary encoded as text infers as string. ([Apache Arrow][9])

### Seekable inference

```rust id="json-infer-seekable"
use arrow_json::reader::infer_json_schema_from_seekable;

let file = File::open("events.ndjson")?;
let mut reader = BufReader::new(file);

let (schema, records_read) = infer_json_schema_from_seekable(&mut reader, Some(10_000))?;

// reader cursor reset to start; build immediately
let mut json_reader = JsonReaderBuilder::new(Arc::new(schema))
    .with_batch_size(65_536)
    .build(reader)?;
```

`infer_json_schema_from_seekable` reads up to `max_read_records`, returns schema plus record count, and seeks the reader back to the start so it can be reused immediately. ([Apache Arrow][10])

### Iterator inference

```rust id="json-infer-value-iterator"
use arrow_json::reader::infer_json_schema_from_iterator;
use serde_json::Value;

let values: Vec<Result<Value, ArrowError>> = vec![
    Ok(serde_json::json!({"id": 1, "name": "a"})),
    Ok(serde_json::json!({"id": 2, "name": "b"})),
];

let schema = infer_json_schema_from_iterator(values.into_iter())?;
```

The iterator inference path has explicit coercion behavior: `Int64` and `Float64` become `Float64`, lists and scalars can coerce to compatible lists, and other mixed cases coerce to `Utf8`. ([Apache Arrow][11])

---

## 9.14 JSON `Decoder`: streaming bytes

### Arbitrary bytes stream

```rust id="json-decoder-bytes-stream"
use bytes::{Buf, Bytes};
use futures::{Stream, StreamExt};
use std::task::{Poll, ready};

fn decode_json_stream<S>(
    mut decoder: arrow_json::reader::Decoder,
    mut input: S,
) -> impl Stream<Item = Result<RecordBatch, ArrowError>>
where
    S: Stream<Item = Bytes> + Unpin,
{
    let mut buffered = Bytes::new();

    futures::stream::poll_fn(move |cx| {
        loop {
            if buffered.is_empty() {
                buffered = match ready!(input.poll_next_unpin(cx)) {
                    Some(b) => b,
                    None => break,
                };
            }

            let decoded = match decoder.decode(buffered.as_ref()) {
                Ok(n) => n,
                Err(e) => return Poll::Ready(Some(Err(e))),
            };

            let read = buffered.len();
            buffered.advance(decoded);

            if decoded != read {
                break;
            }
        }

        Poll::Ready(decoder.flush().transpose())
    })
}
```

`arrow_json::reader::Decoder` is a low-level interface for arbitrary byte streams; `decode(buf)` consumes bytes and can stop at batch size or buffer exhaustion, and `flush()` returns `Ok(None)` when no records are buffered or errors if called partway through a JSON record. ([Apache Arrow][12])

---

## 9.15 JSON serde-compatible conversion

### `serde_json::Value` rows

```rust id="json-serde-value"
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::types::Float32Type;
use arrow_json::ReaderBuilder;
use arrow_schema::{DataType, Field, Schema};

let rows = vec![
    serde_json::json!({"float": 2.3}),
    serde_json::json!({"float": 5.7}),
];

let schema = Schema::new(vec![
    Field::new("float", DataType::Float32, true),
]);

let mut decoder = ReaderBuilder::new(Arc::new(schema))
    .build_decoder()?;

decoder.serialize(&rows)?;

let batch = decoder.flush()?.unwrap();
```

### Strongly typed Rust structs

```rust id="json-serde-struct"
use serde::Serialize;

#[derive(Serialize)]
struct UserRow {
    id: i32,
    name: String,
    active: bool,
}

let rows = vec![
    UserRow { id: 1, name: "alice".into(), active: true },
    UserRow { id: 2, name: "bob".into(), active: false },
];

let schema = Schema::new(vec![
    Field::new("id", DataType::Int32, false),
    Field::new("name", DataType::Utf8, false),
    Field::new("active", DataType::Boolean, false),
]);

let mut decoder = JsonReaderBuilder::new(Arc::new(schema)).build_decoder()?;
decoder.serialize(&rows)?;
let batch = decoder.flush()?.unwrap();
```

`Decoder::serialize` converts serde-compatible structures into Arrow `RecordBatch` values; the docs warn this is likely less performant than custom builders when schemas are known at compile time, but it is a fast way to get Rust structs or `serde_json::Value` into Arrow. ([Apache Arrow][12])

### Deployment rule

```text id="serde-deploy-rule"
Use Decoder::serialize when:
  prototyping
  dynamic serde_json::Value ingestion
  low/medium volume
  schema generated from Rust model

Use Arrow builders when:
  hot path
  high-throughput service
  fixed schema
  predictable field types
```

---

## 9.16 JSON writer

### Line-delimited JSON writer

```rust id="json-line-writer"
use arrow_json::LineDelimitedWriter;

let mut writer = LineDelimitedWriter::new(Vec::new());

writer.write_batches(&vec![&batch])?;
writer.finish()?;

let bytes = writer.into_inner();
```

`LineDelimitedWriter` serializes `RecordBatch`es into newline-delimited JSON objects; `ArrayWriter` serializes batches into one well-formed JSON array. ([Apache Arrow][13])

### JSON array writer

```rust id="json-array-writer"
use arrow_json::ArrayWriter;

let mut writer = ArrayWriter::new(Vec::new());

writer.write_batches(&vec![&batch])?;
writer.finish()?;

let bytes = writer.into_inner();
```

### Custom JSON writer options

```rust id="json-writer-builder"
use arrow_json::writer::{WriterBuilder, LineDelimited};

let mut writer = WriterBuilder::new()
    .with_explicit_nulls(true)
    .with_date_format("%Y-%m-%d".to_string())
    .with_datetime_format("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S".to_string())
    .with_time_format("%H:%M:%S".to_string())
    .with_timestamp_format("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%.f".to_string())
    .build::<_, LineDelimited>(Vec::new());

writer.write_batches(&vec![&batch])?;
writer.finish()?;
```

By default, JSON writers omit keys with null values; `WriterBuilder::with_explicit_nulls(true)` keeps null-valued keys, and `WriterBuilder` also configures struct mode, custom encoder factory, and date/time/timestamp formatting. ([Apache Arrow][13])

---

## 9.17 Encoding, malformed rows, and type conversion

### CSV encoding

```text id="csv-encoding-rules"
Rust arrow-csv:
  expects byte streams parsed into Arrow scalar types
  UTF-8 string handling follows Rust/string conversion paths
  non-UTF8 textual input should be decoded/transcoded before Arrow Utf8 columns
  binary-like CSV content should target Binary or pre-decoded bytes when applicable

PyArrow:
  ReadOptions has encoding parameter
  columns that cannot decode with that encoding can still be read as Binary
```

PyArrow CSV `ReadOptions` exposes `encoding`, `block_size`, threading, skip rows, column names, and autogenerated column names; Rust `arrow-csv` focuses on Rust byte readers plus explicit/inferred Arrow schema and parser options. ([Apache Arrow][14])

### CSV malformed rows

```rust id="csv-truncated-rows"
let mut reader = CsvReaderBuilder::new(schema)
    .with_header(true)
    .with_truncated_rows(true)
    .build(file)?;
```

```text id="csv-malformed-rules"
with_truncated_rows(false):
  row length mismatch -> error

with_truncated_rows(true):
  missing columns -> null
  non-nullable missing field -> error

extra columns:
  treat as malformed unless projection/schema/parser path accounts for them
```

### JSON type conflicts

```rust id="json-ignore-type-conflicts"
let mut reader = JsonReaderBuilder::new(schema)
    .with_ignore_type_conflicts(true)
    .build(buf)?;
```

```text id="json-type-conflict-rules"
ignore_type_conflicts(false):
  incompatible JSON value -> error

ignore_type_conflicts(true):
  incompatible value -> null
  non-nullable target field -> still error
```

`ReaderBuilder::with_ignore_type_conflicts(true)` produces null instead of returning an error for values that cannot be parsed into the specified column type, but inferred nulls still fail for non-nullable fields. ([Apache Arrow][8])

---

## 9.18 Schema inference versus explicit schema

| Workload                       | Recommended schema strategy                                            |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| production ingestion           | explicit `SchemaRef`                                                   |
| one-off CLI                    | infer first N rows                                                     |
| evolving external files        | infer sample, persist schema, validate later                           |
| JSON with nested fields        | explicit schema strongly preferred                                     |
| CSV with dates/decimal/money   | explicit schema strongly preferred                                     |
| compressed non-seekable stream | infer consumes stream; use explicit schema or buffer/rewind equivalent |
| multi-file CSV dataset         | infer across representative files, then freeze schema                  |
| line-delimited JSON service    | explicit schema + strict mode                                          |

### Why explicit schema wins

```text id="explicit-schema-value"
Explicit schema:
  deterministic datatypes
  deterministic nullability
  no sample bias
  stable Parquet/IPC downstream
  safer for money/decimal/date/timestamp
  fewer production surprises
```

### Inference caveats

```text id="inference-caveats"
CSV inference:
  sample-limited
  quoted strings tend to Utf8
  unrepresentable/overflow integers may fall back
  no guarantee future rows match sample

JSON inference:
  JSON lacks exact Arrow type space
  integers infer as Int64
  binary text infers as string
  mixed Int64/Float64 becomes Float64 in iterator inference
  nested/list coercion has defined but non-PyArrow-identical behavior
```

PyArrow JSON docs explicitly note inference rules for nulls, booleans, numbers, date-like strings, arrays, and nested objects, and warn that incremental reading freezes types after the first block unless an explicit schema or large enough block is used. ([Apache Arrow][15])

---

## 9.19 Streaming ingestion patterns

### Sync CSV → per-batch processing

```rust id="sync-csv-per-batch"
fn ingest_csv<R: Read>(
    reader: R,
    schema: SchemaRef,
) -> Result<usize, ArrowError> {
    let mut csv = CsvReaderBuilder::new(schema)
        .with_header(true)
        .with_batch_size(65_536)
        .build(reader)?;

    let mut rows = 0usize;

    while let Some(batch) = csv.next() {
        let batch = batch?;
        rows += batch.num_rows();
        // transform / write / send batch
    }

    Ok(rows)
}
```

### Sync JSON → per-batch processing

```rust id="sync-json-per-batch"
fn ingest_json<R: std::io::BufRead>(
    reader: R,
    schema: SchemaRef,
) -> Result<usize, ArrowError> {
    let mut json = JsonReaderBuilder::new(schema)
        .with_batch_size(65_536)
        .with_strict_mode(true)
        .build(reader)?;

    let mut rows = 0usize;

    while let Some(batch) = json.next() {
        let batch = batch?;
        rows += batch.num_rows();
    }

    Ok(rows)
}
```

### Compression wrapper

```rust id="compressed-json-reader"
use flate2::read::GzDecoder;

let file = File::open("events.ndjson.gz")?;
let decoder = GzDecoder::new(file);
let buf = BufReader::new(decoder);

let mut reader = JsonReaderBuilder::new(schema)
    .with_batch_size(65_536)
    .build(buf)?;
```

### Batch sizing rule

```text id="ingestion-batch-size-rule"
Default:
  8_192 to 65_536 rows

High-throughput batch ETL:
  65_536 rows, byte cap separately

Low-latency stream:
  1_024 to 8_192 rows

String/nested-heavy JSON:
  cap by approximate bytes, not only rows
```

---

## 9.20 PyArrow equivalence table

| PyArrow                                                        | Rust Arrow                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pyarrow.csv.read_csv(path)`                                   | `CsvReaderBuilder::new(schema).build(file)` + collect batches |
| `pyarrow.csv.open_csv(path)`                                   | `CsvReaderBuilder` as iterator / `RecordBatchReader`          |
| `pyarrow.csv.ReadOptions(block_size=...)`                      | `.with_batch_size(rows)` not byte block size                  |
| `pyarrow.csv.ReadOptions(skip_rows=...)`                       | `.with_bounds(start, end)` or pre-skip externally             |
| `pyarrow.csv.ParseOptions(delimiter=...)`                      | `.with_delimiter(b'...')`                                     |
| `pyarrow.csv.ParseOptions(quote_char=...)`                     | `.with_quote(b'...')`                                         |
| `pyarrow.csv.ParseOptions(escape_char=...)`                    | `.with_escape(b'...')`                                        |
| `pyarrow.csv.ConvertOptions(column_types=...)`                 | explicit `Schema`                                             |
| `pyarrow.csv.ConvertOptions(null_values=...)`                  | `.with_null_regex(regex)`                                     |
| `pyarrow.csv.ConvertOptions(include_columns=...)`              | `.with_projection(indices)`                                   |
| `pyarrow.csv.write_csv(table, path)`                           | `CsvWriterBuilder::new().build(file).write(&batch)`           |
| `pyarrow.json.read_json(path)`                                 | `JsonReaderBuilder::new(schema).build(buf)` + collect         |
| `pyarrow.json.open_json(path)`                                 | JSON reader iterator / decoder stream                         |
| `pyarrow.json.ParseOptions(explicit_schema=...)`               | explicit `SchemaRef`                                          |
| `pyarrow.json.ParseOptions(unexpected_field_behavior="error")` | `.with_strict_mode(true)`                                     |
| `pyarrow.json.ReadOptions(block_size=...)`                     | `.with_batch_size(rows)` plus decoder chunking                |
| `pyarrow.Table` result                                         | `Vec<RecordBatch>`                                            |
| `pyarrow.RecordBatchReader`                                    | `RecordBatchReader` / iterator                                |

PyArrow `read_csv` and `read_json` both return in-memory `pyarrow.Table` values; Rust Arrow readers are naturally batch iterators, so stream batches unless the API explicitly requires eager table-like materialization. ([Apache Arrow][2])

---

## 9.21 DataFusion integration rule

```text id="datafusion-integration-rule"
Use arrow-csv / arrow-json when:
  local parser control
  custom ingestion service
  per-batch transform
  Rust struct -> RecordBatch
  custom stream decoder

Use DataFusion when:
  SQL over CSV/JSON files
  multi-file discovery
  projection/filter/query planning
  joins/aggregations/windows after ingestion
  object-store table scans
```

### Pattern: local CSV parse then register batches

```rust id="csv-register-batches"
let batches: Vec<RecordBatch> = reader.collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;

let schema = batches[0].schema();
let mem = datafusion::datasource::MemTable::try_new(schema, vec![batches])?;

ctx.register_table("csv_data", Arc::new(mem))?;
```

## 9.22 Error handling and boundary normalization

```rust id="csv-json-error-normalization"
fn csv_json_error_context(path: &str, err: ArrowError) -> ArrowError {
    ArrowError::ParseError(format!("failed to parse {path}: {err}"))
}
```

```text id="ingestion-error-categories"
CSV:
  row length mismatch
  non-nullable missing field
  invalid type conversion
  invalid UTF-8/text conversion
  malformed quoting/escaping
  bad delimiter/comment/terminator assumptions

JSON:
  malformed JSON
  partial record on flush
  unknown field in strict mode
  type conflict
  null for non-nullable field
  unsupported root structure unless new_with_field
```

### Boundary rule

```text id="ingestion-boundary-rule"
At service/API boundary:
  include path/source offset if available
  include format profile name
  include schema version
  include line/batch number if tracked
  do not expose raw parser internals to end users unless debug mode
```

## 9.23 Deployment advisory

### CSV production ingestion

```text id="csv-production-advisory"
DO:
  use explicit schema
  set header/delimiter/quote/escape explicitly
  use anchored null regex
  batch by rows and downstream byte pressure
  use projection for column pruning
  reject truncated rows unless contract permits them
  persist schema version with outputs

DON'T:
  infer schema from a tiny sample in production
  accept broad null regex
  rely on inferred nullability
  use CSV as long-term typed storage
```

### JSON production ingestion

```text id="json-production-advisory"
DO:
  prefer NDJSON / one record per logical row
  use explicit schema
  enable strict_mode when schema contract is closed
  use ignore_type_conflicts only for nullable soft-fail columns
  use new_with_field for non-object root values
  use Decoder for async/object-store streams

DON'T:
  treat arbitrary pretty-printed JSON arrays as equivalent to NDJSON without testing
  infer schema on first tiny block and freeze silently
  encode binary data as JSON unless format contract says how
  use serde conversion in hot path if builders are feasible
```

### Writer advisory

```text id="writer-advisory"
CSV writer:
  choose null string explicitly
  choose quote style explicitly when downstream is Spark/Excel/db loader
  choose timestamp formats explicitly
  test round-trip against target parser

JSON writer:
  choose line-delimited vs JSON array explicitly
  choose explicit_nulls policy
  choose struct mode
  test null omission semantics with downstream
```

---

## 9.24 Anti-pattern catalog

| Anti-pattern                                               | Failure mode                   | Correct pattern                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| infer CSV schema from 10 rows and ship                     | later type failures            | explicit schema or representative inference + validation |
| broad null regex like `.*NULL.*`                           | corrupt valid strings          | anchored null regex                                      |
| rely on PyArrow byte `block_size` mental model             | wrong Rust batching assumption | Rust reader `with_batch_size(rows)`                      |
| collect entire CSV/JSON into `Vec<RecordBatch>` by default | memory blowup                  | per-batch streaming                                      |
| call JSON `flush()` mid-record                             | error                          | flush only when decoder has complete buffered records    |
| ignore JSON unknown fields accidentally                    | silent data loss               | `strict_mode(true)` for closed schema                    |
| `ignore_type_conflicts(true)` on non-nullable fields       | still errors                   | make field nullable or reject data                       |
| write JSON with omitted nulls when downstream expects keys | schema drift downstream        | `with_explicit_nulls(true)`                              |
| assume Rust auto-decompresses by extension                 | file parse failure             | wrap with decompressor                                   |
| use serde conversion for high-throughput fixed schema      | slower                         | Arrow builders                                           |

## 9.25 Golden test matrix

```rust id="csv-json-golden-tests"
#[test]
fn csv_empty_string_is_null_by_default() -> Result<(), ArrowError> {
    let schema = Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![
        Field::new("x", DataType::Utf8, true),
    ]));

    let data = "x\n\n";
    let mut reader = CsvReaderBuilder::new(schema)
        .with_header(true)
        .build(data.as_bytes())?;

    let batch = reader.next().unwrap()?;
    assert!(batch.column(0).is_null(0));
    Ok(())
}

#[test]
fn json_unknown_field_errors_in_strict_mode() -> Result<(), ArrowError> {
    let schema = Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![
        Field::new("x", DataType::Int32, true),
    ]));

    let data = br#"{"x":1,"extra":2}"#;

    let mut reader = JsonReaderBuilder::new(schema)
        .with_strict_mode(true)
        .build(&data[..])?;

    assert!(reader.next().unwrap().is_err());
    Ok(())
}
```

Test categories:

```text id="ingestion-test-categories"
CSV:
  header true/false
  custom delimiter
  quote + escaped quote
  empty field null
  custom null regex
  malformed row length
  truncated row allowed/disallowed
  projection
  schema inference sample mismatch
  compressed wrapper

JSON:
  NDJSON objects
  top-level scalar via new_with_field
  top-level list via new_with_field
  unknown field strict/non-strict
  type conflict ignore/error
  nullable/non-nullable nulls
  nested struct/list/map
  serde_json::Value conversion
  Rust struct serialize conversion
  line-delimited writer explicit_nulls true/false
```

---

## 9.26 Value case

```text id="csv-json-value-case"
arrow-csv ReaderBuilder:
  value = deterministic CSV -> RecordBatch ingestion with parser/schema/null/projection controls.

arrow-csv Format inference:
  value = bootstrap schemas from CSV samples; not a production schema registry.

arrow-csv Decoder:
  value = arbitrary byte-stream ingestion for object stores, HTTP, async, compressed streams.

arrow-csv WriterBuilder:
  value = controlled CSV export for external systems.

arrow-json ReaderBuilder:
  value = NDJSON/JSON sequence -> typed RecordBatch ingestion with strict/type-conflict controls.

arrow-json Decoder:
  value = streaming JSON parsing independent of IO runtime.

Decoder::serialize:
  value = serde-compatible Rust data -> RecordBatch without manual builders.

JSON writers:
  value = RecordBatch -> NDJSON or JSON array output with null/struct formatting policy.

Explicit schema:
  value = stable downstream IPC/Parquet/DataFusion contracts.

Streaming ingestion:
  value = bounded memory, early processing, backpressure compatibility.
```

Final agent rule:

```text id="csv-json-final-rule"
For production ingestion:
  explicit schema + streaming batches + strict malformed-data policy.

For exploration:
  infer schema + inspect + persist schema + rerun with explicit schema.

For async/object-store:
  build_decoder + feed bytes + flush at batch/record boundaries.

For PyArrow equivalence:
  PyArrow returns Table; Rust should usually stream RecordBatch values and only collect when explicitly required.
```

# 10) IPC, Arrow files, streams, and Feather

Style target: dense, syntax-first, agent-ready technical reference; aligned with the uploaded advanced-reference pattern. 

---

## 10.0 Mental model

```text id="ipc-mental-model"
Arrow IPC =
  binary serialization for Schema + DictionaryBatch + RecordBatch messages

IPC stream format =
  schema first
  then zero or more dictionary / record batch messages
  sequential processing
  no random access
  good for pipes, sockets, Flight internals, streaming services

IPC file format =
  magic bytes + schema/messages + footer
  fixed set of record batches
  footer contains block metadata
  random access
  good for files, mmap, Feather V2, local interchange

Feather V2 =
  Arrow IPC file format on disk
```

The `arrow-ipc` crate defines two IPC variants: streaming format with `StreamReader` / `StreamWriter`, and file/random-access format with `FileReader` / `FileWriter`. The file reader requires a seekable reader, while the stream reader only requires sequential `Read`. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 10.1 Cargo profiles

### Facade IPC

```toml id="ipc-cargo-facade"
[dependencies]

```

```toml id="ipc-cargo-facade-compression"

```

The `arrow` crate enables `csv`, `ipc`, and `json` by default; its `ipc_compression` feature enables `arrow-ipc/lz4`, `arrow-ipc/zstd`, and the `ipc` feature. ([Docs.rs][2])


`arrow-ipc 58.4.0` exposes no enabled default compression features; optional `lz4` enables `lz4_flex`, and optional `zstd` enables `zstd`. ([Docs.rs][3])

```rust id="ipc-imports"
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{BufReader, BufWriter, Cursor, Read, Write, Seek};
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::{ArrayRef, Int32Array, RecordBatch, RecordBatchReader, StringArray};
use arrow_buffer::Buffer;

use arrow_ipc::writer::{FileWriter, StreamWriter, IpcWriteOptions};
```
