## 10.3 IPC stream format

### Use when

```text id="ipc-stream-use"
Use StreamWriter / StreamReader for:
  stdin/stdout pipes
  TCP/unix socket payloads
  HTTP body streams
  object-store chunk streams
  process-to-process streaming
  RecordBatchReader export
  Flight-like sequential transport
```

### Write IPC stream

```rust id="ipc-stream-write"
use arrow_ipc::writer::StreamWriter;

fn write_ipc_stream<W: Write>(
    mut writer: W,
    schema: &Schema,
    batches: impl IntoIterator<Item = RecordBatch>,
) -> Result<W, ArrowError> {
    let mut ipc = StreamWriter::try_new(&mut writer, schema)?;

    for batch in batches {
        ipc.write(&batch)?;
    }

    ipc.finish()?;
    drop(ipc);

    Ok(writer)
}
```

`StreamWriter` writes `RecordBatch` values using the IPC streaming format; the schema must be known in advance, batches are written sequentially, and `finish()` flushes all buffers/termination data. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Read IPC stream

```rust id="ipc-stream-read"
use arrow_ipc::reader::StreamReader;

fn read_ipc_stream<R: Read>(reader: R) -> Result<usize, ArrowError> {
    let projection = None;
    let mut ipc = StreamReader::try_new(reader, projection)?;

    let schema = ipc.schema();
    let mut rows = 0usize;

    while let Some(batch) = ipc.next() {
        let batch = batch?;
        rows += batch.num_rows();
    }

    assert!(ipc.is_finished());
    Ok(rows)
}
```

`StreamReader::try_new(reader, projection)` errors if the first stream message is not a schema; it implements `Iterator<Item = Result<RecordBatch, ArrowError>>` and `RecordBatchReader`, exposes `schema()`, and can report `is_finished()`. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Buffered stream reader

```rust id="ipc-stream-buffered-reader"
let file = File::open("data.arrow_stream")?;
let reader = StreamReader::try_new_buffered(file, None)?;
```

`StreamReader::try_new` has no internal buffering; use `try_new_buffered` when buffered reads are needed. ([Docs.rs][5])

---

## 10.4 IPC file format

### Use when

```text id="ipc-file-use"
Use FileWriter / FileReader for:
  local Arrow files
  Feather V2-compatible files
  random access to batches
  memory-mapped read patterns
  fixed finite datasets
  compact table snapshots
```

### Write IPC file

```rust id="ipc-file-write"
use arrow_ipc::writer::FileWriter;

fn write_ipc_file<W: Write>(
    mut writer: W,
    schema: &Schema,
    batches: impl IntoIterator<Item = RecordBatch>,
) -> Result<W, ArrowError> {
    let mut ipc = FileWriter::try_new(&mut writer, schema)?;

    for batch in batches {
        ipc.write(&batch)?;
    }

    ipc.finish()?;
    drop(ipc);

    Ok(writer)
}
```

`FileWriter` writes `RecordBatch` values in the IPC file format; it writes the schema as part of the header, writes batches, and `finish()` writes final footer/termination data. ([Docs.rs][6])

### Read IPC file

```rust id="ipc-file-read"
use arrow_ipc::reader::FileReader;

fn read_ipc_file<R: Read + Seek>(reader: R) -> Result<usize, ArrowError> {
    let projection = None;
    let mut ipc = FileReader::try_new(reader, projection)?;

    let schema = ipc.schema();
    let batches = ipc.num_batches();

    let mut rows = 0usize;
    for batch in ipc {
        rows += batch?.num_rows();
    }

    Ok(rows)
}
```

`FileReader` reads IPC file-format bytes, provides random access to record batches, requires `Read + Seek`, exposes `num_batches()`, `schema()`, `custom_metadata()`, and `set_index()`, and implements both `Iterator` and `RecordBatchReader`. ([Docs.rs][7])

### Random access batch read

```rust id="ipc-file-random-access"
let mut reader = FileReader::try_new(file, None)?;

reader.set_index(5)?;
let batch = reader.next()
    .ok_or_else(|| ArrowError::IpcError("missing batch at index 5".into()))??;
```

`FileReader::set_index(index)` sets the current block index and enables random reads over the finite set of record batches. ([Docs.rs][7])

### Projection

```rust id="ipc-projection"
let projection = Some(vec![0, 3, 4]);

let file_reader = FileReader::try_new(file, projection.clone())?;
let stream_reader = StreamReader::try_new(stream, projection)?;
```

Projection is zero-based column selection at reader construction for both stream and file readers.

---

## 10.5 File versus stream decision matrix

| Requirement                             | Choose                                     | Reason                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| stdin/stdout                            | IPC stream                                 | no seek                                            |
| socket / pipe                           | IPC stream                                 | sequential                                         |
| HTTP response body                      | IPC stream                                 | chunkable                                          |
| Flight-like service payload             | IPC stream / Flight                        | record batch stream                                |
| local file snapshot                     | IPC file                                   | footer + random access                             |
| memory-mapped random reads              | IPC file                                   | seekable, footer metadata                          |
| Feather V2 compatibility                | IPC file                                   | Feather V2 is IPC file format                      |
| unknown number of batches while writing | IPC stream                                 | no footer block table required                     |
| need `num_batches()`                    | IPC file                                   | footer has batch metadata                          |
| read batch N                            | IPC file                                   | `set_index`                                        |
| append after finish                     | neither                                    | IPC formats are immutable once finished            |
| cloud object store random ranges        | IPC file possible but Parquet often better | object-store range planning / compression tradeoff |

Arrow’s Python IPC docs define streaming format as an arbitrary-length sequence processed start-to-end without random access, and file/random-access format as a fixed number of record batches with random access support, useful with memory maps. ([Apache Arrow][8])

---

## 10.6 Compression

### Cargo

```toml id="ipc-compression-cargo"
[dependencies]
arrow-ipc = { version = "58.4.0", features = ["lz4", "zstd"] }
```

or:

```toml id="ipc-compression-arrow-cargo"
[dependencies]
arrow = { version = "58.4.0", features = ["ipc_compression"] }
```

### Write compressed IPC

```rust id="ipc-compressed-write"
use arrow_ipc::writer::{FileWriter, IpcWriteOptions};
use arrow_ipc::CompressionType;

let options = IpcWriteOptions::default()
    .try_with_compression(Some(CompressionType::LZ4_FRAME))?;

let mut writer = FileWriter::try_new_with_options(file, schema.as_ref(), options)?;

for batch in batches {
    writer.write(&batch)?;
}

writer.finish()?;
```

```rust id="ipc-zstd-write"
let options = IpcWriteOptions::default()
    .try_with_compression(Some(CompressionType::ZSTD))?;
```

`IpcWriteOptions` controls IPC write behavior, including alignment, metadata version, compression, and dictionary handling; `try_with_compression` configures compression and returns a runtime error if the corresponding feature is not enabled. ([Apache Arrow][9])

### Compression codecs

```text id="ipc-codecs"
Supported IPC compression:
  LZ4 frame
  ZSTD

Rust feature gates:
  arrow-ipc/lz4
  arrow-ipc/zstd
  arrow/ipc_compression
```

The Arrow IPC compression implementation uses `CompressionCodec::Lz4Frame` and `CompressionCodec::Zstd`; missing feature gates produce errors such as “lz4 IPC compression requires the lz4 feature.” ([Apache Arrow][10])

### Compression advisory

```text id="ipc-compression-advisory"
LZ4:
  lower CPU
  fast local interchange
  good default for Feather-like files

ZSTD:
  better compression ratio
  higher CPU
  useful for network/disk-constrained paths

Uncompressed:
  fastest decode when IO is not bottleneck
  best for mmap/zero-copy-like local analytics

Always test:
  payload width
  string/binary cardinality
  storage medium
  CPU budget
```

Feather V2 supports LZ4 and ZSTD compression; PyArrow docs state LZ4 is used by default if available and can be faster than uncompressed in some cases due to reduced disk IO. ([Apache Arrow][11])

---

## 10.7 Dictionary handling

### Delta dictionaries

```rust id="ipc-delta-dict"
use arrow_ipc::writer::{DictionaryHandling, IpcWriteOptions, StreamWriter};

let options = IpcWriteOptions::default()
    .with_dictionary_handling(DictionaryHandling::Delta);

let mut writer = StreamWriter::try_new_with_options(
    sink,
    schema.as_ref(),
    options,
)?;
```

### Builder requirement

```rust id="ipc-delta-dict-builder"
use arrow_array::builder::StringDictionaryBuilder;
use arrow_array::types::Int32Type;

let mut builder = StringDictionaryBuilder::<Int32Type>::new();

builder.append("a")?;
builder.append("b")?;
let batch1_dict = builder.finish_preserve_values();

builder.append("a")?;
builder.append("d")?;
let batch2_dict = builder.finish_preserve_values();
```

`StreamWriter` docs show efficient delta dictionaries using `DictionaryHandling::Delta` plus dictionary builders’ `finish_preserve_values`; without preserving values/key assignments, a later batch may force replacement dictionaries instead of small deltas. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Dictionary advisory

```text id="ipc-dictionary-advisory"
Use delta dictionaries when:
  same low-cardinality dictionary evolves across batches
  streaming repeated categories
  writer controls batch construction

Avoid assuming stable keys when:
  batches come from independent sources
  dictionary arrays are built per batch independently
  downstream compares dictionary keys instead of values
```

---

## 10.8 Low-level stream decoder

### Push bytes into `StreamDecoder`

```rust id="ipc-stream-decoder"
use arrow_buffer::Buffer;
use arrow_ipc::reader::StreamDecoder;

fn decode_ipc_chunks<I>(chunks: I) -> Result<Vec<RecordBatch>, ArrowError>
where
    I: IntoIterator<Item = Buffer>,
{
    let mut decoder = StreamDecoder::new();
    let mut out = Vec::new();

    for mut chunk in chunks {
        while !chunk.is_empty() {
            if let Some(batch) = decoder.decode(&mut chunk)? {
                out.push(batch);
            }

            if let Some(schema) = decoder.schema() {
                // schema available after schema message
                let _ = schema;
            }
        }
    }

    decoder.finish()?;
    Ok(out)
}
```

`StreamDecoder` is a low-level push-based IPC stream decoder for arbitrary byte ranges; `decode` consumes bytes from a `Buffer`, may return `None` until enough bytes are available, exposes schema once decoded, and `finish()` errors if partial data remains. ([Docs.rs][12])

### Alignment mode

```rust id="ipc-stream-decoder-alignment"
let decoder = StreamDecoder::new()
    .with_require_alignment(true);
```

With `require_alignment(true)`, `StreamDecoder` errors on insufficiently aligned input buffers; by default it will allocate aligned buffers and copy only when input is not properly aligned, while aligned buffers remain zero-copy. ([Docs.rs][12])

### Validation skip

```rust id="ipc-stream-decoder-skip-validation"
let decoder = unsafe {
    StreamDecoder::new().with_skip_validation(true)
};
```

`with_skip_validation(true)` is unsafe and must only be used when input data is trusted and known-valid Arrow IPC stream data; otherwise undefined behavior may result. ([Docs.rs][12])

---

## 10.9 Validation and safety

```text id="ipc-validation-rules"
Trusted self-written spill file:
  skip_validation may be considered with benchmark proof

Untrusted user file:
  never skip validation

Network input:
  never skip validation

Object-store input:
  never skip validation unless producer and integrity envelope are controlled

FFI/IPC external buffers:
  require or repair alignment
```

`FileReader` and `StreamReader` expose unsafe `with_skip_validation`; docs say validation defaults to false for skipping and point to decoder safety requirements. The stream decoder safety docs explicitly warn that skipping validation on untrusted input may result in undefined behavior. ([Docs.rs][7])

---

## 10.10 Feather V2

```text id="feather-v2-model"
Feather V2:
  exactly Arrow IPC file format on disk
  supports all Arrow data types
  supports LZ4 / ZSTD compression
  default in modern PyArrow

Feather V1:
  legacy
  distinct from Arrow IPC
  lacks full Arrow type support
  lacks compression support
```

Feather V2 is exactly represented as the Arrow IPC file format on disk, supports all Arrow data types and LZ4/ZSTD compression, while Feather V1 is legacy, distinct from Arrow IPC, lacks many Arrow type features, and lacks compression. ([Apache Arrow][11])

### Rust write Feather V2-compatible file

```rust id="feather-v2-write-rust"
let mut writer = FileWriter::try_new(file, schema.as_ref())?;

for batch in batches {
    writer.write(&batch)?;
}

writer.finish()?;
```

### Rust read Feather V2-compatible file

```rust id="feather-v2-read-rust"
let mut reader = FileReader::try_new(file, None)?;

for batch in reader {
    let batch = batch?;
}
```

### Compatibility rule

```text id="feather-compat-rule"
Rust arrow-ipc FileWriter output:
  Arrow IPC file
  Feather V2-compatible at format layer

Rust arrow-ipc FileReader input:
  reads Arrow IPC file / Feather V2-style files

Not guaranteed:
  Feather V1 read/write support through arrow-ipc
```

---

## 10.11 Interprocess and cross-language compatibility

### Cross-language read/write target

```text id="ipc-cross-language"
Rust FileWriter/StreamWriter output can be consumed by:
  PyArrow IPC readers
  Arrow Java/C++/R/Go implementations
  DataFusion/Arrow Rust readers
  systems implementing Arrow IPC spec

Rust FileReader/StreamReader can consume:
  PyArrow IPC file/stream output
  Feather V2 files
  Arrow IPC streams from other implementations
```

Arrow IPC serializes `RecordBatch` data to/from files or byte streams and is designed for IPC / serialization across Arrow implementations; Arrow Flight builds on gRPC and the IPC format for high-performance data services. ([Docs.rs][1])

### PyArrow equivalents

| PyArrow                                 | Rust                                        |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `pa.ipc.new_stream(sink, schema)`       | `StreamWriter::try_new(sink, schema)`       |
| `pa.ipc.open_stream(source)`            | `StreamReader::try_new(source, projection)` |
| `pa.ipc.new_file(sink, schema)`         | `FileWriter::try_new(sink, schema)`         |
| `pa.ipc.open_file(source)`              | `FileReader::try_new(source, projection)`   |
| `pa.feather.write_feather(table, path)` | `FileWriter` over `Vec<RecordBatch>`        |
| `pa.feather.read_table(path)`           | `FileReader` collect to `Vec<RecordBatch>`  |
| `pyarrow.RecordBatchReader`             | `RecordBatchReader` / `StreamReader`        |
| `pyarrow.Table`                         | `Vec<RecordBatch>` / `arrow_pyarrow::Table` |

---

## 10.12 IPC versus C Data Interface versus Flight

| Mechanism        | Boundary                     | Transport/storage            | Copies                                                   | Rust crate/API                                  | Use                                   |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| IPC stream       | byte stream                  | pipe/socket/file/stdout      | serialize/deserialize buffers; can preserve Arrow layout | `StreamReader`, `StreamWriter`, `StreamDecoder` | sequential `RecordBatch` transfer     |
| IPC file         | seekable bytes               | local file/mmap/object bytes | file footer + batch metadata                             | `FileReader`, `FileWriter`                      | random-access files / Feather V2      |
| C Data Interface | in-process ABI               | pointers/structs             | designed for zero-copy in process                        | `arrow/ffi`, `pyo3-arrow`, `arrow_pyarrow`      | Python/Rust/C++ same-process exchange |
| Flight           | network RPC                  | gRPC + IPC payloads          | optimized Arrow stream transport                         | `arrow-flight`                                  | client/server data services           |
| Parquet          | persisted analytical storage | file/object store            | columnar encoded/compressed, not Arrow memory format     | `parquet`                                       | long-term lake storage                |

### Decision rules

```text id="ipc-vs-cdata-flight"
Use IPC file:
  finite local file
  Feather V2
  random access
  mmap-like workflows

Use IPC stream:
  producer/consumer pipeline
  byte stream
  stdout/stdin
  simple network body
  no service metadata needed

Use C Data / PyCapsule:
  same process
  Python/Rust interop
  zero-copy transfer
  no byte serialization desired

Use Flight:
  client/server
  authentication/TLS/middleware
  discovery/metadata methods
  upload/download streams
  Flight SQL protocol

Use Parquet:
  durable analytics storage
  predicate/statistics/row-group pruning
  object store data lake
```

Arrow Flight is defined as an RPC framework for high-performance data services based on Arrow data, built on gRPC and IPC, organized around streams of Arrow record batches with metadata methods for discovery and introspection. ([Apache Arrow][13])

---

## 10.13 File/mmap and zero-copy notes

```text id="ipc-mmap-notes"
IPC file + mmap:
  suitable for local random-access reads
  file footer enables batch location lookup
  can reduce copies if buffers are aligned and memory mapping is used

IPC stream:
  not random access
  cannot jump to batch N
  schema must appear first
  process start-to-end

Alignment:
  IPC readers/decoders may copy unaligned buffers into aligned allocations
  require_alignment can force error instead of copy
```

`FileReader` docs point to mmap/zero-copy IPC examples for IPC files, while `StreamDecoder` docs describe alignment behavior: default mode can copy unaligned input into aligned buffers, and `require_alignment(true)` turns unaligned input into an error. ([Docs.rs][7])

---

## 10.14 Custom metadata

### File reader metadata

```rust id="ipc-custom-metadata-read"
let reader = FileReader::try_new(file, None)?;
let metadata = reader.custom_metadata();

for (k, v) in metadata {
    eprintln!("{k}={v}");
}
```

`FileReader::custom_metadata()` returns user-defined custom metadata from the IPC file footer. ([Docs.rs][7])

### File writer metadata note

```text id="ipc-metadata-note"
FileWriter:
  supports write_metadata method
  schema metadata remains in Schema
  footer custom metadata accessible through FileReader::custom_metadata

Stream format:
  metadata is carried in schema/messages, not a final random-access footer
```


### Object-store/chunked stream decoder

```toml id="ipc-profile-object-stream"
[dependencies]
arrow-buffer = "58.4.0"
arrow-array = "58.4.0"
arrow-schema = "58.4.0"
arrow-ipc = "58.4.0"
bytes = "1"
futures = "0.3"
object_store = { version = "0.13.2", features = ["aws", "gcp", "azure", "http"] }
```

```text id="ipc-profile-object-stream-use"
Use:
  object_store get stream
  StreamDecoder
  no FileReader unless object is seekable/range-addressable and full file footer accessible
```

### Service transport

```toml id="ipc-profile-flight"
[dependencies]
```

```text id="ipc-profile-flight-use"
Use:
  Flight for RPC
  not raw IPC stream if service discovery/auth/upload/download semantics matter
```

## 10.16 Error handling

```text id="ipc-errors"
FileReader construction errors:
  footer requirements not met
  file endianness mismatch
  non-seekable reader
  malformed IPC file

StreamReader construction errors:
  first message is not schema
  malformed stream

Decoder errors:
  partial data at finish
  malformed IPC messages
  alignment violations if require_alignment true
  validation errors unless skipped

Writer errors:
  underlying Write failure
  schema/header/footer write failure
  compression feature missing
  schema mismatch across batches
```

`FileReader::try_new` can error if the file does not meet Arrow footer requirements or if file endianness does not match target endianness; `StreamReader::try_new` can error if it does not encounter a schema as the first message. ([Docs.rs][7])

### Error translation

```rust id="ipc-error-translation"
fn ipc_to_io_error(err: ArrowError) -> std::io::Error {
    std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, err.to_string())
}

fn ipc_to_tonic_status(err: ArrowError) -> tonic::Status {
    tonic::Status::invalid_argument(err.to_string())
}
```

---

## 10.17 Performance guidance

```text id="ipc-performance-guidance"
Fast path:
  write/read RecordBatch streams
  preserve batch boundaries
  use BufReader/BufWriter when underlying IO benefits
  prefer IPC file for local random-access workloads
  prefer IPC stream for pipeline workloads
  use LZ4 when IO-bound and CPU available

Potential slow path:
  collect all stream batches into Vec<RecordBatch>
  tiny batches
  compressed IPC with high CPU budget pressure
  unaligned external buffers requiring copies
  unbounded FileReader -> Vec without row/byte limit
  ZSTD on many small batches without benchmarking
```

`FileWriter::try_new` and `StreamReader::try_new` docs note they are not internally buffered; buffered constructors are available when buffering is desired. ([Docs.rs][6])

---

## 10.18 Batch sizing for IPC

```text id="ipc-batch-sizing"
Small:
  1k–8k rows
  low latency, high message overhead

Default:
  8k–64k rows
  good CLI/service balance

Large:
  64k–1M rows
  lower per-message overhead, higher latency/memory

Rule:
  cap by rows and bytes
  split before network boundaries
  avoid one-row IPC messages
```

```rust id="ipc-batch-size-check"
fn approx_batch_bytes(batch: &RecordBatch) -> usize {
    batch.get_array_memory_size()
}

fn should_flush(rows: usize, bytes: usize) -> bool {
    rows >= 65_536 || bytes >= 64 * 1024 * 1024
}
```

---

## 10.19 Anti-pattern catalog

| Anti-pattern                                          | Failure mode                                     | Correct pattern                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Use `FileReader` on stdin/socket                      | requires seek                                    | `StreamReader`                                  |
| Use `StreamReader` when random batch access needed    | cannot seek                                      | `FileReader`                                    |
| Forget `finish()` on writer                           | invalid/truncated IPC                            | always `finish()` / `into_inner()`              |
| Enable compression without feature flag               | runtime error                                    | `arrow/ipc_compression` or `arrow-ipc/lz4,zstd` |
| Skip validation on user/network input                 | UB risk                                          | validate by default                             |
| Use raw IPC stream for RPC service with metadata/auth | reinvent Flight                                  | use `arrow-flight`                              |
| Use IPC as long-term lake storage                     | limited pruning/statistics compared with Parquet | use Parquet for lake storage                    |
| Assume Feather V1 is IPC                              | compatibility bug                                | only Feather V2 is IPC file                     |
| Collect all batches from stream by default            | memory blowup                                    | process stream incrementally                    |
| Tiny batches over IPC                                 | high overhead                                    | coalesce/sensible batch sizing                  |
| Assume compressed IPC is always faster                | CPU may dominate                                 | benchmark LZ4/ZSTD/uncompressed                 |

---

## 10.20 Golden test matrix

```rust id="ipc-golden-tests"
#[test]
fn ipc_file_round_trip() -> Result<(), ArrowError> {
    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
        ("id", Arc::new(Int32Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef),
        ("name", Arc::new(StringArray::from(vec!["a", "b", "c"])) as ArrayRef),
    ])?;

    let schema = batch.schema();
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();

    {
        let mut writer = FileWriter::try_new(&mut bytes, schema.as_ref())?;
        writer.write(&batch)?;
        writer.finish()?;
    }

    let cursor = Cursor::new(bytes);
    let mut reader = FileReader::try_new(cursor, None)?;

    assert_eq!(reader.num_batches(), 1);
    assert_eq!(reader.schema().as_ref(), schema.as_ref());

    let out = reader.next().unwrap()?;
    assert_eq!(out.num_rows(), 3);

    Ok(())
}

#[test]
fn ipc_stream_round_trip() -> Result<(), ArrowError> {
    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
        ("id", Arc::new(Int32Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef),
    ])?;

    let schema = batch.schema();
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();

    {
        let mut writer = StreamWriter::try_new(&mut bytes, schema.as_ref())?;
        writer.write(&batch)?;
        writer.finish()?;
    }

    let mut reader = StreamReader::try_new(Cursor::new(bytes), None)?;
    let out = reader.next().unwrap()?;

    assert_eq!(out.num_rows(), 3);
    assert!(reader.is_finished() || reader.next().is_none());

    Ok(())
}
```

Test categories:

```text id="ipc-test-categories"
File:
  round trip
  projection
  num_batches
  set_index
  custom metadata
  compression LZ4
  compression ZSTD
  malformed footer
  non-seekable rejection

Stream:
  round trip
  projection
  schema first message
  partial stream error
  StreamDecoder chunk boundaries
  decoder finish with partial data

Interop:
  Rust file -> PyArrow open_file
  PyArrow new_file -> Rust FileReader
  Rust stream -> PyArrow open_stream
  PyArrow new_stream -> Rust StreamReader
  Rust FileWriter -> pyarrow.feather.read_table

Safety:
  validation enabled for external files
  skip_validation only for self-written temp/spill
  alignment tests for decoder
```

---

## 10.21 Value case

```text id="ipc-value-case"
IPC stream:
  value = sequential, low-latency Arrow batch transport over byte streams.

IPC file:
  value = finite Arrow batch storage with footer metadata and random access.

Feather V2:
  value = Arrow IPC file compatibility for data-frame/table interchange.

Compression:
  value = disk/network reduction while preserving Arrow IPC semantics.

StreamDecoder:
  value = arbitrary chunked byte-source integration without assuming Read boundaries.

FileReader random access:
  value = batch-level seeking and metadata inspection.

C Data Interface:
  value = same-process zero-copy ABI, not byte serialization.

Flight:
  value = RPC/service protocol built on gRPC + IPC payloads.

Parquet comparison:
  value = durable analytic storage, statistics, encoding, pruning; not an Arrow-memory snapshot.
```

Final agent rule:

```text id="ipc-final-rule"
Use IPC stream for sequential batch transfer.
Use IPC file for Feather V2 / random-access local snapshots.
Use C Data / PyCapsule for same-process zero-copy interop.
Use Flight for networked services.
Use Parquet for durable data lakes.
Always finish writers.
Never skip validation on untrusted IPC.
```

# 11) Parquet core: reading, writing, metadata, and schema mapping

Style target: dense, syntax-first, agent-ready technical reference; same advanced-doc structure as the uploaded reference. 

---

## 11.0 Mental model

```text id="parquet-core-mental-model"
Parquet =
  durable analytical columnar storage format
  optimized for compression, encoding, pruning, and scan efficiency

Arrow =
  in-memory columnar compute format
  optimized for vectorized execution and zero-copy interchange

Rust parquet crate =
  official native Rust Parquet implementation
  Arrow bridge: RecordBatch <-> Parquet
  metadata APIs
  row-group/page/statistics APIs
  async/object-store APIs behind features
```

The `parquet` crate is the official native Rust implementation of Apache Parquet and is part of the Apache Arrow project; most Arrow-facing users will write with `ArrowWriter` and read with `ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder`. The crate-level feature list includes Arrow read/write support, async APIs, object-store integration via feature composition, compression features, checksum verification, experimental APIs, and encryption support. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

The `parquet` default feature set includes Arrow support plus common compression support such as Brotli, gzip/flate2, LZ4, ZSTD, Snappy, and SIMD UTF-8 validation; `crc` enables page checksum verification when present, and `experimental`/`variant_experimental`/`geospatial` are explicitly unstable feature surfaces. ([Docs.rs][2])

## 11.2 Imports

```rust id="parquet-imports"
use std::fs::File;
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::{ArrayRef, Int32Array, RecordBatch, StringArray};
use arrow_schema::{DataType, Field, Schema, SchemaRef};

use parquet::arrow::arrow_reader::{
    ArrowReaderMetadata, ArrowReaderOptions, ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder,
    ProjectionMask,
};
use parquet::arrow::arrow_writer::{ArrowWriter, ArrowWriterOptions};
use parquet::basic::{Compression, Encoding, ZstdLevel};
use parquet::errors::ParquetError;
use parquet::file::metadata::{ParquetMetaData, RowGroupMetaData};
use parquet::file::properties::{EnabledStatistics, WriterProperties};
use parquet::schema::types::ColumnPath;
```

---

## 11.3 Write path: `ArrowWriter`

### Basic file write

```rust id="arrowwriter-basic"
let file = File::create("out.parquet")?;

let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
    ("id", Arc::new(Int32Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef),
    ("name", Arc::new(StringArray::from(vec!["a", "b", "c"])) as ArrayRef),
])?;

let mut writer = ArrowWriter::try_new(
    file,
    batch.schema(),
    None, // WriterProperties
)?;

writer.write(&batch)?;
writer.close()?; // finalizes footer
```

`ArrowWriter::try_new(writer, schema, props)` creates a Parquet writer from an Arrow schema, `write(&RecordBatch)` encodes batches, and `close()` finalizes the file; writer creation fails if the underlying `SerializedFileWriter` cannot be created or if the Arrow schema contains unsupported datatypes such as unions. ([Docs.rs][3])

### In-memory write

```rust id="arrowwriter-memory"
let mut buf = Vec::new();

{
    let mut writer = ArrowWriter::try_new(&mut buf, batch.schema(), None)?;
    writer.write(&batch)?;
    writer.close()?;
}

// buf contains complete Parquet file bytes
```

### Multi-batch write

```rust id="arrowwriter-multi-batch"
fn write_batches<W: std::io::Write + Send>(
    writer: W,
    schema: SchemaRef,
    batches: impl IntoIterator<Item = RecordBatch>,
    props: Option<WriterProperties>,
) -> parquet::errors::Result<()> {
    let mut parquet = ArrowWriter::try_new(writer, schema, props)?;

    for batch in batches {
        parquet.write(&batch)?;
    }

    parquet.close()?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Writer finalization rule

```text id="arrowwriter-finalization-rule"
Must call:
  writer.close()

Otherwise:
  footer may not be written
  file may be unreadable/truncated
  row-group metadata may be incomplete

Use:
  close() for finalization
  flush() only for early row-group flush, not file finalization
```

---

## 11.4 `ArrowWriter` memory and row-group buffering

```text id="arrowwriter-memory-model"
Parquet writer buffers an entire row group before flushing.
Most data buffered encoded.
Dictionary keys / large strings / deeply nested data can still consume significant memory.
```

`ArrowWriter` docs state Parquet requires buffering an entire row group before it can be flushed, and expose `memory_size()` for current estimated memory use, `in_progress_size()` for estimated encoded size of the current row group, and `flush()` to trigger early row-group flushes under memory pressure. Smaller row groups can increase metadata overhead and worsen compression/query performance. ([Docs.rs][3])

### Memory-threshold flush

```rust id="arrowwriter-memory-flush"
const MAX_IN_PROGRESS_BYTES: usize = 256 * 1024 * 1024;

writer.write(&batch)?;

if writer.in_progress_size() > MAX_IN_PROGRESS_BYTES {
    writer.flush()?; // row group boundary
}
```

### Monitor rows and bytes

```rust id="arrowwriter-monitoring"
eprintln!(
    "rows={} encoded_estimate={} memory_estimate={}",
    writer.in_progress_rows(),
    writer.in_progress_size(),
    writer.memory_size(),
);
```

### Advisory

```text id="arrowwriter-memory-advisory"
DO:
  set max row group row/byte limits in WriterProperties
  monitor in_progress_size and memory_size for string/nested/dictionary-heavy data
  flush early only under pressure

DON'T:
  flush every batch by default
  use tiny row groups for analytics
  assume batch size == row group size
```

---

## 11.5 `WriterProperties`: core tuning surface

### Basic writer properties

```rust id="writerproperties-basic"
use parquet::basic::{Compression, ZstdLevel};
use parquet::file::properties::{EnabledStatistics, WriterProperties};

let props = WriterProperties::builder()
    .set_compression(Compression::ZSTD(ZstdLevel::try_new(3)?))
    .set_dictionary_enabled(true)
    .set_max_row_group_row_count(1_000_000)
    .set_max_row_group_bytes(128 * 1024 * 1024)
    .set_data_page_size_limit(1024 * 1024)
    .set_statistics_enabled(EnabledStatistics::Page)
    .build();
```

`WriterProperties` exposes row-group row and byte limits, write batch sizing, page sizing, compression, encoding, dictionary encoding, statistics, bloom filters, sorting columns, truncation lengths, content-defined chunking options, and per-column overrides. `max_row_group_size` is deprecated in favor of `max_row_group_row_count`. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Per-column override

```rust id="writerproperties-column-overrides"
let props = WriterProperties::builder()
    .set_compression(Compression::SNAPPY)
    .set_column_compression(
        ColumnPath::from("payload_json"),
        Compression::ZSTD(ZstdLevel::try_new(5)?),
    )
    .set_column_dictionary_enabled(
        ColumnPath::from("high_cardinality_id"),
        false,
    )
    .set_column_bloom_filter_enabled(
        ColumnPath::from("customer_id"),
        true,
    )
    .build();
```

Per-column property setters override global defaults for compression, dictionary encoding, dictionary page size, statistics, page-header statistics, bloom filters, and related settings. ([Apache Arrow][5])

---

## 11.6 Compression strategy

### Codec syntax

```rust id="compression-syntax"
let snappy = Compression::SNAPPY;
let zstd_3 = Compression::ZSTD(ZstdLevel::try_new(3)?);
let uncompressed = Compression::UNCOMPRESSED;
```

### Selection matrix

| Codec             | Use                                             | Tradeoff               |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `SNAPPY`          | broad ecosystem, fast default-ish analytics     | moderate compression   |
| `ZSTD(level)`     | storage/network-sensitive analytics             | better ratio, more CPU |
| `UNCOMPRESSED`    | benchmark baseline, already-compressed payloads | largest files          |
| `LZ4_RAW`         | fast decompression where ecosystem supports it  | less universal         |
| `GZIP` / `BROTLI` | high ratio legacy/interchange cases             | more CPU               |

`Compression::ZSTD` is documented as a good balance of compression, performance, and ecosystem support; `LZ4_RAW` offers faster decompression at the cost of typically worse compression ratio and less universal ecosystem support. ([Docs.rs][6])

### Deployment rule

```text id="compression-deploy-rule"
Default service/lake:
  ZSTD level 3 or SNAPPY

Maximum compatibility:
  SNAPPY

Benchmark baseline:
  UNCOMPRESSED

Do not choose codec blindly:
  benchmark read path + write path + storage cost + downstream reader support
```

---

## 11.7 Encoding, dictionary, and page sizing

### Encoding and dictionary knobs

```rust id="encoding-dictionary-knobs"
let props = WriterProperties::builder()
    .set_dictionary_enabled(true)
    .set_dictionary_page_size_limit(1024 * 1024)
    .set_data_page_size_limit(1024 * 1024)
    .build();
```

`set_dictionary_enabled` should be used to control dictionary encoding rather than setting dictionary encoding directly through `set_encoding`, and `set_data_page_size_limit` / `set_dictionary_page_size_limit` are best-effort limits controlled by write batch sizing. Smaller pages may increase file size but can improve page-index-based predicate pushdown. ([Apache Arrow][5])

### Page-size advisory

```text id="page-size-advisory"
Large pages:
  better compression
  fewer page headers
  coarser page-level pruning

Small pages:
  more metadata
  worse compression
  finer page-level pruning

Default-ish:
  1 MiB data page limit is common and documented as default in writer source.

Tune only after:
  filter selectivity known
  row-group size chosen
  query engine page-index usage confirmed
```

---

## 11.8 Statistics and page indexes

### Enable statistics

```rust id="statistics-enable"
let props = WriterProperties::builder()
    .set_statistics_enabled(EnabledStatistics::Page)
    .set_write_page_header_statistics(false)
    .build();
```

`EnabledStatistics` controls whether no statistics, row-group/column-chunk statistics, or page-level statistics are computed; statistics make files larger and footers slower to read but can enable row-group/page pruning in query engines. The writer documentation recommends modern implementations use `ParquetColumnIndex` min/max values rather than page-header statistics, and page-header statistics can greatly increase file size with little added benefit. ([Apache Arrow][5])

### Statistics advisory

```text id="statistics-advisory"
DO:
  keep statistics enabled for analytical data
  prefer page/index metadata for selective filters
  truncate long min/max values when needed
  test downstream engine pruning

DON'T:
  disable statistics unless privacy/file-size constraints require it
  rely on stats for correctness
  write page-header statistics blindly
```

---

## 11.9 Bloom filters

### Global bloom filter

```rust id="bloom-global"
let props = WriterProperties::builder()
    .set_bloom_filter_enabled(true)
    .set_bloom_filter_max_ndv(1_000_000)
    .build();
```

### Column bloom filter

```rust id="bloom-column"
let props = WriterProperties::builder()
    .set_column_bloom_filter_enabled(ColumnPath::from("customer_id"), true)
    .set_column_bloom_filter_max_ndv(ColumnPath::from("customer_id"), 1_000_000)
    .set_column_bloom_filter_fpp(ColumnPath::from("customer_id"), 0.01)
    .build();
```

Bloom filter NDV is used to initially size the filter at the configured false-positive probability, and a good heuristic is to set NDV to the expected number of rows in the row group; per-column bloom settings override global settings. ([Apache Arrow][5])

### Bloom advisory

```text id="bloom-advisory"
Use bloom filters for:
  high-selectivity equality predicates
  IDs, keys, tenant_id, customer_id
  columns queried with point lookups

Avoid bloom filters for:
  low-selectivity booleans/enums
  columns rarely filtered
  range-only predicates
  high write-throughput paths without read benefit
```

---

## 11.10 Read path: `ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder`

### Basic sync read

```rust id="parquet-read-basic"
let file = File::open("out.parquet")?;

let builder = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(file)?;
let schema = builder.schema().clone();
let metadata = builder.metadata();

eprintln!("row_groups={}", metadata.num_row_groups());

let mut reader = builder
    .with_batch_size(65_536)
    .build()?;

while let Some(batch) = reader.next() {
    let batch = batch?;
    // process RecordBatch
}
```

`ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new` builds a reader from anything implementing `ChunkReader`, such as `File` or `Bytes`; the builder exposes metadata such as row-group layout before building, and `build()` returns a `ParquetRecordBatchReader` iterator over Arrow `RecordBatch` values. ([Apache Arrow][7])

### Projection pushdown

```rust id="parquet-projection"
let file = File::open("out.parquet")?;

let builder = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(file)?;

let mask = ProjectionMask::roots(
    builder.metadata().file_metadata().schema_descr(),
    [0, 2, 5],
);

let mut reader = builder
    .with_projection(mask)
    .with_batch_size(65_536)
    .build()?;
```

`ArrowReaderBuilder` supports projection pushdown through `with_projection`, which reads only selected column indexes; row group filtering, row selection, row filtering, offset, limit, and cached metadata are also builder-level features. ([Apache Arrow][8])

### Row-group selection

```rust id="parquet-row-groups"
let reader = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(file)?
    .with_row_groups(vec![0, 3, 5])
    .build()?;
```

`with_row_groups` reads only specified row group indexes and is the low-level API for row-group pruning. ([Apache Arrow][8])

### Offset and limit

```rust id="parquet-offset-limit"
let reader = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(file)?
    .with_offset(1_000)
    .with_limit(10_000)
    .build()?;
```

`with_limit` and `with_offset` apply after any row selection or row filter; docs recommend enabling page-index reading for more efficient skipping when using these features. ([Apache Arrow][8])

---

## 11.11 Metadata caching and parallel readers

### Load metadata once

```rust id="parquet-metadata-cache"
let file = File::open("data.parquet")?;

let metadata = ArrowReaderMetadata::load(&file, Default::default())?;

let mut reader_a = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::new_with_metadata(
    file.try_clone()?,
    metadata.clone(),
)
.with_row_groups(vec![0])
.build()?;

let mut reader_b = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::new_with_metadata(
    file,
    metadata,
)
.with_row_groups(vec![1])
.build()?;
```

`ArrowReaderMetadata` is cheaply cloneable because it consists of `Arc`s and is designed for loading metadata once, constructing multiple readers over the same metadata, and caching metadata instead of rereading the file footer for each reader. ([Apache Arrow][9])

### Advisory

```text id="metadata-cache-advisory"
Use metadata caching when:
  repeated projections over same file
  parallel row-group readers
  object-store footer reads expensive
  query planner evaluates metadata before scan

Avoid reloading footer per scan.
```

---

## 11.12 `ParquetMetaData` inspection

### Basic metadata traversal

```rust id="metadata-inspection"
let builder = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(file)?;
let meta: &ParquetMetaData = builder.metadata();

let file_meta = meta.file_metadata();
let schema_descr = file_meta.schema_descr();

println!("rows={}", file_meta.num_rows());
println!("row_groups={}", meta.num_row_groups());
println!("created_by={:?}", file_meta.created_by());

for (rg_idx, rg) in meta.row_groups().iter().enumerate() {
    println!(
        "row_group={} rows={} total_byte_size={}",
        rg_idx,
        rg.num_rows(),
        rg.total_byte_size()
    );

    for col_idx in 0..rg.num_columns() {
        let col = rg.column(col_idx);
        println!(
            "  col={} path={} compression={:?} encodings={:?}",
            col_idx,
            col.column_path(),
            col.compression(),
            col.encodings()
        );

        if let Some(stats) = col.statistics() {
            println!("    stats={stats:?}");
        }
    }
}
```

`ParquetMetaData` is parsed from the file footer and contains file-level metadata, row-group metadata, optional column index, optional offset index, and optional decryptor; it can be read by readers or directly via `ParquetMetaDataReader`. ([Apache Arrow][10])

### Metadata levels

```text id="metadata-levels"
FileMetaData:
  file schema
  row count
  created_by
  key-value metadata
  schema descriptor

RowGroupMetaData:
  rows
  byte size
  column chunks

ColumnChunkMetaData:
  path
  physical type
  compression
  encodings
  statistics
  offsets
```

---

## 11.13 Statistics, pruning, and predicate pushdown architecture

```text id="pruning-layers"
File pruning:
  external catalog / partition metadata / file-level stats

Row-group pruning:
  Parquet row-group statistics
  builder.with_row_groups(selected_indexes)

Page/range pruning:
  page index -> RowSelection
  builder.with_row_selection(selection)

Row-level filtering:
  RowFilter during decoding
  builder.with_row_filter(filter)

Post-decode filtering:
  Arrow/DataFusion filter after RecordBatch decode
```

The Parquet Arrow reader builder exposes low-level APIs for projection pushdown, row-group filtering, range/page filtering through `RowSelection`, row-level filtering through `RowFilter`, offset/limit skipping, cached metadata, and metrics; it deliberately does not implement full predicate evaluation logic because predicate pushdown varies significantly across systems. ([Apache Arrow][8])

### Agent rule

```text id="pruning-agent-rule"
If user asks for SQL/dataset predicate pushdown:
  prefer DataFusion or custom planner using metadata.

If user asks for low-level Parquet read:
  use metadata inspection + with_row_groups / with_row_selection.

Do not claim ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder automatically evaluates arbitrary Expr predicates.
```

### Bloom filter read hook

```rust id="bloom-filter-read-hook"
let builder = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(file)?;

let maybe_filter = builder.get_row_group_column_bloom_filter(
    0, // row group
    2, // column index
)?;
```

The builder can read a row-group column bloom filter and returns `None` if the column does not have one; docs recommend calling it after other pruning forms such as projection and predicate pushdown. ([Apache Arrow][7])

---

## 11.14 Arrow schema mapping and `ARROW:schema`

```text id="schema-mapping-model"
Parquet schema:
  physical + logical storage schema

Arrow schema:
  in-memory logical schema

Mapping:
  not bijective
  writer embeds Arrow schema hint
  reader uses hint when compatible
  Parquet schema remains authoritative if conflict exists
```

The Rust Parquet Arrow module states Parquet and Arrow have different type systems and are not always one-to-one; writers add an Arrow schema hint in the `ARROW_SCHEMA_META_KEY` metadata key so original Arrow types can be recovered, following the same convention as PyArrow. The `ARROW_SCHEMA_META_KEY` constant is `"ARROW:schema"` and stores the serialized Arrow IPC schema base64-encoded. ([Docs.rs][11])

### Skip Arrow schema metadata

```rust id="skip-arrow-metadata"
let options = ArrowWriterOptions::new()
    .with_properties(props)
    .with_skip_arrow_metadata(true);

let mut writer = ArrowWriter::try_new_with_options(
    file,
    schema.clone(),
    options,
)?;
```

`ArrowWriterOptions::with_skip_arrow_metadata(true)` skips encoding embedded Arrow metadata; by default, Parquet files generated by `ArrowWriter` contain embedded Arrow schema metadata. ([Apache Arrow][12])

### Reader schema override

```rust id="reader-schema-override"
let options = ArrowReaderOptions::new()
    .with_schema(explicit_arrow_schema.clone());

let builder = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new_with_options(
    file,
    options,
)?;
```

`ArrowReaderOptions::with_schema` provides an explicit Arrow schema hint that takes precedence over embedded Arrow metadata; the provided schema must have the same number of columns and matching column names and must be compatible with the Parquet file schema. ([Apache Arrow][13])

### Schema advisory

```text id="schema-mapping-advisory"
DO:
  keep embedded Arrow schema for round-trip fidelity
  override schema only when intentionally normalizing logical types
  treat Parquet physical/logical schema as authoritative on conflict

DON'T:
  disable Arrow metadata unless compatibility/privacy/file-size policy requires it
  assume Parquet can preserve every Arrow logical nuance without ARROW:schema
```

---

## 11.15 Nested types and logical type mapping

### Supported write model

```text id="nested-write-model"
Supported by ArrowWriter:
  Arrow types with direct Parquet mapping
  StructArray
  ListArray
  logically equivalent string/binary variants
  native or dictionary arrays with compatible values

Not supported:
  Arrow Union types
  IntervalMonthDayNanoArray
```

`ArrowWriter` supports Arrow datatypes with direct Parquet mappings, including `StructArray` and `ListArray`, and accepts logically equivalent Arrow types for a column such as `String`/`LargeString`/`StringView`, `Binary`/`LargeBinary`/`BinaryView`, plus native and dictionary-encoded arrays when dictionary values are compatible. It explicitly does not support `IntervalMonthDayNanoArray`; writer creation also fails for unsupported schema datatypes such as unions. ([Docs.rs][3])

### Nested schema example

```rust id="nested-schema-parquet"
let schema = Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![
    Field::new("id", DataType::Int64, false),
    Field::new_list(
        "tags",
        Arc::new(Field::new("item", DataType::Utf8, false)),
        true,
    ),
    Field::new_struct(
        "address",
        vec![
            Field::new("city", DataType::Utf8, true),
            Field::new("zip", DataType::Utf8, true),
        ],
        true,
    ),
]));
```

### Nested advisory

```text id="nested-advisory"
Use stable child names:
  list item = "item"
  map entries/key/value = conventional names

Avoid:
  Union in Parquet
  MonthDayNano interval in Parquet
  relying on reader-specific nested path quirks

Test:
  Rust -> PyArrow
  PyArrow -> Rust
  DataFusion scan
  projection of nested columns
```

---

## 11.16 Reading dictionary-encoded columns

```text id="dictionary-read-model"
Parquet dictionary encoding:
  storage encoding detail

Arrow DictionaryArray:
  logical Arrow array representation

Read behavior:
  Rust reader typically returns Arrow logical type based on schema/hints/options
  use ArrowReaderOptions/schema hints when exact Arrow representation matters
```

PyArrow’s `read_table` exposes `read_dictionary` for reading BYTE_ARRAY storage as dictionary-encoded arrays, including nested paths; Rust Parquet’s low-level reader exposes Arrow schema hints and reader options rather than a direct one-to-one `read_dictionary` parameter in the same shape. ([Apache Arrow][14])

Agent rule:

```text id="dictionary-read-rule"
If exact dictionary output matters:
  inspect schema metadata
  use explicit Arrow schema when compatible
  write golden round-trip tests with PyArrow and Rust
```

---

## 11.17 PyArrow API mapping

| PyArrow                                    | Rust equivalent                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pq.write_table(table, path)`              | `ArrowWriter::try_new(file, schema, props).write(batch)...close()`           |
| `pq.read_table(path)`                      | `ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(file)?.build()?` + collect batches |
| `pq.ParquetFile(path)`                     | `ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder` + `metadata()` / `FileReader`-level APIs   |
| `ParquetFile.iter_batches(batch_size=...)` | builder `.with_batch_size(n).build()?` iterator                              |
| `ParquetFile.read_row_group(i)`            | builder `.with_row_groups(vec![i]).build()?`                                 |
| `ParquetFile.read_row_groups([...])`       | builder `.with_row_groups(vec![...]).build()?`                               |
| `read_table(columns=[...])`                | `ProjectionMask::roots(..., indices)` + `.with_projection(mask)`             |
| `read_table(filters=...)`                  | DataFusion, or manual metadata pruning + row selection/filter                |
| `write_table(compression=...)`             | `WriterProperties::builder().set_compression(...)`                           |
| `write_table(row_group_size=...)`          | `set_max_row_group_row_count(...)`                                           |
| `write_table(write_statistics=...)`        | `set_statistics_enabled(...)`                                                |
| `write_table(use_dictionary=...)`          | `set_dictionary_enabled(...)` / per-column override                          |
| `write_table(write_page_index=...)`        | page-index/statistics writer settings; verify exact Rust property set        |
| `metadata` / `num_row_groups`              | `builder.metadata()` / `ParquetMetaData`                                     |

PyArrow’s `ParquetFile` offers metadata, `num_row_groups`, `schema`, `schema_arrow`, `iter_batches`, `read`, `read_row_group`, and `read_row_groups`; those map naturally to Rust builder metadata inspection plus row-group/projection/batch-size configuration. ([Apache Arrow][15])

---

## 11.18 `read_table`-style eager collection

```rust id="read-table-style"
fn read_table_like(path: &str) -> parquet::errors::Result<Vec<RecordBatch>> {
    let file = File::open(path)?;
    let reader = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(file)?
        .with_batch_size(65_536)
        .build()?;

    reader.collect()
}
```

### Guarded collection

```rust id="read-table-bounded"
fn read_table_bounded(path: &str, max_rows: usize) -> parquet::errors::Result<Vec<RecordBatch>> {
    let file = File::open(path)?;
    let mut reader = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(file)?
        .with_batch_size(65_536)
        .build()?;

    let mut rows = 0usize;
    let mut batches = Vec::new();

    while let Some(batch) = reader.next() {
        let batch = batch?;
        rows += batch.num_rows();

        if rows > max_rows {
            return Err(ParquetError::General(format!(
                "row limit exceeded: {rows} > {max_rows}"
            )));
        }

        batches.push(batch);
    }

    Ok(batches)
}
```

### Advisory

```text id="read-table-advisory"
Use eager Vec<RecordBatch> for:
  tests
  bounded files
  small CLI output
  Python Table export

Use streaming iterator for:
  large files
  services
  transformations
  writer pipelines
  object-store scans
```

---

## 11.19 `write_table`-style batch writer

```rust id="write-table-style"
fn write_table_like(
    path: &str,
    schema: SchemaRef,
    batches: impl IntoIterator<Item = RecordBatch>,
) -> parquet::errors::Result<()> {
    let file = File::create(path)?;

    let props = WriterProperties::builder()
        .set_compression(Compression::ZSTD(ZstdLevel::try_new(3)?))
        .set_max_row_group_row_count(1_000_000)
        .set_data_page_size_limit(1024 * 1024)
        .set_dictionary_enabled(true)
        .set_statistics_enabled(EnabledStatistics::Page)
        .build();

    let mut writer = ArrowWriter::try_new(file, schema, Some(props))?;

    for batch in batches {
        writer.write(&batch)?;
    }

    writer.close()?;
    Ok(())
}
```

## 11.20 Error handling

```text id="parquet-error-categories"
Writer errors:
  unsupported Arrow datatype
  schema mismatch across batches
  Write failure
  compression feature unavailable
  invalid writer property level/value
  close/finalization failure

Reader errors:
  invalid parquet footer
  unsupported physical/logical conversion
  schema override incompatibility
  corrupted page
  checksum failure when crc enabled
  IO/chunk reader failure

Metadata errors:
  missing/invalid metadata
  incompatible embedded Arrow schema
  malformed statistics
```

### Boundary normalization

```rust id="parquet-error-normalize"
fn parquet_to_io(err: ParquetError) -> std::io::Error {
    std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, err.to_string())
}
```

### ETL writer

```text id="etl-writer-profile"
Properties:
  ZSTD(3) or SNAPPY
  dictionary enabled

  row group rows: 100k–1M
  row group bytes: 128–512 MiB target
  data page size: ~1 MiB
  embedded Arrow schema enabled
```

### Lakehouse scan writer

```text id="lakehouse-writer-profile"
Properties:
  ZSTD or SNAPPY depending read/write tradeoff
  statistics page/column index enabled
  bloom filters on equality-key columns
  stable row group sizing
  avoid tiny files
  schema metadata with schema version
```

### Interop writer

```text id="interop-writer-profile"
Properties:
  SNAPPY
  no experimental features
  embedded Arrow schema enabled
  avoid unsupported Arrow logical types
  validate with PyArrow, Spark, DuckDB, DataFusion
```

### Low-latency point lookup

```text id="lookup-profile"
Properties:
  bloom filters for point-lookup columns
  smaller row groups if query selectivity benefits
  page index/statistics enabled
  careful file-size/metadata tradeoff testing
```

## 11.22 Anti-pattern catalog

| Anti-pattern                                   | Failure mode                         | Correct pattern                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| forget `close()`                               | corrupt/incomplete file              | always close writer                                 |
| one row group for huge file                    | high memory, poor pruning            | row-group row/byte limits                           |
| tiny row group per input batch                 | metadata bloat, worse compression    | coalesce or set row-group policy                    |
| disable stats globally                         | no pruning                           | keep stats unless policy demands                    |
| enable bloom on every column                   | file/CPU overhead                    | only selective equality columns                     |
| use Union in Parquet schema                    | writer failure                       | encode as struct/tag/value or JSON/variant strategy |
| assume Rust reader evaluates arbitrary filters | wrong                                | DataFusion or custom pruning logic                  |
| skip Arrow schema metadata                     | logical type loss                    | keep default unless intentional                     |
| infer Arrow schema from Parquet only           | lost timezone/duration/large offsets | use `ARROW:schema` or explicit schema               |
| use eager collect for large files              | memory blowup                        | stream batches                                      |
| enable experimental features in public API     | semver instability                   | hide behind internal feature gates                  |

## 11.23 Golden test matrix

```rust id="parquet-golden-tests"
#[test]
fn parquet_round_trip_basic() -> parquet::errors::Result<()> {
    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
        ("id", Arc::new(Int32Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef),
        ("name", Arc::new(StringArray::from(vec!["a", "b", "c"])) as ArrayRef),
    ])?;

    let mut bytes = Vec::new();

    {
        let mut writer = ArrowWriter::try_new(&mut bytes, batch.schema(), None)?;
        writer.write(&batch)?;
        writer.close()?;
    }

    let reader = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(bytes::Bytes::from(bytes))?
        .with_batch_size(1024)
        .build()?;

    let batches: Vec<RecordBatch> = reader.collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
    assert_eq!(batches, vec![batch]);

    Ok(())
}
```

Test categories:

```text id="parquet-test-categories"
Write/read:
  primitive
  string/binary
  decimal
  timestamp with timezone
  list
  struct
  map
  dictionary
  nullable/all-null
  empty batch / empty file policy

WriterProperties:
  compression codec
  dictionary enabled/disabled
  row-group limits
  page-size limits
  statistics levels
  bloom filters
  custom metadata

Reader:
  projection
  row group selection
  offset/limit
  schema override
  cached metadata
  corrupted file
  checksum if crc enabled

Interop:
  Rust write -> PyArrow read
  PyArrow write -> Rust read
  Rust write -> DataFusion scan
  Rust write -> DuckDB/Spark if target ecosystem
```

## 11.24 Value case

```text id="parquet-value-case"
ArrowWriter:
  value = Arrow RecordBatch -> durable Parquet with schema fidelity and writer tuning.

ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder:
  value = Parquet -> streaming Arrow RecordBatch with projection, row-group, row-selection, limit/offset, metadata reuse.

WriterProperties:
  value = explicit control of compression, encoding, statistics, bloom filters, row groups, pages, metadata, CDC.

Metadata APIs:
  value = planning, pruning, introspection, validation, lakehouse/catalog integration.

ARROW:schema:
  value = recover Arrow-specific logical types not natively preserved by Parquet schema.

Statistics/page index:
  value = scan pruning and lower IO for selective predicates.

Bloom filters:
  value = equality-predicate pruning for high-cardinality keys.

Streaming read/write:
  value = bounded memory and composable pipelines.

PyArrow mapping:
  value = migrate `read_table`, `write_table`, `ParquetFile`, metadata workflows to Rust without forcing eager table materialization.
```

Final agent rule:

```text id="parquet-final-rule"
Use ArrowWriter for RecordBatch -> Parquet.
Use ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder for Parquet -> RecordBatch.
Keep embedded Arrow schema by default.
Tune row groups, pages, compression, statistics, and bloom filters deliberately.
Stream by default.
Collect only when bounded.
Use DataFusion for dataset-level predicate pushdown and relational scans.
```

# 12) Advanced Parquet: async, cloud, predicate pushdown, CDC, bloom filters

Style target: dense, syntax-first, agent-ready technical reference; aligned with the uploaded advanced-reference pattern. 

---

## 12.0 Mental model

```text id="advanced-parquet-model"
Advanced Parquet in Rust =
  async read/write
  object-store range IO
  projection pushdown
  row-group pruning
  page/range pruning via RowSelection
  decode-time RowFilter
  bloom-filter read/write hooks
  CDC writer options
  variant logical type behind experimental feature
  encryption behind feature gate
```

Rust Parquet’s advanced APIs are deliberately low-level: the crate exposes the hooks needed for pruning, async/object-store IO, row filters, row selections, page indexes, bloom filters, CDC, and experimental features, but it does not pretend to be a full dataset/query planner. For SQL/dataset predicate pushdown, use DataFusion or a custom planner that consumes Parquet metadata and then configures the Parquet reader. ([Apache Arrow][1])

---

CDC is exposed through `WriterProperties::set_content_defined_chunking(Some(CdcOptions::default()))`; the crate docs mark content-defined chunking as **experimental**, and it is only supported through the Arrow writer interface. ([Docs.rs][2])

The Rust Parquet crate documents the `variant_experimental` feature for reading and writing the Parquet Variant Binary Encoding logical type, intended for efficient semi-structured data such as JSON. ([Docs.rs][2])


Rust Parquet exposes an `encryption` feature and the Arrow module includes an example for reading encrypted Parquet files with `FileDecryptionProperties`; the docs note that this requires the experimental `encryption` feature at compile time. ([Docs.rs][3])
