## 12.3 Async reader: `ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder`

### Local async file

```rust id="async-read-local"
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> parquet::errors::Result<()> {
    let file = tokio::fs::File::open("events.parquet").await?;

    let builder = ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder::new(file)
        .await?
        .with_batch_size(65_536);

    let schema = builder.schema().clone();
    let metadata = builder.metadata();

    eprintln!("schema={schema}");
    eprintln!("row_groups={}", metadata.num_row_groups());

    let mut stream = builder.build()?;

    while let Some(batch) = stream.try_next().await? {
        eprintln!("rows={}", batch.num_rows());
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

`ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder<T>` is the async counterpart of `ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder`; it reads metadata first, then builds a stream that decodes `RecordBatch` values incrementally without downloading the full file. It supports the same core builder options such as batch size, projection, row groups, filtering, offset, and limit. ([Apache Arrow][4])

### Async builder with metadata reuse

```rust id="async-read-metadata-reuse"
let mut file = tokio::fs::File::open("events.parquet").await?;

let metadata = ArrowReaderMetadata::load_async(&mut file, ArrowReaderOptions::new()).await?;

let stream_a = ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder::new_with_metadata(
    file.try_clone().await?,
    metadata.clone(),
)
.with_row_groups(vec![0])
.build()?;

let stream_b = ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder::new_with_metadata(
    file,
    metadata,
)
.with_row_groups(vec![1])
.build()?;
```

`new_with_metadata` exists so agents can load metadata once, clone cheap metadata state, and create multiple readers with different options or row-group assignments without rereading the footer. ([Apache Arrow][1])

### Parallel row-group streams

```rust id="async-read-parallel-row-groups"
use futures::TryStreamExt;

let mut file = tokio::fs::File::open("events.parquet").await?;
let metadata = ArrowReaderMetadata::load_async(&mut file, ArrowReaderOptions::new()).await?;
let num_row_groups = metadata.metadata().num_row_groups();

let streams = (0..num_row_groups)
    .map(|rg| {
        let meta = metadata.clone();
        let file = file.try_clone();
        async move {
            let file = file.await?;
            let stream = ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder::new_with_metadata(file, meta)
                .with_row_groups(vec![rg])
                .build()?;
            parquet::errors::Result::Ok(stream)
        }
    });

let results = futures::stream::iter(streams)
    .buffered(4)
    .try_collect::<Vec<_>>()
    .await?;
```

The async docs explicitly describe creating independent streams per row group and polling them in parallel; each stream needs its own source instance so it can issue independent IO requests. ([Apache Arrow][1])

---

## 12.4 `ParquetObjectReader`: object-store range reads

### Object-store reader from metadata

```rust id="parquet-object-reader-basic"
let store: Arc<dyn ObjectStore> = Arc::new(InMemory::new());
let location = Path::from("events.parquet");

let meta = store.head(&location).await?;

let reader = ParquetObjectReader::new(store.clone(), meta.location)
    .with_file_size(meta.size);

let builder = ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder::new(reader)
    .await?
    .with_batch_size(65_536);

let mut stream = builder.build()?;

while let Some(batch) = stream.try_next().await? {
    // process batch
}
```

`ParquetObjectReader` reads Parquet files through `object_store::ObjectStore`; `with_file_size(size)` is an important optimization because it lets the reader use bounded range requests and avoid extra calls when the store lacks suffix-range support. ([Apache Arrow][5])

### S3-style construction

```rust id="parquet-object-reader-s3"
let store: Arc<dyn ObjectStore> = Arc::new(
    AmazonS3Builder::new()
        .with_bucket_name("my-bucket")
        .with_region("us-east-1")
        .build()?
);

let path = Path::from("lake/events/part-000.parquet");
let meta = store.head(&path).await?;

let reader = ParquetObjectReader::new(store, path)
    .with_file_size(meta.size)
    .with_footer_size_hint(128 * 1024)
    .with_preload_column_index(true)
    .with_preload_offset_index(true);

let stream = ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder::new(reader)
    .await?
    .build()?;
```

`ParquetObjectReader` supports footer-size hints, file-size hints, column-index preloading, offset-index preloading, and an optional runtime handle. Its `AsyncFileReader` implementation fetches byte ranges, multiple byte ranges, metadata, and suffixes from the object store. ([Apache Arrow][5])

### Object-store runtime advisory

```text id="object-store-runtime-advisory"
Object-store Parquet scan:
  prefer ParquetObjectReader
  supply file_size from object metadata
  preload page indexes only when pruning path needs them
  use separate runtime handle for IO if CPU decode saturates main Tokio runtime
  preserve streaming output; avoid eager Vec<RecordBatch>
```

The docs warn that running IO and CPU-bound Parquet decoding on the same cooperative Tokio runtime can degrade throughput and dropped connections, and `ParquetObjectReader::with_runtime` exists to perform IO on a provided Tokio runtime handle. ([Apache Arrow][5])

---

## 12.5 Async writer: local and object-store writes

### Local async writer

```rust id="async-writer-local"
let file = tokio::fs::File::create("out.parquet").await?;

let props = WriterProperties::builder()
    .set_compression(Compression::ZSTD(ZstdLevel::try_new(3)?))
    .set_max_row_group_row_count(1_000_000)
    .build();

let mut writer = AsyncArrowWriter::try_new(
    file,
    schema.clone(),
    Some(props),
)?;

for batch in batches {
    writer.write(&batch).await?;

    if writer.in_progress_size() > 256 * 1024 * 1024 {
        writer.flush().await?;
    }
}

writer.close().await?;
```

`AsyncArrowWriter` encodes `RecordBatch` values to Parquet and writes to an `AsyncFileWriter`; it eagerly writes bytes as soon as possible, but still must buffer an entire row group because of Parquet’s columnar layout. `memory_size`, `in_progress_size`, `in_progress_rows`, `flush`, `write`, and `close` expose the same operational controls as the sync writer. ([Apache Arrow][6])

### Object-store writer

```rust id="async-writer-object-store"
let store: Arc<dyn ObjectStore> = Arc::new(InMemory::new());
let path = Path::from("out/events.parquet");

let object_writer = ParquetObjectWriter::new(store.clone(), path.clone());

let mut writer = AsyncArrowWriter::try_new(
    object_writer,
    schema.clone(),
    None,
)?;

writer.write(&batch).await?;
writer.close().await?;

let bytes = store.get(&path).await?.bytes().await?;
```

`ParquetObjectWriter` is the object-store write-side companion for `ParquetObjectReader`; it implements `AsyncFileWriter`, writes to an `ObjectStore` path, and can be constructed from a custom buffered writer when writer behavior needs configuration. ([Apache Arrow][7])

### `AsyncFileWriter` trait contract

```text id="async-file-writer-contract"
AsyncFileWriter:
  write(Bytes) -> Future<Result<()>>
  complete() -> Future<Result<()>>

Implementer may:
  buffer bytes
  write immediately
  implement retry logic

Caller must:
  not write again after complete/close succeeds
```

The `AsyncFileWriter` trait is the interface consumed by `AsyncArrowWriter`; it has `write(Bytes)` and `complete()` methods, permits buffering/retry logic in implementations, and says callers should not call `write` after `complete` returns successfully. ([Apache Arrow][8])

---

## 12.6 Range-read mechanics and metadata

```text id="range-read-model"
Parquet read requires:
  footer metadata
  schema
  row group metadata
  column chunk locations
  page locations where page/offset index exists

Object-store optimization:
  fetch footer suffix/range
  read selected row groups
  read selected column chunks
  read selected pages/ranges when RowSelection/page index available
```

`AsyncFileReader` exposes `get_bytes(range)`, `get_byte_ranges(ranges)`, and `get_metadata(options)`. The metadata API may read the footer and other metadata from disk or a remote source, and can be accelerated by cached or prefetched metadata. ([Apache Arrow][9])

### Read path layering

```text id="read-path-layers"
File pruning:
  external catalog / object metadata / partition pruning

Row-group pruning:
  ArrowReaderBuilder::with_row_groups(...)

Page/range pruning:
  RowSelection + page/offset index

Decode-time predicate:
  RowFilter with ArrowPredicateFn

Post-decode filtering:
  Arrow compute / DataFusion filter after RecordBatch materialization
```

---

## 12.7 Projection pushdown

### Sync projection

```rust id="projection-pushdown-sync"
let builder = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(file)?;
let schema_descr = builder.metadata().file_metadata().schema_descr();

let mask = ProjectionMask::roots(schema_descr, [0, 3, 5]);

let mut reader = builder
    .with_projection(mask)
    .with_batch_size(65_536)
    .build()?;
```

### Async projection

```rust id="projection-pushdown-async"
let reader = ParquetObjectReader::new(store, path).with_file_size(file_size);

let builder = ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder::new(reader).await?;
let schema_descr = builder.metadata().file_metadata().schema_descr();

let mask = ProjectionMask::roots(schema_descr, [1, 2, 6]);

let stream = builder
    .with_projection(mask)
    .with_batch_size(65_536)
    .build()?;
```

`ArrowReaderBuilder` lists projection pushdown as a first-class feature via `with_projection`, and the async builder docs show reading metadata first, creating a `ProjectionMask`, and then building a projected stream. ([Apache Arrow][1])

---

## 12.8 Row-group pruning

```rust id="row-group-pruning"
let selected_row_groups = vec![0, 2, 5];

let mut reader = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(file)?
    .with_row_groups(selected_row_groups)
    .build()?;
```

`with_row_groups` is the low-level row-group pruning hook; query engines typically derive the selected row groups from partition metadata, row-group statistics, external catalogs, or other metadata. ([Apache Arrow][1])

### Agent rule

```text id="row-group-pruning-rule"
Do:
  evaluate row-group statistics/catalog metadata externally
  pass only selected row-group indexes to the reader

Do not:
  expect ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder to evaluate arbitrary SQL Expr filters
```

---

## 12.9 `RowSelection`: page/range pruning

### Manual row selection

```rust id="row-selection-basic"
let selection: RowSelection = vec![
    RowSelector::select(1_000),
    RowSelector::skip(50),
    RowSelector::select(50),
    RowSelector::skip(900),
].into();

let mut reader = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(file)?
    .with_row_selection(selection)
    .build()?;
```

`RowSelection` is a list of `RowSelector` values that selects or skips row ranges before column data is read, so it can avoid fetching data into memory. A typical use case is deriving row selections from the Parquet page index. Adjacent selectors are combined when constructing the selection. ([Apache Arrow][10])

### Offset / limit after pushed-down filters

```rust id="limit-offset-after-filter"
let reader = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(file)?
    .with_row_selection(selection)
    .with_limit(10_000)
    .with_offset(1_000)
    .build()?;
```

`with_limit` and `with_offset` apply after any row selection and row filter, allowing them to bound or skip the final decoded rows after pushed-down predicates. ([Apache Arrow][1])

### Page-index advisory

```text id="row-selection-page-index-advisory"
If using RowSelection:
  enable page index reading/writing when possible
  derive selections from column/offset indexes
  remember row selection is relative to selected row groups
  do not include skipped whole row groups in RowSelection selector counts
```

The builder docs recommend enabling page index reading when using row selection, because page/offset indexes can make data-page skipping more efficient. ([Apache Arrow][1])

---

## 12.10 Page index policy

```rust id="page-index-options"
use parquet::arrow::arrow_reader::{ArrowReaderOptions, PageIndexPolicy};

let options = ArrowReaderOptions::new()
    .with_page_index_policy(PageIndexPolicy::Required);

let builder = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new_with_options(file, options)?;
```

`ArrowReaderOptions` controls metadata reading. Its page-index policy can load the Parquet column index and offset index; the column index contains page-level min/max statistics that can be used for predicate pushdown and page-level pruning. ([Apache Arrow][11])

### Policy rule

```text id="page-index-policy-rule"
Required:
  fail if page index missing
  use when query correctness/performance contract assumes page index

Optional:
  use if present, proceed if absent

Skip:
  default/minimal metadata load
  use when no page-level pruning path exists
```

---

## 12.11 Decode-time `RowFilter`

### Basic single-column predicate

```rust id="row-filter-basic"
use arrow_ord::cmp::neq;

let builder = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(file)?;
let schema_desc = builder.metadata().file_metadata().schema_descr_ptr();

// Parquet leaf column index for int_col
let projection = ProjectionMask::leaves(&schema_desc, [4]);

let predicate = ArrowPredicateFn::new(projection, |batch: RecordBatch| {
    let int_col = batch.column(0);
    neq(int_col, &Int32Array::new_scalar(1))
});

let row_filter = RowFilter::new(vec![Box::new(predicate)]);

let mut reader = builder
    .with_row_filter(row_filter)
    .build()?;
```

`ArrowPredicateFn` wraps a closure plus a `ProjectionMask`; the closure receives batches containing only the predicate projection columns and returns a `BooleanArray` with the same length, where `true` keeps a row and `false` or `null` drops it. `RowFilter` is a sequence of such predicates and is applied during Parquet decoding. ([Apache Arrow][12])

### Multi-stage filter ordering

```rust id="row-filter-multi"
let cheap_selective = ArrowPredicateFn::new(mask_user_id, |batch| {
    // cheap high-selectivity predicate
    gt(batch.column(0).as_primitive::<Int64Type>(), &Int64Array::new_scalar(1000))
});

let expensive_less_selective = ArrowPredicateFn::new(mask_payload, |batch| {
    // heavier predicate over wider/string/nested payload
    // return BooleanArray
    todo!()
});

let row_filter = RowFilter::new(vec![
    Box::new(cheap_selective),
    Box::new(expensive_less_selective),
]);
```

`RowFilter` can reduce IO and CPU by refining row selections after each predicate, but predicate shape matters: a cheap single-column predicate that filters out most rows can improve performance, while a wide predicate that filters out few rows may be slower than post-decode filtering. ([Apache Arrow][13])

### Cache sizing for async row filters

```rust id="row-filter-cache-size"
let stream = ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder::new(reader)
    .await?
    .with_row_filter(row_filter)
    .with_max_predicate_cache_size(256 * 1024 * 1024)
    .build()?;
```

The async reader has a predicate cache used to store decoded arrays for predicate evaluation; `with_max_predicate_cache_size` configures the per-row-group cache size and defaults to 100 MiB. ([Apache Arrow][1])

---

## 12.12 Predicate pushdown architecture

```text id="predicate-pushdown-architecture"
Level 0: file pruning
  skip files using partition columns / catalog stats

Level 1: row-group pruning
  skip row groups using row-group statistics
  configure with_row_groups

Level 2: page pruning
  skip page ranges using page index
  configure RowSelection + page index

Level 3: decode-time row filtering
  evaluate RowFilter during decode

Level 4: post-decode filter
  Arrow/DataFusion filter over decoded RecordBatch
```

Rust Parquet exposes low-level APIs for each pruning level, but it does not implement a complete predicate-pushdown planner because predicate support, schema evolution, multi-file evaluation, external catalogs, and IO/decode scheduling are system-specific. ([Apache Arrow][1])

### Use DataFusion when appropriate

```text id="datafusion-pushdown-rule"
If user request:
  SQL WHERE
  dataset filters
  joins with filters
  multi-file pruning
  object-store data lake predicate pushdown

Use:
  DataFusion

If user request:
  low-level custom parquet scanner
  exact row-group/page/filter control

Use:
  Parquet metadata + with_row_groups + RowSelection + RowFilter
```

---

## 12.13 Bloom filters: write configuration

### Global bloom filter

```rust id="bloom-global"
let props = WriterProperties::builder()
    .set_bloom_filter_enabled(true)
    .set_bloom_filter_fpp(0.01)
    .set_bloom_filter_max_ndv(1_000_000)
    .build();
```

### Per-column bloom filter

```rust id="bloom-column"
let props = WriterProperties::builder()
    .set_column_bloom_filter_enabled(ColumnPath::from("customer_id"), true)
    .set_column_bloom_filter_fpp(ColumnPath::from("customer_id"), 0.01)
    .set_column_bloom_filter_max_ndv(ColumnPath::from("customer_id"), 5_000_000)
    .build();
```

`WriterPropertiesBuilder` exposes bloom-filter settings globally and per column, including false-positive probability and maximum expected number of distinct values; per-column settings take precedence over global settings. ([Apache Arrow][14])

### Bloom filter selection rules

```text id="bloom-filter-selection"
Use bloom filters for:
  high-cardinality equality predicates
  customer_id
  tenant_id
  trace_id
  session_id
  event_id

Avoid bloom filters for:
  booleans
  low-cardinality enums
  range predicates only
  columns rarely filtered
  write-heavy workloads with little read benefit
```

### Dynamic sizing note

`set_bloom_filter_properties` treats both false-positive probability and NDV as explicit and does not override them with build-time row-group-size fallback. For dynamic NDV sizing, use the simpler bloom enable/fpp APIs rather than hardcoding explicit bloom properties. ([Apache Arrow][14])

---

## 12.14 Bloom filters: read/check hook

```rust id="bloom-read"
let builder = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(file)?;

let maybe_filter = builder.get_row_group_column_bloom_filter(
    0, // row group index
    2, // column index
)?;

if let Some(sbbf) = maybe_filter {
    // use sbbf with query literal hashing logic
}
```

`get_row_group_column_bloom_filter(row_group_idx, column_idx)` reads a row-group column bloom filter and returns `None` if the column has no bloom filter. The docs recommend calling this after other pruning stages such as projection and predicate pushdown. ([Apache Arrow][1])

### Agent rule

```text id="bloom-read-agent-rule"
Bloom filters answer:
  definitely absent
  probably present

Use them for pruning.
Never use them for correctness.
Always verify predicates against decoded data.
```

---

## 12.15 Content-defined chunking: CDC

### Enable default CDC

```rust id="cdc-default"
let props = WriterProperties::builder()
    .set_content_defined_chunking(Some(CdcOptions::default()))
    .build();
```

### Custom CDC options

```rust id="cdc-custom"
let props = WriterProperties::builder()
    .set_content_defined_chunking(Some(CdcOptions {
        min_chunk_size: 128 * 1024,
        max_chunk_size: 512 * 1024,
        norm_level: 0,
    }))
    .build();
```

CDC creates Parquet data-page boundaries based on a rolling hash over logical column values, so unchanged data across file versions can produce identical byte sequences and be deduplicated by content-addressable storage systems. Rust marks this API experimental, and PyArrow documents the equivalent `use_content_defined_chunking` writer option as experimental. ([Docs.rs][2])

### CDC parameters

```text id="cdc-parameters"
min_chunk_size:
  default 256 KiB
  rolling hash not updated until minimum reached

max_chunk_size:
  default 1024 KiB
  force page boundary when exceeded

norm_level:
  default 0
  higher value increases probability of boundary discovery
  improves dedupe ratio
  increases small-page fragmentation risk
```

`CdcOptions` documents defaults and effects: chunk size is computed from logical values before encoding/compression; data sent through the hash includes definition/repetition levels; smaller chunks can improve deduplication but increase the number of small Parquet data pages. ([Apache Arrow][15])

### CDC deployment advisory

```text id="cdc-advisory"
Use CDC when:
  storage backend is content-addressable
  repeated file versions contain mostly same data
  upload/download deduplication matters
  write settings can remain stable across versions

Avoid CDC when:
  normal object-store/lake scan performance is the only goal
  write options vary between versions
  small-page fragmentation hurts scan performance
  interoperability risk is unacceptable
```

PyArrow’s CDC docs explicitly warn that changing write options such as compression, encoding, or row-group size across writes can prevent effective deduplication and reduce storage efficiency. ([Apache Arrow][16]) DataFusion 54 exposes this same parquet-rs CDC machinery through session configuration — see §12.25.

```toml id="variant-cargo"
[dependencies]
parquet = { version = "58.4.0", features = ["arrow", "variant_experimental"] }
```

```text id="variant-model"
Parquet Variant:

  intended for JSON-like data
  efficient binary encoding
  experimental Rust feature gate
```

Rust Parquet documents the `variant_experimental` feature for reading and writing Parquet files with the Variant Binary Encoding logical type; the feature targets efficient semi-structured data such as JSON. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Variant advisory

```text id="variant-advisory"
Use Variant only when:
  downstream readers support Parquet Variant
  semi-structured data dominates
  schema-on-read is acceptable

Avoid Variant when:

  structured Arrow Schema is available and stable
```

## 12.17 Modular encryption status

### PyArrow baseline

PyArrow documents Parquet modular/columnar encryption support, including envelope encryption using data encryption keys and master encryption keys, KMS client integration, file encryption/decryption properties, footer keys, column keys, encryption algorithms, plaintext footers, double wrapping, internal/external key material, and nested-column key paths. ([Apache Arrow][16])

### Rust status

```toml id="encryption-cargo"
[dependencies]
parquet = { version = "58.4.0", features = ["arrow", "encryption"] }
```

```rust id="encryption-read-sketch"
use parquet::arrow::arrow_reader::{ArrowReaderMetadata, ArrowReaderOptions, ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder};
use parquet::encryption::decrypt::FileDecryptionProperties;

let footer_key = b"0123456789012345".to_vec();

let decryption_properties = FileDecryptionProperties::builder(footer_key)
    .build()?;

let options = ArrowReaderOptions::default()
    .with_file_decryption_properties(decryption_properties);

let reader_metadata = ArrowReaderMetadata::load(&file, options.clone())?;

let mut reader = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new_with_options(file, options)?
    .build()?;
```

The Rust Arrow Parquet docs include an encrypted-read example with `FileDecryptionProperties`, including footer and column-specific keys, and state that this requires the experimental `encryption` feature. ([Docs.rs][3])

### Parity advisory

```text id="encryption-parity"
Do not assume full PyArrow encryption parity.

Track separately:
  read encrypted footer
  read uniform encryption
  read column-specific encryption
  write encrypted files
  KMS integration
  nested column path handling
  plaintext footer behavior
  algorithm support
  interoperability with PyArrow
```

### Deployment rule

```text id="encryption-deploy-rule"
Use Rust encrypted Parquet only after:
  feature-gated compile
  PyArrow/Rust round-trip tests
  KMS/key-management design review
  threat-model review
  nested column path tests
  footer/plaintext-footer compatibility tests
```

## 12.18 PyArrow parity map

| PyArrow capability                  | Rust Parquet status                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pq.read_table(..., columns=...)`   | `ProjectionMask` + `with_projection`                                                                     |
| `pq.read_table(..., filters=...)`   | DataFusion recommended; low-level Rust requires metadata pruning + row groups/page selection/row filters |
| `ParquetFile.iter_batches(...)`     | `ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder` or `ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder`                                   |
| Cloud read via filesystem           | `ParquetObjectReader` + `object_store`                                                                   |
| Async read                          | `ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder`                                                                        |
| Async write                         | `AsyncArrowWriter`                                                                                       |
| Cloud write                         | `ParquetObjectWriter` + `AsyncArrowWriter`                                                               |
| `use_content_defined_chunking=True` | `WriterProperties::set_content_defined_chunking(Some(CdcOptions::default()))`                            |
| CDC dict options                    | `CdcOptions { min_chunk_size, max_chunk_size, norm_level }`                                              |
| Bloom filter write                  | `WriterPropertiesBuilder` bloom APIs                                                                     |
| Bloom filter read                   | `get_row_group_column_bloom_filter`                                                                      |
| Modular encryption                  | Rust feature-gated/experimental; verify feature-by-feature                                               |
| Variant logical type                | `variant_experimental` feature                                                                           |

## 12.19 End-to-end cloud scan skeleton

```rust id="cloud-scan-skeleton"
use futures::TryStreamExt;

async fn scan_projected_parquet_from_store(
    store: Arc<dyn ObjectStore>,
    path: Path,
    file_size: u64,
) -> parquet::errors::Result<usize> {
    let reader = ParquetObjectReader::new(store, path)
        .with_file_size(file_size)
        .with_preload_column_index(true)
        .with_preload_offset_index(true);

    let builder = ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder::new(reader).await?;
    let schema_descr = builder.metadata().file_metadata().schema_descr();

    let projection = ProjectionMask::roots(schema_descr, [0, 1, 3]);

    let mut stream = builder
        .with_projection(projection)
        .with_batch_size(65_536)
        .build()?;

    let mut rows = 0usize;
    while let Some(batch) = stream.try_next().await? {
        rows += batch.num_rows();
    }

    Ok(rows)
}
```

---

## 12.20 End-to-end cloud write skeleton with CDC + bloom filters

```rust id="cloud-write-cdc-bloom"
async fn write_cloud_parquet(
    store: Arc<dyn ObjectStore>,
    path: Path,
    schema: SchemaRef,
    batches: impl IntoIterator<Item = RecordBatch>,
) -> parquet::errors::Result<()> {
    let props = WriterProperties::builder()
        .set_compression(Compression::ZSTD(ZstdLevel::try_new(3)?))
        .set_max_row_group_row_count(1_000_000)
        .set_max_row_group_bytes(256 * 1024 * 1024)
        .set_statistics_enabled(EnabledStatistics::Page)
        .set_column_bloom_filter_enabled(ColumnPath::from("customer_id"), true)
        .set_column_bloom_filter_fpp(ColumnPath::from("customer_id"), 0.01)
        .set_content_defined_chunking(Some(CdcOptions::default()))
        .build();

    let object_writer = ParquetObjectWriter::new(store, path);

    let mut writer = AsyncArrowWriter::try_new(
        object_writer,
        schema,
        Some(props),
    )?;

    for batch in batches {
        writer.write(&batch).await?;

        if writer.in_progress_size() > 256 * 1024 * 1024 {
            writer.flush().await?;
        }
    }

    writer.close().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

## 12.21 Deployment patterns

```text id="deployment-patterns"
Cloud analytical lake:
  DataFusion for planning
  object_store for cloud IO
  ParquetObjectReader for direct low-level scan
  ZSTD/SNAPPY
  row-group stats + page index
  bloom filters only on equality-key columns

CAS / Xet-like storage:
  CDC enabled
  stable writer options across file versions
  avoid random compression/encoding changes
  test upload/download dedupe gains

Low-latency point lookup:
  bloom filters
  smaller row groups if selectivity wins
  page index
  row-group pruning
  decode-time RowFilter only when selective

Encrypted data:
  feature-gated Rust path
  interop tests with PyArrow
  key management outside Parquet writer/reader logic
  no “parity” claims without full test matrix
```

## 12.22 Anti-pattern catalog

| Anti-pattern                                        | Failure mode                                   | Correct pattern                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Assume Rust builder evaluates SQL predicates        | no automatic arbitrary predicate evaluator     | DataFusion or custom pruning                           |
| Use `RowFilter` for wide low-selectivity predicates | slower than post-decode filtering              | filter after decode                                    |
| Enable bloom filters on all columns                 | file/CPU bloat                                 | only high-cardinality equality keys                    |
| Enable CDC everywhere                               | smaller-page fragmentation, experimental risk  | only CAS/dedupe-oriented storage                       |
| Change writer options between CDC versions          | poor deduplication                             | stable compression/encoding/row groups                 |
| Omit file size for object stores                    | extra metadata calls / suffix range dependence | use `head` and `with_file_size`                        |
| Run CPU decode and IO on same saturated runtime     | degraded throughput                            | use runtime separation or controlled concurrency       |
| Collect async streams eagerly                       | memory blowup                                  | process batches as stream                              |
| Treat encryption as drop-in PyArrow parity          | failed interop/security gaps                   | feature-by-feature validation                          |
| Use Variant for stable lake schemas                 | compatibility risk                             | structured schema unless Variant support is guaranteed |

---

## 12.23 Golden test matrix

```text id="advanced-parquet-test-matrix"
Async local:
  tokio::fs::File read
  tokio::fs::File write
  batch size
  stream early cancellation

Object store:
  InMemory read/write
  S3/GCS/Azure integration smoke
  with_file_size on/off
  footer size hint
  preload column index
  preload offset index

Projection/pruning:
  projection mask roots/leaves
  row group selection
  row selection skip/select ranges
  offset/limit after selection/filter
  page index required/optional/skip

RowFilter:
  cheap selective predicate
  wide low-selectivity predicate
  null predicate values
  multi-stage predicate order
  async predicate cache sizing

Bloom:
  write enabled column
  read bloom filter present
  read bloom filter absent
  false positive behavior never used for correctness

CDC:
  default CdcOptions
  custom CdcOptions
  stable writer options across versions
  file-size/page-count regression

Variant:
  gated compile
  Rust write/read
  PyArrow/other reader compatibility if claimed

Encryption:
  uniform encryption
  column-specific encryption
  nested field encryption paths
  Rust read PyArrow write
  PyArrow read Rust write if write path used
```

---

## 12.24 Value case

```text id="advanced-parquet-value-case"
Async readers:
  value = nonblocking streaming of RecordBatch values from local/cloud sources.

ParquetObjectReader:
  value = object-store range reads, metadata-aware IO, cloud-native scan primitive.

AsyncArrowWriter:
  value = nonblocking Parquet writes while retaining row-group memory controls.

ParquetObjectWriter:
  value = direct Parquet writes to object_store targets.

Projection pushdown:
  value = avoid reading unnecessary columns.

Row-group pruning:
  value = skip large contiguous row groups using metadata/catalog predicates.

RowSelection:
  value = page/range-level skipping before decoding.

RowFilter:
  value = decode-time late materialization for selective predicates.

Bloom filters:
  value = equality-predicate row-group pruning with no false negatives.

CDC:
  value = dedupe-friendly stable byte sequences for content-addressable storage.

Variant:
  value = efficient semi-structured payload storage when reader ecosystem supports it.

Encryption:
  value = columnar confidentiality controls, but requires feature-gated, security-reviewed, interop-tested deployment.
```

Final agent rule:

```text id="advanced-parquet-final-rule"
Use DataFusion for normal dataset predicate pushdown.
Use Parquet advanced APIs when building a custom scanner.
Use ParquetObjectReader/Writer for cloud.
Use RowSelection for range/page pruning.
Use RowFilter only for selective decode-time predicates.
Use bloom filters only for high-cardinality equality pruning.
Use CDC only for CAS/dedupe storage.
Treat Variant and encryption as feature-gated compatibility projects, not automatic PyArrow parity.
```

## 12.25 DataFusion 54 Parquet integration notes: CDC config, nested leaf pushdown, coerce_int96_tz

Secondary coverage — the DF-side Parquet story is primary in `datafusion_rust.md` §15. What changed with DataFusion 54 on top of the parquet-rs surfaces in this section:

### Content-defined chunking through DataFusion config

DataFusion 54 exposes the parquet-rs CDC writer machinery of §12.15 as session configuration (`datafusion-common` `config.rs`, carried as `ParquetCdcOptions` into `parquet::file::properties::WriterProperties::content_defined_chunking`):

```text
datafusion.execution.parquet.content_defined_chunking.enabled = false   # default off, experimental
datafusion.execution.parquet.content_defined_chunking.min_chunk_size    # default 256 KiB
datafusion.execution.parquet.content_defined_chunking.max_chunk_size    # default 1 MiB
datafusion.execution.parquet.content_defined_chunking.norm_level        # default 0
```

Caveats: the feature is experimental and default-off, and enabling it **disables DataFusion's parallel Parquet writing** — weigh dedupe benefits against write throughput. The chunking semantics (rolling hash over logical values, min/max bounds, normalization level) are exactly the `CdcOptions` behavior described in §12.15.

### Nested leaf projection and filter pushdown

DataFusion 54 projects and filter-pushes individual leaves of nested Parquet columns (struct fields, list elements) instead of materializing whole nested roots, reducing decode work for `struct_col.field`-style access and nested predicates. This is planner behavior on top of the parquet-rs projection-mask machinery in §12.7.

### INT96 timestamp coercion

`datafusion.execution.parquet.coerce_int96` (unit) plus new-in-54 `datafusion.execution.parquet.coerce_int96_tz` (timezone) let scans read legacy INT96 timestamps as `Timestamp(<unit>, Some(<tz>))` instead of the naive default — relevant for old Spark/Impala-written files.

# 13) Dataset-equivalent workflows

Style target: dense, syntax-first, agent-ready technical reference; follows the uploaded advanced-reference format. 

---

## 13.0 Mental model

```text id="dataset-mental-model"
PyArrow dataset()
  Dataset
  Fragment
  FileFormat
  FileSystem
  Partitioning
  Scanner
  Expression filter
  projected columns / derived columns
  write_dataset

Rust / DataFusion equivalent
  SessionContext
  TableProvider
  ListingTable       # multi-file local/remote directory table
  ListingOptions     # file format, extension, partition columns, stats, target partitions
  ListingTableConfig # paths + schema + listing options
  MemTable           # in-memory Vec<RecordBatch>
  StreamingTable     # partitioned stream source
  DataFrame          # lazy logical plan wrapper
  Expr               # projection/filter/derived expressions
  SendableRecordBatchStream
```

PyArrow’s dataset module is a unified interface for tabular, potentially larger-than-memory, multi-file data across formats and filesystems; it covers source discovery, directory partitioning, schema normalization, projection, predicate pushdown, and optional parallel reads. DataFusion’s `ListingTable` is the closest Rust-native equivalent for file-backed datasets: it reads one or more Parquet, JSON, CSV, or Avro files as a single table from local or remote object stores, supports Hive-style partitioning, schema merging, projection/filter/limit pushdown where formats support it, statistics/pruning, metadata caching, and statistics caching. ([Apache Arrow][1])

---

```rust id="dataset-imports"
};

use datafusion::datasource::file_format::json::JsonFormat;
```

## 13.3 PyArrow dataset concept mapping

| PyArrow dataset concept        | DataFusion/Rust equivalent                                                                  | Notes                                         |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `ds.dataset(path, format=...)` | `ctx.read_parquet/read_csv/read_json` or `ListingTable`                                     | quick API vs configurable provider            |
| `FileSystemDataset`            | `ListingTable`                                                                              | file/object-store-backed table                |
| `Fragment`                     | file/object metadata + scan task inside `ListingTable`/`DataSourceExec`                     | no direct user-level fragment object required |
| `FileFormat`                   | DataFusion `FileFormat`, e.g. `ParquetFormat`, `CsvFormat`, `JsonFormat`                    | format-specific scan/write planning           |
| `partitioning="hive"`          | `ListingOptions::with_table_partition_cols(...)` or factory inference                       | Hive-style `col=value` directories            |
| `Scanner`                      | lazy `DataFrame`, `execute_stream()`                                                        | stream result batches                         |
| `filter=Expression`            | DataFusion `Expr` in `df.filter(...)`                                                       | false/null rows excluded                      |
| `columns=[...]`                | `df.select(...)` or projection pushdown                                                     | optimizer may push projection into scan       |
| derived projection             | `df.select(vec![expr.alias(...)])`                                                          | DataFusion expressions                        |
| `to_table()`                   | `df.collect().await?`                                                                       | eager materialization                         |
| `count_rows(filter=...)`       | `df.filter(...).aggregate(... count(...))` or SQL                                           | DataFusion aggregate                          |
| `write_dataset(...)`           | `DataFrame::write_parquet` for simple writes; custom partition writer for Hive-style output | DataFusion write API differs from PyArrow     |

PyArrow exposes dataset fragments and scanners directly, while DataFusion generally expresses the same workflow as a lazy logical plan over a `TableProvider` and executes either with `collect` or streaming; `collect` buffers results into `Vec<RecordBatch>`, whereas `execute_stream` incrementally computes output as it is polled. ([Apache Arrow][1])

---

## 13.4 `SessionContext`: dataset control plane

### Quick registration/read APIs

```rust id="sessioncontext-quick-read"
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion_common::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let df = ctx
        .read_parquet("s3://bucket/events/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
        .await?
        .filter(
            col("event_type").eq(lit("click"))
                .and(col("date").eq(lit("2026-05-22")))
        )?
        .select(vec![
            col("user_id"),
            col("event_type"),
            col("amount"),
        ])?;

    let mut stream = df.execute_stream().await?;

    while let Some(batch) = stream.next().await {
        let batch = batch?;
        // sink batch
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

### SQL external table path

```rust id="sessioncontext-sql-external"
ctx.sql(r#"
    CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE events
    STORED AS PARQUET
    LOCATION 's3://bucket/events/'
"#).await?;

let df = ctx.sql(r#"
    SELECT user_id, count(*) AS n
    FROM events
    WHERE event_type = 'click'
    GROUP BY user_id
"#).await?;
```

DataFusion’s `DataFrame` is lazy and wraps a `LogicalPlan` plus `SessionState`; execution begins only through APIs such as `collect`, `execute_stream`, writes, or display methods, which allows additional optimizations before reading data. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

---

## 13.5 `ListingTable`: file-backed dataset provider

### Manual Parquet `ListingTable`

```rust id="listingtable-parquet"
async fn parquet_listing_table(
    session: &dyn datafusion::execution::context::Session,
    table_path: &str,
) -> datafusion_common::Result<Arc<dyn TableProvider>> {
    let table_path = ListingTableUrl::parse(table_path)?;

    let file_format = ParquetFormat::new()
        .with_enable_pruning(true)
        .with_metadata_size_hint(Some(128 * 1024));

    let listing_options = ListingOptions::new(Arc::new(file_format))
        .with_file_extension(".parquet")
        .with_collect_stat(true);

    let schema = listing_options
        .infer_schema(session, &table_path)
        .await?;

    let config = ListingTableConfig::new(table_path)
        .with_listing_options(listing_options)
        .with_schema(schema);

    Ok(Arc::new(ListingTable::try_new(config)?))
}
```

`ListingTable` is a built-in `TableProvider` that reads one or more files as a single table using an `ObjectStore`, including local files and remote objects such as S3. It supports multiple files, Hive-style partitioning, compatible schema merging, pushdown for formats that support it, statistics collection/pruning, pre-existing sort order, metadata caching, and statistics caching. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Register manual provider

```rust id="register-listingtable"
let provider = parquet_listing_table(ctx.state().as_ref(), "s3://bucket/events/").await?;
ctx.register_table("events", provider)?;
```

### Direct `ListingOptions` knobs

```rust id="listingoptions-knobs"
let listing_options = ListingOptions::new(Arc::new(ParquetFormat::new()))
    .with_file_extension(".parquet")
    .with_table_partition_cols(vec![
        ("year".to_string(), DataType::Int32),
        ("month".to_string(), DataType::Int32),
        ("day".to_string(), DataType::Int32),
    ])
    .with_collect_stat(true)
    .with_target_partitions(32);
```

`ListingOptions` stores the file extension filter, file format, expected partition columns, whether statistics should be collected, target partition count, and optional known file sort order; `with_collect_stat(true)` can add overhead because files may need to be opened or partially parsed. ([Docs.rs][5])

---

## 13.6 Hive partitioning

### Directory shape

```text id="hive-layout"
s3://bucket/events/
  year=2026/
    month=05/
      day=22/
        part-000.parquet
        part-001.parquet
```

### Manual partition column schema

```rust id="hive-partition-cols"
let listing_options = ListingOptions::new(Arc::new(ParquetFormat::new()))
    .with_file_extension(".parquet")
    .with_table_partition_cols(vec![
        ("year".to_string(), DataType::Int32),
        ("month".to_string(), DataType::Int32),
        ("day".to_string(), DataType::Int32),
    ]);
```

### Query

```rust id="hive-partition-query"
let df = ctx
    .table("events")
    .await?
    .filter(
        col("year").eq(lit(2026_i32))
            .and(col("month").eq(lit(5_i32)))
            .and(col("day").eq(lit(22_i32)))
    )?;
```

`ListingTable` reads Hive-style directories such as `date=2024-06-01`, adds partition columns to the table output, and can prune directories when a query predicate filters on the partition column; DataFusion’s listing-table factory can also infer Hive-compliant partition columns by default. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Partitioning advisory

```text id="partitioning-advisory"
DO:
  use low/medium cardinality partition columns
  use stable value encoding
  use typed partition columns in ListingOptions
  use partition predicates for file/directory pruning

DON'T:
  partition by high-cardinality IDs
  partition by floating values
  mix partition column types across directories
  rely on path parsing if values contain unescaped '/' or '='
```

---

## 13.7 Multi-file scans

### Simple API

```rust id="multifile-simple"
let df = ctx
    .read_parquet("s3://bucket/events/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
    .await?;
```

### Configured listing provider

```rust id="multifile-configured"
let table_path = ListingTableUrl::parse("s3://bucket/events/")?;

let file_format = ParquetFormat::new()
    .with_enable_pruning(true)
    .with_metadata_size_hint(Some(256 * 1024));

let options = ListingOptions::new(Arc::new(file_format))
    .with_file_extension(".parquet")
    .with_collect_stat(true)
    .with_target_partitions(64);

let schema = options.infer_schema(ctx.state().as_ref(), &table_path).await?;

let config = ListingTableConfig::new(table_path)
    .with_listing_options(options)
    .with_schema(schema);

let table = ListingTable::try_new(config)?;
ctx.register_table("events", Arc::new(table))?;
```

`ListingTable` groups file lists for scan execution and exposes `list_files_for_scan(ctx, filters, limit)` to return scan files and file-level statistics grouped for distribution across execution threads/executors. ([Docs.rs][4])

---

## 13.8 Format-specific dataset providers

### Parquet

```rust id="parquet-format-config"
let parquet = ParquetFormat::new()
    .with_enable_pruning(true)
    .with_metadata_size_hint(Some(128 * 1024))
    .with_skip_metadata(false)
    .with_force_view_types(true);
```

`ParquetFormat` can enable statistics-based row-group pruning, provide a metadata-size hint to reduce footer reads, skip embedded metadata to avoid schema conflicts, force string/binary view types when the table schema uses them, read binary columns as strings, and configure INT96 coercion. ([Apache Arrow][6])

### CSV

```rust id="csv-listing-format"
let csv = CsvFormat::default();

let listing_options = ListingOptions::new(Arc::new(csv))
    .with_file_extension(".csv")
    .with_table_partition_cols(vec![
        ("date".to_string(), DataType::Utf8),
    ]);
```

### JSON / NDJSON

```rust id="json-listing-format"
let json = JsonFormat::default();

let listing_options = ListingOptions::new(Arc::new(json))
    .with_file_extension(".json")
    .with_target_partitions(16);
```

Use Parquet for performance-critical data lakes because it exposes richer metadata, statistics, compression, column pruning, and row-group/page-level optimization opportunities; CSV/JSON listing tables are useful for ingestion, interoperability, debugging, and source-of-record text feeds, but they are usually less efficient scan formats. This follows from DataFusion’s ListingTable format support and the Parquet-specific pruning/metadata options. ([Docs.rs][4])

---

## 13.9 `MemTable`: in-memory dataset

### Construct

```rust id="memtable-construct"
let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
    ("id", Arc::new(Int32Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef),
    ("name", Arc::new(StringArray::from(vec!["a", "b", "c"])) as ArrayRef),
])?;

let schema = batch.schema();

// partitions: Vec<Vec<RecordBatch>>
let table = MemTable::try_new(schema.clone(), vec![vec![batch]])?;

ctx.register_table("users_mem", Arc::new(table))?;
```

### Empty table

```rust id="memtable-empty"
let empty = MemTable::try_new(schema.clone(), vec![vec![]])?;
```

`MemTable` presents a `Vec<RecordBatch>` as a DataFusion table so it can be queried repeatedly without additional file IO; it requires at least one partition, and an empty table is represented as `vec![vec![]]`. ([Docs.rs][7])

### Use cases

```text id="memtable-use-cases"
Use MemTable for:
  tests
  small dimension tables
  generated in-memory data
  cached bounded results
  Python/Rust boundary materialized batches
  UDF fixture tables

Avoid MemTable for:
  unbounded streams
  large object-store datasets
  source-of-truth storage
  data too large for process memory
```

---

## 13.10 `StreamingTable`: stream-backed dataset

### Conceptual construction

```rust id="streamingtable-concept"
let table = StreamingTable::try_new(
    schema.clone(),
    vec![
        partition_stream_0,
        partition_stream_1,
    ],
)?
.with_infinite_table(false);
```

`StreamingTable` is a simplified `TableProvider` for streaming partitioned datasets; it streams a set of `PartitionStream` values and can be marked infinite or assigned known sort order. For custom stream sources, DataFusion’s custom-table-provider guide emphasizes that `scan()` and `execute()` should stay lightweight and return stream/execution objects; real work should happen when the `SendableRecordBatchStream` is polled. ([Docs.rs][8])

### Use cases

```text id="streamingtable-use-cases"
Use StreamingTable for:
  external API streams
  Kafka-like/custom stream wrappers
  generated data streams
  continuous/incremental sources
  unbounded or bounded partitioned streams

Avoid StreamingTable when:
  source is already file/object-store-backed
  ListingTable can scan it
  source requires complex pushdown and metadata planning
```

---

## 13.11 Scanner-equivalent execution

### PyArrow-ish scanner

```python id="pyarrow-scanner-equivalent-source"
scanner = dataset.scanner(
    columns=["user_id", "amount"],
    filter=(pc.field("date") == "2026-05-22")
)
table = scanner.to_table()
```

### DataFusion lazy scanner

```rust id="datafusion-scanner-equivalent"
let scanner_like_df = ctx
    .table("events")
    .await?
    .filter(col("date").eq(lit("2026-05-22")))?
    .select(vec![
        col("user_id"),
        col("amount"),
    ])?;

// eager table-like materialization
let batches: Vec<RecordBatch> = scanner_like_df.clone().collect().await?;

// streaming scanner
let stream = scanner_like_df.execute_stream().await?;
```

DataFusion `collect` executes and buffers all output into `Vec<RecordBatch>`, while `execute_stream` returns a `SendableRecordBatchStream` and produces `RecordBatch` values incrementally; dropping the stream aborts query execution. ([Docs.rs][9])

### Agent rule

```text id="scanner-rule"
PyArrow scanner.to_table():
  DataFusion df.collect().await?

PyArrow scanner.to_batches():
  DataFusion df.execute_stream().await?

PyArrow scanner.count_rows():
  DataFusion df.aggregate(vec![], vec![count(lit(1)).alias("count")])
```

---

## 13.12 Projection and filter pushdown

### Projection

```rust id="dataset-projection"
let df = ctx
    .table("events")
    .await?
    .select(vec![
        col("user_id"),
        col("amount"),
        (col("amount") + col("tax")).alias("gross"),
    ])?;
```

### Filter

```rust id="dataset-filter"
let df = ctx
    .table("events")
    .await?
    .filter(
        col("year").eq(lit(2026_i32))
            .and(col("month").eq(lit(5_i32)))
            .and(col("event_type").eq(lit("click")))
    )?;
```

### Pushdown layers

```text id="dataset-pushdown-layers"
Partition pruning:
  directory/path predicates, e.g. year=2026/month=05

File pruning:
  file metadata / external index / list-files cache / catalog

Row-group pruning:
  Parquet statistics

Page/range pruning:
  Parquet page index when supported/configured

Projection pushdown:
  scan only referenced columns

Post-scan filtering:
  remaining predicates after source-level pruning
```

`ListingTable` documents pushdown for limit, filter, and projection when the file format supports it, and statistics/pruning based on file metadata; DataFusion’s Parquet format specifically has a pruning switch for statistics-based row-group pruning. ([Docs.rs][4])

---

## 13.13 File metadata caching

### What caches exist

```text id="metadata-caches"
ListingTable cache categories:
  ListFilesCache        # file listing results per table
  FileMetadataCache     # expensive file metadata, e.g. Parquet row groups/stats
  FileStatisticsCache   # collected table/file statistics
```

DataFusion’s CLI docs describe a default File Metadata Cache used by `ListingTable` to avoid rereading expensive file metadata while scanning many files; the `metadata_cache`, `statistics_cache`, and `list_files_cache` table functions expose cache contents and metadata such as paths, file sizes, etags, versions, metadata sizes, and hit counts. ([Apache DataFusion][10])

### Inspect cache in SQL

```sql id="metadata-cache-sql"
SELECT * FROM metadata_cache();

SELECT sum(metadata_size_bytes)
FROM metadata_cache();

SELECT *
FROM list_files_cache();

SELECT *
FROM statistics_cache();
```

### Rust-level ListingTable cache hook

```rust id="listingtable-with-cache"
let table = ListingTable::try_new(config)?
    .with_cache(ctx.runtime_env().cache_manager.get_file_statistic_cache());
```

`ListingTable::with_cache(Option<Arc<dyn FileStatisticsCache>>)` sets the statistics cache used by the table. In DataFusion 54 the file-statistics cache is centrally owned by the runtime `CacheManager` and is memory-limited: fetch the shared instance with `runtime_env.cache_manager.get_file_statistic_cache()` rather than constructing a competing app-level cache. `FileStatisticsCache` is a trait (`datafusion_execution::cache::cache_manager::FileStatisticsCache`) with default implementation `DefaultFileStatisticsCache`; its capacity is configured with `datafusion.runtime.file_statistics_cache_limit` (byte size with `K`/`M`/`G` suffixes; `0` disables the cache) or `RuntimeEnvBuilder`/`CacheManagerConfig::with_file_statistics_cache_limit(limit)`. If `None` is supplied to `with_cache`, a query-scoped default statistics cache is created. ([Docs.rs][4])

### External metadata/index advisory

```text id="external-index-advisory"
Use built-in caches when:
  repeated queries over same table location
  many Parquet files
  metadata reads are nontrivial

Use external metadata stores/indexes when:
  file count is huge
  object-store LIST cost dominates
  partition/catalog state is maintained externally
  query latency requires avoiding runtime directory crawl
```

DataFusion’s external-indexes blog emphasizes that caching parsed Parquet metadata and using external indexes/catalogs can significantly speed query processing, especially because there is no one-size-fits-all indexing design and different systems choose different metadata/index tradeoffs. ([Apache DataFusion][11])

---

## 13.14 Config settings relevant to datasets

```text id="dataset-configs"
datafusion.execution.listing_table_ignore_subdirectory = true
  ignore subdirectories when scanning non-partitioned directories

datafusion.execution.listing_table_factory_infer_partitions = true
  infer Hive-compliant partition columns in ListingTableFactory

datafusion.execution.split_file_groups_by_statistics = false
  experimental attempt to pack/sort files using non-overlapping statistics

datafusion.execution.keep_partition_by_columns = false
  controls whether partition_by columns are kept in output RecordBatches
```

These settings are documented in DataFusion’s runtime configuration: listing-table subdirectories are ignored by default for non-partitioned directory scans, Hive partition inference is enabled by default through `ListingTableFactory`, statistics-based file-group splitting is experimental, and partition-by columns are not kept in output batches by default. ([Apache DataFusion][12])

### Config skeleton

```rust id="dataset-config-skeleton"
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use datafusion::execution::context::SessionConfig;

let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .set_bool("datafusion.execution.listing_table_factory_infer_partitions", true)
    .set_bool("datafusion.execution.listing_table_ignore_subdirectory", true)
    .set_bool("datafusion.execution.keep_partition_by_columns", false);

let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config(config);
```

## 13.15 Writing datasets: DataFusion native simple writes

### Write DataFrame to Parquet

```rust id="df-write-parquet"
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;

df.write_parquet(
    "s3://bucket/output/",
    DataFrameWriteOptions::new(),
    None, // Option<TableParquetOptions>
).await?;
```

### Write CSV / JSON

```rust id="df-write-csv-json"
df.clone()
    .write_csv("s3://bucket/out_csv/", DataFrameWriteOptions::new(), None)
    .await?;

df.write_json("s3://bucket/out_json/", DataFrameWriteOptions::new(), None)
    .await?;
```

DataFusion executes a `DataFrame` and streams results to output files for supported formats including CSV, JSON, Arrow, Avro, and Parquet; `write_parquet`, `write_csv`, and `write_json` execute eagerly and return write-result batches, with `write_parquet` available behind the Parquet feature. ([Docs.rs][9])

### Advisory

```text id="df-write-advisory"
DataFusion writes are good for:
  query result export
  repartitioned/simple file outputs
  SQL/ETL pipelines

Rust-native custom writer needed for:
  exact Hive directory layout control
  per-partition file naming
  PyArrow write_dataset-style existing-data policies
  file visitor / metadata manifest collection
  partition-column drop/keep semantics
```

---

## 13.16 Writing partitioned datasets: PyArrow behavior baseline

```python id="pyarrow-write-dataset"
import pyarrow.dataset as ds

ds.write_dataset(
    table,
    base_dir="s3://bucket/events/",
    format="parquet",
    partitioning=["year", "month", "day"],
    basename_template="part-{i}.parquet",
    existing_data_behavior="delete_matching",
)
```

`pyarrow.dataset.write_dataset` writes a dataset to a format and supports existing-data behavior modes: default `error`, `overwrite_or_ignore`, and `delete_matching`; `pyarrow.parquet.write_to_dataset` wraps `dataset.write_dataset` and writes Hive-style partition subdirectories such as `group=value` for each combination of partition column values. ([Apache Arrow][13])

---

## 13.17 Rust-native partitioned writer pattern

### Partition key function

```rust id="partition-key"
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
struct PartitionKey {
    year: i32,
    month: i32,
    day: i32,
}

impl PartitionKey {
    fn hive_path(&self) -> String {
        format!("year={}/month={:02}/day={:02}", self.year, self.month, self.day)
    }
}
```

### Batch routing skeleton

```rust id="partition-writer-routing"
use std::collections::HashMap;
use parquet::arrow::async_writer::{AsyncArrowWriter, ParquetObjectWriter};
use parquet::file::properties::WriterProperties;
use object_store::{ObjectStore, path::Path};

struct PartitionSink {
    writer: AsyncArrowWriter<ParquetObjectWriter>,
    rows: usize,
}

struct PartitionedDatasetWriter {
    store: Arc<dyn ObjectStore>,
    root: Path,
    schema: SchemaRef,
    props: WriterProperties,
    sinks: HashMap<PartitionKey, PartitionSink>,
    file_counter: usize,
}

impl PartitionedDatasetWriter {
    async fn write_partition_batch(
        &mut self,
        key: PartitionKey,
        batch_without_partition_cols: RecordBatch,
    ) -> parquet::errors::Result<()> {
        let root = self.root.clone();
        let store = self.store.clone();
        let schema = self.schema.clone();
        let props = self.props.clone();
        let file_id = self.file_counter;

        let sink = self.sinks.entry(key.clone()).or_insert_with(|| {
            let file_path = root
                .child(key.hive_path())
                .child(format!("part-{file_id}.parquet"));

            let object_writer = ParquetObjectWriter::new(store, file_path);

            let writer = AsyncArrowWriter::try_new(
                object_writer,
                schema,
                Some(props),
            ).expect("writer create");

            PartitionSink { writer, rows: 0 }
        });

        sink.writer.write(&batch_without_partition_cols).await?;
        sink.rows += batch_without_partition_cols.num_rows();

        if sink.writer.in_progress_size() > 256 * 1024 * 1024 {
            sink.writer.flush().await?;
        }

        Ok(())
    }

    async fn close(mut self) -> parquet::errors::Result<()> {
        for (_, mut sink) in self.sinks.drain() {
            sink.writer.close().await?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

### Critical missing step: split batch by partition

```text id="split-by-partition"
Input batch:
  contains partition columns: year, month, day

Writer step:
  compute partition key per row
  group row indices by PartitionKey
  take rows per key into partition-specific RecordBatch
  optionally drop partition columns from file payload
  write to root/year=YYYY/month=MM/day=DD/part-N.parquet
```

This custom writer pattern is required when the application needs PyArrow `write_dataset`-style partition directory layout, existing-data semantics, file naming, partition-column dropping, or file-level metadata collection beyond DataFusion’s normal `DataFrame::write_*` APIs. DataFusion’s own write APIs stream DataFrame results to files, while PyArrow’s write_dataset has explicit partitioning and existing-data behavior knobs. ([Apache Arrow][13])

---

## 13.18 Existing data behavior: Rust policy layer

```text id="existing-data-behavior"
error:
  fail if destination root or matching partition has files

overwrite_or_ignore:
  write files with unique names
  overwrite only name collisions
  leave unrelated existing files

delete_matching:
  first time partition key is encountered:
    delete target partition directory/prefix
  then write new files
```

```rust id="existing-data-enum"
enum ExistingDataBehavior {
    Error,
    OverwriteOrIgnore,
    DeleteMatching,
}
```

### Object-store delete-matching skeleton

```rust id="delete-matching-skeleton"
use std::collections::HashSet;

struct ExistingDataPolicy {
    behavior: ExistingDataBehavior,
    deleted_partitions: HashSet<PartitionKey>,
}

impl ExistingDataPolicy {
    async fn before_write_partition(
        &mut self,
        store: Arc<dyn ObjectStore>,
        root: &Path,
        key: &PartitionKey,
    ) -> object_store::Result<()> {
        match self.behavior {
            ExistingDataBehavior::Error => {
                // list destination prefix; error if any objects exist
            }
            ExistingDataBehavior::OverwriteOrIgnore => {
                // ensure unique file names to avoid accidental overwrite
            }
            ExistingDataBehavior::DeleteMatching => {
                if self.deleted_partitions.insert(key.clone()) {
                    let prefix = root.child(key.hive_path());
                    let objects = store.list(Some(&prefix));
                    // collect and delete listed objects
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

Use a dataset-writer policy layer because PyArrow’s `existing_data_behavior` modes are explicit API semantics, while Rust/DataFusion write APIs do not automatically replicate PyArrow’s `delete_matching` partition lifecycle. ([Apache Arrow][13])

---

## 13.19 Schema normalization and evolution

```text id="schema-normalization"
PyArrow dataset:
  discovery can crawl directories, handle partitioned datasets, and normalize schemas

DataFusion ListingTable:
  can merge schemas from files with compatible but non-identical schemas
  ListingOptions::infer_schema resolves common schema
  ParquetFormat can skip embedded metadata to avoid schema conflicts
```

`ListingTable` documents compatible schema merging across files, and `ParquetFormat::with_skip_metadata(true)` can clear schema metadata before schema merging to help avoid metadata-driven conflicts. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Recommended contract

```text id="schema-normalization-rule"
Production:
  maintain canonical SchemaRef externally
  use explicit ListingTableConfig::with_schema(schema)
  reject incompatible files early
  allow metadata-skipping only when metadata is not part of contract

Exploration:
  infer schema
  inspect
  persist canonical schema
```

---

## 13.20 Predicate pushdown and statistics pruning

### DataFusion path

```rust id="dataset-predicate-datafusion"
let df = ctx
    .table("events")
    .await?
    .filter(
        col("tenant_id").eq(lit("acme"))
            .and(col("year").eq(lit(2026_i32)))
            .and(col("amount").gt(lit(100_i64)))
    )?
    .select(vec![col("tenant_id"), col("amount"), col("event_ts")])?;
```

### Internal pruning targets

```text id="pruning-targets"
Partition columns:
  year/month/day/tenant_id from Hive paths

File metadata:
  object path, size, etag, version, cached listing metadata

Parquet metadata:
  row-group statistics
  column indexes / page indexes if used by format path
  row counts / file statistics cache

DataFusion optimizer:
  pushes projection/filter into scan where supported
```

`ListingTable` supports statistics collection and pruning based on file metadata, while DataFusion’s metadata and statistics caches can expose file sizes, etags, versions, row counts, column counts, table sizes, and metadata sizes; external indexes and cached Parquet metadata are recommended for high-performance custom systems with large file counts. ([Docs.rs][4])

---

## 13.21 Multi-file scan performance rules

```text id="multifile-performance-rules"
DO:
  use Parquet for large analytical datasets
  use Hive partition columns for coarse pruning
  use Parquet statistics for row-group pruning
  configure metadata caches for repeated scans
  avoid object-store relisting per query where possible
  tune target_partitions to match executor parallelism
  use execute_stream for large result sets

DON'T:
  scan hundreds of thousands of object-store files without catalog/cache strategy
  infer schema on every query
  store many tiny files if query throughput matters
  collect unbounded DataFrames into Vec<RecordBatch>
```

DataFusion’s ListingTable cache docs explicitly call out file metadata and list-files caches to speed repeated directory scans, while its external-indexes blog explains that custom metadata stores, caches, and indexes are often necessary for high-performance custom systems over Parquet. ([Apache DataFusion][10])

---

## 13.22 DataFrame cache versus file metadata cache

```rust id="dataframe-cache"
let cached = ctx
    .table("events")
    .await?
    .filter(col("year").eq(lit(2026_i32)))?
    .cache()
    .await?;
```

`DataFrame::cache()` materializes a DataFrame as a memory table according to the configured cache factory, while `ListingTable` metadata caches avoid repeated expensive file metadata/listing/statistics reads; these are different layers and solve different performance problems. ([Docs.rs][9])

```text id="cache-layer-rule"
DataFrame.cache():
  caches query result rows/batches

ListingTable metadata/list files/statistics caches:
  cache scan planning metadata, not data rows

External catalog/index:
  caches table/file/partition/page metadata outside process/session
```

---

## 13.23 DataFusion write versus custom partition writer

| Requirement                                  |               Use DataFusion `write_*` | Use custom Rust partition writer |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------: | -------------------------------: |
| export query result to Parquet               |                                    yes |                         optional |
| write one output path                        |                                    yes |                         optional |
| exact Hive partition layout                  |      maybe not enough / verify version |                              yes |
| `existing_data_behavior=delete_matching`     | no direct PyArrow-equivalent guarantee |                              yes |
| partition-specific file naming               |                    no direct guarantee |                              yes |
| collect file metadata visitor                |                          custom needed |                              yes |
| drop partition columns from payload          |                          custom needed |                              yes |
| row-group/file-size policy per partition     |                                limited |                              yes |
| object-store atomic/conditional write policy |                          custom needed |                              yes |

DataFusion’s write APIs execute and stream DataFrame contents to output files, but PyArrow’s `write_dataset`/`write_to_dataset` APIs expose partitioning, basename template, file visitor, and existing-data behavior semantics that often require an application-level writer policy in Rust. ([Docs.rs][9])

---

## 13.24 End-to-end read workflow

```rust id="end-to-end-read-workflow"
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion_common::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let table_path = ListingTableUrl::parse("s3://bucket/events/")?;

    let parquet = ParquetFormat::new()
        .with_enable_pruning(true)
        .with_metadata_size_hint(Some(256 * 1024));

    let options = ListingOptions::new(Arc::new(parquet))
        .with_file_extension(".parquet")
        .with_table_partition_cols(vec![
            ("year".to_string(), DataType::Int32),
            ("month".to_string(), DataType::Int32),
            ("day".to_string(), DataType::Int32),
        ])
        .with_collect_stat(true)
        .with_target_partitions(64);

    let schema = options.infer_schema(ctx.state().as_ref(), &table_path).await?;

    let config = ListingTableConfig::new(table_path)
        .with_listing_options(options)
        .with_schema(schema);

    ctx.register_table("events", Arc::new(ListingTable::try_new(config)?))?;

    let df = ctx
        .table("events")
        .await?
        .filter(
            col("year").eq(lit(2026_i32))
                .and(col("month").eq(lit(5_i32)))
                .and(col("day").eq(lit(22_i32)))
                .and(col("event_type").eq(lit("click")))
        )?
        .select(vec![
            col("user_id"),
            col("event_ts"),
            col("amount"),
        ])?;

    let mut stream = df.execute_stream().await?;

    while let Some(batch) = stream.next().await {
        let batch = batch?;
        // write to sink
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

## 13.25 End-to-end simple write workflow

```rust id="end-to-end-write-simple"
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;

let result_df = ctx.sql(r#"
    SELECT user_id, count(*) AS n
    FROM events
    WHERE year = 2026 AND month = 5
    GROUP BY user_id
"#).await?;

result_df.write_parquet(
    "s3://bucket/results/click_counts/",
    DataFrameWriteOptions::new(),
    None,
).await?;
```

Use this pattern for simple result exports. Use a custom partitioned writer when output layout and overwrite semantics must mirror PyArrow `write_dataset`. DataFusion writes stream DataFrame results to supported file formats, while PyArrow `write_dataset` additionally models partitioned dataset write policies. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

## 13.26 Anti-pattern catalog

| Anti-pattern                                                          | Failure mode                              | Correct pattern                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| reimplement dataset scanner with manual object-store loops            | misses optimizer/pushdown/cache machinery | `ListingTable` / DataFusion                      |
| infer schema on every query                                           | latency + instability                     | infer once, persist canonical schema             |
| scan object-store directories without metadata/listing cache strategy | slow repeated queries                     | built-in caches / external catalog               |
| use `MemTable` for large lake data                                    | memory blowup                             | `ListingTable`                                   |
| collect DataFrame before writing                                      | unnecessary memory pressure               | `write_parquet` or stream                        |
| assume DataFusion write equals PyArrow `write_dataset` semantics      | overwrite/partition mismatch              | explicit custom writer policy                    |
| partition by high-cardinality values                                  | tiny files/directories                    | choose coarse partition keys                     |
| ignore partition column types                                         | wrong pruning/filter behavior             | typed `with_table_partition_cols`                |
| disable statistics collection/pruning blindly                         | more IO                                   | keep stats unless cost/privacy demands otherwise |
| rely on Hive inference in production without tests                    | path parsing drift                        | explicit partition column declarations           |

---

## 13.27 Golden test matrix

```text id="dataset-test-matrix"
ListingTable:
  single file
  multi-file same schema
  multi-file compatible schema merge
  incompatible schema rejection
  explicit schema
  inferred schema
  file extension filtering
  target_partitions effect

Hive partitioning:
  one partition column
  multiple partition columns
  typed Int32 partition values
  partition predicate pruning
  partition column output presence
  malformed partition path

Projection/filter:
  projected columns only
  derived column
  partition-only filter
  data-column filter
  combined partition + data filter
  limit pushdown

Caching:
  metadata_cache visible after query
  list_files_cache reused
  statistics_cache when stats collection enabled
  repeated query avoids repeated metadata reads where expected

MemTable:
  one partition
  multiple partitions
  empty table vec![vec![]]
  schema mismatch rejection

StreamingTable/custom provider:
  finite stream
  infinite flag
  schema mismatch rejection
  stream error propagation

Writing:
  DataFrame write_parquet simple
  custom partition writer directory layout
  existing_data_behavior=error
  existing_data_behavior=overwrite_or_ignore
  existing_data_behavior=delete_matching
  file naming uniqueness
  partition column drop/keep policy
```

## 13.28 Value case

```text id="dataset-value-case"
SessionContext:
  value = query/session/catalog/runtime root.

ListingTable:
  value = PyArrow dataset-like multi-file scan over local/object-store paths.

ListingOptions:
  value = file format, extension filtering, partition columns, statistics collection, target partitions, known sort order.

Hive partitioning:
  value = coarse file/directory pruning and partition columns materialized into table schema.

MemTable:
  value = bounded in-memory RecordBatch dataset for tests/caches/small dimensions.

StreamingTable:
  value = TableProvider for partitioned streaming sources.

DataFrame:
  value = lazy Scanner-like logical plan with projection/filter/aggregate/join/write execution.

Metadata caches:
  value = repeated scan acceleration and object-store/listing/footer-read reduction.

Predicate pushdown:
  value = avoid reading files, row groups, columns, and rows that cannot match.

Custom partition writer:
  value = PyArrow write_dataset-style layout, overwrite policy, file naming, and metadata collection under Rust control.
```

Final agent rule:

```text id="dataset-final-rule"
For reading datasets:
  use DataFusion ListingTable or SessionContext read_* APIs.

For scanner-like behavior:
  build lazy DataFrame with filter/select and use execute_stream.

For bounded table materialization:
  collect.

For in-memory data:
  MemTable.

For stream sources:
  StreamingTable or custom TableProvider.

For partitioned writes with PyArrow write_dataset semantics:
  implement an explicit Rust writer policy over object_store + parquet writers.

Never assume DataFusion write APIs exactly replicate PyArrow write_dataset overwrite/partition/file-visitor semantics.
```

## 13.29 Typed per-file extensions: `PartitionedFile.extensions` (DataFusion 54)

Secondary coverage — primary deep dive is `datafusion_rust.md` §14. DataFusion 54 replaces the untyped `Arc<dyn Any>` extension slot on `PartitionedFile` with a typed extension map:

```rust
// datafusion-datasource src/mod.rs
pub type FileExtensions = datafusion_common::extensions::Extensions;

pub struct PartitionedFile {
    // …
    pub extensions: FileExtensions,
}
```

```rust
// Attach multiple independent typed values to one file:
let file = PartitionedFile::new(path, size)
    .with_extension(access_plan)        // e.g. a ParquetAccessPlan
    .with_extension(MyScanHints { .. }); // custom per-file info

// Typed retrieval — no manual downcast bookkeeping:
if let Some(hints) = file.extension::<MyScanHints>() {
    // …
}
```

Key points:

```text
FileExtensions is a by-type map (datafusion_common::extensions::Extensions):
  insert / insert_arc / insert_dyn / get / get_arc / contains / merge
  one value per Rust type; values must be Any + Send + Sync

with_extension(value) / extension::<T>() are the DF-54 idiomatic surface;
the legacy with_extensions(Arc<dyn Any + Send + Sync>) is retained for
migration but stores a single untyped payload.

Use cases:
  ParquetAccessPlan for row-group/page selection plus custom index or
  cache metadata on the same PartitionedFile without wrapper structs.
```

Custom `TableProvider`s that previously multiplexed several payloads through one `Arc<dyn Any>` should attach each payload as its own typed extension instead.
