# 14) Filesystem and object-store layer

Style target: dense, syntax-first, agent-ready technical reference; continues the uploaded advanced-reference structure. 

---

## 14.0 Mental model

```text id="object-store-mental-model"
PyArrow fs layer:
  FileSystem abstraction
  cursor-like input/output streams
  local/S3/GCS/Azure/HDFS-style filesystem API

Rust object_store layer:
  ObjectStore trait
  async object-store-native API
  stateless path operations
  byte-range reads
  conditional reads/writes
  atomic object writes
  multipart upload
  list streams
  object metadata
```

`object_store` provides a uniform async API for object storage services and local files through the `ObjectStore` trait; it supports in-memory storage by default and feature-gated local filesystem, Google Cloud Storage, Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, and HTTP/WebDAV implementations. It intentionally mirrors object-store APIs rather than cursor-based filesystem APIs, which gives atomic object writes, object-store-native preconditions, stateless range reads, and portability across cloud/local backends. ([Docs.rs][1]) ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 14.1 Cargo profiles

### Memory-only tests

```toml id="object-store-cargo-memory"
[dependencies]
object_store = "0.13.2"
bytes = "1"
futures = "0.3"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros"] }
```

### Local filesystem

```toml id="object-store-cargo-local"
[dependencies]
object_store = { version = "0.13.2", features = ["fs"] }
bytes = "1"
futures = "0.3"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros", "fs", "io-util"] }
```

### Cloud stores

```toml id="object-store-cargo-cloud"
[dependencies]
object_store = { version = "0.13.2", features = ["aws", "gcp", "azure", "http"] }
bytes = "1"
futures = "0.3"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros"] }
url = "2"
```

### TLS root bundle profile

```toml id="object-store-cargo-tls"
[dependencies]
object_store = {
  version = "0.13.2",
  features = ["aws", "gcp", "azure", "http", "tls-webpki-roots"]
}
```

By default, HTTPS/TLS stores use system-bundled certificates, and the `tls-webpki-roots` feature can additionally bundle Mozilla root certificates into the application. ([Docs.rs][1])

## 14.2 Imports

```rust id="object-store-imports"
use std::ops::Range;
use std::sync::Arc;

use bytes::Bytes;
use futures::{StreamExt, TryStreamExt};

use object_store::{
    ObjectStore, ObjectStoreExt,
    Error, GetOptions, GetResult,
    PutMode, PutOptions, PutPayload, PutPayloadMut,
    PutMultipartOptions, MultipartUpload,
    UpdateVersion,
    path::Path,
    memory::InMemory,
};

#[cfg(feature = "fs")]
use object_store::local::LocalFileSystem;

#[cfg(feature = "aws")]
use object_store::aws::AmazonS3Builder;

#[cfg(feature = "gcp")]
use object_store::gcp::GoogleCloudStorageBuilder;

#[cfg(feature = "azure")]
use object_store::azure::MicrosoftAzureBuilder;

#[cfg(feature = "http")]
use object_store::http::HttpBuilder;
```

`ObjectStoreExt` is the user-facing convenience extension trait containing methods such as `put`, `get`, `get_range`, `head`, `delete`, `copy`, `copy_if_not_exists`, `rename`, and `rename_if_not_exists`; `ObjectStore` itself is now the lower-level implementor contract and most convenience methods moved to `ObjectStoreExt` in the `0.13.0` redesign. ([Docs.rs][2]) ([Docs.rs][3])

## 14.3 PyArrow filesystem equivalents

| PyArrow `pyarrow.fs`          | Rust `object_store` equivalent                        | Notes                                     |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `fs.LocalFileSystem()`        | `LocalFileSystem::new()` / `new_with_prefix(...)`     | local files through object-store API      |
| `fs.S3FileSystem(...)`        | `AmazonS3Builder` / `parse_url("s3://...")`           | S3 and S3-compatible stores               |
| `fs.GcsFileSystem(...)`       | `GoogleCloudStorageBuilder` / `parse_url("gs://...")` | GCS                                       |
| `fs.AzureFileSystem(...)`     | `MicrosoftAzureBuilder` / Azure URL/config            | Azure Blob                                |
| `fs.FileSystem.from_uri(uri)` | `object_store::parse_url` / `parse_url_opts`          | returns store + inner path                |
| `open_input_file`             | `get`, `get_range`, `get_ranges`                      | object-store range reads, not cursor seek |
| `open_input_stream`           | `get(...).into_stream()`                              | async byte stream                         |
| `open_output_stream`          | `put` / `put_multipart`                               | atomic whole-object write                 |
| `get_file_info`               | `head`, `list`, `list_with_delimiter`                 | metadata/listing                          |
| `copy_file`                   | `copy` / `copy_if_not_exists`                         | same-store copy                           |
| `move`                        | `rename` / `rename_if_not_exists`                     | may be copy+delete                        |
| `delete_file`                 | `delete`                                              | object delete                             |
| directory selector/list       | `list(Some(prefix))`                                  | recursive prefix listing                  |

PyArrow’s filesystem interface exposes `FileSystem.from_uri`, local/S3/GCS/Azure-backed filesystems, metadata and copy/delete/move methods, and cursor-style input/output streams; `object_store` instead exposes object-store-native operations and returns `(store, path)` from `parse_url_opts`. ([Apache Arrow][4]) ([Apache Arrow][5]) ([Docs.rs][6])

---

## 14.4 Core trait: `ObjectStore`

### Required / provided method surface

```text id="objectstore-methods"
Required ObjectStore methods:
  put_opts
  put_multipart_opts
  get_opts
  delete_stream
  list
  list_with_delimiter
  copy_opts

Provided ObjectStore methods:
  get_ranges
  list_with_offset
  rename_opts
```

The current `ObjectStore` trait is `Display + Send + Sync + Debug + 'static`; its required methods include `put_opts`, `put_multipart_opts`, `get_opts`, `delete_stream`, `list`, `list_with_delimiter`, and `copy_opts`, while `get_ranges`, `list_with_offset`, and `rename_opts` have provided implementations. ([Docs.rs][3]) ([Docs.rs][3])

### Trait object pattern

```rust id="objectstore-trait-object"
use std::sync::Arc;
use object_store::{ObjectStore, memory::InMemory};

let store: Arc<dyn ObjectStore> = Arc::new(InMemory::new());
```

### Clone semantics

```text id="clone-semantics"
Clone of store handle:
  clones handle/config/state reference
  does not clone object data

InMemory::fork():
  copies current in-memory content into a separate store
```

The `ObjectStore` docs state that cloning a store handle does not clone/fork the underlying key-value data; `InMemory::fork` is the explicit API that copies current in-memory content into a new store. ([Docs.rs][3]) ([Docs.rs][7])

---

## 14.5 Path model

```rust id="objectstore-paths"
use object_store::path::Path;

let p1 = Path::from("data/file.parquet");
let p2 = Path::from("year=2026/month=05/part-000.parquet");

assert_eq!(p1.as_ref(), "data/file.parquet");
```

```text id="path-rules"
Object path:
  slash-delimited logical object path
  not std::path::PathBuf
  no implicit current directory
  no filesystem cursor
  no path mutation through open file handle
```

`object_store::path::Path` is the logical object-storage path abstraction; local filesystem support maps it to local files, and local paths follow file-URI semantics with `/` as the delimiter. ([Docs.rs][1]) ([Docs.rs][8])

---

## 14.6 Backend construction

### In-memory

```rust id="inmemory-store"
let store = InMemory::new();
let store: Arc<dyn ObjectStore> = Arc::new(store);
```

`InMemory` is intended for tests or opting out of cloud storage, and it implements `ObjectStore` and multipart store behavior. ([Docs.rs][7])

### Local filesystem

```rust id="local-store"
#[cfg(feature = "fs")]
let store = LocalFileSystem::new_with_prefix("/tmp/my-dataset")?;

#[cfg(feature = "fs")]
let store: Arc<dyn ObjectStore> = Arc::new(store);
```

`LocalFileSystem` is available behind the `fs` feature on non-WebAssembly targets, implements `ObjectStore` for local disk, and may be created with an optional directory prefix. ([Docs.rs][8])

### S3

```rust id="s3-store"
#[cfg(feature = "aws")]
let s3 = AmazonS3Builder::from_env()
    .with_bucket_name("my-bucket")
    .with_region("us-east-1")
    .build()?;

#[cfg(feature = "aws")]
let store: Arc<dyn ObjectStore> = Arc::new(s3);
```

`AmazonS3Builder` configures S3 connections by bucket, region, and credentials; `from_env` reads regular AWS environment variables such as `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, endpoint variables, session token, web-identity token file, and role ARN. ([Docs.rs][9]) ([Docs.rs][9])

### GCS

```rust id="gcs-store"
#[cfg(feature = "gcp")]
let gcs = GoogleCloudStorageBuilder::from_env()
    .with_bucket_name("my-bucket")
    .build()?;

#[cfg(feature = "gcp")]
let store: Arc<dyn ObjectStore> = Arc::new(gcs);
```

`GoogleCloudStorageBuilder` configures a GCS connection, is enabled by the `gcp` feature, supports methods such as `from_env`, `with_bucket_name`, `with_service_account_key`, `with_service_account_path`, `with_application_credentials`, `with_base_url`, `with_skip_signature`, and client/proxy/retry configuration, and sources credentials from the environment when none are explicitly provided. ([Docs.rs][10]) ([Docs.rs][10])

### Azure Blob

```rust id="azure-store"
#[cfg(feature = "azure")]
let azure = MicrosoftAzureBuilder::new()
    .with_account("account")
    .with_container_name("container")
    .with_access_key("account-key")
    .build()?;

#[cfg(feature = "azure")]
let store: Arc<dyn ObjectStore> = Arc::new(azure);
```

`MicrosoftAzureBuilder` configures Azure Blob Storage containers and supports access key, account, container, SAS, bearer token, client secret, federated token, MSI endpoint, Azure CLI, emulator, endpoint, authority host, retry, proxy, and HTTP connector configuration; Azure streaming uploads use `put_multipart_opts`, uploading blocks and composing them into a blob. ([Docs.rs][11]) ([Docs.rs][12])

### HTTP / WebDAV

```rust id="http-store"
#[cfg(feature = "http")]
let http = HttpBuilder::new()
    .with_url("https://example.com/data/")
    .build()?;

#[cfg(feature = "http")]
let store: Arc<dyn ObjectStore> = Arc::new(http);
```

`HttpBuilder` configures a generic HTTP server object store, is enabled by the `http` feature, and supports URL, retry, client options, HTTP connector, and config-based construction. ([Docs.rs][13]) ([Docs.rs][13])

## 14.7 URL-based configuration

### Parse URL

```rust id="parse-url"
use object_store::{parse_url, parse_url_opts};
use url::Url;

let url = Url::parse("s3://bucket/path/to/file.parquet")?;
let (store, path) = parse_url(&url)?;

assert_eq!(path.as_ref(), "path/to/file.parquet");
```

### Parse URL with options

```rust id="parse-url-opts"
let url = Url::parse("s3://bucket/path/to/file.parquet")?;

let (store, path) = parse_url_opts(
    &url,
    [
        ("aws_region", "us-east-1"),
        ("aws_access_key_id", "..."),
        ("aws_secret_access_key", "..."),
    ],
)?;
```

`parse_url_opts(url, options)` creates an `ObjectStore` from a URL scheme and key-value builder options, returning both the store and the object path; examples include `file:///path/to/my/file` returning a `LocalFileSystem` and `s3://bucket/path` returning an S3 store when the `aws` feature is enabled. ([Docs.rs][6])

### Runtime-config pattern

```rust id="storage-config-struct"
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct StorageUrl {
    pub url: url::Url,
    pub options: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

pub fn store_from_config(cfg: &StorageUrl) -> object_store::Result<(Box<dyn ObjectStore>, Path)> {
    object_store::parse_url_opts(
        &cfg.url,
        cfg.options.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.as_str(), v.as_str())),
    )
}
```

The crate-level configuration system is inspired by fsspec, PyArrow FileSystem, and Hadoop FileSystem APIs and is intended to create store implementations from URLs plus optional key-value configuration without large application-specific code paths. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 14.8 Core operations: put/get/head/delete/list

### Put + get

```rust id="put-get"
let store: Arc<dyn ObjectStore> = Arc::new(InMemory::new());
let path = Path::from("data/hello.txt");

store.put(&path, Bytes::from_static(b"hello").into()).await?;

let result = store.get(&path).await?;
let bytes = result.bytes().await?;

assert_eq!(&bytes[..], b"hello");
```

`ObjectStoreExt::put` saves bytes atomically: the operation either writes the entire payload or fails, and clients should not observe a partial object; `ObjectStoreExt::get` returns stored bytes, and `GetResult::bytes()` buffers the full object in memory. ([Docs.rs][2]) ([Docs.rs][1])

### Stream get result

```rust id="get-stream"
let result = store.get(&path).await?;
let mut stream = result.into_stream();

while let Some(chunk) = stream.try_next().await? {
    // chunk: Bytes
}
```

The crate docs show streaming object data through `get(...).into_stream()` as the alternative to buffering the entire object with `bytes()`. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Head

```rust id="head"
let meta = store.head(&path).await?;

println!("path={} size={} last_modified={:?}", meta.location, meta.size, meta.last_modified);
```

`ObjectStoreExt::head` returns `ObjectMeta` for a location. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Delete

```rust id="delete"
store.delete(&path).await?;
```

### List recursively

```rust id="list-recursive"
let prefix = Path::from("data/");
let mut stream = store.list(Some(&prefix));

while let Some(meta) = stream.try_next().await? {
    println!("{} {}", meta.location, meta.size);
}
```

`ObjectStore::list(Some(prefix))` returns an async stream of object metadata for all objects recursively below that prefix, and the crate-level docs show this working for both S3 prefixes and local directories. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 14.9 Range reads and vectored IO

### Single byte range

```rust id="range-read"
let bytes = store.get_range(&path, 0..1024).await?;
```

`ObjectStoreExt::get_range` returns the bytes stored at a location in the given byte range; to read a range from a versioned object, use `ObjectStore::get_opts` with `GetOptions`. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Multiple ranges

```rust id="vectored-read"
let ranges: Vec<Range<u64>> = vec![0..16, 1024..2048, 4096..8192];

let chunks: Vec<Bytes> = store.get_ranges(&path, &ranges).await?;

assert_eq!(chunks.len(), ranges.len());
```

`ObjectStore::get_ranges` is designed for multiple potentially non-contiguous ranges of the same object and can coalesce adjacent ranges into an appropriate number of parallel requests, which is especially useful for structured file formats such as Parquet. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Versioned/ranged get

```rust id="get-opts-range"
let opts = GetOptions::default().with_range(Some(90..100));
let result = store.get_opts(&path, opts).await?;
let bytes = result.bytes().await?;
```

---

## 14.10 Conditional fetch

```rust id="conditional-fetch"
let first = store.get(&path).await?;
let etag = first.meta.e_tag.clone();
let cached = first.bytes().await?;

if let Some(etag) = etag {
    let opts = GetOptions::new().with_if_none_match(Some(etag));

    match store.get_opts(&path, opts).await {
        Ok(updated) => {
            let new_bytes = updated.bytes().await?;
        }
        Err(Error::NotModified { .. }) => {
            // cached is still current
        }
        Err(e) => return Err(e),
    }
}
```

`get_opts` supports conditional fetches such as `if-none-match`, which can refresh caches without refetching unchanged object data; the crate docs demonstrate using an object ETag with `GetOptions::new().with_if_none_match(...)` and handling `Error::NotModified`. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 14.11 Conditional put and optimistic concurrency

### Create-only write

```rust id="conditional-put-create"
match store
    .put_opts(
        &path,
        Bytes::from_static(b"new").into(),
        PutMode::Create.into(),
    )
    .await
{
    Ok(_) => {}
    Err(Error::AlreadyExists { .. }) => {
        // object already exists
    }
    Err(e) => return Err(e),
}
```

### Compare-and-swap update

```rust id="conditional-put-update"
loop {
    let current = store.get(&path).await?;

    let version = UpdateVersion {
        e_tag: current.meta.e_tag.clone(),
        version: current.meta.version.clone(),
    };

    let new_bytes = Bytes::from(do_update(current.bytes().await?));

    match store
        .put_opts(&path, new_bytes.into(), PutMode::Update(version).into())
        .await
    {
        Ok(_) => break,
        Err(Error::Precondition { .. }) => continue,
        Err(e) => return Err(e),
    }
}
```

`PutMode` configures put preconditions: `Overwrite` atomically overwrites, `Create` atomically creates and errors if the object exists, and `Update(UpdateVersion)` atomically writes only if the current object version matches, otherwise returning a precondition error. The crate docs explicitly frame conditional put as a way to implement optimistic-concurrency transactions for metadata catalogs on object storage. ([Docs.rs][14]) ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 14.12 Vectored writes

```rust id="vectored-write"
let mut payload = PutPayloadMut::new().with_block_size(8192);

for chunk in chunks {
    payload.extend_from_slice(&chunk);
}

let payload = payload.freeze();

store.put(&path, payload).await?;
```

`PutPayload` does not require contiguous memory regions; `PutPayloadMut` lets writers build chunked payloads without repeated `Vec` reallocation/copying, and the docs show block-based accumulation into multiple allocations followed by `put`. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 14.13 Multipart uploads

### Simple multipart upload

```rust id="multipart-simple"
let mut upload = store.put_multipart(&path).await?;

let p1 = upload.put_part(Bytes::from(vec![0_u8; 10 * 1024 * 1024]).into());
let p2 = upload.put_part(Bytes::from(vec![1_u8; 10 * 1024 * 1024]).into());

futures::try_join!(p1, p2)?;

let result = upload.complete().await?;
```

`MultipartUpload` writes an object in fixed-size chunks; multiple `put_part` futures may be polled in parallel, and `complete()` makes the entire uploaded object visible as an atomic operation. Stores typically require every part except the last to be at least 5 MiB, and clients seeking compatibility should write fixed-size blocks larger than 5 MiB. ([Docs.rs][15])

### Abort on failure

```rust id="multipart-abort"
let mut upload = store.put_multipart(&path).await?;

let result = async {
    upload.put_part(first.into()).await?;
    upload.put_part(second.into()).await?;
    upload.complete().await
}
.await;

if result.is_err() {
    // best effort cleanup
    let _ = upload.abort().await;
}
```

The S3 module warns that failed multipart writers can leave uploaded but unused parts that may incur charges, and recommends aborting or automatic cleanup of stale unused parts. ([Docs.rs][16])

### Upload-size rule

```text id="multipart-size-rule"
Small object:
  store.put(path, payload)

Large known/unknown object:
  put_multipart / multipart writer

Part size:
  fixed blocks > 5 MiB for broad compatibility

Failure:
  abort multipart upload
  cleanup stale orphan parts where backend requires it
```

---

## 14.14 Copy and rename semantics

```rust id="copy-rename"
store.copy(&from, &to).await?;
store.rename(&from, &to).await?;
```

```text id="copy-rename-semantics"
copy:
  same-store copy
  destination overwritten by default

copy_if_not_exists:
  errors if destination exists
  atomic only if backend supports it

rename:
  move object
  default may be copy then delete
  destination overwritten by default

rename_if_not_exists:
  backend-dependent atomicity
```

`ObjectStoreExt::copy` overwrites an existing destination; `copy_if_not_exists` errors if the destination exists and is atomic only when the backend supports it, while `rename` is described as move/copy+delete behavior and may not check that the deleted source is the same object originally copied. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Advisory

```text id="rename-advisory"
Object-store-safe commit pattern:
  write final object path with PutMode::Create or PutMode::Update

Avoid:
  temp file + rename as commit primitive
  assuming rename is atomic on S3/GCS/Azure
```

The object-store API design intentionally avoids pretending object stores have filesystem rename semantics and emphasizes atomic object creation/conditional writes instead. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 14.15 Why object-store APIs differ from filesystems

```text id="object-vs-filesystem"
Object store:
  key -> immutable-ish object bytes
  stateless operations
  range reads
  atomic whole-object put
  conditional preconditions
  list by prefix
  multipart upload
  no cursor seek/write handle semantics
  no guaranteed atomic rename

Filesystem:
  directories/files
  open/read/seek/write handles
  append/update-in-place
  rename often atomic locally
  path hierarchy has stronger local semantics
```

`object_store` explicitly states that the interface mirrors object-store APIs rather than filesystem APIs, using stateless APIs instead of cursor-based `Read`/`Seek`; the design provides atomic operations, direct mapping to cloud-store APIs, portability, operation preconditions, and atomic multipart upload. It includes `BufReader`/`BufWriter` adapters for filesystem-like use, but says they should be used with care. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 14.16 Credential and config patterns

### Environment-first

```rust id="credential-env"
let s3 = AmazonS3Builder::from_env()
    .with_bucket_name("bucket")
    .build()?;

let gcs = GoogleCloudStorageBuilder::from_env()
    .with_bucket_name("bucket")
    .build()?;

let azure = MicrosoftAzureBuilder::from_env()
    .with_container_name("container")
    .build()?;
```

### Explicit credentials

```rust id="credential-explicit"
let s3 = AmazonS3Builder::new()
    .with_region("us-east-1")
    .with_bucket_name("bucket")
    .with_access_key_id(access_key)
    .with_secret_access_key(secret_key)
    .build()?;

let gcs = GoogleCloudStorageBuilder::new()
    .with_bucket_name("bucket")
    .with_service_account_path("/secrets/gcp.json")
    .build()?;

let azure = MicrosoftAzureBuilder::new()
    .with_account("acct")
    .with_container_name("container")
    .with_access_key(access_key)
    .build()?;
```

### Deployment rule

```text id="credential-rule"
Production:
  prefer workload identity / IAM role / environment provider chain
  avoid hardcoded keys
  avoid logging URL query strings containing credentials
  pass secrets through secret manager / env / credential provider

Testing:
  InMemory for unit tests
  LocalFileSystem for integration tests
  explicit localstack/minio/azurite endpoints for backend tests
```

S3, GCS, and Azure builders all expose environment/config and explicit credential/config methods; PyArrow’s S3 and GCS filesystems similarly rely on native cloud credential mechanisms by default. ([Docs.rs][9]) ([Docs.rs][10]) ([Docs.rs][11]) ([Apache Arrow][5])

## 14.17 TLS and HTTP client customization

```rust id="client-options-sketch"
use object_store::client::ClientOptions;

// exact config keys depend on backend and object_store version
let client_options = ClientOptions::new();
```

Object-store implementations that use HTTPS/TLS can source CA certificates from the system bundle by default, with `tls-webpki-roots` available for bundled Mozilla roots; many cloud implementations permit HTTP client customization through `HttpConnector` and the `client` module, including custom headers and alternate Tokio runtime IO. ([Docs.rs][1])

```text id="tls-guidance"
DO:
  configure CA roots intentionally in containers/distroless images
  use proxy configuration where required
  isolate custom HTTP clients/connectors at store construction
  validate TLS behavior in the same runtime/container image shipped to production

DON'T:
  disable signatures/TLS except for local emulators
  compile custom root behavior without deployment tests
```

---

## 14.18 Rate limiting, throttling, and concurrency

```text id="object-store-adapters"
Adapters:
  LimitStore      # maximum concurrent requests
  ThrottleConfig  # rate throttling
  PrefixStore     # constant path prefix wrapper
```

The crate-level docs list adapters for rate throttling and concurrent request limiting, and modules include `limit`, `throttle`, `prefix`, `registry`, and `signer`. ([Docs.rs][1]) ([Docs.rs][1])

```rust id="limit-store-sketch"
use object_store::limit::LimitStore;

// constructor signature may vary by version; pattern:
// let limited = LimitStore::new(inner_store, max_concurrent_requests);
```

### Concurrency guidance

```text id="concurrency-guidance"
Cloud range reads:
  bound concurrency
  use vectored reads for multiple non-contiguous ranges
  coalesce adjacent ranges
  avoid one request per tiny range
  separate IO runtime from CPU decode for heavy Parquet workloads

Uploads:
  use multipart for large objects
  use fixed part sizes > 5 MiB
  limit parallel part uploads
  abort on failure
```

---

## 14.19 Best practices for Parquet/cloud range reads

### Direct `object_store` read

```rust id="cloud-range-read"
let meta = store.head(&path).await?;
let footer_hint = 128 * 1024_u64;
let start = meta.size.saturating_sub(footer_hint);

let footer_bytes = store.get_range(&path, start..meta.size).await?;
```

### Vectored ranges

```rust id="cloud-vectored-read"
let ranges = vec![
    0..4096,
    8_388_608..8_392_704,
    16_777_216..16_781_312,
];

let chunks = store.get_ranges(&path, &ranges).await?;
```

### Parquet integration

```rust id="parquet-object-reader-with-store"
use parquet::arrow::async_reader::store::ParquetObjectReader;
use parquet::arrow::async_reader::ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder;

let meta = store.head(&path).await?;

let reader = ParquetObjectReader::new(store.clone(), path.clone())
    .with_file_size(meta.size)
    .with_footer_size_hint(128 * 1024);

let stream = ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder::new(reader)
    .await?
    .with_batch_size(65_536)
    .build()?;
```

`get_ranges` is designed for structured-data access patterns needing multiple non-contiguous byte ranges, and Parquet’s `ParquetObjectReader` builds directly on `object_store` for cloud-native range reads; providing file size and footer hints reduces metadata/suffix-read overhead. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 14.20 Error handling

```rust id="error-patterns"
match store.head(&path).await {
    Ok(meta) => println!("size={}", meta.size),
    Err(Error::NotFound { .. }) => {
        // missing object
    }
    Err(Error::NotModified { .. }) => {
        // conditional GET not modified
    }
    Err(Error::Precondition { .. }) => {
        // conditional write/update failed
    }
    Err(e) => return Err(e),
}
```

```text id="error-guidance"
Handle explicitly:
  NotFound
  AlreadyExists
  NotModified
  Precondition
  NotImplemented
  Permission / Unauthorized style backend errors
  transport/retry exhaustion
```

The docs demonstrate `NotModified` for conditional fetch and `Precondition` for conditional update; `PutMode::Create` can return `AlreadyExists`, and `PutMode::Update` can return `Precondition` when the version does not match. ([Docs.rs][1]) ([Docs.rs][14])

---

## 14.21 Object-store registry pattern

```rust id="store-registry"
use std::collections::HashMap;
use url::Url;

pub struct StoreRegistry {
    stores: HashMap<String, Arc<dyn ObjectStore>>,
}

impl StoreRegistry {
    pub fn resolve(&self, url: &Url) -> object_store::Result<(Arc<dyn ObjectStore>, Path)> {
        let (boxed, path) = object_store::parse_url(url)?;
        Ok((Arc::from(boxed), path))
    }
}
```

The object_store crate includes a registry module for mapping object URLs to stores, and DataFusion uses object-store registries internally for path-based table access. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 14.22 PyArrow-to-Rust operational mapping

| PyArrow operation                        | Rust `object_store` pattern                                |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `FileSystem.from_uri("s3://bucket/key")` | `parse_url(&Url::parse(...))?`                             |
| `fs.get_file_info(path)`                 | `store.head(&Path::from(path)).await?`                     |
| recursive `FileSelector`                 | `store.list(Some(&prefix))`                                |
| `open_input_file(path).read_at(...)`     | `store.get_range(&path, range).await?`                     |
| `open_input_stream(path)`                | `store.get(&path).await?.into_stream()`                    |
| `open_output_stream(path)`               | `store.put(&path, payload).await?`                         |
| output stream for large object           | `store.put_multipart(&path).await?`                        |
| `copy_file(src, dest)`                   | `store.copy(&src, &dest).await?`                           |
| `move(src, dest)`                        | `store.rename(&src, &dest).await?`, but beware copy+delete |
| conditional metadata cache               | `get_opts(... if_none_match ...)`                          |
| atomic create                            | `put_opts(..., PutMode::Create.into())`                    |
| compare-and-swap update                  | `PutMode::Update(UpdateVersion { ... })`                   |

---

## 14.23 Deployment patterns

### Test layer

```rust id="test-layer"
pub fn test_store() -> Arc<dyn ObjectStore> {
    Arc::new(InMemory::new())
}
```

### Local integration layer

```rust id="local-integration-layer"
pub fn local_store(root: &str) -> object_store::Result<Arc<dyn ObjectStore>> {
    Ok(Arc::new(LocalFileSystem::new_with_prefix(root)?))
}
```

### Cloud layer

```rust id="cloud-layer"
pub fn s3_store(bucket: &str, region: &str) -> object_store::Result<Arc<dyn ObjectStore>> {
    let s3 = AmazonS3Builder::from_env()
        .with_bucket_name(bucket)
        .with_region(region)
        .build()?;
    Ok(Arc::new(s3))
}
```

### Runtime URL layer

```rust id="runtime-url-layer"
pub fn parse_store(url: &str) -> object_store::Result<(Arc<dyn ObjectStore>, Path)> {
    let url = url::Url::parse(url)
        .map_err(|e| object_store::Error::Generic {
            store: "url",
            source: Box::new(e),
        })?;

    let (store, path) = object_store::parse_url(&url)?;
    Ok((Arc::from(store), path))
}
```

---

## 14.24 Anti-pattern catalog

| Anti-pattern                                   | Failure mode                    | Correct pattern                          |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| use `std::path::PathBuf` in public storage API | local-only semantics leak       | `object_store::path::Path`               |
| temp object + rename as commit on S3           | non-atomic/copy+delete behavior | `PutMode::Create` / `PutMode::Update`    |
| read full object for Parquet footer            | unnecessary IO/memory           | `get_range` / `ParquetObjectReader`      |
| one request per tiny range                     | high latency/cost               | `get_ranges` / coalescing                |
| ignore ETag/version for catalog writes         | lost updates                    | conditional put                          |
| use multipart for small payloads               | extra requests                  | `put`                                    |
| forget multipart abort on failure              | orphaned parts/cost             | best-effort `abort()`                    |
| assume local FS behavior equals cloud behavior | portability bugs                | test with InMemory + real cloud/emulator |
| unbounded cloud request concurrency            | throttling/cost/failures        | `LimitStore` / bounded tasks             |
| log URLs with embedded secrets                 | credential leak                 | redact config                            |
| use filesystem adapters everywhere             | hidden object-store costs       | use native object APIs                   |

---

## 14.25 Golden test matrix

```rust id="object-store-golden-tests"
#[tokio::test]
async fn memory_put_get_range_delete() -> object_store::Result<()> {
    let store = InMemory::new();
    let path = Path::from("data/file.bin");

    store.put(&path, Bytes::from_static(b"hello world").into()).await?;

    let meta = store.head(&path).await?;
    assert_eq!(meta.size, 11);

    let bytes = store.get_range(&path, 0..5).await?;
    assert_eq!(&bytes[..], b"hello");

    store.delete(&path).await?;

    assert!(matches!(
        store.head(&path).await,
        Err(Error::NotFound { .. })
    ));

    Ok(())
}
```

Test categories:

```text id="object-store-test-categories"
Backends:
  InMemory
  LocalFileSystem
  S3/minio/localstack
  GCS emulator or integration
  Azure/azurite
  HTTP/WebDAV fixture

Operations:
  put/get/head/delete
  list prefix
  list_with_delimiter
  get_range
  get_ranges
  conditional get NotModified
  PutMode::Create AlreadyExists
  PutMode::Update Precondition
  multipart success
  multipart abort
  copy/copy_if_not_exists
  rename/rename_if_not_exists backend behavior

Cloud:
  retries
  concurrency limiting
  proxy/TLS config
  credential source resolution
  large-object streaming
  ParquetObjectReader range reads
```

---

## 14.26 Value case

```text id="object-store-value-case"
ObjectStore:
  value = one async storage API across memory/local/S3/GCS/Azure/HTTP.

ObjectStoreExt:
  value = ergonomic user operations while ObjectStore remains implementor contract.

InMemory:
  value = deterministic unit tests and cloud-free development.

LocalFileSystem:
  value = local integration testing and file-backed development.

S3/GCS/Azure builders:
  value = provider-native credentials/config while preserving common trait boundary.

parse_url / parse_url_opts:
  value = runtime-configurable stores from user/application URLs.

Atomic put:
  value = no partial-object visibility.

Conditional put:
  value = optimistic concurrency for metadata catalogs.

Range/vectored reads:
  value = efficient Parquet/IPC/footer/page access on cloud objects.

Multipart upload:
  value = large-object streaming with atomic final visibility.

Adapters/limits/throttles:
  value = operational safety under cloud rate/cost constraints.

Object-store-native API:
  value = correctness and performance over cloud storage without pretending it is POSIX.
```

Final agent rule:

```text id="object-store-final-rule"
Use object_store for PyArrow filesystem equivalents in Rust.
Model paths as object keys, not local files.
Use get_range/get_ranges for structured formats.
Use put for small atomic objects.
Use multipart for large streaming writes.
Use PutMode::Create/Update for commit protocols.
Avoid rename-based commits.
Configure credentials/TLS/retries at store construction.
Bound concurrency in cloud.
Test with InMemory, LocalFileSystem, and at least one real/emulated cloud backend before claiming portability.
```

# 15) DataFusion SQL and DataFrame API

Style target: dense, syntax-first, agent-ready technical reference; follows the uploaded advanced-reference style target. 

---

## 15.0 Mental model

```text id="df-mental-model"
SessionContext =
  query/session root
  table registry
  function registry
  object-store registry
  config/runtime holder
  SQL planner entrypoint
  DataFrame constructor entrypoint

DataFrame =
  lazy logical plan handle
  transformations build plan
  collect/show/execute_stream execute plan

LogicalPlan =
  relation-level plan DAG
  scan/projection/filter/aggregate/join/sort/limit/write/etc.

Expr =
  expression tree
  column refs, literals, arithmetic, boolean predicates, aggregate funcs, window funcs

RecordBatch output =
  Vec<RecordBatch> via collect()
  stream via execute_stream()
```

`SessionContext` is the main interface for executing queries in DataFusion; it creates DataFrames from files, registers data sources as SQL tables, registers custom sources, and executes SQL. `DataFrame` represents a logical set of rows and is lazy: transformation methods build a plan, while execution methods such as `collect`, `show`, and stream execution trigger computation. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

`read_avro` and `register_avro` are gated behind DataFusion’s `avro` crate feature. ([Docs.rs][1])

Pretty formatting utilities such as `pretty_format_batches` and `print_batches` are available only with the `prettyprint` feature. ([Docs.rs][2])

## 15.2 Imports

```rust id="df-imports"
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::{ArrayRef, Int32Array, RecordBatch, StringArray};
use arrow_schema::{DataType, Field, Schema, SchemaRef};

use datafusion::prelude::*;
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;
use datafusion::datasource::listing::{
    ListingOptions, ListingTable, ListingTableConfig, ListingTableUrl,
};
use datafusion::datasource::file_format::parquet::ParquetFormat;
use datafusion::datasource::memory::MemTable;
use datafusion_common::{DataFusionError, Result, ScalarValue};
use datafusion_expr::{col, lit, Expr, JoinType, TableProvider};
use futures::{StreamExt, TryStreamExt};
```

The `datafusion::prelude` re-exports common user-facing items including `DataFrame`, `SessionContext`, `SessionConfig`, `SQLOptions`, and read options for CSV, Parquet, JSON, and Avro. ([Docs.rs][3])

---

## 15.3 `SessionContext`

### Default context

```rust id="sessioncontext-default"
let ctx = SessionContext::new();
```

### Configured context

```rust id="sessioncontext-config"
use datafusion::execution::context::{SessionConfig, SessionContext};

let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .with_batch_size(64 * 1024)
    .set_bool("datafusion.execution.listing_table_factory_infer_partitions", true)
    .set_bool("datafusion.execution.listing_table_ignore_subdirectory", true);

let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config(config);
```

### Shared runtime / memory limits

```rust id="sessioncontext-runtime"
use datafusion::execution::runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let config = SessionConfig::new().with_batch_size(4 * 1024);

let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_memory_limit(1024 * 1024 * 1024, 0.80)
    .build_arc()
    .unwrap();

let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config_rt(config, runtime);
```

`SessionContext`, `SessionState`, and `TaskContext` split DataFusion state across user/session, planning, and execution layers. If multiple contexts need shared process-wide resource limits, configure them with the same `RuntimeEnv`; otherwise, each new context creates a new runtime environment. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Security-sensitive URL tables

```rust id="enable-url-table"
let ctx = SessionContext::new()
    .enable_url_table();
```

`enable_url_table()` permits SQL queries such as `SELECT * FROM 'my_file.parquet'`; the DataFusion docs mark this as security-sensitive because it enables direct file access through SQL. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 15.4 Registering file-backed tables

### CSV

```rust id="register-csv"
let ctx = SessionContext::new();

ctx.register_csv(
    "events_csv",
    "data/events.csv",
    CsvReadOptions::new(),
).await?;

let df = ctx.sql("SELECT * FROM events_csv LIMIT 10").await?;
```

### Parquet

```rust id="register-parquet"
ctx.register_parquet(
    "events",
    "s3://bucket/events/",
    ParquetReadOptions::default(),
).await?;
```

### JSON / NDJSON

```rust id="register-json"
ctx.register_json(
    "events_json",
    "data/events.ndjson",
    JsonReadOptions::default(),
).await?;
```

### Avro

```rust id="register-avro"
ctx.register_avro(
    "events_avro",
    "data/events.avro",
    AvroReadOptions::default(),
).await?;
```

`register_csv`, `register_json`, `register_parquet`, and `register_avro` register file-backed tables that can be referenced from SQL; Parquet and Avro availability depends on the relevant DataFusion crate features. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Arrow IPC file

```rust id="register-arrow"
ctx.register_arrow(
    "events_arrow",
    "data/events.arrow",
    ArrowReadOptions::default(),
).await?;
```

`register_arrow` registers an Arrow file as a SQL table; `read_arrow` creates a DataFrame for Arrow data sources. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 15.5 Reading files directly as `DataFrame`

### CSV single or multiple files

```rust id="read-csv"
let df = ctx
    .read_csv("tests/data/example.csv", CsvReadOptions::new())
    .await?;

let multi = ctx
    .read_csv(
        vec!["tests/data/example.csv", "tests/data/example.csv"],
        CsvReadOptions::new(),
    )
    .await?;
```

### Parquet

```rust id="read-parquet"
let df = ctx
    .read_parquet("s3://bucket/events/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
    .await?;
```

### JSON

```rust id="read-json"
let df = ctx
    .read_json("data/events.ndjson", JsonReadOptions::default())
    .await?;
```

### Avro

```rust id="read-avro"
let df = ctx
    .read_avro("data/events.avro", AvroReadOptions::default())
    .await?;
```

`read_csv`, `read_json`, `read_parquet`, `read_avro`, and `read_arrow` create lazy DataFrames for file data sources; the docs recommend `read_table` with `ListingTable` when more control over multiple files is needed. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 15.6 Registering memory and custom tables

### `register_batch`

```rust id="register-batch"
let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
    ("id", Arc::new(Int32Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef),
    ("name", Arc::new(StringArray::from(vec!["a", "b", "c"])) as ArrayRef),
])?;

ctx.register_batch("users", batch)?;
```

`register_batch` registers a single `RecordBatch` as a table under a name. ([Docs.rs][1])

### `read_batch` / `read_batches`

```rust id="read-batches"
let df_one = ctx.read_batch(batch)?;

let df_many = ctx.read_batches(vec![batch1, batch2, batch3])?;
```

`read_batch` creates a DataFrame from one `RecordBatch`; `read_batches` creates a DataFrame from a `Vec<RecordBatch>`. ([Docs.rs][1])

### `MemTable`

```rust id="memtable-register"
let schema = batch.schema();
let partitions = vec![vec![batch]];

let mem = MemTable::try_new(schema, partitions)?;
ctx.register_table("users_mem", Arc::new(mem))?;
```

DataFusion includes `MemTable` for in-memory `RecordBatch`es and `ListingTable` for one or more Parquet/JSON/CSV/Avro files in local or remote directories. ([Docs.rs][4])

### `register_table` for custom providers

```rust id="register-table"
let provider: Arc<dyn TableProvider> = Arc::new(mem);
ctx.register_table("custom_table", provider)?;
```

`register_table` registers any `TableProvider` so it can be referenced from SQL; `ctx.table("name").await?` retrieves a DataFrame for a registered table. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 15.7 `ListingTable`

### Manual Parquet listing table

```rust id="listing-table"
let table_path = ListingTableUrl::parse("s3://bucket/events/")?;

let file_format = ParquetFormat::new()
    .with_enable_pruning(true)
    .with_metadata_size_hint(Some(128 * 1024));

let listing_options = ListingOptions::new(Arc::new(file_format))
    .with_file_extension(".parquet")
    .with_table_partition_cols(vec![
        ("year".to_string(), DataType::Int32),
        ("month".to_string(), DataType::Int32),
    ])
    .with_collect_stat(true)
    .with_target_partitions(32);

let schema = listing_options
    .infer_schema(ctx.state().as_ref(), &table_path)
    .await?;

let config = ListingTableConfig::new(table_path)
    .with_listing_options(listing_options)
    .with_schema(schema);

let table = ListingTable::try_new(config)?;
ctx.register_table("events", Arc::new(table))?;
```

`ListingTable` reads one or more Parquet, JSON, CSV, or Avro files from local or remote directories and supports Hive-style partitioning, compression, remote object stores, file metadata caching, and more. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Direct registration helper

```rust id="register-listing-table"
ctx.register_listing_table(
    "events",
    "s3://bucket/events/",
    listing_options,
    Some(schema),
    None,
).await?;
```

`register_listing_table` registers a `ListingTable` assembled from object-store locations and may resolve schema asynchronously. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 15.8 Object store registration

```rust id="register-object-store"
use object_store::local::LocalFileSystem;
use object_store::ObjectStore;
use datafusion::prelude::SessionContext;
use url::Url;

let ctx = SessionContext::new();

let object_store_url = Url::parse("file://")?;
let object_store = LocalFileSystem::new();

ctx.register_object_store(&object_store_url, Arc::new(object_store));
```

`register_object_store` registers an `ObjectStore` for a URL prefix; the docs show using it to map the `file://` prefix to `LocalFileSystem`. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 15.9 SQL API

### Register table + SQL

```rust id="sql-basic"
let ctx = SessionContext::new();

ctx.register_csv(
    "example",
    "tests/data/example.csv",
    CsvReadOptions::new(),
).await?;

let results = ctx
    .sql("SELECT a, MIN(b) FROM example GROUP BY a LIMIT 100")
    .await?
    .collect()
    .await?;
```

### SQL with `DataFrame` follow-up

```rust id="sql-then-dataframe"
let df = ctx
    .sql("SELECT * FROM users")
    .await?
    .filter(col("bank_account").gt_eq(lit(8000)))?;

let results = df.collect().await?;
```

`SessionContext::sql` parses and plans SQL into a DataFrame; the official examples show registering CSV and then collecting SQL query output as `Vec<RecordBatch>`. ([Docs.rs][1])

### SQL options

```rust id="sql-with-options"
let df = ctx
    .sql_with_options(
        "SELECT * FROM events LIMIT 10",
        SQLOptions::new()
    )
    .await?;
```

Use `sql_with_options` when the application needs explicit SQL planning options; normal generated code should use `sql` unless DDL/DML/access restrictions are required. `SessionState` is the lower-level planning state and allows finer-grained query planning control such as disallowing DDL. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 15.10 DataFrame API: projection, filter, aggregate, sort, limit

### Projection

```rust id="df-select"
let df = ctx
    .read_csv("tests/data/example.csv", CsvReadOptions::new())
    .await?
    .select(vec![
        col("a"),
        (col("b") * col("c")).alias("b_times_c"),
    ])?;
```

`select` projects arbitrary expressions into a new DataFrame; `select_columns` filters to named columns, and `select_exprs` parses SQL expression strings when the `sql` feature is enabled. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Filtering

```rust id="df-filter"
let df = df.filter(
    col("amount").gt(lit(0_i64))
        .and(col("country").eq(lit("US")))
)?;
```

`filter` returns only rows where the predicate evaluates to `true`; rows where the predicate is `false` or `null` are filtered out. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Aggregation

```rust id="df-aggregate"
let df = df.aggregate(
    vec![col("country")],
    vec![
        count(col("user_id")).alias("n"),
        sum(col("amount")).alias("total_amount"),
        min(col("amount")).alias("min_amount"),
        max(col("amount")).alias("max_amount"),
    ],
)?;
```

`aggregate(group_expr, aggr_expr)` creates a new DataFrame that aggregates rows, optionally grouping by expressions. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Sort

```rust id="df-sort"
let df = df.sort(vec![
    col("total_amount").sort(false, false), // DESC, nulls last
    col("country").sort(true, true),        // ASC, nulls first
])?;
```

`sort` accepts sort expressions; any expression can be turned into a sort expression with `.sort(ascending, nulls_first)`. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Limit

```rust id="df-limit"
let df = df.limit(0, Some(100))?;
let df = df.limit(1_000, Some(10_000))?;
```

`limit(skip, fetch)` skips a number of rows and returns at most `fetch` rows. ([Docs.rs][5])

---

## 15.11 Joins

### Equi-join

```rust id="df-join"
let joined = left.join(
    right,
    JoinType::Inner,
    &["customer_id"],
    &["id"],
    None,
)?;
```

### Equi-join with additional filter

```rust id="df-join-filter"
let joined = left.join(
    right,
    JoinType::Left,
    &["customer_id"],
    &["id"],
    Some(col("amount").gt(lit(0_i64))),
)?;
```

### Expression join

```rust id="df-join-on"
let joined = left.join_on(
    right,
    JoinType::Inner,
    [
        col("left_key").eq(col("right_key")),
        col("tenant").eq(col("tenant2")),
    ],
)?;
```

`join` accepts explicit left/right column names plus an optional filter; `join_on` accepts expressions, and DataFusion automatically identifies and optimizes equality predicates. For outer joins, the optional `filter` on `join` is applied only to matched rows. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Join type quick map

```text id="join-types"
JoinType::Inner
JoinType::Left
JoinType::Right
JoinType::Full
JoinType::LeftSemi
JoinType::RightSemi
JoinType::LeftAnti
JoinType::RightAnti
```

---

## 15.12 Windows and unnest

### Window expressions

```rust id="df-window"
let df = df.window(vec![
    // Expr::WindowFunction values, often easier via SQL for complex windows
])?;
```

`window` adds results of one or more window-function expressions to the existing columns. ([Docs.rs][5])

### SQL window fallback

```rust id="sql-window"
let df = ctx.sql(r#"
    SELECT
      user_id,
      ts,
      amount,
      SUM(amount) OVER (
        PARTITION BY user_id
        ORDER BY ts
        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
      ) AS running_amount
    FROM events
"#).await?;
```

### Unnest list/struct columns

```rust id="df-unnest"
let df = ctx
    .read_json("tests/data/unnest.json", JsonReadOptions::default())
    .await?
    .unnest_columns(&["items", "payload"])?;
```

`unnest_columns` expands list/struct columns into rows and/or new columns, and the docs show nested struct fields flattening into dotted field names such as `d.e` and `d.f`. ([Docs.rs][5])

---

## 15.13 Set operations

```rust id="df-set-ops"
let union = df1.clone().union(df2.clone())?;
let union_distinct = df1.clone().union_distinct(df2.clone())?;

let by_name = df1.clone().union_by_name(df2.clone())?;
let by_name_distinct = df1.clone().union_by_name_distinct(df2.clone())?;

let intersection = df1.clone().intersect(df2.clone())?;
let intersection_distinct = df1.clone().intersect_distinct(df2.clone())?;

let except = df1.except(df2)?;
```

`union` and `union_distinct` require identical schemas by position; `union_by_name` and `union_by_name_distinct` align by column names and fill missing columns with null. Intersections and exceptions require matching schemas. ([Docs.rs][5])

---

## 15.14 Logical plans and expressions

### Inspect plan

```rust id="df-plan-inspect"
let plan = df.logical_plan();
println!("{plan:?}");

let explain = df.clone().explain(false, false)?;
explain.show().await?;
```

`logical_plan()` returns the unoptimized logical plan. `into_unoptimized_plan` and `into_optimized_plan` are mainly for testing because they lose the DataFrame’s attached `SessionState` snapshot; `explain` returns a DataFrame containing plan explanation and can optionally run the plan for metrics. ([Docs.rs][5])

### DataFusion plan model

```text id="plan-model"
LogicalPlan:
  schema-aware relational DAG
  independent of physical execution

Expr:
  schema-aware expression nodes inside logical plans
  can be simplified/re-written

ExecutionPlan:
  physical operator tree
  partitioned execution
  emits RecordBatch streams
```

DataFusion’s docs describe logical planning as producing `LogicalPlan` nodes and `Expr` expression trees, where logical plans are DAGs independent of physical execution and expressions can be simplified or rewritten. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Convert DataFrame into view

```rust id="df-into-view"
let view_provider = df.into_view();
ctx.register_table("my_view", view_provider)?;
```

`into_view` converts a DataFrame into a `TableProvider` that can be registered as a view, but it discards the DataFrame’s attached `SessionState` in favor of the state supplied during provider scanning. ([Docs.rs][5])

---

## 15.15 Collecting, streaming, and formatting

### Collect into memory

```rust id="df-collect"
let batches: Vec<RecordBatch> = df.collect().await?;
```

`collect()` executes the DataFrame and buffers all resulting `RecordBatch`es into memory; it triggers computation because DataFrame transformations are lazy. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Stream results

```rust id="df-execute-stream"
let mut stream = df.execute_stream().await?;

while let Some(batch) = stream.next().await {
    let batch = batch?;
    // process batch
}
```

`execute_stream()` executes the DataFrame and returns a single-partition stream without buffering all results; dropping the stream aborts query execution and releases resources. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Partitioned execution

```rust id="df-partitioned"
let partitions: Vec<Vec<RecordBatch>> = df.clone().collect_partitioned().await?;

let streams = df.execute_stream_partitioned().await?;
```

`collect_partitioned()` buffers results while preserving partitioning; `execute_stream_partitioned()` returns one stream per partition. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Show and string formatting

```rust id="df-show"
df.clone().show().await?;
df.clone().show_limit(10).await?;

let s = df.to_string().await?;
println!("{s}");
```

`show()` executes and prints all results to the console; `show_limit(n)` prints only the first `n` rows; `to_string()` executes and returns a formatted string representation. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Pretty formatting batches

```rust id="pretty-batches"
use datafusion::common::arrow::util::pretty::{
    pretty_format_batches,
    print_batches,
};

let batches = df.collect().await?;
let rendered = pretty_format_batches(&batches)?.to_string();

print_batches(&batches)?;
```

`pretty_format_batches` creates a visual representation of `RecordBatch`es, while `print_batches` prints them to stdout; both require the `prettyprint` feature. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 15.16 SQL/DataFrame mapping from PyArrow-style workflows

| PyArrow-style operation             | DataFusion DataFrame                                       |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `table.select(["a", "b"])`          | `df.select_columns(&["a", "b"])?`                          |
| `table.filter(mask_expr)`           | `df.filter(expr)?`                                         |
| `pc.field("a") > 5`                 | `col("a").gt(lit(5))`                                      |
| `table.append_column("x", expr)`    | `df.with_column("x", expr)?`                               |
| `table.drop(["x"])`                 | `df.drop_columns(&["x"])?`                                 |
| `group_by("k").aggregate(sum("v"))` | `df.aggregate(vec![col("k")], vec![sum(col("v"))])?`       |
| `join(left, right, keys=...)`       | `left.join(right, JoinType::Inner, &["k"], &["k"], None)?` |
| `sort_by([("x", "descending")])`    | `df.sort(vec![col("x").sort(false, false)])?`              |
| `head(10)`                          | `df.limit(0, Some(10))?`                                   |
| `to_batches()`                      | `df.execute_stream().await?`                               |
| `to_table()`                        | `df.collect().await?`                                      |
| `write_dataset(...)` simple export  | `df.write_parquet(...)` / `write_csv` / `write_json`       |
| SQL query over registered table     | `ctx.sql("SELECT ...").await?`                             |

---

## 15.17 End-to-end SQL pattern

```rust id="end-to-end-sql"
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion_common::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    ctx.register_parquet(
        "events",
        "s3://bucket/events/",
        ParquetReadOptions::default(),
    ).await?;

    let df = ctx.sql(r#"
        SELECT
          country,
          COUNT(*) AS n,
          SUM(amount) AS total_amount
        FROM events
        WHERE year = 2026
          AND month = 5
          AND event_type = 'click'
        GROUP BY country
        ORDER BY total_amount DESC
        LIMIT 100
    "#).await?;

    df.show_limit(100).await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

---

## 15.18 End-to-end DataFrame pattern

```rust id="end-to-end-dataframe"
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion_common::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let events = ctx
        .read_parquet("s3://bucket/events/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
        .await?;

    let users = ctx
        .read_parquet("s3://bucket/users/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
        .await?
        .select(vec![
            col("id").alias("user_id"),
            col("country"),
        ])?;

    let result = events
        .filter(
            col("year").eq(lit(2026_i32))
                .and(col("month").eq(lit(5_i32)))
                .and(col("event_type").eq(lit("click")))
        )?
        .join(
            users,
            JoinType::Inner,
            &["user_id"],
            &["user_id"],
            None,
        )?
        .select(vec![
            col("country"),
            col("amount"),
            (col("amount") + col("tax")).alias("gross"),
        ])?
        .aggregate(
            vec![col("country")],
            vec![
                count(lit(1)).alias("n"),
                sum(col("gross")).alias("gross_total"),
            ],
        )?
        .sort(vec![col("gross_total").sort(false, false)])?
        .limit(0, Some(100))?;

    let batches = result.collect().await?;
    datafusion::common::arrow::util::pretty::print_batches(&batches)?;

    Ok(())
}
```

---

## 15.19 Writing query results

### DataFrame writer APIs

```rust id="dataframe-write"
df.clone()
    .write_parquet(
        "s3://bucket/out/parquet/",
        DataFrameWriteOptions::new(),
        None,
    )
    .await?;

df.clone()
    .write_csv(
        "s3://bucket/out/csv/",
        DataFrameWriteOptions::new(),
        None,
    )
    .await?;

df.write_json(
    "s3://bucket/out/json/",
    DataFrameWriteOptions::new(),
    None,
).await?;
```

DataFrame examples show `write_parquet` executing a DataFrame and writing sorted output; `SessionContext` also exposes lower-level `write_csv`, `write_json`, and `write_parquet` methods that accept physical execution plans and write partitioned output. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Advisory

```text id="write-advisory"
Use DataFrame write_* for:
  query result export
  simple batch pipeline output
  DataFusion-native writes

Use custom object_store + parquet writer for:
  exact Hive write_dataset semantics
  custom existing-data behavior
  file naming policy
  partition-level delete/overwrite policy
  metadata manifest collection
```

---

## 15.20 Resource and security deployment rules

```text id="resource-security-rules"
SessionContext:
  one per logical user/session/workflow unless shared state is deliberate
  share RuntimeEnv when memory/disk limits must be process-global

collect():
  bounded only
  use max row/byte/time limits for user queries

execute_stream():
  default for services and large results

enable_url_table():
  security-sensitive
  avoid for multi-tenant SQL unless sandboxed

register_object_store():
  register stores explicitly for cloud prefixes
  keep credentials out of SQL text

SQL:
  use SQLOptions / SessionState controls when user SQL should not execute DDL/DML
```

`enable_url_table` is documented as security-sensitive, and DataFusion notes shared `RuntimeEnv` is required to enforce resource limits across multiple `SessionContext` instances in one process. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 15.21 API selection rules

```text id="api-selection-rules"
Use SQL API when:
  user-authored query
  complex joins/windows/CTEs/subqueries
  query text is persisted/audited
  SQL compatibility matters

Use DataFrame API when:
  programmatic query generation
  compile-time Rust construction
  safer expression composition
  embedding query builder in service

Use Arrow kernels when:
  one batch/array local transform
  no relational operator needed

Use ListingTable when:
  multi-file dataset
  Hive partitioning
  object-store scan
  metadata/pruning controls needed

Use MemTable/register_batch when:
  bounded in-memory data
  tests
  small dimension table
```

---

## 15.22 Error handling

```rust id="df-error-normalization"
fn normalize_datafusion_error(err: DataFusionError) -> tonic::Status {
    match err {
        DataFusionError::Plan(msg) => tonic::Status::invalid_argument(msg),
        DataFusionError::SchemaError(e, _) => tonic::Status::invalid_argument(e.to_string()),
        DataFusionError::Execution(msg) => tonic::Status::internal(msg),
        DataFusionError::ResourcesExhausted(msg) => tonic::Status::resource_exhausted(msg),
        other => tonic::Status::internal(other.to_string()),
    }
}
```

```text id="df-error-categories"
Plan:
  invalid SQL
  missing table/column/function
  incompatible types
  invalid logical expression

Schema:
  schema mismatch
  ambiguous columns
  missing fields

Execution:
  runtime operator failure
  IO failure
  UDF failure
  Parquet/CSV/JSON decode failure

ResourcesExhausted:
  memory/disk/limit failure
```

---

## 15.23 Anti-pattern catalog

| Anti-pattern                                        | Failure mode                     | Correct pattern                         |
| --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `collect()` on unbounded user query                 | memory blowup                    | `execute_stream()` + limits             |
| enable URL tables in multi-tenant SQL               | arbitrary file access risk       | explicit registered tables only         |
| manual Arrow kernels for joins/group-by             | reimplemented query engine       | DataFusion join/aggregate               |
| SQL strings for generated simple projections        | quoting/injection/parse overhead | typed `Expr` DataFrame API              |
| DataFrame API for arbitrary user SQL                | reimplements SQL parser          | `ctx.sql(...)`                          |
| `into_unoptimized_plan()` in production flow        | loses state snapshot             | inspect `logical_plan()` or `explain()` |
| `register_batch` for large data lake                | memory-resident table            | `ListingTable`                          |
| no shared `RuntimeEnv` across contexts              | limits not process-global        | `new_with_config_rt` shared runtime     |
| `show()` for large result                           | console/memory/runtime cost      | `show_limit()` or stream                |
| assuming `write_parquet` == PyArrow `write_dataset` | overwrite/partition mismatch     | custom dataset writer policy            |

---

## 15.24 Golden test matrix

```rust id="df-golden-test"
#[tokio::test]
async fn dataframe_filter_aggregate_collect() -> datafusion_common::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
        ("id", Arc::new(Int32Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef),
        ("grp", Arc::new(StringArray::from(vec!["a", "a", "b"])) as ArrayRef),
        ("v", Arc::new(Int32Array::from(vec![10, 20, 30])) as ArrayRef),
    ])?;

    ctx.register_batch("t", batch)?;

    let out = ctx.table("t").await?
        .filter(col("v").gt(lit(10_i32)))?
        .aggregate(
            vec![col("grp")],
            vec![sum(col("v")).alias("total")],
        )?
        .collect()
        .await?;

    assert!(!out.is_empty());
    Ok(())
}
```

Test categories:

```text id="df-test-matrix"
SessionContext:
  default context
  configured batch size
  shared RuntimeEnv memory limit
  register_object_store

Sources:
  read_csv
  register_csv + SQL
  read_parquet
  register_parquet + SQL
  read_json
  register_json + SQL
  read_avro/register_avro with avro feature
  register_batch
  read_batches
  ListingTable

DataFrame:
  select_columns
  select
  select_exprs
  filter null drops
  aggregate grouped/global
  join/join_on
  sort
  limit
  union/union_by_name
  unnest
  explain

Execution:
  collect bounded
  execute_stream
  collect_partitioned
  execute_stream_partitioned
  dropped stream cancellation

Formatting:
  show
  show_limit
  to_string
  pretty_format_batches

Security/resource:
```

## 15.25 Value case

```text id="df-value-case"
SessionContext:
  value = single query/session control plane.

Table registration:
  value = SQL-visible named datasets from files, memory, listing tables, or custom providers.

SQL API:
  value = user-facing declarative query surface.

DataFrame API:
  value = programmatic, composable, lazy query builder.

Expr:
  value = typed logical expression construction for projection/filter/aggregate/join/window plans.

LogicalPlan:
  value = inspectable/rewriteable query representation before physical execution.

collect():
  value = bounded eager Vec<RecordBatch> materialization.

execute_stream():
  value = service-scale streaming with cancellation and lower memory pressure.

show/to_string/prettyprint:
  value = CLI/test/debug result rendering.

ListingTable:
  value = PyArrow dataset-like multi-file scan over local/object-store paths.

MemTable/register_batch:
  value = in-memory test/dimension/result tables.

PyArrow mapping:
  value = replace filter/project/group-by/join/table workflows with lazy optimized DataFusion plans instead of manual Arrow kernels.
```

Final agent rule:

```text id="df-final-rule"
Use SessionContext as the root.
Register sources as tables for SQL.
Use DataFrame API for generated query plans.
Use SQL for user-authored query strings.
Use collect only for bounded results.
Use execute_stream for services and large data.
Use ListingTable for multi-file/object-store datasets.
Use MemTable/register_batch for bounded in-memory data.
Use Arrow kernels only inside local transforms or UDF implementations, not for relational query planning.
```

# 16) Query planning, optimization, and execution internals

Style target: dense, agent-ready technical reference consistent with the uploaded advanced-reference template. 

---

## 16.0 Pipeline invariant

```text
SQL string
  -> sqlparser AST Statement
  -> DataFusion LogicalPlan + Expr
  -> AnalyzerRule pass
  -> OptimizerRule pass
  -> PhysicalPlanner
  -> ExecutionPlan
  -> PhysicalOptimizerRule pass
  -> ExecutionPlan::execute(partition, TaskContext)
  -> SendableRecordBatchStream
  -> RecordBatch
```

DataFusion parses SQL strings with `sqlparser`, converts AST nodes to `LogicalPlan` / `Expr` via `SqlToRel`, applies analyzer rules and logical optimizer rules, converts the logical plan to an `ExecutionPlan`, applies physical optimizer rules such as sort/join selection, and executes by polling `SendableRecordBatchStream` values that yield Arrow `RecordBatch`es. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 16.1 Cargo profiles

### Application / service profile

```toml
[dependencies]
datafusion = "54.1.0"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros"] }
futures = "0.3"
object_store = { version = "0.13.2", features = ["aws", "gcp", "azure", "http"] }
```

### Planning / optimizer extension profile

```toml
[dependencies]
arrow-array = "58.4.0"
arrow-schema = "58.4.0"

datafusion = "54.1.0"
datafusion-common = "54.1.0"
datafusion-expr = "54.1.0"
datafusion-optimizer = "54.1.0"
datafusion-physical-plan = "54.1.0"
datafusion-physical-expr = "54.1.0"
datafusion-physical-optimizer = "54.1.0"

tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros"] }
futures = "0.3"
```

DataFusion is internally split into modular crates such as `datafusion_expr`, `datafusion_optimizer`, `datafusion_execution`, `datafusion_datasource`, and others, while the top-level `datafusion` crate re-exports the normal application surface. ([Docs.rs][2])

## 16.2 Imports

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::RecordBatch;

};

};
use datafusion::physical_optimizer::PhysicalOptimizerRule;
use datafusion_common::{DataFusionError, Result};
use datafusion_common::config::ConfigOptions;
use datafusion_expr::{col, lit, Expr, LogicalPlan, LogicalPlanBuilder};
```
