## 20.3 Imports

```rust id="so1id8"
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::{ArrayRef, Float64Array, Int64Array, RecordBatch, RecordBatchReader, StringArray};
use arrow_schema::{DataType, Field, Schema};

use adbc_core::{
    Connection, Database, Driver, Statement,
};
use adbc_core::options::{
    AdbcVersion, IngestMode, OptionConnection, OptionDatabase, OptionStatement, OptionValue,
};
use adbc_core::schemas::{
    InfoCode, ObjectDepth,
};

use adbc_datafusion::DataFusionDriver;

use adbc_driver_manager::ManagedDriver;
```

---

## 20.4 Core trait graph

```text id="1pbrhw"
Driver
  -> new_database(...)
  -> Database

Database
  -> new_connection(...)
  -> Connection

Connection
  -> new_statement()
  -> get_info()
  -> get_objects()
  -> get_table_schema()
  -> get_table_types()
  -> get_statistics()
  -> commit()
  -> rollback()
  -> read_partition()

Statement
  -> set_sql_query()
  -> set_substrait_plan()
  -> prepare()
  -> get_parameter_schema()
  -> bind(RecordBatch)
  -> bind_stream(Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send>)
  -> execute() -> Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send>
  -> execute_update() -> Option<i64>
  -> execute_schema() -> Schema
  -> execute_partitions()
  -> cancel()
```

The native Rust ADBC API uses associated types: `Driver::DatabaseType`, `Database::ConnectionType`, and `Connection::StatementType`. These traits are not object-safe/dyn-compatible, which is one reason the driver manager exposes managed wrapper types for dynamic FFI-loaded drivers. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Driver.html)) ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Database.html))

---

## 20.5 `Driver`

### Trait surface

```rust id="o3nrza"
pub trait Driver {
    type DatabaseType: Database;

    fn new_database(&mut self) -> adbc_core::Result<Self::DatabaseType>;

    fn new_database_with_opts(
        &mut self,
        opts: impl IntoIterator<Item = (OptionDatabase, OptionValue)>,
    ) -> adbc_core::Result<Self::DatabaseType>;
}
```

`Driver` is the top-level ADBC driver handle; it allocates and initializes `Database` handles, optionally with pre-initialization database options. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Driver.html))

### Native DataFusion driver

```rust id="f2ql0b"
let mut driver = DataFusionDriver {};
let db = driver.new_database()?;
let mut conn = db.new_connection()?;
```

The official Rust quickstart shows exactly this DataFusion-driver sequence: create `DataFusionDriver`, call `new_database`, then call `new_connection`. ([github.com](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/main/docs/source/rust/quickstart.rst?plain=true))

### With options

```rust id="d9rh5a"
let db = driver.new_database_with_opts([
    (OptionDatabase::Uri, "memory://".into()),
])?;
```

`OptionDatabase` has canonical variants such as `Uri`, `Username`, and `Password`, plus `Other(String)` for driver-specific keys; `OptionValue` supports string, bytes, integer, and double values. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/options/enum.OptionDatabase.html)) ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/options/enum.OptionValue.html))

---

## 20.6 `Database`

### Trait surface

```rust id="s7dtp9"
pub trait Database: adbc_core::options::Optionable<Option = OptionDatabase> {
    type ConnectionType: Connection;

    fn new_connection(&self) -> adbc_core::Result<Self::ConnectionType>;

    fn new_connection_with_opts(
        &self,
        opts: impl IntoIterator<Item = (OptionConnection, OptionValue)>,
    ) -> adbc_core::Result<Self::ConnectionType>;
}
```

A `Database` holds state shared by multiple connections, such as configuration, caches, or ownership of an in-memory database; docs state the database must remain alive as long as any connections exist. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Database.html))

### Usage

```rust id="fb6o0g"
let mut driver = DataFusionDriver {};
let db = driver.new_database()?;

let mut conn_a = db.new_connection()?;
let mut conn_b = db.new_connection()?;
```

### Deployment rule

```text id="vnx10i"
Database:
  long-lived per database/config/cache scope

Connection:
  shorter-lived per session / transaction / worker

Statement:
  shortest-lived per query / prepared statement / ingest operation
```

---

## 20.7 `Connection`

### Metadata and transaction surface

```rust id="uls38m"
let mut conn = db.new_connection()?;

// Database/driver info.
let info_reader = conn.get_info(None)?;

// Catalog hierarchy.
let objects_reader = conn.get_objects(
    ObjectDepth::All,
    None, // catalog
    None, // db_schema
    None, // table_name
    None, // table_type
    None, // column_name
)?;

// Table schema.
let schema = conn.get_table_schema(None, None, "my_table")?;

// Table types.
let table_types = conn.get_table_types()?;

// Statistics, if supported.
let stats = conn.get_statistics(None, None, Some("my_table"), true)?;
```

`Connection` exposes query/prepared-statement creation, cancellation, catalog metadata, table schemas/types, statistics, transactions, and partition reads. Catalog/info/statistics APIs return Arrow `RecordBatchReader`s, and connection docs state connections start in autocommit mode unless the autocommit connection option is set to false. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Connection.html))

### Transactions

```rust id="myw72e"
conn.set_option(OptionConnection::AutoCommit, "false".into())?;

let mut stmt = conn.new_statement()?;
stmt.set_sql_query("INSERT INTO t VALUES (1)")?;
stmt.execute_update()?;

conn.commit()?;
// or:
conn.rollback()?;
```

### Transaction rule

```text id="a5kcl3"
Autocommit true:
  each statement commits according to driver/database behavior

Autocommit false:
  caller owns commit/rollback
  driver may support isolation-level options
  always rollback/close on error paths
```

---

## 20.8 `Statement`

### Execute SQL and read Arrow result sets

```rust id="asx1sp"
let mut stmt = conn.new_statement()?;

stmt.set_sql_query("SELECT 1 AS one")?;

let mut reader = stmt.execute()?;

while let Some(batch) = reader.next() {
    let batch = batch?;
    println!("{batch:?}");
}
```

`Statement::execute` returns `Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send + 'static>`, invalidates any prior result sets, and is the normal query-result path. `set_sql_query` sets SQL text; `set_substrait_plan` sets a Substrait binary plan; `execute_update` returns an optional affected-row count for non-result-set statements. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Statement.html))

### Execute update

```rust id="w8frqh"
let mut stmt = conn.new_statement()?;

stmt.set_sql_query("CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT 1 AS one")?;

let affected: Option<i64> = stmt.execute_update()?;
```

### Schema-only execution

```rust id="u5wjeu"
let mut stmt = conn.new_statement()?;
stmt.set_sql_query("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = 1")?;

let result_schema = stmt.execute_schema()?;
```

`execute_schema` retrieves the schema of a query without executing it, and the docs note some drivers may require preparing first. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Statement.html))

### Prepared statements and parameter schema

```rust id="j5wp2l"
let mut stmt = conn.new_statement()?;

stmt.set_sql_query("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = ?")?;
stmt.prepare()?;

let param_schema = stmt.get_parameter_schema()?;

let params = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
    ("", Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![42])) as ArrayRef),
])?;

stmt.bind(params)?;

let reader = stmt.execute()?;
```

`prepare` turns a statement into a prepared statement; `get_parameter_schema` returns an Arrow schema describing parameter ordinal positions, names, and types where known, and should be called after prepare. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Statement.html))

---

## 20.9 Result sets as Arrow data

```text id="uiftcm"
ADBC SELECT result:
  Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send + 'static>

ADBC metadata result:
  Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send + 'static>

ADBC parameter binding:
  RecordBatch
  or Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send>

ADBC bulk ingest:
  bind Arrow data
  set target table / ingest options
  execute_update
```

ADBC result sets are Arrow streams: `Statement::execute`, connection metadata calls such as `get_info`/`get_objects`, and table-type/statistics APIs return `RecordBatchReader`s; `Statement::bind` and `bind_stream` accept Arrow `RecordBatch` data for bulk inserts or prepared-statement parameters. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Connection.html)) ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Statement.html))

### Bounded collection

```rust id="j78e4m"
fn collect_bounded(
    mut reader: Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send + 'static>,
    max_rows: usize,
) -> adbc_core::Result<Vec<RecordBatch>> {
    let mut rows = 0usize;
    let mut out = Vec::new();

    while let Some(batch) = reader.next() {
        let batch = batch?;
        rows += batch.num_rows();

        if rows > max_rows {
            return Err(adbc_core::error::Error::with_message_and_status(
                "row limit exceeded",
                adbc_core::error::Status::InvalidArguments,
            ));
        }

        out.push(batch);
    }

    Ok(out)
}
```

### Streaming rule

```text id="gc5p55"
Default:
  consume RecordBatchReader incrementally

Only collect when:
  result is bounded
  tests
  CLI preview
  downstream API requires Vec<RecordBatch>
```

---

## 20.10 Bulk ingestion

### Driver-manager example shape

```rust id="lct2lm"
let columns: Vec<ArrayRef> = vec![
    Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3, 4])),
    Arc::new(Float64Array::from(vec![1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0])),
    Arc::new(StringArray::from(vec!["a", "b", "c", "d"])),
];

let schema = Schema::new(vec![
    Field::new("a", DataType::Int64, true),
    Field::new("b", DataType::Float64, true),
    Field::new("c", DataType::Utf8, true),
]);

let input = RecordBatch::try_new(Arc::new(schema), columns)?;

let mut stmt = conn.new_statement()?;

stmt.set_option(OptionStatement::TargetTable, "my_table".into())?;
stmt.bind(input)?;
stmt.execute_update()?;
```

The driver-manager crate example shows ingesting Arrow data by setting the target table on a statement, binding a `RecordBatch`, and calling `execute_update`, then querying the table back as Arrow batches. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_driver_manager/latest/adbc_driver_manager/))

### Ingest options

```rust id="b2fvx6"
stmt.set_option(OptionStatement::TargetTable, "events".into())?;
stmt.set_option(OptionStatement::IngestMode, IngestMode::CreateAppend.into())?;
stmt.bind_stream(reader)?;
stmt.execute_update()?;
```

### Ingestion advisory

```text id="ykng12"
Do:
  use bind_stream for large Arrow inputs
  configure target table explicitly
  configure ingest mode explicitly
  chunk RecordBatch sizes deliberately
  validate schema before ingest

Do not:
  convert Arrow batches to rows unless the driver forces it
  collect huge inputs before bind_stream
  assume every driver supports bulk ingestion
```

The ADBC driver status page tracks bulk-ingestion support separately by driver, so agents must treat ingestion capability as driver-specific rather than universal. ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/main/driver/status.html))

---

## 20.11 Partitioned results

```rust id="fuegqm"
let mut stmt = conn.new_statement()?;
stmt.set_sql_query("SELECT * FROM huge_table")?;

let partitioned = stmt.execute_partitions()?;

// Partition payloads are opaque bytes.
for partition in partitioned.partitions {
    let reader = conn.read_partition(partition)?;
    for batch in reader {
        let batch = batch?;
        // worker-local processing
    }
}
```

`Statement::execute_partitions` returns a partitioned result set, and `Connection::read_partition` retrieves a partition by opaque bytes. ADBC uses opaque partition handles so drivers can expose distributed result sets without forcing a uniform partition representation. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Statement.html)) ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Connection.html))

### Partitioning rule

```text id="u8w3hr"
Use execute_partitions when:
  driver supports distributed result sets
  workers can independently fetch partitions
  scheduler wants partition handles

Do not:
  deserialize opaque partition bytes unless driver-specific docs say how
  assume partitions are ordered
  assume all drivers support partitioned results
```

---

## 20.12 Native Rust drivers versus driver manager

### Native Rust driver

```text id="jvf7nm"
Native Rust:
  adbc_core traits implemented directly
  no C FFI
  type-safe associated-type API
  usually fastest/safest Rust path
  compile-time driver dependency
```

### Driver manager

```text id="v52f58"
Driver manager:
  dynamically loads C-compatible ADBC drivers
  supports drivers not written in Rust
  runtime driver selection
  FFI boundary
  managed wrapper types serialize operations internally
```

`adbc_driver_manager` loads ADBC drivers either statically via `ManagedDriver::load_static` or dynamically with `load_dynamic_from_name` / `load_dynamic_from_filename`, using the driver’s `AdbcDriverInit`-style entrypoint. Managed driver/database/connection/statement types are cheaply cloneable and can be used across threads, but operations are serialized internally. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_driver_manager/latest/adbc_driver_manager/))

### Native DataFusion example

```rust id="nhfbc4"
let mut driver = adbc_datafusion::DataFusionDriver {};
let db = driver.new_database()?;
let mut conn = db.new_connection()?;

let mut stmt = conn.new_statement()?;
stmt.set_sql_query("SELECT 1")?;

let reader = stmt.execute()?;
for batch in reader {
    println!("{:?}", batch?);
}
```

### Driver-manager SQLite example

```rust id="p3e8zr"
let mut driver = ManagedDriver::load_dynamic_from_name(
    "adbc_driver_sqlite",
    None,
    AdbcVersion::V100,
)?;

let db = driver.new_database_with_opts([
    (OptionDatabase::Uri, ":memory:".into()),
])?;

let mut conn = db.new_connection()?;
```

### Driver-manager filename example

```rust id="iysgsx"
let mut driver = ManagedDriver::load_dynamic_from_filename(
    "/opt/adbc/libadbc_driver_sqlite.so",
    None,
    AdbcVersion::default(),
)?;

let db = driver.new_database()?;
let mut conn = db.new_connection()?;
```

The Rust driver-manager documentation shows loading a dynamic driver by filename and creating database/connection handles through the same ADBC trait flow. ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/main/rust/driver_manager.html))

---

## 20.13 DataFusion ADBC driver

```rust id="f7h605"
use adbc_core::{Connection, Database, Driver, Statement};

let mut driver = adbc_datafusion::DataFusionDriver {};
let db = driver.new_database()?;
let mut conn = db.new_connection()?;

let mut stmt = conn.new_statement()?;
stmt.set_sql_query("SELECT 1 AS one")?;

let reader = stmt.execute()?;
for batch in reader {
    let batch = batch?;
    println!("{batch:?}");
}
```

`adbc_datafusion` exposes structs such as `DataFusionDriver`, `DataFusionDatabase`, `DataFusionConnection`, `DataFusionStatement`, and a `Runtime` enum; its current crate metadata shows dependencies on DataFusion `53.x`, Arrow `58.x`, and `datafusion-substrait`, and current ADBC driver-status docs mark the Rust DataFusion driver as experimental. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_datafusion/latest/adbc_datafusion/)) ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/main/driver/status.html))

### DataFusion driver deployment role

```text id="h2w371"
Use adbc_datafusion when:
  you want ADBC API compatibility around an embedded DataFusion engine
  the client code should be database-generic over ADBC
  you need SQL and Substrait entrypoints through ADBC
  tests need a local Arrow-native database backend

Prefer native DataFusion API when:
  you need direct SessionContext control
  you need custom TableProvider/catalog/UDF registration
  you need DataFrame API
  you need optimizer/runtime configuration
```

### Substrait plan path

```rust id="i08sfo"
let mut stmt = conn.new_statement()?;

let substrait_bytes: Vec<u8> = build_or_load_substrait_plan();
stmt.set_substrait_plan(substrait_bytes)?;

let reader = stmt.execute()?;
```

`Statement::set_substrait_plan` sets a Substrait binary plan to execute, mirroring ADBC’s support for SQL and Substrait query execution. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Statement.html))

---

## 20.14 Flight SQL driver through driver manager

### Dynamic load

```rust id="j2vdj4"
let mut driver = ManagedDriver::load_dynamic_from_name(
    "adbc_driver_flightsql",
    None,
    AdbcVersion::V100,
)?;

let db = driver.new_database_with_opts([
    (OptionDatabase::Uri, "grpc://localhost:8080".into()),
])?;

let mut conn = db.new_connection()?;
```

The Flight SQL ADBC driver provides access to databases implementing Arrow Flight SQL endpoints, is implemented in Go with stable status, and can be used from Rust via the driver manager. The Flight SQL docs specify `uri` as the database construction option and list authentication, TLS, custom headers, OAuth, sessions, distributed result sets, and timeout options. ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/main/driver/flight_sql.html))

### Auth and TLS options

```rust id="n3jt9o"
let db = driver.new_database_with_opts([
    (OptionDatabase::Uri, "grpc+tls://flight.example.com:443".into()),

    (
        OptionDatabase::Other("adbc.flight.sql.authorization_header".to_string()),
        "Bearer <token>".into(),
    ),

    (
        OptionDatabase::Other("adbc.flight.sql.client_option.tls_root_certs".to_string()),
        std::fs::read_to_string("ca.pem")?.into(),
    ),

    (
        OptionDatabase::Other("adbc.flight.sql.client_option.with_max_msg_size".to_string()),
        "16777216".into(),
    ),
])?;
```

`OptionDatabase::Other(String)` is the Rust API path for driver-specific option keys. Flight SQL driver docs list `adbc.flight.sql.authorization_header`, TLS root certificates, TLS hostname override, mTLS cert/key options, custom call headers, OAuth options, cookie middleware, and max gRPC message size. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/options/enum.OptionDatabase.html)) ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/main/driver/flight_sql.html))

### Timeout options

```rust id="v0cwc1"
conn.set_option(
    OptionConnection::Other("adbc.flight.sql.rpc.timeout_seconds.fetch".to_string()),
    "30.0".into(),
)?;
```

Flight SQL driver docs state that timeouts are not used by default and recommend setting them to avoid unexpectedly stuck RPC calls. ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/main/driver/flight_sql.html))

### Flight SQL driver caveats

```text id="w3ni6v"
Current Flight SQL ADBC driver:
  stable Go implementation
  usable from Rust through driver manager
  no dedicated Flight SQL bulk-ingest API
  fetches returned FlightEndpoints in unspecified order
  supports ADBC partitioned result sets by serializing FlightInfo per partition
```

Flight SQL driver docs explicitly state it currently does not implement bulk ingestion because Flight SQL has no dedicated bulk-ingestion API, and that distributed result partitions are fetched in unspecified order unless application-level ordering is imposed. ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/main/driver/flight_sql.html))

---

## 20.15 Catalog and metadata APIs

### Database / driver info

```rust id="mrmvyb"
let info = conn.get_info(None)?;

for batch in info {
    let batch = batch?;
    println!("{batch:?}");
}
```

`Connection::get_info(None)` retrieves all available database/driver metadata as an Arrow dataset with fields such as `info_name` and `info_value`, where `info_value` is a dense union containing possible string, boolean, integer, bitmask, list, and map values. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Connection.html))

### Object hierarchy

```rust id="h57bwj"
let objects = conn.get_objects(
    ObjectDepth::Columns,
    None,          // catalog
    Some("public"),
    Some("orders"),
    None,          // table_type filter
    None,          // column_name filter
)?;
```

`get_objects` returns a hierarchical view of catalogs, database schemas, tables, and columns, with filters for catalog, schema, table name, table types, and column name. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Connection.html))

### Table schema and table types

```rust id="p00mx0"
let schema = conn.get_table_schema(None, Some("public"), "orders")?;
let table_types = conn.get_table_types()?;
```

### Statistics

```rust id="h5a6gv"
let stat_names = conn.get_statistic_names()?;

let stats = conn.get_statistics(
    None,              // catalog
    Some("public"),    // db_schema
    Some("orders"),    // table_name
    true,              // approximate
)?;
```

ADBC exposes statistics APIs to support federation/planning scenarios, but support is driver-specific and tracked in driver-status documentation. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/adbc_core/latest/adbc_core/sync/trait.Connection.html)) ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/main/driver/status.html))

---

## 20.16 Error handling

### Error model

```text id="fr4xml"
ADBC errors:
  adbc_core::error::Error
  status code
  message
  optional driver-specific metadata depending on driver/binding

Common status buckets:
  invalid arguments
  not implemented
  not found
  internal
  IO / transport / authentication driver-specific errors
```

### Boundary wrapper

```rust id="kzyy7a"
fn normalize_adbc_error(err: adbc_core::error::Error) -> anyhow::Error {
    anyhow::anyhow!("ADBC error: {err}")
}
```

### Service translation

```rust id="x5uvdq"
fn adbc_to_status(err: adbc_core::error::Error) -> tonic::Status {
    use adbc_core::error::Status;

    match err.status {
        Status::InvalidArguments => tonic::Status::invalid_argument(err.to_string()),
        Status::NotImplemented => tonic::Status::unimplemented(err.to_string()),
        Status::NotFound => tonic::Status::not_found(err.to_string()),
        _ => tonic::Status::internal(err.to_string()),
    }
}
```

Agent rules:

```text id="b1su59"
Do:
  preserve ADBC status in logs
  include driver name/version in diagnostics
  include SQL hash/query id, not always raw SQL
  distinguish driver unsupported from user invalid input

Do not:
  stringify and discard status
  leak passwords/auth headers in option dumps
  assume every driver uses identical error metadata
```

---

## 20.17 ADBC versus DataFusion versus direct database crates

| Requirement                                        | Prefer                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| database-generic SQL client returning Arrow        | ADBC                                   |
| runtime-selectable drivers                         | ADBC driver manager                    |
| Flight SQL endpoint access through standard DB API | ADBC Flight SQL driver                 |
| embedded analytical query engine in Rust           | DataFusion native API                  |
| custom optimizer/TableProvider/UDF/DataFrame work  | DataFusion native API                  |
| low-level PostgreSQL-specific features             | direct `tokio-postgres` / vendor crate |
| low-level SQLite-specific embedded features        | direct `rusqlite`                      |
| transactional OLTP with row-level operations       | direct DB crate or mature driver       |
| Arrow-native bulk result transfer                  | ADBC / Flight SQL / DataFusion         |
| Python/R/Ruby/C++ interop with same driver         | ADBC driver manager-compatible driver  |
| async Rust-first app with rich driver-specific API | direct async database crate            |
| Substrait plan execution through common API        | ADBC if driver supports it             |

ADBC’s value is the common Arrow-native database API and driver ecosystem; DataFusion’s value is being an embeddable query engine with optimizer/runtime customization; direct database crates are still appropriate when you need driver-specific protocol features, transaction controls, connection pools, or async APIs not surfaced through ADBC. ADBC’s own introduction frames it as a vendor-neutral API where applications receive Arrow data and avoid per-database Arrow conversion glue. ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/blog/2023/01/05/introducing-arrow-adbc/))

---

## 20.18 Deployment patterns

### Pattern A — local embedded analytical database through ADBC

```rust id="ejf7ek"
let mut driver = DataFusionDriver {};
let db = driver.new_database()?;
let mut conn = db.new_connection()?;

let mut stmt = conn.new_statement()?;
stmt.set_sql_query("SELECT 1 AS one")?;

let reader = stmt.execute()?;
```

Use for tests, adapter conformance, or database-generic code where DataFusion is the backend.

### Pattern B — dynamic database driver loading

```rust id="mw35qm"
let mut driver = ManagedDriver::load_dynamic_from_name(
    "adbc_driver_postgresql",
    None,
    AdbcVersion::V100,
)?;

let db = driver.new_database_with_opts([
    (OptionDatabase::Uri, "postgresql://localhost:5432/db".into()),
    (OptionDatabase::Username, "user".into()),
    (OptionDatabase::Password, std::env::var("DB_PASSWORD")?.into()),
])?;

let mut conn = db.new_connection()?;
```

Use when the database vendor driver should be installed/deployed independently from the Rust application.

### Pattern C — Flight SQL database connectivity

```rust id="a17nyt"
let mut driver = ManagedDriver::load_dynamic_from_name(
    "adbc_driver_flightsql",
    None,
    AdbcVersion::V100,
)?;

let db = driver.new_database_with_opts([
    (OptionDatabase::Uri, "grpc+tls://warehouse.example.com:443".into()),
    (
        OptionDatabase::Other("adbc.flight.sql.authorization_header".to_string()),
        format!("Bearer {}", std::env::var("FLIGHTSQL_TOKEN")?).into(),
    ),
])?;

let mut conn = db.new_connection()?;
```

Use when the backend speaks Flight SQL and you want the standard ADBC client abstraction rather than raw `arrow-flight` calls.

### Pattern D — ADBC result to DataFusion `MemTable`

```rust id="u8ywc5"
let mut stmt = conn.new_statement()?;
stmt.set_sql_query("SELECT * FROM remote_table")?;

let reader = stmt.execute()?;
let schema = reader.schema();
let batches: Vec<RecordBatch> = reader.collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;

let mem = datafusion::datasource::memory::MemTable::try_new(
    schema,
    vec![batches],
)?;

ctx.register_table("remote_snapshot", Arc::new(mem))?;
```

Use only for bounded remote results; for large federation, implement a custom `TableProvider` that consumes ADBC result streams incrementally.

---

## 20.19 Security and credentials

```text id="mqddtz"
DO:
  source credentials from secret manager / env / profile
  use TLS for network drivers
  set Flight SQL RPC timeouts
  set max message sizes where needed
  avoid logging OptionDatabase::Password
  avoid logging authorization headers
  enforce tenant/catalog authorization above ADBC if driver is generic

DON'T:
  hard-code connection strings with passwords
  put bearer tokens in SQL text
  use tls_skip_verify outside local testing
  assume all driver-manager-loaded drivers have identical credential semantics
```

Flight SQL driver docs list username/password, authorization header, OAuth flows, mTLS, TLS root certificates, hostname override, and TLS skip-verify options; they also state timeouts are off by default and should be set to avoid stuck RPCs. ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/main/driver/flight_sql.html))

---

## 20.20 Performance rules

```text id="n47pwi"
Do:
  stream RecordBatchReader results
  use bind_stream for bulk Arrow inputs
  use execute_schema when only schema is needed
  use execute_partitions where driver supports distributed fetch
  push filters/projection into SQL/Substrait
  avoid row-by-row extraction
  align Arrow crate versions
  keep native Rust drivers when available for low-overhead Rust apps

Do not:
  collect unbounded result sets
  convert Arrow to rows unless required by caller
  assume partition order
  assume every driver supports statistics/ingest/prepared statements
  use driver manager when a stable native Rust driver with needed features exists
```

---

## 20.21 Anti-pattern catalog

| Anti-pattern                                                          | Failure mode                        | Correct pattern                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| treating ADBC as a row API                                            | copies and lost Arrow benefit       | consume `RecordBatchReader`                |
| collecting huge `execute()` result                                    | memory blowup                       | stream batches                             |
| assuming every driver supports bulk ingest                            | runtime unsupported errors          | check driver status / feature docs         |
| using direct `DataFusionDriver` when custom DataFusion setup required | lost `SessionContext` control       | native DataFusion API                      |
| loading FFI drivers without deployment tests                          | missing shared library / entrypoint | driver-manager smoke tests                 |
| logging options wholesale                                             | credential leak                     | redact `Password`, auth headers, tokens    |
| assuming Flight SQL result partitions are ordered                     | wrong output ordering               | explicit SQL `ORDER BY` and ordering logic |
| using `tls_skip_verify` in production                                 | MITM risk                           | root cert / mTLS config                    |
| ignoring autocommit state                                             | transactional surprises             | set and test transaction policy            |
| mixing Arrow major versions                                           | Rust type mismatch                  | `cargo tree -d`, align versions            |

---

```text id="nepo8k"
Core traits:
```

## 20.23 Value case

```text id="iykzb5"
ADBC:
  value = Arrow-native vendor-neutral database access.

adbc_core:
  value = Rust trait contract for Driver / Database / Connection / Statement.

Driver:
  value = database-handle factory and driver configuration entrypoint.

Database:
  value = shared database configuration/cache/lifetime root.

Connection:
  value = session/transaction/catalog/query context.

Statement:
  value = SQL/Substrait/prepared/bind/execute container.

RecordBatchReader results:
  value = streaming Arrow output with no row conversion layer.

bind / bind_stream:
  value = Arrow-native parameters and bulk ingestion.

Driver manager:
  value = runtime loading of non-Rust or C-compatible ADBC drivers.

DataFusion driver:
  value = ADBC-compliant facade over an embedded Rust analytical engine.

Flight SQL driver:
  value = database connectivity to remote Flight SQL services through ADBC.

Direct database crates:
  value = driver-specific low-level features and async/control surfaces outside ADBC.
```

Final agent rule:

```text id="i9qgko"
Use ADBC when the API contract should be database-generic and Arrow-native.
Use adbc_datafusion when DataFusion should look like a database driver.
Use adbc_driver_manager when loading vendor/shared-library drivers at runtime.
Use Flight SQL driver for standard remote Arrow SQL services.
Use native DataFusion APIs when query-engine customization matters.
Use direct database crates when driver-specific protocol, OLTP, pooling, or async control matters more than Arrow-native portability.
Stream `RecordBatchReader` results by default.
```


# 21) Python interop: PyArrow, PyCapsule, PyO3, and zero-copy extension modules

Style target: dense, syntax-first, agent-ready technical reference; aligned with the uploaded advanced-reference format. 

---

## 21.0 Mental model

```text id="mt5r32"
Rust Arrow <-> Python Arrow interop surfaces:

1. Arrow C Data Interface
   in-process ABI for ArrowSchema + ArrowArray
   array / record-batch exchange
   zero-copy by design
   not storage, not IPC, not cross-process transport

2. Arrow C Stream Interface
   in-process ABI for ArrowArrayStream
   stream / table / chunked data exchange
   batch-at-a-time pull model

3. Arrow PyCapsule Interface
   Python protocol around C Data / C Stream / C Device structs
   __arrow_c_schema__
   __arrow_c_array__
   __arrow_c_stream__
   __arrow_c_device_array__
   __arrow_c_device_stream__

4. arrow_pyarrow
   PyArrow-specific Rust bridge in arrow-rs
   wrapper: PyArrowType<T>
   target: pyarrow objects

5. pyo3-arrow
   generic Python Arrow ecosystem bridge
   wrappers: PyArray, PyRecordBatch, PyRecordBatchReader, PyTable
   exports to arro3 / pyarrow / nanoarrow
   accepts protocol-compatible Python objects

6. maturin + PyO3
   Rust cdylib -> importable Python extension wheel/module
```

The Arrow C Data Interface exposes a small ABI-stable C interface designed for zero-copy sharing of Arrow data between independent runtimes in the same process, while Arrow IPC remains the cross-process/storage format. The PyCapsule Interface standardizes Python methods and capsule names for Arrow C Data, C Stream, and C Device structs so Python libraries can exchange Arrow data without hardcoding PyArrow-specific APIs. ([Apache Arrow][1])

---

## 21.1 Cargo profiles

### `pyo3-arrow`: generic Python Arrow ecosystem

```toml id="wfuust"
[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib"]

[dependencies]
pyo3 = { version = "0.28", features = ["extension-module"] }

pyo3-arrow = "0.17.0"

arrow-array = "58.4.0"
arrow-schema = "58.4.0"
arrow-select = "58.4.0"
arrow-cast = "58.4.0"
```

`pyo3-arrow 0.17.0` is documented as a lightweight PyO3 integration layer for zero-copy FFI conversions between Python Arrow objects and Rust `arrow` objects through the Arrow PyCapsule Interface; it currently depends on PyO3 `0.28` and Arrow Rust `58` crates. ([Docs.rs][2])

### `arrow_pyarrow`: PyArrow-specific bridge

```toml id="bnlkpo"
[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib"]

[dependencies]
pyo3 = { version = "0.28", features = ["extension-module"] }
arrow = { version = "58.4.0", features = ["pyarrow"] }
```

`arrow_pyarrow` is the Arrow Rust crate for passing objects to and from PyArrow using Arrow’s C Data Interface and PyO3; it maps PyArrow `DataType`, `Field`, `Schema`, `Array`, `RecordBatch`, `RecordBatchReader`, and `Table` to corresponding Arrow Rust types or wrappers. ([Apache Arrow][3])

### Mixed Rust/Python package profile

```toml id="ic400j"
[build-system]
requires = ["maturin>=1.0,<2.0"]
build-backend = "maturin"

[project]
name = "my-arrow-ext"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = [
  "pyarrow>=15",
  "arro3-core>=0.8",
]

[tool.maturin]
bindings = "pyo3"
module-name = "my_arrow_ext._native"
python-source = "python"
strip = true
```

Maturin supports mixed Rust/Python projects, `python-source`, `module-name`, PEP 621 metadata in `pyproject.toml`, and requires the Rust `#[pymodule]` name to match the final module name segment, such as `_native` for `my_arrow_ext._native`. ([maturin.rs][4])

```rust id="f1e8x4"
use std::sync::Arc;

    StringArray,
};
use arrow_schema::{ArrowError, DataType, Field, FieldRef, Schema, SchemaRef};

use arrow_select::take::take;

use pyo3_arrow::{
    PyArray, PyRecordBatch, PyRecordBatchReader, PyTable,
    error::PyArrowResult,
```

## 21.3 Arrow C Data Interface

```text id="8x41d0"
Arrow C Data Interface structs:
  ArrowSchema
    format
    name
    metadata
    flags
    children
    dictionary
    release callback
    private_data

  ArrowArray
    length
    null_count
    offset
    buffers
    children
    dictionary
    release callback
    private_data
```

Use case:

```text id="aq90ej"
Use C Data Interface for:
  same-process Rust <-> Python Arrow array / record-batch exchange
  zero-copy protocol boundary
  language/runtime-neutral Arrow memory handoff

Do not use C Data Interface for:
  files
  sockets
  process boundaries
  persistence
  compression
  remote transport
```

The Arrow C Data Interface explicitly lists ABI stability, zero-copy sharing, and avoiding a separate marshalling layer as goals; it also says cross-process transport and storage persistence are non-goals, where IPC or Flight are the correct layers. ([Apache Arrow][1])

---

## 21.4 Arrow C Stream Interface

```text id="3v0jd3"
Arrow C Stream Interface:
  ArrowArrayStream
    get_schema
    get_next
    get_last_error
    release
    private_data

Semantic shape:
  stream schema once
  pull next ArrowArray / RecordBatch until end
  consumer owns stream after import
```

Rust-facing use:

```text id="e62ar5"
Python object with __arrow_c_stream__:
  pyarrow.Table
  pyarrow.RecordBatchReader
  arro3.Table
  Polars DataFrame / Series where supported
  pandas DataFrame where supported
  DuckDB relation where supported

Rust import target:
  Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send>
  ArrowArrayStreamReader
  PyRecordBatchReader
```

The PyCapsule Interface defines `__arrow_c_stream__(requested_schema=None)` for tables, dataframes, and streams and requires it to return a capsule named `arrow_array_stream`; schema requests are best-effort representation requests, not arbitrary transformations. ([Apache Arrow][5])

---

## 21.5 Arrow PyCapsule Interface

### Protocol names

```python id="pycapsule-python-protocols"
class ArrowSchemaExportable:
    def __arrow_c_schema__(self) -> object: ...

class ArrowArrayExportable:
    def __arrow_c_array__(self, requested_schema: object | None = None) -> tuple[object, object]: ...

class ArrowStreamExportable:
    def __arrow_c_stream__(self, requested_schema: object | None = None) -> object: ...
```

### Capsule names

```text id="yzti77"
ArrowSchema            -> "arrow_schema"
ArrowArray             -> "arrow_array"
ArrowArrayStream       -> "arrow_array_stream"
ArrowDeviceArray       -> "arrow_device_array"
ArrowDeviceArrayStream -> "arrow_device_array_stream"
```

The PyCapsule standard requires specific names so consumers can verify capsule contents; capsules should carry destructors that call the underlying Arrow release callback if the consumer never takes ownership, and capsules can only be consumed once. ([Apache Arrow][5])

### Device support

```text id="hfh9c8"
CPU-only methods:
  __arrow_c_array__
  __arrow_c_stream__

Device-aware methods:
  __arrow_c_device_array__
  __arrow_c_device_stream__

CPU-only consumer:
  may consume CPU versions
  should be prepared for producer to expose device versions
  absence of device method implies CPU-only data
```

The PyCapsule Interface defines device-aware methods for non-CPU memory and states CPU-only versions must contain valid CPU pointers; if exporting non-CPU data through CPU-only methods, the producer should raise or copy to CPU. ([Apache Arrow][5])

---

## 21.6 `arrow_pyarrow::PyArrowType`

### PyArrow-specific conversion map

```text id="9xkafp"
pyarrow.DataType           <-> arrow_schema::DataType
pyarrow.Field              <-> arrow_schema::Field
pyarrow.Schema             <-> arrow_schema::Schema
pyarrow.Array              <-> arrow_data::ArrayData
pyarrow.RecordBatch        <-> arrow_array::RecordBatch
pyarrow.RecordBatchReader  <-> ArrowArrayStreamReader / Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send>
pyarrow.Table              <-> arrow_pyarrow::Table
```

`arrow_pyarrow` is useful when the Python API intentionally targets PyArrow classes rather than the broader Arrow PyCapsule ecosystem. It also explicitly recommends stream-based approaches over forcing eager `Vec<RecordBatch>` table conversion when possible. ([Apache Arrow][3])

### Accept and return PyArrow `Array`

```rust id="bize5b"
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow::array::{Array, Int64Array, make_array};
use arrow::array::ArrayData;
use arrow::pyarrow::PyArrowType;
use pyo3::prelude::*;
use pyo3::exceptions::PyTypeError;

#[pyfunction]
fn double_i64_array(
    array: PyArrowType<ArrayData>,
) -> PyResult<PyArrowType<ArrayData>> {
    let data = array.0;
    let array_ref: Arc<dyn Array> = make_array(data);

    let input = array_ref
        .as_any()
        .downcast_ref::<Int64Array>()
        .ok_or_else(|| PyTypeError::new_err("expected pyarrow.Int64Array"))?;

    let output: Int64Array = input
        .iter()
        .map(|x| x.map(|v| v * 2))
        .collect();

    Ok(PyArrowType(output.into_data()))
}
```

### Return PyArrow `RecordBatchReader`

```rust id="hhja3q"
use arrow::pyarrow::PyArrowType;
use arrow_array::{RecordBatch, RecordBatchIterator, RecordBatchReader};

#[pyfunction]
fn make_reader() -> PyResult<PyArrowType<Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send>>> {
    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
        ("id", Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef),
    ]).map_err(|e| PyRuntimeError::new_err(e.to_string()))?;

    let schema = batch.schema();

    let reader: Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send> =
        Box::new(RecordBatchIterator::new(vec![Ok(batch)], schema));

    Ok(PyArrowType(reader))
}
```

### Return PyArrow `Table`

```rust id="d5s4sj"
use arrow::pyarrow::{PyArrowType, Table};

#[pyfunction]
fn make_table() -> PyResult<PyArrowType<Table>> {
    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
        ("id", Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef),
    ]).map_err(|e| PyRuntimeError::new_err(e.to_string()))?;

    let schema = batch.schema();
    let table = Table::try_new(vec![batch], schema)
        .map_err(|e| PyRuntimeError::new_err(e.to_string()))?;

    Ok(PyArrowType(table))
}
```

### `arrow_pyarrow` rules

```text id="qp4tdb"
Use arrow_pyarrow when:
  Python API explicitly promises PyArrow objects
  pyarrow is a required dependency
  PyArrow class conversion is desired
  you want PyArrowType<T> ergonomics

Avoid arrow_pyarrow when:
  accepting arbitrary Arrow PyCapsule producers
  pyarrow should be optional
  returning arro3/nanoarrow objects is preferable
  generic Arrow protocol interop is the public contract
```

---

## 21.7 `pyo3-arrow`: generic Python Arrow bridge

### Core wrappers

```text id="n5mslk"
PyDataType
PyField
PySchema
PyArray
PyScalar
PyRecordBatch
PyRecordBatchReader
PyTable
PyArrayReader
PyChunkedArray
```

`pyo3-arrow` automatically extracts compatible Python Arrow objects into Rust Arrow objects via zero-copy FFI and exports Rust Arrow values back to Python as `arro3`, `pyarrow`, or `nanoarrow` objects through helper methods such as `into_arro3`, `into_pyarrow`, and `to_nanoarrow`. ([Docs.rs][2])

### `PyArray`

```rust id="dkbeal"
#[pyfunction]
fn take_array<'py>(
    py: Python<'py>,
    values: PyArray,
    indices: PyArray,
) -> PyArrowResult<Bound<'py, PyAny>> {
    let output_array = py.detach(|| {
        take(values.as_ref(), indices.as_ref(), None)
    })?;

    Ok(PyArray::new(output_array, values.field().clone()).into_pyarrow(py)?)
}
```

`PyArray` wraps both an `ArrayRef` and a `FieldRef` because `__arrow_c_array__` exports both schema/field metadata and array data; retaining `FieldRef` is required to preserve extension metadata through the C Data Interface. `PyArray::to_pyarrow` requires PyArrow >=14, while `into_arro3` targets `arro3.core.Array`. ([Docs.rs][6])

### `PyRecordBatch`

```rust id="yhdkdp"
#[pyfunction]
fn batch_num_rows(batch: PyRecordBatch) -> PyArrowResult<usize> {
    Ok(batch.as_ref().num_rows())
}

#[pyfunction]
fn echo_batch<'py>(
    py: Python<'py>,
    batch: PyRecordBatch,
) -> PyArrowResult<Bound<'py, PyAny>> {
    Ok(PyRecordBatch::new(batch.into_inner()).into_pyarrow(py)?)
}
```

`PyRecordBatch` is a Python-facing wrapper around `RecordBatch`, supports `new`, `from_arrow_pycapsule`, `into_inner`, and exports to `arro3`, `nanoarrow`, or PyArrow; its `into_pyarrow` method requires PyArrow >=14. ([Docs.rs][7])

### `PyRecordBatchReader`

```rust id="jxi2xy"
#[pyfunction]
fn count_rows_from_reader(reader: PyRecordBatchReader) -> PyArrowResult<usize> {
    let mut reader = reader.into_reader()?;
    let mut rows = 0usize;

    while let Some(batch) = reader.next() {
        let batch = batch?;
        rows += batch.num_rows();
    }

    Ok(rows)
}

#[pyfunction]
fn make_batch_reader<'py>(py: Python<'py>) -> PyArrowResult<Bound<'py, PyAny>> {
    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
        ("id", Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef),
    ])?;

    let schema = batch.schema();

    let reader: Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send> =
        Box::new(RecordBatchIterator::new(vec![Ok(batch)], schema));

    Ok(PyRecordBatchReader::new(reader).into_pyarrow(py)?)
}
```

`PyRecordBatchReader` wraps `Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send>`, can be constructed from raw Arrow C Stream capsules, can be consumed only once through `into_reader`, and exports to `arro3`, `nanoarrow`, or PyArrow; `into_pyarrow` requires PyArrow >=15. ([Docs.rs][8])

### `PyTable`

```rust id="2mpwer"
#[pyfunction]
fn materialize_table<'py>(
    py: Python<'py>,
    reader: PyRecordBatchReader,
) -> PyArrowResult<Bound<'py, PyAny>> {
    let table = reader.into_table()?;
    Ok(table.into_pyarrow(py)?)
}

#[pyfunction]
fn table_num_batches(table: PyTable) -> PyArrowResult<usize> {
    Ok(table.batches().len())
}
```

`PyTable` is an eager wrapper around `Vec<RecordBatch>` plus `SchemaRef`, has `try_new`, `batches`, and `into_inner`, and can export to `arro3`, `nanoarrow`, or PyArrow; `into_pyarrow` requires PyArrow >=14. ([Docs.rs][9])

---

## 21.8 Accepting PyArrow, Polars, pandas, nanoarrow, and arro3

### Protocol-first input policy

```text id="ngksg5"
Array-like input:
  require __arrow_c_array__
  Rust wrapper: PyArray

Batch-like input:
  require __arrow_c_array__
  Rust wrapper: PyRecordBatch

Table / DataFrame / stream input:
  require __arrow_c_stream__
  Rust wrapper: PyRecordBatchReader or PyTable

Schema-like input:
  require __arrow_c_schema__
  Rust wrapper: PySchema / PyField / PyDataType
```

`arro3` documents Python Arrow protocol inputs: objects with `__arrow_c_array__` include arro3 arrays/record batches and PyArrow arrays/record batches; objects with `__arrow_c_stream__` include arro3 tables/readers/chunked arrays, Polars `Series`/`DataFrame` where supported, DuckDB table-like objects, PyArrow `RecordBatchReader`/`Table`/`ChunkedArray`, pandas `DataFrame` where supported, and Ibis tables. ([kylebarron.dev][10])

### Public Python contract

```python id="nj5scg"
from typing import Protocol, Any

class ArrowArrayExportable(Protocol):
    def __arrow_c_array__(self, requested_schema: object | None = None) -> tuple[object, object]: ...

class ArrowStreamExportable(Protocol):
    def __arrow_c_stream__(self, requested_schema: object | None = None) -> object: ...
```

### Rust signature strategy

```rust id="0cvzs9"
#[pyfunction]
fn process_array(array: PyArray) -> PyArrowResult<PyArray> {
    // accepts any Python object pyo3-arrow can extract through Arrow protocols
    Ok(array)
}

#[pyfunction]
fn process_stream(reader: PyRecordBatchReader) -> PyArrowResult<usize> {
    let mut reader = reader.into_reader()?;
    let mut rows = 0;
    while let Some(batch) = reader.next() {
        rows += batch?.num_rows();
    }
    Ok(rows)
}
```

### Agent rules

```text id="utlv4s"
Do:
  document protocol requirement, not library-specific class list
  accept PyRecordBatchReader for table/dataframe-sized input
  keep PyTable only for bounded/eager APIs
  test pyarrow + arro3 at minimum
  add Polars/pandas/nanoarrow tests only when they are supported deployment dependencies

Do not:
  promise pandas/Polars support without versioned tests
  force conversion through pyarrow.Table when __arrow_c_stream__ is available
  assume every Python dataframe exports CPU Arrow buffers
```

---

```rust id="h4gepp"
use pyo3::prelude::*;
use pyo3_arrow::{PyArray, error::PyArrowResult};

#[pyfunction]
fn identity_array(array: PyArray) -> PyArrowResult<PyArray> {
    Ok(array)
}

#[pymodule]
#[pyo3(name = "_native")]
fn module(m: &Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> {
    m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(identity_array, m)?)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

PyO3’s extension-module builds require a `cdylib` and special build configuration; packaging tools such as maturin set the required `PYO3_BUILD_EXTENSION_MODULE` environment automatically, while manual builds must manage it themselves. ([pyo3.rs][11])

### Python shim

```bash id="lqxov1"
maturin build --release --out dist
```

---

## 21.10 GIL release patterns

### `py.detach` for Rust kernels

```rust id="ignfdv"
#[pyfunction]
fn take_without_gil<'py>(
    py: Python<'py>,
    values: PyArray,
    indices: PyArray,
) -> PyArrowResult<Bound<'py, PyAny>> {
    let output = py.detach(|| {
        arrow_select::take::take(values.as_ref(), indices.as_ref(), None)
    })?;

    Ok(PyArray::new(output, values.field().clone()).into_pyarrow(py)?)
}
```

PyO3 documents `Python::detach` as a way to temporarily release the GIL so Python can do other work while Rust computation continues; the `pyo3-arrow` usage example applies `py.detach` around `arrow_select::take::take`. ([pyo3.rs][12])

### GIL rules

```text id="va6ezv"
Release GIL around:
  Arrow compute kernels
  Parquet/IPC/CSV/JSON Rust IO
  CPU-heavy transformations
  DataFusion collect/execute if no Python object access
  Rayon / parallel Rust loops

Do not access while detached:
  Python objects
  Bound<'py, PyAny>
  Python exceptions
  Python reference counts
  PyDict / PyList / PyModule
  calling back into Python

Safe detached inputs:
  ArrayRef
  RecordBatch
  SchemaRef
  cloned Rust-owned values
```

### Error mapping around detached work

```rust id="jzqrit"
#[pyfunction]
fn checked_transform<'py>(
    py: Python<'py>,
    array: PyArray,
) -> PyArrowResult<Bound<'py, PyAny>> {
    let field = array.field().clone();

    let output: ArrayRef = py.detach(|| -> Result<ArrayRef, ArrowError> {
        // Rust-only Arrow work here.
        Ok(array.as_ref().clone())
    })?;

    Ok(PyArray::try_new(output, field)?.into_pyarrow(py)?)
}
```

### Return `pyarrow.Array`

```rust id="e2ueaf"
#[pyfunction]
fn make_pyarrow_array<'py>(py: Python<'py>) -> PyArrowResult<Bound<'py, PyAny>> {
    let array: ArrayRef = Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3]));
    let field: FieldRef = Arc::new(Field::new("item", DataType::Int64, true));

    Ok(PyArray::new(array, field).into_pyarrow(py)?)
}
```

### Return `arro3.core.Array`

```rust id="ddj0by"
#[pyfunction]
fn make_arro3_array<'py>(py: Python<'py>) -> PyArrowResult<Bound<'py, PyAny>> {
    let array: ArrayRef = Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3]));
    let field: FieldRef = Arc::new(Field::new("item", DataType::Int64, true));

    Ok(PyArray::new(array, field).into_arro3(py)?)
}
```

### Return `pyarrow.RecordBatch`

```rust id="cpgw2r"
#[pyfunction]
fn make_record_batch<'py>(py: Python<'py>) -> PyArrowResult<Bound<'py, PyAny>> {
    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
        ("id", Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef),
        ("name", Arc::new(StringArray::from(vec!["a", "b", "c"])) as ArrayRef),
    ])?;

    Ok(PyRecordBatch::new(batch).into_pyarrow(py)?)
}
```

### Return `pyarrow.RecordBatchReader`

```rust id="nrz657"
#[pyfunction]
fn make_reader_pyarrow<'py>(py: Python<'py>) -> PyArrowResult<Bound<'py, PyAny>> {
    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
        ("id", Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef),
    ])?;

    let schema = batch.schema();

    let reader: Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send> =
        Box::new(RecordBatchIterator::new(vec![Ok(batch)], schema));

    Ok(PyRecordBatchReader::new(reader).into_pyarrow(py)?)
}
```

### Return `pyarrow.Table`

```rust id="w623mx"
#[pyfunction]
fn make_table_pyarrow<'py>(py: Python<'py>) -> PyArrowResult<Bound<'py, PyAny>> {
    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
        ("id", Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef),
    ])?;

    let schema = batch.schema();
    let table = PyTable::try_new(vec![batch], schema)?;

    Ok(table.into_pyarrow(py)?)
}
```

### Return-object rules

```text id="of3qar"
Default for large output:
  PyRecordBatchReader

Default for single array transform:
  PyArray

Default for batch transform:
  PyRecordBatch

Use PyTable only when:
  output is bounded
  caller explicitly wants table
  compatibility requires eager table

Prefer arro3 output when:
  pyarrow dependency should be optional
  minimal Arrow Python wrapper is desired

Prefer pyarrow output when:
  public API promises PyArrow classes
  user ecosystem expects pyarrow.Array/Table
```

## 21.12 Accepting and transforming streams

### Stream-to-stream pattern

```rust id="z1mx5b"
struct MapReader<R> {
    inner: R,
    schema: SchemaRef,
}

impl<R> Iterator for MapReader<R>
where
    R: RecordBatchReader,
{
    type Item = Result<RecordBatch, ArrowError>;

    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
        self.inner.next().map(|batch| {
            let batch = batch?;
            // transform batch here
            Ok(batch)
        })
    }
}

impl<R> RecordBatchReader for MapReader<R>
where
    R: RecordBatchReader,
{
    fn schema(&self) -> SchemaRef {
        self.schema.clone()
    }
}

#[pyfunction]
fn stream_identity<'py>(
    py: Python<'py>,
    reader: PyRecordBatchReader,
) -> PyArrowResult<Bound<'py, PyAny>> {
    let reader = reader.into_reader()?;
    let schema = reader.schema();

    let mapped: Box<dyn RecordBatchReader + Send> =
        Box::new(MapReader { inner: reader, schema });

    Ok(PyRecordBatchReader::new(mapped).into_pyarrow(py)?)
}
```

### Stream rules

```text id="qslj9i"
Use stream in / stream out when:
  input may be large
  output may be large
  caller passed DataFrame/Table/RecordBatchReader
  transformation is batch-local

Avoid:
  reader.into_table()
  Vec<RecordBatch> collection
  pyarrow.Table materialization
  holding whole dataset before output
```

## 21.13 Error handling

### Convert Arrow errors to Python errors

```rust id="8mdq2a"
fn arrow_err_to_py(err: ArrowError) -> PyErr {
    PyRuntimeError::new_err(err.to_string())
}

#[pyfunction]
fn strict_i64(array: PyArray) -> PyArrowResult<usize> {
    if array.array().data_type() != &DataType::Int64 {
        return Err(PyTypeError::new_err(format!(
            "expected Int64, got {:?}",
            array.array().data_type()
        )).into());
    }

    Ok(array.array().len())
}
```

### Use `PyArrowResult`

```rust id="qup4tx"
#[pyfunction]
fn maybe_fail(array: PyArray) -> PyArrowResult<usize> {
    Ok(array.as_ref().len())
}
```

### Boundary rules

```text id="u1ce3y"
Type mismatch:
  PyTypeError

Value/domain validation:
  PyValueError

Rust Arrow / IO / compute failure:
  PyRuntimeError or PyArrowResult conversion

Unsupported protocol/object:
  PyTypeError

Unsupported device memory:
  PyTypeError or NotImplementedError-equivalent

Do not:
  panic
  unwrap
  expose Rust backtraces by default
  leak internal path/credentials in errors
```

## 21.14 `pyo3-arrow` versus `arrow_pyarrow`

| Requirement                                                         | Prefer                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| accept PyArrow only                                                 | `arrow_pyarrow`                                    |
| accept PyArrow + arro3 + nanoarrow + compatible PyCapsule producers | `pyo3-arrow`                                       |
| return PyArrow classes                                              | either; `pyo3-arrow.into_pyarrow` or `PyArrowType` |
| return arro3 classes                                                | `pyo3-arrow`                                       |
| preserve extension metadata on arrays                               | `pyo3-arrow::PyArray` with `FieldRef`              |
| expose PyArrow `Table` from `Vec<RecordBatch>`                      | `arrow_pyarrow::Table` or `pyo3_arrow::PyTable`    |
| stream large data                                                   | `PyRecordBatchReader` / `ArrowArrayStreamReader`   |
| keep pyarrow dependency optional                                    | `pyo3-arrow` + arro3/nanoarrow output              |
| simplest PyArrow-specific wrapper                                   | `PyArrowType<T>`                                   |

### Decision rule

```text id="77rlti"
New extension module:
  default to pyo3-arrow unless API is explicitly PyArrow-only.

Existing PyArrow-only ecosystem:
  use arrow_pyarrow for PyArrowType ergonomics.

Large data:
  use RecordBatchReader, not Table.

Small/bounded data:
  PyTable acceptable.
```

## 21.15 ABI and Python version strategy

### PyO3 extension-module build

```toml id="osr7pu"
[dependencies]
pyo3 = { version = "0.28", features = ["extension-module"] }
```

### `abi3` caveat

```toml id="5q6p8a"
[dependencies]
pyo3 = { version = "0.28", features = ["extension-module", "abi3-py311"] }
```

PyO3 supports `abi3` / limited Python API wheels for multi-version compatibility, but extension modules normally target the Python version they are compiled against unless `abi3` is enabled; PyO3’s build docs describe this distinction. ([pyo3.rs][11])

### `pyo3-arrow` buffer protocol caveat

```text id="ahp3ko"
pyo3-arrow default feature:
  buffer_protocol

Requirement:
  non-abi3 wheels
  or pyo3 abi3-py311-compatible setup
```

The `pyo3-arrow` Cargo metadata states that its default `buffer_protocol` feature requires either non-`abi3` wheels or the `abi3-py311` PyO3 feature. ([Docs.rs][13])

### Wheel matrix

```text id="kgomau"
Recommended initial matrix:
  CPython 3.10
  CPython 3.11
  CPython 3.12
  CPython 3.13
  CPython 3.14 if project supports it

Linux:
  manylinux2014 or newer policy
  x86_64, aarch64 as needed

macOS:
  x86_64, arm64, universal2 if needed

Windows:
  amd64

Interop deps:
  pyarrow min version
  arro3-core min version
  optional polars/pandas/nanoarrow tests
```

## 21.16 Python API design patterns

### Pattern A — compute kernel over any Arrow array

```rust id="w5mqxq"
#[pyfunction]
fn double_i64<'py>(
    py: Python<'py>,
    array: PyArray,
) -> PyArrowResult<Bound<'py, PyAny>> {
    let field = array.field().clone();

    let input = array
        .array()
        .as_any()
        .downcast_ref::<Int64Array>()
        .ok_or_else(|| PyTypeError::new_err("expected Int64 array"))?;

    let output: ArrayRef = py.detach(|| {
        let out: Int64Array = input.iter().map(|x| x.map(|v| v * 2)).collect();
        Ok::<ArrayRef, ArrowError>(Arc::new(out))
    })?;

    Ok(PyArray::new(output, field).into_pyarrow(py)?)
}
```

### Pattern B — bounded table API

```rust id="tjvgvo"
#[pyfunction]
fn table_num_rows(table: PyTable) -> PyArrowResult<usize> {
    Ok(table.batches().iter().map(|b| b.num_rows()).sum())
}
```

### Pattern C — streaming table API

```rust id="ic9cja"
#[pyfunction]
fn count_reader_rows(reader: PyRecordBatchReader) -> PyArrowResult<usize> {
    let mut reader = reader.into_reader()?;
    let mut rows = 0;

    while let Some(batch) = reader.next() {
        rows += batch?.num_rows();
    }

    Ok(rows)
}
```

### Pattern D — return stream instead of table

```rust id="7f1n3r"
#[pyfunction]
fn transform_reader<'py>(
    py: Python<'py>,
    reader: PyRecordBatchReader,
) -> PyArrowResult<Bound<'py, PyAny>> {
    let reader = reader.into_reader()?;
    Ok(PyRecordBatchReader::new(reader).into_pyarrow(py)?)
}
```

## 21.17 Deployment best practices

```text id="zc1oy5"
DO:
  use PyArray / PyRecordBatch / PyRecordBatchReader in public signatures
  release GIL around Rust-only compute
  return Arrow protocol objects, not Python lists
  preserve FieldRef for arrays to keep extension metadata
  stream large inputs/outputs
  pin pyarrow minimum when returning pyarrow objects
  test multiple producers: pyarrow, arro3, optionally polars/pandas/nanoarrow
  add import smoke test for built wheel
  align Arrow Rust crate versions across workspace

DON'T:
  convert to pandas/NumPy unless explicitly requested
  collect unbounded streams into PyTable
  call Python APIs inside py.detach closure
  expose raw PyCapsule manipulation unless necessary
  promise GPU/device support unless implemented and tested
  depend on pyarrow if arro3/nanoarrow output is sufficient
```

---

## 21.18 Anti-pattern catalog

| Anti-pattern                                               | Failure mode                           | Correct pattern                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `Vec<T>` / Python list output for large data               | copy, Python object explosion          | `PyArray` / `PyRecordBatchReader`    |
| accept only `pyarrow.Table` when protocol stream exists    | unnecessary dependency/materialization | `PyRecordBatchReader`                |
| return `PyTable` for unbounded output                      | memory blowup                          | return reader                        |
| drop `FieldRef` on array export                            | extension metadata loss                | `PyArray::new(array, field)`         |
| use `PyArray::new` with mismatched field type              | panic                                  | `PyArray::try_new`                   |
| access Python object inside `py.detach`                    | GIL violation / UB risk                | clone Rust-owned Arrow objects first |
| skip wheel import smoke tests                              | broken module-name / PyInit mismatch   | maturin develop/build + import test  |
| enable `abi3` without checking buffer protocol constraints | build/runtime mismatch                 | test wheel matrix                    |
| promise pandas/Polars input without versioned CI           | protocol mismatch                      | support matrix tests                 |
| manually pass C pointers as integers                       | leaks/unsafe                           | PyCapsule Interface                  |

## 21.20 Value case

```text id="yio79k"
Arrow C Data Interface:
  value = ABI-stable same-process zero-copy Arrow array exchange.

Arrow C Stream Interface:
  value = streaming table/dataframe exchange without eager materialization.

Arrow PyCapsule Interface:
  value = Python protocol standard for Arrow C Data / Stream / Device capsules.

arrow_pyarrow::PyArrowType:
  value = simple PyArrow-specific Rust <-> Python conversion wrapper.

pyo3-arrow::PyArray:
  value = protocol-generic array input/output with FieldRef metadata preservation.

pyo3-arrow::PyRecordBatch:
  value = protocol-generic record-batch boundary.

pyo3-arrow::PyRecordBatchReader:
  value = large-data stream boundary and PyArrow/arro3/nanoarrow-compatible output.

pyo3-arrow::PyTable:
  value = bounded eager table compatibility.

maturin:
  value = reproducible Rust extension-module wheel packaging.

py.detach:
  value = release GIL during Rust Arrow compute and IO.

Protocol-first input:
  value = accept PyArrow, arro3, nanoarrow, Polars, pandas, and other producers where they implement Arrow PyCapsule protocols.
```

Final agent rule:

```text id="o3kciq"
Default to pyo3-arrow for new zero-copy Python Arrow extensions.
Use arrow_pyarrow only for PyArrow-specific APIs.
Accept streams for table-sized input.
Return readers for large output.
Release the GIL around Rust-only work.
Preserve FieldRef metadata.
Use maturin for packaging.
Pin and test producer/consumer libraries instead of assuming every Python dataframe supports every Arrow protocol.
```

# 22) DataFrame ergonomics: Polars versus DataFusion versus raw Arrow

Style target: dense, syntax-first, agent-ready technical reference; aligned with the uploaded advanced-reference format. 

---

## 22.0 Mental model

```text id="znn7ye"
Raw Arrow:
  memory model
  arrays / buffers / schemas / RecordBatch
  explicit kernels
  no DataFrame UX
  no relational optimizer
  best for libraries, kernels, FFI, file-format bridges

Polars:
  ergonomic DataFrame / Series / LazyFrame API
  expression DSL
  eager + lazy execution
  strong user-facing dataframe ergonomics
  good Python/pandas-like migration target
  Rust core based on Arrow memory model

DataFusion:
  embeddable query engine
  SQL + DataFrame APIs
  catalogs / TableProvider / object_store / Flight integration
  relational optimizer and physical execution plans
  best for database/lakehouse/server/query-engine workloads
```

Polars is a Rust DataFrame library based on Apache Arrow’s memory model, with `DataFrame`, `Series`, and `ChunkedArray` as core data structures; its docs recommend building lazy queries directly because expressions can be optimized and evaluated in parallel. DataFusion is an extensible Rust query engine using Apache Arrow as its memory format, with SQL/DataFrame APIs, built-in CSV/Parquet/JSON/Avro support, a streaming multi-threaded vectorized execution engine, object-store IO, optimizers, and many extension points. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

Use `pyo3-arrow` at the Python boundary and choose raw Arrow, Polars, or DataFusion internally based on workload shape.

---

## 22.2 Decision matrix

| Requirement                                 | Prefer                                       | Reason                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| implement Arrow kernel                      | raw Arrow                                    | lowest layer, no DataFrame/query dependency                     |
| expose Rust library API over Arrow data     | raw Arrow                                    | stable `ArrayRef`, `RecordBatch`, `SchemaRef` contracts         |
| manipulate local tabular data ergonomically | Polars                                       | DataFrame/Series UX                                             |
| pandas-like Rust workflow                   | Polars                                       | expressive DataFrame DSL                                        |
| lazy dataframe transformations              | Polars `LazyFrame` or DataFusion `DataFrame` | choose by deployment context                                    |
| SQL over files/tables                       | DataFusion                                   | SQL engine + catalog/table providers                            |
| multi-file object-store lake scan           | DataFusion                                   | `ListingTable`, object_store, predicate/projection pushdown     |
| custom query engine / database              | DataFusion                                   | optimizer, physical plans, extension points                     |
| user-facing dataframe library               | Polars                                       | ergonomic expression API and eager/lazy modes                   |
| Flight SQL / server query backend           | DataFusion                                   | query engine + stream integration                               |
| Python Arrow protocol extension             | raw Arrow + `pyo3-arrow`                     | avoid forcing Polars/DataFusion unless needed                   |
| one-shot CSV/Parquet ETL                    | Polars or DataFusion                         | Polars for ergonomic transforms; DataFusion for SQL/lake/server |
| grouped analytics over local single table   | Polars                                       | concise DataFrame DSL                                           |
| grouped analytics over registered datasets  | DataFusion                                   | relational planning/source pushdown                             |
| no-copy buffer/schema work                  | raw Arrow                                    | direct memory model                                             |

---

## 22.3 When PyArrow users really want a DataFrame library

```text id="rv3tp8"
PyArrow user says:
  "filter rows"
  "select columns"
  "group by"
  "join"
  "sort"
  "window"
  "pivot"
  "with column"
  "dataframe"
  "pandas-like"
  "lazy transformations"
  "read parquet then aggregate"

Likely need:
  Polars or DataFusion

PyArrow user says:
  "build arrays"
  "schema"
  "IPC"
  "C Data Interface"
  "zero-copy"
  "RecordBatch"
  "Parquet writer"
  "Flight stream"

Likely need:
  raw Arrow / parquet / arrow-flight
```

Agent rule:

```text id="k4m0mz"
If the user asks for tabular analytics:
  choose Polars or DataFusion.

If the user asks for Arrow interoperability/memory/file-format primitives:
  choose raw Arrow crates.

If the user asks for SQL, query engine, object-store lake, service, catalog, pushdown:
  choose DataFusion.

If the user asks for dataframe ergonomics, local transformations, pandas migration:
  choose Polars.
```

---

## 22.4 Raw Arrow: canonical role

### Construct batch

```rust id="rbvmxm"
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::{ArrayRef, Int64Array, RecordBatch, StringArray};
use arrow_schema::{DataType, Field, Schema};

let schema = Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![
    Field::new("id", DataType::Int64, false),
    Field::new("name", DataType::Utf8, true),
]));

let batch = RecordBatch::try_new(
    schema,
    vec![
        Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef,
        Arc::new(StringArray::from(vec![Some("a"), None, Some("c")])) as ArrayRef,
    ],
)?;
```

### Apply Arrow kernel

```rust id="i375mi"
use arrow_ord::cmp::gt;
use arrow_select::filter::filter_record_batch;

let id = batch.column_by_name("id").unwrap();
let mask = gt(id.as_ref(), &Int64Array::new_scalar(1))?;
let filtered = filter_record_batch(&batch, &mask)?;
```

### Raw Arrow use cases

```text id="xykkn7"
Use raw Arrow for:
  zero-copy interop
  stable public data contracts
  kernel libraries
  UDF internals
  file-format readers/writers
  RecordBatch stream adapters
  Python extension internals
  custom DataFusion operators
```

### Raw Arrow non-goals

```text id="x1kowm"
Do not use raw Arrow alone for:
  SQL
  joins
  grouped aggregations
  windows
  dataframe ergonomics
  multi-file planning
  object-store dataset pruning
```
