## 24.14 Deployment recommendations

```text
Default Rust Arrow deployment:
  CPU-only
  raw Arrow arrays / RecordBatches
  Arrow IPC / Parquet / Flight
  PyCapsule CPU interop
  no CUDA promises

GPU-aware experimental deployment:
  feature-gated
  exact CUDA toolkit / driver matrix
  exact crate versions
  device support behind explicit API flags
  CPU fallback explicit
  safety audit required
  interop test matrix required
  no silent device pointer reinterpretation
```

### Build features

```toml
[features]
default = ["cpu"]
cpu = []
cuda-experimental = []
dlpack-experimental = []
arrow-device-experimental = []
```

### Public documentation wording

```text
Recommended:
  "GPU/device support is experimental. CPU Arrow is the stable path.
   Device inputs are accepted only when the cuda-experimental feature is enabled.
   Unsupported device arrays return an error unless fallback='copy_to_cpu' is set."

Avoid:
  "PyArrow CUDA equivalent"
  "zero-copy GPU support"
  "supports CUDA arrays"
  "DLPack support"
unless each claim has exact type/device/null coverage and tests.
```

---

## 24.15 Anti-pattern catalog

| Anti-pattern                               | Failure mode             | Correct pattern                       |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| treat device pointer as CPU `Buffer`       | crash / UB               | explicit device wrapper               |
| claim PyArrow CUDA parity                  | false capability         | mark gap/edge                         |
| DLPack nullable Arrow array                | lost null semantics      | reject or fallback                    |
| forget stream/event synchronization        | race / stale reads       | sync contract                         |
| double-consume PyCapsule                   | use-after-release        | consume once                          |
| free device memory with wrong allocator    | crash / corruption       | allocator identity in owner           |
| ignore device id/context                   | wrong-device access      | validate device/context               |
| silently copy GPU to CPU                   | hidden performance cliff | explicit fallback policy              |
| use GPU path for unsupported nested arrays | wrong layout             | CPU fallback or error                 |
| expose raw pointers in safe API            | safety hole              | opaque handles + audited unsafe layer |

---

## 24.16 Golden test matrix

```text
CPU baseline:
  Int64 array
  Float64 array
  nullable Int64 array
  string array
  struct/list array
  RecordBatch
  RecordBatchReader

DLPack:
  PyTorch CPU tensor from PyArrow primitive
  NumPy from PyArrow primitive
  JAX from PyArrow primitive
  null-containing Arrow array rejection
  unsupported dtype rejection
  CPU-only behavior asserted

Device:
  CuPy DLPack tensor if implemented
  nanoarrow CDeviceArray if implemented
  CUDA device id mismatch
  missing synchronization event
  copy_to_cpu fallback
  unsupported nested type fallback
  release callback once
  double-consumption rejection

PyCapsule:
  __arrow_c_array__
  __arrow_c_stream__
  __arrow_c_device_array__
  __arrow_c_device_stream__
  requested_schema accepted/rejected correctly
  capsule name validation

Rust safety:
  MIRI for CPU FFI wrappers where possible
  ASAN/TSAN where C/CUDA boundary permits
  cargo features without CUDA build cleanly
  cuda-experimental builds only in CUDA CI image
```

---

## 24.17 Value case

```text
PyArrow CUDA:
  value = Python-facing GPU Arrow buffer/context/IPC integration.

DLPack:
  value = tensor-library device-aware interchange for dense numeric arrays.

Arrow C Device Data Interface:
  value = columnar Arrow device-memory interchange for nullable/nested arrays and streams.

Rust CPU Arrow:
  value = stable, safe, official CPU Arrow implementation.

Rust GPU gap register:
  value = prevents false parity claims and isolates unsafe integration work.

CPU fallback:
  value = correctness and broad compatibility when device semantics are unsupported.

Feature-gated GPU path:
  value = opt-in experimental deployment without destabilizing CPU Arrow users.

Explicit ownership/synchronization contracts:
  value = prevents device-memory use-after-free, races, and wrong-context access.
```

Final agent rule:

```text
Treat CUDA/GPU/device arrays as a gap/edge area in Rust PyArrow-equivalent docs.
Use CPU Arrow as the stable default.
Use DLPack only for dense primitive tensor interop and never for nullable Arrow semantics.
Use Arrow C Device Interface only behind experimental feature gates and audited FFI wrappers.
Require explicit device type, device id, ownership, release, and synchronization contracts.
Provide CPU fallback as an explicit policy, not a hidden behavior.
Do not claim PyArrow CUDA parity in Rust unless every API in the parity table has an implemented, tested Rust equivalent.
```

[1]: https://arrow.apache.org/docs/5.0/python/api/cuda.html "CUDA Integration — Apache Arrow v5.0.0"
[2]: https://arrow.apache.org/docs/python/dlpack.html "The DLPack Protocol — Apache Arrow v24.0.0"
[3]: https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/CDeviceDataInterface.html "The Arrow C Device data interface — Apache Arrow v24.0.0"
[4]: https://docs.rs/crate/arrow/latest/source/README.md "arrow 58.4.0 - Docs.rs"
[5]: https://arrow.apache.org/docs/python/generated/pyarrow.cuda.Context.html "pyarrow.cuda.Context — Apache Arrow v24.0.0"
[6]: https://arrow.apache.org/blog/2024/10/07/nanoarrow-0.6.0-release/ "Apache Arrow nanoarrow 0.6.0 Release | Apache Arrow"
[7]: https://arrow.apache.org/blog/2020/05/03/introducing-arrow-c-data-interface/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Introducing the Apache Arrow C Data Interface"



# 25) Substrait and portable query plans

Style target: dense, syntax-first, agent-ready technical reference.

---

## 25.0 Mental model

```text
SQL:
  human-readable query language
  engine parses and binds against catalog
  not a portable physical/logical plan format

DataFusion LogicalPlan:
  Rust-native logical relational plan
  rich DataFusion-specific semantics
  optimizer input/output
  not directly portable across engines

Substrait Plan:
  protobuf-defined relational algebra representation
  portable query-plan exchange format
  intended for cross-language / cross-engine interoperability
  incomplete relative to every engine's native plan surface

datafusion-substrait:
  DataFusion LogicalPlan / ExecutionPlan <-> substrait::proto types
  producer = DataFusion -> Substrait
  consumer = Substrait -> DataFusion
```

Substrait is a cross-language format for describing compute operations on structured data, focused on interoperable relational algebra semantics. DataFusion’s `datafusion-substrait` crate serializes and deserializes DataFusion `LogicalPlan` and `ExecutionPlan` values to and from generated `substrait::proto` types, but the crate docs explicitly warn that Substrait does not yet cover the full range of DataFusion plans and expressions. ([substrait.io][1])

---

## 25.1 Cargo profiles

### Logical-plan Substrait profile

```toml
[dependencies]
datafusion = "54.1.0"
datafusion-substrait = "54.1.0"

prost = "0.14"
serde_json = "1"

tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros"] }
```

### Physical-plan Substrait profile

```toml
[dependencies]
datafusion = "54.1.0"
datafusion-substrait = { version = "54.1.0", features = ["physical"] }

prost = "0.14"
serde_json = "1"

tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros"] }
```

The `datafusion-substrait` crate is released in lockstep with DataFusion (`54.1.0`) and depends on the DataFusion crates, `prost`, and the `substrait` proto crate; its physical-plan module is feature-gated behind the `physical` feature. ([Docs.rs][2])

## 25.2 Imports

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::{ArrayRef, Int32Array, RecordBatch};
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use datafusion_expr::LogicalPlan;

use datafusion_substrait::{
    logical_plan::{consumer, producer},
    substrait,
};

use prost::Message;
```

## 25.3 PyArrow Substrait integration

### Schema serialization

```python
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.substrait as pa_substrait

schema = pa.schema([
    pa.field("x", pa.int32()),
    pa.field("y", pa.string()),
])

substrait_schema = pa_substrait.serialize_schema(schema)

# NamedStruct bytes
named_struct_bytes = bytes(substrait_schema.schema)

# ExtendedExpression bytes with extension information
extended_expr_bytes = bytes(substrait_schema.expression)

round_tripped = pa_substrait.deserialize_schema(substrait_schema)
```

PyArrow can serialize Arrow schemas to a `SubstraitSchema`, whose `.schema` is a Substrait `NamedStruct` and whose `.expression` is an `ExtendedExpression` containing extension information needed for custom Arrow types; `deserialize_schema` reverses a `NamedStruct` or `SubstraitSchema` back to a PyArrow `Schema`. ([Apache Arrow][3])

### Expression serialization

```python
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.compute as pc
import pyarrow.substrait as pa_substrait

schema = pa.schema([
    pa.field("x", pa.int32()),
    pa.field("y", pa.int32()),
])

buf = pa_substrait.serialize_expressions(
    exprs=[pc.field("x") + pc.field("y")],
    names=["total"],
    schema=schema,
    allow_arrow_extensions=False,
)

bound = pa_substrait.deserialize_expressions(buf)

assert bound.names == ["total"]
```

PyArrow serializes compute expressions to Substrait `ExtendedExpression` messages with `serialize_expressions(exprs, names, schema, allow_arrow_extensions=False)`. Expressions must be bound to a schema because Substrait function resolution depends on concrete input types; setting `allow_arrow_extensions=True` allows Arrow-specific or user-defined functions, but the result may not be accepted by other compute libraries. ([Apache Arrow][4])

### Query execution with Substrait

```python
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.substrait as pa_substrait

def table_provider(names: list[str], expected_schema: pa.Schema) -> pa.Table:
    if names == ["t"]:
        return pa.table({"x": [1, 2, 3]})
    raise KeyError(names)

reader = pa_substrait.run_query(
    substrait_plan_bytes,
    table_provider=table_provider,
    use_threads=True,
)

for batch in reader:
    ...
```

PyArrow’s `run_query` accepts a Substrait query plan and a `table_provider` callback that resolves `NamedTable` relations to `pyarrow.Table` objects, and it returns a `RecordBatchReader`. ([Apache Arrow][5])

### PyArrow scope rules

```text
PyArrow Substrait strongest path:
  schema serialization
  expression serialization
  ExtendedExpression execution in dataset scanner
  run_query with table_provider callback

PyArrow Substrait weaker / caution path:
  full cross-engine plan interchange
  Arrow extension functions
  UDFs
  engine-specific semantics
```

PyArrow’s documented Substrait integration focuses on schema serialization, expression serialization/deserialization, and dataset scanner execution of `BoundExpressions`; full engine-to-engine plan portability still depends on function coverage, extension handling, table resolution, and compatible semantics. ([Apache Arrow][3])

## 25.4 DataFusion Substrait export: `LogicalPlan -> substrait::proto::Plan`

### SQL → optimized logical plan → Substrait plan

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::{ArrayRef, Int32Array, RecordBatch};
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use datafusion_substrait::logical_plan::producer::to_substrait_plan;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion_common::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![(
        "x",
        Arc::new(Int32Array::from(vec![42])) as ArrayRef,
    )])?;

    ctx.register_batch("t", batch)?;

    let df = ctx.sql("SELECT x FROM t").await?;
    let plan = df.into_optimized_plan()?;

    let substrait_plan = to_substrait_plan(&plan, &ctx.state())?;

    Ok(())
}
```

The `datafusion-substrait` docs show this exact flow: create a DataFusion plan, call `logical_plan::producer::to_substrait_plan(&plan, &ctx.state())`, then later consume it back with `logical_plan::consumer::from_substrait_plan`. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Serialize to protobuf bytes

```rust
use datafusion_substrait::logical_plan::producer::to_substrait_plan;
use prost::Message;

let substrait_plan = to_substrait_plan(&plan, &ctx.state())?;

let mut bytes = Vec::new();
substrait_plan.encode(&mut bytes)?;
```

The `datafusion-substrait` crate re-exports the generated `substrait` crate, and its docs state that generated protobuf types such as `substrait::proto::Plan` can be serialized/deserialized to bytes, JSON, and other protobuf ecosystem formats using `prost` and related Rust protobuf tooling. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Deserialize protobuf bytes

```rust
use datafusion_substrait::substrait::proto::Plan;
use prost::Message;

let decoded = Plan::decode(bytes.as_slice())?;
```

### Export wrapper

```rust
pub async fn sql_to_substrait_bytes(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    sql: &str,
) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let df = ctx.sql(sql).await?;
    let plan = df.into_optimized_plan()?;

    let substrait_plan =
        datafusion_substrait::logical_plan::producer::to_substrait_plan(
            &plan,
            &ctx.state(),
        )?;

    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    substrait_plan.encode(&mut bytes)?;

    Ok(bytes)
}
```

---

## 25.5 DataFusion Substrait import: `substrait::proto::Plan -> LogicalPlan`

### Plan bytes → DataFusion `LogicalPlan`

```rust
use datafusion_substrait::logical_plan::consumer::from_substrait_plan;
use datafusion_substrait::substrait::proto::Plan;
use prost::Message;

pub async fn substrait_bytes_to_logical_plan(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    bytes: &[u8],
) -> anyhow::Result<LogicalPlan> {
    let proto = Plan::decode(bytes)?;

    let logical = from_substrait_plan(&ctx.state(), &proto).await?;

    // Re-run DataFusion logical optimizer after import.
    let optimized = ctx.state().optimize(&logical)?;

    Ok(optimized)
}
```

`from_substrait_plan(state, plan)` converts a Substrait `Plan` into a DataFusion `LogicalPlan`; the crate example optimizes the returned plan with `ctx.state().optimize(&logical_round_trip)` before comparing with the original optimized plan. ([Docs.rs][6])

### Execute imported plan

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use datafusion_expr::LogicalPlan;

pub async fn execute_imported_plan(
    ctx: SessionContext,
    logical: LogicalPlan,
) -> datafusion_common::Result<Vec<RecordBatch>> {
    let df = DataFrame::new(ctx.state(), logical);
    df.collect().await
}
```

### Import wrapper

```rust
pub async fn run_substrait_plan_bytes(
    ctx: SessionContext,
    bytes: &[u8],
) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<RecordBatch>> {
    let logical = substrait_bytes_to_logical_plan(&ctx, bytes).await?;
    let df = DataFrame::new(ctx.state(), logical);
    Ok(df.collect().await?)
}
```

---

## 25.6 Custom Substrait consumers

### Why customize

```text
Default consumer:
  standard Substrait -> DataFusion LogicalPlan

Custom consumer:
  custom table resolution
  custom extension relations
  custom extension expressions
  custom user-defined types
  custom user-defined literals
  custom function mapping
```

`SubstraitConsumer` is the trait used to convert Substrait plans to DataFusion logical plans; users can implement it to customize relation, expression, extension, table-resolution, function-registry, user-defined-type, and user-defined-literal handling. ([Docs.rs][7])

### Custom table resolution skeleton

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use async_trait::async_trait;
use datafusion::catalog::Session;
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use datafusion_catalog::TableProvider;
use datafusion_common::TableReference;
use datafusion_substrait::extensions::Extensions;
use datafusion_substrait::logical_plan::consumer::{
    from_project_rel, SubstraitConsumer,
};
use datafusion_substrait::substrait::proto::{
    ProjectRel, FilterRel, ExtensionLeafRel,
};

struct CustomConsumer {
    extensions: Arc<Extensions>,
    state: Arc<SessionState>,
}

#[async_trait]
impl SubstraitConsumer for CustomConsumer {
    async fn resolve_table_ref(
        &self,
        table_ref: &TableReference,
    ) -> datafusion_common::Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>> {
        let table = table_ref.table().to_string();
        let schema = self.state.schema_for_ref(table_ref.clone())?;
        let provider = schema.table(&table).await?;
        Ok(provider)
    }

    fn get_extensions(&self) -> &Extensions {
        self.extensions.as_ref()
    }

    fn get_function_registry(&self) -> &impl datafusion_execution::FunctionRegistry {
        self.state.as_ref()
    }

    async fn consume_project(
        &self,
        rel: &ProjectRel,
    ) -> datafusion_common::Result<LogicalPlan> {
        let plan = from_project_rel(self, rel).await?;

        if let Some(ext) = rel.advanced_extension.as_ref() {
            return datafusion_common::not_impl_err!(
                "project advanced_extension not implemented: {:?}",
                ext
            );
        }

        Ok(plan)
    }

    async fn consume_extension_leaf(
        &self,
        rel: &ExtensionLeafRel,
    ) -> datafusion_common::Result<LogicalPlan> {
        datafusion_common::not_impl_err!(
            "extension leaf not implemented: {:?}",
            rel.detail.as_ref().map(|d| &d.type_url)
        )
    }
}
```

The `SubstraitConsumer` docs show a custom consumer resolving tables through `SessionState`, reusing existing conversion functions such as `from_project_rel`, overriding `consume_filter`, and adding handlers for extension relations, user-defined types, and user-defined literals. ([Docs.rs][8])

### Use custom consumer

```rust
use datafusion_substrait::logical_plan::consumer::from_substrait_plan_with_consumer;

let consumer = CustomConsumer {
    extensions: Arc::new(Extensions::default()),
    state: Arc::new(ctx.state()),
};

let logical =
    from_substrait_plan_with_consumer(&consumer, &substrait_plan).await?;
```

The consumer module exposes both `from_substrait_plan` and `from_substrait_plan_with_consumer`, where the latter uses a supplied consumer implementation. ([Docs.rs][9])

---

## 25.7 Custom Substrait producers

```text
Producer customization:
  DataFusion Expr -> Substrait Rex
  DataFusion LogicalPlan -> Substrait Rel
  DataFusion UDF -> Substrait extension function
  DataFusion extension node -> Substrait extension relation
  DataFusion custom type -> Substrait user-defined type
```

The crate pairs `SubstraitConsumer` with `SubstraitProducer` for customizable Substrait serialization/deserialization; the producer module includes conversion functions such as `to_substrait_plan`, `to_substrait_rel`, `to_substrait_rex`, and relation-specific conversion helpers. ([Docs.rs][8])

### Export rules

```text
Default producer can export:
  supported DataFusion logical operators
  supported expressions
  supported function mappings
  supported table references

Custom producer needed for:
  DataFusion extension logical nodes
  UDFs not mapped to Substrait extension functions
  engine-specific data types
  custom relation metadata
  custom scalar literal encodings
```

---

## 25.8 Physical plan serialization

```toml
[dependencies]
datafusion-substrait = { version = "54.1.0", features = ["physical"] }
```

```text
Physical Substrait support:
  DataFusion ExecutionPlan <-> substrait::proto
  feature-gated by datafusion-substrait/physical
  more engine-specific than logical plans
  less suitable for generic cross-engine portability
```

The crate description says `datafusion-substrait` provides support for both DataFusion `LogicalPlan` and `ExecutionPlan` serialization/deserialization, and the physical-plan module is available only with the `physical` feature. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Agent rule

```text
Prefer logical-plan Substrait for:
  cross-engine exchange
  SQL-to-plan portability
  FFI boundaries
  client/server query submission
  long-lived serialized plans

Use physical-plan Substrait only for:
  DataFusion-specific execution exchange
  controlled homogeneous deployments
  experimental/diagnostic workflows
  version-pinned systems
```

---

## 25.9 Plan serialization boundaries

| Boundary                         | Use                                            | Avoid                                                |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| user query input                 | SQL text                                       | Substrait unless generated by a trusted planner      |
| Rust internal optimizer state    | DataFusion `LogicalPlan`                       | serializing unless crossing boundary                 |
| cross-engine logical plan        | Substrait `Plan` bytes                         | DataFusion `Debug` output                            |
| DataFusion-only plan persistence | consider `datafusion-proto`                    | Substrait if full coverage needed                    |
| Python ↔ Rust plan transfer      | Substrait bytes or DataFusion Python API       | raw Rust structs                                     |
| node-to-node query dispatch      | Substrait logical plan bytes                   | SQL text if binding already resolved                 |
| physical execution dispatch      | physical Substrait only in homogeneous systems | generic cross-engine assumption                      |
| expression-only transfer         | Substrait `ExtendedExpression`                 | full plan wrapper if only projections/filters needed |

The `datafusion-substrait` docs explicitly state that Substrait does not support the full range of DataFusion plans and expressions and point to `datafusion-proto` for a DataFusion-specific format with broader DataFusion coverage; therefore, agents should not use Substrait as a universal persistence format for DataFusion-native plans. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 25.10 SQL versus Substrait

| Dimension                  | SQL                         | Substrait                                             |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| intended author            | human / app                 | planner / engine                                      |
| readability                | high                        | low protobuf                                          |
| binding                    | late, by engine catalog     | usually already resolved to relations/functions/types |
| portability                | syntax varies by dialect    | semantic plan format                                  |
| optimization               | engine-specific after parse | engine may still optimize imported plan               |
| table names                | text identifiers            | `ReadRel` / named table references                    |
| functions                  | dialect-specific names      | extension URIs and function anchors                   |
| types                      | dialect-specific            | Substrait type system                                 |
| good for APIs              | public query interface      | engine-to-engine/query-plan interface                 |
| good for long-term archive | yes if dialect is stable    | only with version/function-extension control          |

Agent rule:

```text
External user API:
  SQL

Internal planner boundary:
  Substrait

Cross-engine tests:
  SQL result == DataFusion result == imported Substrait result

Long-term persisted DataFusion-specific plan:
  consider datafusion-proto, not Substrait
```

---

## 25.11 Function and extension mapping

```text
Substrait function identity:
  extension URI
  extension function declaration
  function anchor
  argument types/options
  output type/nullability

DataFusion function identity:
  FunctionRegistry lookup
  scalar/aggregate/window UDF name
  type coercion and return-type logic
```

PyArrow’s `serialize_expressions` defaults to core Substrait function definitions only and requires `allow_arrow_extensions=True` for PyArrow-specific functions or UDFs, warning that such plans may not be accepted by other compute libraries. DataFusion’s custom consumer trait provides hooks for custom function, type, literal, and extension relation conversion. ([Apache Arrow][4])

### Agent rules

```text
For portable Substrait:
  use core Substrait functions
  avoid engine-specific UDFs
  avoid Arrow-specific extension functions
  pin function extension URIs
  test import in every target engine

For engine-specific Substrait:
  include custom extension URIs
  implement custom producer/consumer
  version the extension namespace
  fail closed on unknown function anchors
```

---

## 25.12 Table resolution

### DataFusion import contract

```text
Substrait ReadRel / NamedTable:
  identifies table relation

DataFusion consumer:
  must resolve table reference to TableProvider
  needs SessionState / catalog / schema provider

PyArrow run_query:
  table_provider(names, expected_schema) -> pyarrow.Table
```

DataFusion’s `SubstraitConsumer::resolve_table_ref` resolves Substrait table references to `Arc<dyn TableProvider>`, while PyArrow `run_query` requires a `table_provider` callback receiving a list of strings for the table name plus an expected PyArrow schema and returning a `pyarrow.Table`. ([Docs.rs][8])

### DataFusion table setup before import

```rust
let ctx = SessionContext::new();

ctx.register_parquet(
    "orders",
    "s3://bucket/orders/",
    ParquetReadOptions::default(),
).await?;

let plan = substrait_bytes_to_logical_plan(&ctx, &bytes).await?;
```

Agent rule:

```text
Before importing Substrait:
  register required tables
  register required UDFs/UDAFs/UDWFs
  register object stores
  align schemas
  validate table-reference naming convention
```

---

## 25.13 Schema and expression boundary

### PyArrow expression-only interchange

```python
expr_bytes = pa_substrait.serialize_expressions(
    exprs=[
        (pc.field("amount") + pc.field("tax")),
        pc.field("country"),
    ],
    names=["gross", "country"],
    schema=input_schema,
)
```

### DataFusion plan-level interchange

```rust
let df = ctx
    .table("orders")
    .await?
    .select(vec![
        (col("amount") + col("tax")).alias("gross"),
        col("country"),
    ])?;

let plan = df.into_optimized_plan()?;
let substrait_plan = to_substrait_plan(&plan, &ctx.state())?;
```

Use PyArrow `ExtendedExpression` for projection/filter/expression fragments and DataFusion `Plan` serialization for full relational query plans. PyArrow’s expression serialization returns an `ExtendedExpression`, while `datafusion-substrait` works with Substrait `Plan` objects for DataFusion plans. ([Apache Arrow][4])

---

## 25.14 Cross-engine exchange workflow

```text
Producer engine:
  build native logical plan
  normalize/optimize only if desired
  export Substrait Plan bytes
  include version and extension registry metadata
  include table naming convention
  include schema expectations

Transport:
  bytes over Flight/HTTP/FFI/message bus/file

Consumer engine:
  decode protobuf Plan
  resolve tables
  resolve functions/extensions
  convert to native logical plan
  run native analyzer/optimizer
  execute
  compare output with expected tests
```

Substrait’s value case is that each engine can ingest and produce Substrait to participate in a heterogeneous ecosystem, avoiding pairwise custom plan-exchange protocols. ([substrait.io][1])

### Rust producer → Rust consumer

```rust
let bytes = sql_to_substrait_bytes(&ctx_a, "SELECT x FROM t").await?;

let logical = substrait_bytes_to_logical_plan(&ctx_b, &bytes).await?;

let df = DataFrame::new(ctx_b.state(), logical);
let batches = df.collect().await?;
```

---

## 25.15 FFI / Python boundary pattern

### Python sends Substrait bytes

```python
# Python
substrait_bytes: bytes = make_plan_somehow()
rust_module.run_substrait(substrait_bytes)
```

### Rust receives bytes

```rust
#[pyfunction]
fn run_substrait_py<'py>(
    py: Python<'py>,
    plan_bytes: Vec<u8>,
) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyAny>> {
    // 1. Decode protobuf Plan
    // 2. Convert to DataFusion LogicalPlan
    // 3. Execute via SessionContext
    // 4. Return PyRecordBatchReader via pyo3-arrow
    todo!()
}
```

### Preferred output

```text
For bounded output:
  PyTable / Vec<RecordBatch>

For large output:
  PyRecordBatchReader / Arrow C Stream

For plan transfer:
  Substrait bytes, not Rust Debug string
```

DataFusion’s Substrait docs list FFI boundaries such as Python-to-Rust and node-to-node exchange as intended uses of Substrait plan serialization. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 25.16 Plan validation

### Decode-only validation

```rust
pub fn validate_substrait_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let _plan = datafusion_substrait::substrait::proto::Plan::decode(bytes)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### DataFusion import validation

```rust
pub async fn validate_datafusion_import(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    bytes: &[u8],
) -> anyhow::Result<LogicalPlan> {
    let proto = substrait::proto::Plan::decode(bytes)?;
    let logical = consumer::from_substrait_plan(&ctx.state(), &proto).await?;
    let optimized = ctx.state().optimize(&logical)?;
    Ok(optimized)
}
```

### Execution validation

```rust
pub async fn validate_execution(
    ctx: SessionContext,
    logical: LogicalPlan,
    max_rows: usize,
) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<RecordBatch>> {
    let df = DataFrame::new(ctx.state(), logical);

    let batches = df.collect().await?;
    let rows: usize = batches.iter().map(RecordBatch::num_rows).sum();

    anyhow::ensure!(rows <= max_rows, "row limit exceeded");

    Ok(batches)
}
```

---

## 25.17 SQL versus Substrait equivalence tests

### Test pattern

```rust
#[tokio::test]
async fn sql_substrait_round_trip_equivalence() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![(
        "x",
        Arc::new(Int32Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef,
    )])?;

    ctx.register_batch("t", batch)?;

    let sql = "SELECT x FROM t WHERE x > 1";

    let direct = ctx.sql(sql).await?.collect().await?;

    let bytes = sql_to_substrait_bytes(&ctx, sql).await?;
    let logical = substrait_bytes_to_logical_plan(&ctx, &bytes).await?;
    let round_trip = DataFrame::new(ctx.state(), logical).collect().await?;

    assert_eq!(
        format!("{direct:?}"),
        format!("{round_trip:?}")
    );

    Ok(())
}
```

### Better equality strategy

```text
For deterministic output:
  sort both results by stable key
  compare schemas
  compare row counts
  compare normalized RecordBatch content

For nondeterministic output:
  use multiset comparison
  avoid relying on batch boundaries
  avoid relying on row order unless ORDER BY is present

For floating results:
  compare with tolerance
  avoid stringified Debug equality
```

The official `datafusion-substrait` docs compare formatted debug output after round-trip optimization in the simple example, but production equivalence tests should normalize ordering, schemas, and floating-point tolerances instead of relying solely on `Debug` string equality. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 25.18 Coverage matrix

| Feature                       |             PyArrow Substrait |                   DataFusion Substrait | Agent label                      |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------: | -------------------------------------: | -------------------------------- |
| schema serialization          |                           yes |        through plan/schema conversions | usable                           |
| expression serialization      |     yes, `ExtendedExpression` | consumer/producer expression functions | usable with coverage tests       |
| full plan serialization       |    `run_query` consumes plans |                     yes, logical plans | usable with limitations          |
| physical plan serialization   |  no typical PyArrow user path |                          feature-gated | experimental / homogeneous       |
| core scalar functions         |              yes if supported |                          yes if mapped | test                             |
| Arrow-specific functions      | `allow_arrow_extensions=True` |      custom extension mapping required | non-portable                     |
| UDFs                          |           extension-dependent |      custom producer/consumer required | non-portable                     |
| table resolution              |                      callback |       catalog/TableProvider resolution | required setup                   |
| extension relations           |  not generic user convenience |                         consumer hooks | custom                           |
| full DataFusion plan coverage |                not applicable |                           not complete | use `datafusion-proto` if needed |
| cross-engine portability      |                       partial |                                partial | test per target engine           |

---

## 25.19 Deployment recommendations

```text
DO:
  use Substrait for engine-to-engine logical plan exchange
  use SQL for human/user-facing query APIs
  register all tables and UDFs before importing plans
  version custom extension URIs
  serialize with protobuf bytes for transport
  re-optimize imported plans in the target engine
  maintain SQL-vs-Substrait equivalence tests
  reject unknown extension functions/types by default
  include engine/version/function coverage metadata

DON'T:
  persist Substrait as the only source of truth for DataFusion-specific plans
  assume every DataFusion LogicalPlan exports/imports losslessly
  assume physical Substrait is portable across engines
  rely on row order unless ORDER BY is present
  treat Substrait as an authorization boundary
  accept untrusted Substrait plans without table/function/resource controls
```

---

## 25.20 Security and resource controls

```text
Untrusted Substrait input risks:
  expensive scans
  cross-catalog table references
  unsupported functions
  UDF invocation
  very large joins
  Cartesian products
  denial-of-service through deep expression trees
  extension payload abuse

Required controls:
  table allowlist
  function allowlist
  max plan size
  max relation depth
  max expression depth
  max output rows/bytes
  query timeout
  memory pool
  object-store authorization
  EXPLAIN/audit logging
```

Substrait is a plan format, not a sandbox. DataFusion is customizable at data-source, query-language, function, and operator levels, so imported plans must still be authorized against the hosting engine’s catalog, function registry, object-store registry, and runtime limits. ([Apache DataFusion][10])

---

## 25.21 Anti-pattern catalog

| Anti-pattern                                                                              | Failure mode             | Correct pattern                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| treat Substrait as full DataFusion serialization                                          | lost unsupported nodes   | use `datafusion-proto` for DataFusion-specific full coverage |
| import plan before registering tables                                                     | table resolution failure | register catalog/providers first                             |
| allow Arrow-specific extensions in PyArrow and expect Velox/DuckDB/DataFusion portability | consumer rejection       | core Substrait functions only                                |
| compare round-trip outputs without sort                                                   | flaky tests              | sort/normalize                                               |
| expose physical Substrait as public cross-engine API                                      | engine/version lock-in   | logical Substrait                                            |
| store raw SQL and Substrait without schema/function version                               | unreproducible execution | store catalog/schema/function registry version               |
| use Substrait as auth token                                                               | privilege bypass risk    | authorize tables/functions separately                        |
| accept huge untrusted plans                                                               | DoS                      | size/depth/resource limits                                   |
| assume UDF name maps across engines                                                       | wrong function semantics | extension URI + registry tests                               |
| skip target-engine execution tests                                                        | false portability claim  | run equivalence suite per engine                             |

---

## 25.22 Golden test matrix

```text
PyArrow:
  serialize_schema / deserialize_schema
  serialize_expressions / deserialize_expressions
  allow_arrow_extensions=False core functions
  allow_arrow_extensions=True rejection in other engine
  run_query table_provider resolution
  BoundExpressions dataset scanner path

DataFusion export:
  SQL -> optimized LogicalPlan
  LogicalPlan -> Substrait Plan
  protobuf encode/decode
  JSON encode/decode if used
  extension function export failure mode
  unsupported logical node failure mode

DataFusion import:
  Plan -> LogicalPlan
  table resolution success
  missing table failure
  missing function failure
  custom consumer extension relation
  custom user-defined type rejection

Round trip:
  projection
  filter
  aggregate
  join
  sort
  limit
  set operation
  window if supported
  nested expressions
  null semantics
  decimals
  timestamps/timezones

Cross-engine:
  DataFusion -> PyArrow/Acero where supported
  PyArrow expression -> DataFusion consumer where supported
  DataFusion -> target engine
  target engine -> DataFusion

Security:
  table allowlist
  function allowlist
  oversized plan rejection
  deep expression rejection
  timeout
  memory limit
  output row limit
```

---

## 25.23 Value case

```text
Substrait:
  value = portable relational algebra representation across engines/languages.

PyArrow Substrait:
  value = serialize Arrow schemas and compute expressions, execute Substrait plans with table-provider callback, and use Substrait expressions in dataset scans.

datafusion-substrait:
  value = DataFusion LogicalPlan/ExecutionPlan import-export to generated Substrait protobuf types.

SubstraitProducer:
  value = DataFusion-native plan/expression/function/type export surface.

SubstraitConsumer:
  value = customizable import surface for table resolution, functions, extension relations, user-defined types, and literals.

Protobuf bytes:
  value = compact transport/persistence boundary for plans.

SQL-vs-Substrait tests:
  value = prove semantic equivalence between human-facing SQL and engine-facing plan exchange.

Extension registry:
  value = controlled portability for UDFs, non-core functions, and custom types.

DataFusion optimizer after import:
  value = adapt imported logical plan to target runtime, catalog, and physical execution environment.
```

Final agent rule:

```text
Use SQL for humans.
Use DataFusion LogicalPlan for Rust-native planning.
Use Substrait bytes for cross-engine or cross-language plan exchange.
Use PyArrow Substrait for schemas, expressions, and Acero/dataset-facing plan execution.
Use datafusion-substrait for DataFusion plan import/export.
Register tables/functions before import.
Re-optimize after import.
Test SQL and Substrait outputs for equivalence.
Never claim full portability without a target-engine compatibility matrix.
```

# 26) Extension types and custom logical types

Style target: dense, syntax-first, agent-ready technical reference.

---

## 26.0 Mental model

```text
Arrow extension type =
  storage DataType
  + Field metadata:
      ARROW:extension:name
      ARROW:extension:metadata
  + consumer-side interpretation

Physical memory:
  unchanged standard Arrow layout

Logical semantics:
  supplied by extension name + serialized metadata

Correctness rule:
  unknown consumer must still be able to read storage type safely
```

Arrow extension types attach custom logical semantics to a normal Arrow storage type through field metadata; in Rust, extension metadata is represented on `Field`, and the Rust `ExtensionType` trait uses `EXTENSION_TYPE_NAME_KEY` and `EXTENSION_TYPE_METADATA_KEY` for this purpose. ([Apache Arrow][1])

---

## 26.1 Cargo profiles

### Metadata-only extension support

```toml
[dependencies]
arrow-schema = "58.4.0"
```

### Canonical extension types

```toml
[dependencies]
arrow-schema = { version = "58.4.0", features = ["canonical_extension_types"] }
arrow-array = "58.4.0"
```

Canonical extension support in `arrow-schema` is gated behind the `canonical_extension_types` feature. ([Apache Arrow][1])

### IPC / Parquet round-trip profile

```toml
[dependencies]
arrow-array = "58.4.0"
arrow-schema = { version = "58.4.0", features = ["canonical_extension_types"] }
arrow-ipc = "58.4.0"
parquet = { version = "58.4.0", features = ["arrow"] }
```

### Python interop profile

```toml
[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib"]

[dependencies]
pyo3 = { version = "0.28", features = ["extension-module"] }
pyo3-arrow = "0.17.0"

arrow-array = "58.4.0"
arrow-schema = { version = "58.4.0", features = ["canonical_extension_types"] }
```

---

## 26.2 PyArrow extension types

### Python definition pattern

```python
import pyarrow as pa


class RationalType(pa.ExtensionType):
    def __init__(self, value_type: pa.DataType):
        if not pa.types.is_integer(value_type):
            raise TypeError(f"value_type must be integer, got {value_type}")

        storage_type = pa.struct([
            ("numer", value_type),
            ("denom", value_type),
        ])

        super().__init__(storage_type, "com.example.rational")

    def __arrow_ext_serialize__(self) -> bytes:
        # metadata payload; keep deterministic
        return b""

    @classmethod
    def __arrow_ext_deserialize__(cls, storage_type, serialized):
        if not pa.types.is_struct(storage_type):
            raise TypeError("expected struct storage")

        if serialized != b"":
            raise ValueError("unexpected metadata")

        value_type = storage_type[0].type
        return cls(value_type)


pa.register_extension_type(RationalType(pa.int64()))

storage = pa.array([
    {"numer": 1, "denom": 2},
    {"numer": 3, "denom": 4},
])

arr = RationalType(pa.int64()).wrap_array(storage)
```

`pyarrow.ExtensionType` is the concrete base class for Python-defined extension types; it requires an underlying `storage_type` and a unique `extension_name`, and PyArrow uses the extension name when deserializing IPC data. PyArrow extension classes define `__arrow_ext_serialize__` and `__arrow_ext_deserialize__` to serialize and deserialize extension parameters. ([Apache Arrow][2])

### Unknown extension type behavior

```python
# If the extension implementation is not registered,
# PyArrow can represent a Python-defined extension as UnknownExtensionType.
```

`pyarrow.UnknownExtensionType` represents a Python-defined extension type whose Python implementation is unknown; it preserves the storage type and serialized extension payload. ([Apache Arrow][3])

### PyArrow rules

```text
DO:
  use pa.ExtensionType
  use globally unique extension_name
  serialize metadata deterministically
  validate storage_type in deserializer
  register extension type before IPC/Parquet read when concrete type recovery matters

DON'T:
  rely on pickle-based legacy extension behavior
  use ambiguous extension names
  encode values in metadata
  make metadata nondeterministic
  assume every consumer knows the extension implementation
```

---

## 26.3 Rust extension metadata model

### Raw metadata keys

```rust
use std::collections::HashMap;

use arrow_schema::{
    DataType, Field,
    extension::{EXTENSION_TYPE_NAME_KEY, EXTENSION_TYPE_METADATA_KEY},
};

let field = Field::new("payload", DataType::Utf8, true)
    .with_metadata(HashMap::from([
        (
            EXTENSION_TYPE_NAME_KEY.to_string(),
            "com.example.json_payload".to_string(),
        ),
        (
            EXTENSION_TYPE_METADATA_KEY.to_string(),
            r#"{"version":1}"#.to_string(),
        ),
    ]));

assert_eq!(field.extension_type_name(), Some("com.example.json_payload"));
assert_eq!(field.extension_type_metadata(), Some(r#"{"version":1}"#));
```

Rust `Field::extension_type_name()` reads `EXTENSION_TYPE_NAME_KEY`, `Field::extension_type_metadata()` reads `EXTENSION_TYPE_METADATA_KEY`, and absence of either key means the extension name or metadata is absent. ([Apache Arrow][4])

### Rust `ExtensionType` implementation

```rust
use arrow_schema::{
    ArrowError, DataType, Field,
    extension::ExtensionType,
};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct EmailAddress;

impl ExtensionType for EmailAddress {
    const NAME: &'static str = "com.example.email_address";

    type Metadata = ();

    fn metadata(&self) -> &Self::Metadata {
        &()
    }

    fn serialize_metadata(&self) -> Option<String> {
        None
    }

    fn deserialize_metadata(metadata: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self::Metadata, ArrowError> {
        match metadata {
            None => Ok(()),
            Some("") => Ok(()),
            Some(other) => Err(ArrowError::ParseError(format!(
                "unexpected metadata for {}: {other}",
                Self::NAME,
            ))),
        }
    }

    fn supports_data_type(&self, data_type: &DataType) -> Result<(), ArrowError> {
        match data_type {
            DataType::Utf8 | DataType::LargeUtf8 | DataType::Utf8View => Ok(()),
            other => Err(ArrowError::InvalidArgumentError(format!(
                "{} requires Utf8/LargeUtf8/Utf8View storage, got {other}",
                Self::NAME,
            ))),
        }
    }

    fn try_new(data_type: &DataType, metadata: Self::Metadata) -> Result<Self, ArrowError> {
        let ext = Self;
        ext.supports_data_type(data_type)?;
        let _ = metadata;
        Ok(ext)
    }
}

let field = Field::new("email", DataType::Utf8, true)
    .with_extension_type(EmailAddress);

assert!(field.has_valid_extension_type::<EmailAddress>());
let parsed = field.try_extension_type::<EmailAddress>()?;
assert_eq!(parsed, EmailAddress);
```

Rust `ExtensionType` requires an identifying `NAME`, a `Metadata` type, metadata serialization/deserialization, storage datatype validation through `supports_data_type`, and construction through `try_new`; Rust docs recommend namespace-style names and reserve names beginning with `arrow.` for canonical extension types. ([Apache Arrow][1])

---

## 26.4 Field helper APIs

```rust
let mut field = Field::new("uuid", DataType::FixedSizeBinary(16), false);

// Fallible: preferred at boundaries.
field.try_with_extension_type(EmailAddress)?;

// Infallible wrapper that panics on invalid storage type.
let field = Field::new("email", DataType::Utf8, true)
    .with_extension_type(EmailAddress);

// Fast check.
if field.extension_type_name() == Some(EmailAddress::NAME) {
    assert!(field.has_valid_extension_type::<EmailAddress>());
}

// Parse full extension instance.
let ext = field.try_extension_type::<EmailAddress>()?;
```

`Field::try_with_extension_type` writes extension name/metadata only after validating the storage datatype; `with_extension_type` panics on validation failure; `has_valid_extension_type` checks name and validates metadata/type without constructing the extension instance; `try_extension_type` deserializes metadata and validates storage type. ([Apache Arrow][4])

---

## 26.5 Canonical extension types

```toml
[dependencies]
arrow-schema = { version = "58.4.0", features = ["canonical_extension_types"] }
```

Canonical extension types are standardized extension definitions intended to improve interoperability across Arrow implementations; canonical extension names must start with `arrow.`, and standardized canonical types are expected to be stable with backward-compatibility guarantees. ([Apache Arrow][5])

| Canonical type        | Extension name                | Storage type                                          |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| fixed-shape tensor    | `arrow.fixed_shape_tensor`    | `FixedSizeList` with metadata describing tensor shape |
| variable-shape tensor | `arrow.variable_shape_tensor` | physical tensor data plus shape metadata              |
| JSON                  | `arrow.json`                  | `String`, `LargeString`, or `StringView`              |
| UUID                  | `arrow.uuid`                  | `FixedSizeBinary(16)`                                 |
| opaque                | `arrow.opaque`                | any storage type; `Null` if no underlying data        |
| 8-bit boolean         | `arrow.bool8`                 | `Int8`, where `0` is false and nonzero is true        |
| Parquet Variant       | `arrow.parquet.variant`       | constrained `Struct` with metadata/value fields       |
| timestamp with offset | `arrow.timestamp_with_offset` | `Struct(timestamp, offset_minutes)`                   |

JSON storage is UTF-8 text in `String`, `LargeString`, or `StringView`; UUID storage is `FixedSizeBinary(16)` with big-endian notation and no UUID-version interpretation; Bool8 storage is `Int8`; and Opaque is designed to preserve uninterpretable external types without falsely implying semantic support. ([Apache Arrow][5])

### Canonical UUID

```rust
use arrow_schema::{
    DataType, Field,
    extension::{CanonicalExtensionType, Uuid},
};

let field = Field::new("id", DataType::FixedSizeBinary(16), false)
    .with_extension_type(Uuid);

assert!(field.has_valid_extension_type::<Uuid>());

let canonical = field.try_canonical_extension_type()?;
match canonical {
    CanonicalExtensionType::Uuid(_) => {}
    other => panic!("unexpected canonical type: {other:?}"),
}
```

`Field::try_canonical_extension_type()` returns a `CanonicalExtensionType` when the field has a supported canonical extension and errors if the metadata is missing, mismatched, unsupported, or invalid. ([Apache Arrow][4])

### Canonical JSON

```rust
use arrow_schema::{
    DataType, Field,
    extension::canonical::Json,
};

let field = Field::new("payload", DataType::Utf8, true)
    .with_extension_type(Json);
```

### Canonical selection rules

```text
Prefer canonical extension types when:
  semantic type is already standardized
  cross-language interoperability matters
  PyArrow / Java / Go / Rust consumers should agree
  Parquet logical type maps to canonical Arrow extension

Use custom extension types when:
  domain-specific semantics are not canonical
  metadata schema is product-specific
  extension name belongs to your namespace
```

---

## 26.6 Custom extension-name design

```text
Good:
  com.example.email_address
  org.mycompany.money
  io.vendor.product.semantic_version
  geoarrow.wkb

Bad:
  email
  uuid
  json
  arrow.my_custom_type
  ExtensionType
```

Rust docs recommend namespace-style prefixes such as `myorg.name_of_type`; extension names beginning with `arrow.` are reserved for canonical extension types and should not be used by third-party extensions. ([Apache Arrow][1])

### Metadata design

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
struct MoneyMetadata {
    currency: String,
    scale: i32,
    version: u32,
}
```

```json
{"version":1,"currency":"USD","scale":2}
```

Metadata rules:

```text
DO:
  use UTF-8 string metadata
  use deterministic JSON for parameterized metadata
  include metadata schema version
  validate strictly
  keep metadata small
  treat unknown future fields according to your compatibility policy

DON'T:
  put per-row values in extension metadata
  use nondeterministic JSON ordering if fingerprints matter
  use local class names as extension names
  use "arrow." prefix for custom types
```

---

## 26.7 Custom logical type example: money

### Rust storage contract

```text
Logical type:
  com.example.money

Storage:
  Decimal128(precision, scale)

Metadata:
  {"version":1,"currency":"USD"}
```

### Rust implementation

```rust
use arrow_schema::{ArrowError, DataType, Field, extension::ExtensionType};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
struct MoneyMeta {
    version: u32,
    currency: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct MoneyType(MoneyMeta);

impl ExtensionType for MoneyType {
    const NAME: &'static str = "com.example.money";

    type Metadata = MoneyMeta;

    fn metadata(&self) -> &Self::Metadata {
        &self.0
    }

    fn serialize_metadata(&self) -> Option<String> {
        Some(serde_json::to_string(&self.0).expect("metadata serialization"))
    }

    fn deserialize_metadata(metadata: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self::Metadata, ArrowError> {
        let raw = metadata.ok_or_else(|| {
            ArrowError::ParseError("money metadata missing".to_string())
        })?;

        let meta: MoneyMeta = serde_json::from_str(raw)
            .map_err(|e| ArrowError::ParseError(format!("money metadata invalid: {e}")))?;

        if meta.version != 1 {
            return Err(ArrowError::ParseError(format!(
                "unsupported money metadata version {}",
                meta.version
            )));
        }

        if meta.currency.len() != 3 {
            return Err(ArrowError::ParseError(
                "currency must be ISO-4217-like 3-letter code".to_string(),
            ));
        }

        Ok(meta)
    }

    fn supports_data_type(&self, data_type: &DataType) -> Result<(), ArrowError> {
        match data_type {
            DataType::Decimal128(_, _) | DataType::Decimal256(_, _) => Ok(()),
            other => Err(ArrowError::InvalidArgumentError(format!(
                "{} requires Decimal128/Decimal256 storage, got {other}",
                Self::NAME,
            ))),
        }
    }

    fn try_new(data_type: &DataType, metadata: Self::Metadata) -> Result<Self, ArrowError> {
        let ext = MoneyType(metadata);
        ext.supports_data_type(data_type)?;
        Ok(ext)
    }
}

let money = MoneyType(MoneyMeta {
    version: 1,
    currency: "USD".to_string(),
});

let field = Field::new("amount", DataType::Decimal128(18, 2), true)
    .with_extension_type(money);

assert!(field.has_valid_extension_type::<MoneyType>());
```

---

## 26.8 PyArrow equivalent for money

```python
import json
import pyarrow as pa


class MoneyType(pa.ExtensionType):
    def __init__(self, precision: int, scale: int, currency: str):
        self.precision = precision
        self.scale = scale
        self.currency = currency

        super().__init__(
            pa.decimal128(precision, scale),
            "com.example.money",
        )

    def __arrow_ext_serialize__(self) -> bytes:
        payload = {
            "version": 1,
            "currency": self.currency,
        }
        return json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()

    @classmethod
    def __arrow_ext_deserialize__(cls, storage_type, serialized):
        if not pa.types.is_decimal(storage_type):
            raise TypeError(f"expected decimal storage, got {storage_type}")

        payload = json.loads(serialized.decode())
        if payload["version"] != 1:
            raise ValueError("unsupported metadata version")

        return cls(
            storage_type.precision,
            storage_type.scale,
            payload["currency"],
        )


pa.register_extension_type(MoneyType(18, 2, "USD"))

storage = pa.array(["10.50", "20.00"], type=pa.decimal128(18, 2))
arr = MoneyType(18, 2, "USD").wrap_array(storage)
```

PyArrow extension types define storage and extension name in the constructor, then serialize parameters through `__arrow_ext_serialize__` and recover them in `__arrow_ext_deserialize__`. ([Apache Arrow][2])

---

## 26.9 IPC preservation

```text
IPC preservation:
  Schema contains Field metadata
  Field metadata contains extension name / metadata
  Consumer with registered extension implementation can reconstruct logical extension type
  Consumer without implementation can still read storage type and metadata
```

PyArrow states that the extension name is used when deserializing IPC data, and Arrow extension annotations are part of the Arrow specification, so non-Python consumers can potentially recognize them. ([Apache Arrow][2])

### Rust IPC test sketch

```rust
use std::io::Cursor;
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::{ArrayRef, Decimal128Array, RecordBatch};
use arrow_ipc::reader::FileReader;
use arrow_ipc::writer::FileWriter;
use arrow_schema::{DataType, Field, Schema};

let field = Field::new("amount", DataType::Decimal128(18, 2), true)
    .with_extension_type(MoneyType(MoneyMeta {
        version: 1,
        currency: "USD".to_string(),
    }));

let schema = Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![field.clone()]));

let array: ArrayRef = Arc::new(
    Decimal128Array::from(vec![Some(1050_i128), Some(2000_i128)])
        .with_precision_and_scale(18, 2)?
);

let batch = RecordBatch::try_new(schema.clone(), vec![array])?;

let mut bytes = Vec::new();
{
    let mut writer = FileWriter::try_new(&mut bytes, schema.as_ref())?;
    writer.write(&batch)?;
    writer.finish()?;
}

let cursor = Cursor::new(bytes);
let mut reader = FileReader::try_new(cursor, None)?;
let out = reader.next().unwrap()?;

let out_field = out.schema().field(0);
assert_eq!(out_field.extension_type_name(), Some(MoneyType::NAME));
assert!(out_field.has_valid_extension_type::<MoneyType>());
```

---

## 26.10 Parquet preservation

```text
Parquet preservation path:
  ArrowWriter embeds original Arrow schema under ARROW:schema metadata by default
  Rust Parquet reader looks for this schema hint
  if hint is missing, Arrow schema is inferred from Parquet schema
  if hint conflicts with Parquet schema, Parquet schema takes precedence
```

Rust Parquet’s Arrow bridge writes an Arrow schema hint under the `ARROW_SCHEMA_META_KEY` / `ARROW:schema` metadata key to preserve original Arrow logical types, following the same convention as PyArrow; readers look for that hint and otherwise infer Arrow schema from the Parquet schema. ([Apache Arrow][6])

### Rust Parquet round-trip test

```rust
use std::io::Cursor;
use std::sync::Arc;

use parquet::arrow::ArrowWriter;
use parquet::arrow::arrow_reader::ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder;

let mut bytes = Vec::new();

{
    let mut writer = ArrowWriter::try_new(
        &mut bytes,
        batch.schema(),
        None,
    )?;

    writer.write(&batch)?;
    writer.close()?;
}

let cursor = Cursor::new(bytes);

let mut reader = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(cursor)?
    .build()?;

let out = reader.next().unwrap()?;
let out_field = out.schema().field(0);

assert_eq!(out_field.extension_type_name(), Some(MoneyType::NAME));
assert!(out_field.has_valid_extension_type::<MoneyType>());
```

### Explicit schema override on read

```rust
use parquet::arrow::arrow_reader::{
    ArrowReaderOptions,
    ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder,
};

let options = ArrowReaderOptions::new()
    .with_schema(expected_schema.clone());

let reader = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new_with_options(
    file,
    options,
)?;
```

`ArrowReaderOptions::with_schema` provides an explicit schema hint that takes precedence over embedded Arrow metadata and errors if the provided schema is incompatible with the Parquet file schema. ([Apache Arrow][7])

### Parquet rules

```text
DO:
  keep Arrow schema metadata enabled by default
  round-trip extension fields through Rust and PyArrow
  provide explicit schema hint when reading legacy Parquet without ARROW:schema
  test canonical extensions such as arrow.uuid and arrow.json

DON'T:
  assume raw Parquet logical types preserve every Arrow extension
  disable Arrow schema metadata unless compatibility policy requires it
  assume extension semantics survive through non-Arrow Parquet writers
```

---

## 26.11 PyCapsule and C Data Interface compatibility

```text
C Data / PyCapsule compatibility:
  extension metadata is carried through ArrowSchema metadata
  array buffers remain storage-type buffers
  consumer can preserve unknown extension metadata
  consumer must not reinterpret storage buffers without validating extension name/metadata
```

The Arrow C Data Interface is designed as a zero-copy in-process interchange protocol for Arrow memory and includes schema/metadata plus release-callback lifetime handling; the PyCapsule Interface standardizes Python export methods for `ArrowSchema`, `ArrowArray`, `ArrowArrayStream`, and device variants so consumers can call protocol methods instead of hardcoding PyArrow support. ([Apache Arrow][8])

### Python protocol expectations

```python
class ArrowArrayExportable:
    def __arrow_c_array__(self, requested_schema=None):
        ...

class ArrowStreamExportable:
    def __arrow_c_stream__(self, requested_schema=None):
        ...
```

### Rust with `pyo3-arrow`

```rust
use pyo3::prelude::*;
use pyo3_arrow::{PyArray, PyRecordBatchReader, error::PyArrowResult};

#[pyfunction]
fn extension_name(array: PyArray) -> PyArrowResult<Option<String>> {
    Ok(array.field().extension_type_name().map(ToOwned::to_owned))
}

#[pyfunction]
fn pass_through_array(array: PyArray) -> PyArrowResult<PyArray> {
    // Preserves ArrayRef + FieldRef, including extension metadata.
    Ok(array)
}

#[pyfunction]
fn count_stream_rows(reader: PyRecordBatchReader) -> PyArrowResult<usize> {
    let mut reader = reader.into_reader()?;
    let mut rows = 0usize;

    while let Some(batch) = reader.next() {
        rows += batch?.num_rows();
    }

    Ok(rows)
}
```

PyCapsules should have destructors that call Arrow release callbacks if not consumed, and a PyCapsule can only be consumed once; this matters for extension round trips because ownership/lifetime correctness is still governed by the same C Data/PyCapsule release rules. ([Apache Arrow][9])

---

## 26.12 Python/Rust round-trip test strategy

### Python writes IPC / Rust reads

```python
# tests/write_money_ipc.py
import json
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.ipc as ipc


class MoneyType(pa.ExtensionType):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(pa.decimal128(18, 2), "com.example.money")

    def __arrow_ext_serialize__(self):
        return json.dumps(
            {"version": 1, "currency": "USD"},
            sort_keys=True,
            separators=(",", ":"),
        ).encode()

    @classmethod
    def __arrow_ext_deserialize__(cls, storage_type, serialized):
        return cls()


pa.register_extension_type(MoneyType())

storage = pa.array(["10.50", "20.00"], type=pa.decimal128(18, 2))
arr = MoneyType().wrap_array(storage)
batch = pa.record_batch([arr], names=["amount"])

with ipc.new_file("money.arrow", batch.schema) as writer:
    writer.write_batch(batch)
```

### Rust verifies metadata

```rust
let file = std::fs::File::open("money.arrow")?;
let mut reader = arrow_ipc::reader::FileReader::try_new(file, None)?;
let batch = reader.next().unwrap()?;

let field = batch.schema().field(0);

assert_eq!(field.extension_type_name(), Some("com.example.money"));
assert_eq!(
    field.extension_type_metadata(),
    Some(r#"{"currency":"USD","version":1}"#)
);
assert!(field.has_valid_extension_type::<MoneyType>());
```

### Rust writes IPC / Python reads

```rust
// Write RecordBatch with MoneyType field to money_from_rust.arrow.
```

```python
import pyarrow.ipc as ipc

pa.register_extension_type(MoneyType())

with ipc.open_file("money_from_rust.arrow") as reader:
    batch = reader.get_batch(0)

assert batch.schema.field("amount").type.extension_name == "com.example.money"
```

### Parquet round-trip matrix

```text
Rust -> Parquet -> Rust:
  extension name preserved
  extension metadata preserved
  storage type preserved
  array values preserved

Rust -> Parquet -> PyArrow:
  register PyArrow extension class first
  read table
  assert extension type recovered or UnknownExtensionType if unregistered

PyArrow -> Parquet -> Rust:
  write table with extension
  Rust reader sees extension metadata
  Rust ExtensionType validates metadata/storage
```

---

## 26.13 Compatibility classes

```text
Class A: storage-compatible
  consumer does not understand extension
  reads storage DataType
  preserves metadata if it writes Arrow schema back out

Class B: metadata-aware
  consumer recognizes extension name
  validates metadata and storage type
  may expose domain-specific behavior

Class C: canonical-aware
  consumer implements canonical extension type
  interoperates through standardized arrow.* name and metadata

Class D: lossy
  consumer drops field metadata
  extension semantics are lost
  values may remain physically readable
```

### Agent rule

```text
Never rely on extension metadata for physical correctness.
Always choose a storage type that can be safely read by extension-unaware consumers.
Treat extension metadata as semantic enhancement, not mandatory memory-layout data.
```

---

## 26.14 Compatibility with DataFusion and Polars

```text
DataFusion:
  uses Arrow Schema / Field metadata
  may preserve metadata through scans/projections where schemas are propagated
  expressions/kernels generally operate on storage types
  custom semantic behavior requires UDFs, planner rules, or custom TableProvider/ExecutionPlan logic

Polars:
  Arrow extension metadata may not map to first-class Polars logical types
  validate preservation through IPC/Parquet/PyCapsule boundaries
  do not assume domain semantics unless Polars explicitly supports the extension
```

Canonical extension types exist to improve interoperability, but extension-aware behavior is still consumer-dependent; extension-unaware systems can read storage values but may not expose domain semantics. ([Apache Arrow][5])

---

## 26.15 Equality and compatibility rules

```rust
fn extension_fields_compatible(left: &Field, right: &Field) -> bool {
    left.data_type() == right.data_type()
        && left.extension_type_name() == right.extension_type_name()
        && left.extension_type_metadata() == right.extension_type_metadata()
}
```

```text
Strict extension equality:
  storage type equal
  extension name equal
  extension metadata byte/string equal
  nullability policy equal if schema contract requires it

Semantic compatibility:
  storage type compatible
  same extension name
  metadata version compatible
  older metadata accepted by newer reader
  unknown future metadata fields handled by policy
```

Rust `try_extension_type` errors if the extension name is missing or mismatched, if metadata deserialization fails, or if the storage datatype is unsupported for that extension. ([Apache Arrow][4])

---

## 26.16 Metadata versioning pattern

```json
{"version":1,"currency":"USD"}
```

```rust
fn parse_money_metadata(raw: &str) -> Result<MoneyMeta, ArrowError> {
    let meta: MoneyMeta = serde_json::from_str(raw)
        .map_err(|e| ArrowError::ParseError(format!("invalid money metadata: {e}")))?;

    match meta.version {
        1 => Ok(meta),
        other => Err(ArrowError::ParseError(format!(
            "unsupported money metadata version {other}",
        ))),
    }
}
```

Versioning rules:

```text
Backward-compatible change:
  add optional metadata field
  add new value accepted by old reader as unknown if policy allows
  clarify metadata semantics without changing storage

Breaking change:
  change storage type
  change extension name semantics
  change required metadata keys
  reinterpret existing metadata values
  change scale/unit semantics

Recommended:
  new extension name for major semantic changes
  metadata version for parameter schema changes
```

---

## 26.17 IPC / Parquet / C Data preservation matrix

| Boundary                     |                  Extension name |          Extension metadata |                   Values | Notes                                          |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------: | --------------------------: | -----------------------: | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Arrow IPC                    |                             yes |                         yes |                      yes | preferred Arrow-native persistence / transport |
| Arrow C Data Interface       |                             yes |                         yes |                zero-copy | in-process ABI; metadata in schema             |
| Arrow PyCapsule              |                             yes |                         yes | zero-copy where possible | Python protocol wrapper around C Data/Stream   |
| Parquet via Arrow writer     |     yes, through `ARROW:schema` | yes, through `ARROW:schema` |                      yes | depends on Arrow schema hint preservation      |
| Parquet via non-Arrow writer |                  not guaranteed |              not guaranteed |      storage values only | extension semantics may be lost                |
| CSV / JSON text              | no automatic extension contract |                          no |                    maybe | must externalize schema separately             |
| DataFusion query plan        |                schema-dependent |            schema-dependent |                      yes | extension-aware semantics require custom logic |

---

## 26.18 Deployment best practices

```text
DO:
  define extension storage type first
  make storage type safe and meaningful without extension
  use namespace-style extension names
  use canonical extension names only for standardized arrow.* types
  serialize metadata deterministically
  validate metadata and storage type on read
  keep Arrow schema metadata in IPC/Parquet
  write Rust/Python round-trip tests
  test unknown-extension consumer behavior
  expose CPU storage values as fallback

DON'T:
  use extension metadata to change physical buffer layout
  depend on extension-aware behavior in every consumer
  use "arrow." prefix for product-specific types
  put row-level data into metadata
  disable Parquet Arrow schema hints if extension preservation matters
  assume pandas/Polars/DataFusion understand your semantic type
```

---

## 26.19 Anti-pattern catalog

| Anti-pattern                                  | Failure mode                           | Correct pattern                                 |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| custom extension named `uuid`                 | name collision                         | `com.example.uuid_v7` or canonical `arrow.uuid` |
| use `arrow.my_type`                           | reserved namespace violation           | use vendor namespace                            |
| storage type cannot be read without extension | unreadable by generic consumers        | storage-first design                            |
| metadata contains mutable runtime state       | nondeterministic schemas               | deterministic metadata                          |
| no metadata version                           | hard migration                         | `{"version":1,...}`                             |
| skip storage validation                       | wrong physical interpretation          | `supports_data_type`                            |
| assume Parquet always preserves extension     | metadata loss through non-Arrow writer | test `ARROW:schema`                             |
| convert to CSV/JSON without schema sidecar    | extension loss                         | write schema IPC/JSON sidecar                   |
| use extension type for compute semantics only | engine ignores it                      | UDF/planner/operator implementation             |
| ignore PyCapsule lifetime rules               | leaks/use-after-release                | consume once, respect release callback          |

---

## 26.20 Golden test matrix

```text
Rust extension:
  metadata serialize
  metadata deserialize
  missing metadata
  unexpected metadata
  unsupported storage type
  valid storage type
  has_valid_extension_type
  try_extension_type
  try_with_extension_type failure
  canonical_extension_type if canonical

Python extension:
  register_extension_type
  wrap_array
  __arrow_ext_serialize__
  __arrow_ext_deserialize__
  unregistered read -> UnknownExtensionType where applicable
  storage array equality
  extension array equality

IPC:
  Rust -> IPC -> Rust
  Rust -> IPC -> PyArrow
  PyArrow -> IPC -> Rust
  unregistered PyArrow extension behavior
  nested extension fields
  dictionary/list/struct extension fields

Parquet:
  Rust -> Parquet -> Rust
  Rust -> Parquet -> PyArrow
  PyArrow -> Parquet -> Rust
  read with explicit schema hint
  read after non-Arrow writer drops ARROW:schema
  canonical arrow.uuid / arrow.json round trip

C Data / PyCapsule:
  PyArrow array -> Rust PyArray
  arro3 array -> Rust PyArray
  Rust PyArray -> PyArrow
  RecordBatchReader stream
  FieldRef metadata preserved
  capsule consumed once
```

---

## 26.21 Value case

```text
Extension metadata:
  value = semantic typing without changing Arrow physical memory layout.

PyArrow ExtensionType:
  value = Python-defined logical types with storage and parameter serialization.

Rust ExtensionType:
  value = typed validation and metadata serialization/deserialization over Field metadata.

Canonical extension types:
  value = standardized cross-language semantics for common logical types.

IPC preservation:
  value = Arrow-native round-trip of extension schemas and arrays.

Parquet ARROW:schema:
  value = recover Arrow extension metadata despite Parquet’s separate type system.

C Data / PyCapsule:
  value = zero-copy in-process extension-aware schema exchange across Python/Rust libraries.

Unknown-extension fallback:
  value = safe storage-level interoperability even when semantic implementation is absent.

Round-trip tests:
  value = prove extension metadata survives all declared boundaries.
```

Final agent rule:

```text
Design extension types storage-first.
Use canonical arrow.* types when available.
Use vendor namespaces for custom types.
Validate storage and metadata at every boundary.
Preserve Arrow schema metadata through IPC and Parquet.
Use PyCapsule / C Data for in-process zero-copy exchange.
Never assume extension-aware semantics in DataFusion, Polars, pandas, or external Parquet readers without tests.
```

## 26.22 DataFusion 54 extension-type registry and field-aware casts

Secondary coverage — the schema-layer deep dive is `datafusion_schemas_rust.md` S7. Everything earlier in this section describes Arrow-level extension types (field metadata, `ARROW:extension:name`, canonical types). DataFusion 54 adds an engine-level registry so queries can *behave* differently for registered extension types instead of treating them as their storage type:

```text
datafusion_expr::registry:
  trait ExtensionTypeRegistry          # lookup/add/deregister registrations
  trait ExtensionTypeRegistration      # per-type behavior, keyed by extension name
  type  ExtensionTypeRegistryRef       # Arc<dyn ExtensionTypeRegistry>

datafusion_common::types:
  trait DFExtensionType                # engine-side logical view of an extension type
  type  DFExtensionTypeRef             # Arc<dyn DFExtensionType>
```

The registry resolves a `Field`'s `ARROW:extension:name` metadata to a registration (`create_extension_type_for_field`), so planning and casting can honor extension semantics wherever fields flow. `FunctionRegistry` gains matching extension-type-registry methods alongside the UDF registries.

### Metadata-aware SQL/expr functions

```text
with_metadata(v, …)      # attach field metadata to an expression's output field
cast_to_type(v, t)       # cast that consults the extension-type registry
try_cast_to_type(v, t)   # same, NULL on failure
```

(`datafusion-functions` core; see §8.27.)

### Field-aware casts

Casts now carry a full target `Field` (metadata included), not just a `DataType`:

```rust
// logical (datafusion-expr expr.rs) — field named `field`:
pub struct Cast {
    pub expr: Box<Expr>,
    pub field: FieldRef,
}

// physical (datafusion-physical-expr expressions/cast.rs) — named `target_field`:
pub struct CastExpr {
    pub expr: Arc<dyn PhysicalExpr>,
    target_field: FieldRef,          // constructor: CastExpr::new_with_target_field
    cast_options: CastOptions<'static>,
}
```

This means extension metadata survives casts end-to-end. Relationship to the rest of this section: the arrow-schema canonical extension types of §26.5 (bool8, json, uuid, opaque, fixed/variable-shape tensor, …) define the *storage and metadata* contract; a `DFExtensionType` registration is what makes DataFusion queries aware of those semantics. Custom logical types like the §26.7 money example can now get engine-level behavior by registering an `ExtensionTypeRegistration` instead of relying on convention alone.

## 27.0 Performance model

```text
Performance surfaces:
  batch size
  memory layout
  copy boundaries
  projection pushdown
  predicate pushdown
  Parquet row groups/pages/statistics
  object-store range IO
  eager materialization boundaries
  DataFusion partitioning
  Tokio CPU/IO scheduling
  memory pool + spill path
  benchmark isolation
  query-plan snapshots
```

DataFusion’s runtime environment manages memory, disk, cache, and object-store registry resources; its docs describe `RuntimeEnv` as the execution resource manager containing `MemoryPool`, `DiskManager`, `CacheManager`, and `ObjectStoreRegistry`. ([Docs.rs][1])
