## 27.2 Batch sizing

```text
Batch too small:
  high scheduler overhead
  high kernel dispatch overhead
  poor compression amortization
  many tiny IPC/Flight messages
  excessive RecordBatch metadata

Batch too large:
  high peak memory
  delayed first output
  poor cache locality for wide rows
  gRPC/message-size pressure
  worse spill behavior
  large pipeline breakers

Default working range:
  8_192 to 65_536 rows

String/binary/nested-heavy data:
  batch by bytes, not only rows
```

```rust
use arrow_array::RecordBatch;

const TARGET_ROWS: usize = 65_536;
const TARGET_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024 * 1024;

fn approx_batch_bytes(batch: &RecordBatch) -> usize {
    batch
        .columns()
        .iter()
        .map(|array| array.get_buffer_memory_size())
        .sum()
}

fn should_flush(rows: usize, bytes: usize) -> bool {
    rows >= TARGET_ROWS || bytes >= TARGET_BYTES
}
```

DataFusion exposes `datafusion.execution.batch_size` as a runtime configuration; lowering batch size can reduce memory usage but may increase IO and CPU overhead, while increasing it can improve amortization at the cost of memory. ([datafusion.apache.org][3])

---

## 27.3 Zero-copy versus copy boundaries

| Operation                      | Usually zero-copy |            Usually copy | Notes                       |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------: | ----------------------: | --------------------------- |
| `ArrayRef::clone`              |               yes |                      no | `Arc` clone                 |
| `Array::slice`                 |               yes |                      no | retains parent buffers      |
| `RecordBatch::slice`           |               yes |                      no | slices all columns          |
| projection by column reference |               yes |                      no | reuses arrays               |
| `filter`                       |                no |                     yes | creates selected output     |
| `take`                         |                no |                     yes | gathers output              |
| `cast`                         |         sometimes |                   often | depends on type             |
| `concat`                       |                no |                     yes | materializes combined array |
| IPC/FFI import                 |             often |                   maybe | alignment may force copy    |
| tiny slice of huge buffer      |               yes | operationally dangerous | retains huge backing buffer |

```rust
use arrow_array::{Array, Int64Array};

let a = Int64Array::from_iter_values(0..10_000_000);
let tiny = a.slice(100, 10);

// Zero-copy, but retains backing buffers from `a`.
assert_eq!(tiny.len(), 10);
```

```text
Zero-copy rule:
  use for transient pipeline stages
  avoid for long-lived tiny slices of huge arrays
  compact deliberately at cache/storage/API boundaries
```

---

## 27.4 Copy-boundary compaction

```rust
use arrow_array::{Array, ArrayRef, Int64Array};
use std::sync::Arc;

fn compact_i64_slice(array: &Int64Array, offset: usize, len: usize) -> ArrayRef {
    let compact: Int64Array = array
        .slice(offset, len)
        .iter()
        .collect();

    Arc::new(compact)
}
```

```text
Compact when:
  slice retained in cache
  slice crosses tenant/security boundary
  parent buffer is much larger than slice
  process memory footprint matters more than copy cost

Do not compact when:
  slice is short-lived
  downstream immediately consumes it
  filter/take already materializes
```

---

## 27.5 Projection pushdown

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let df = ctx
    .read_parquet("s3://bucket/events/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
    .await?
    .select(vec![
        col("user_id"),
        col("event_ts"),
        col("amount"),
    ])?;
```

```text
Projection pushdown goal:
  avoid reading unneeded columns
  avoid decoding unneeded columns
  avoid transferring unneeded column chunks
  reduce memory pressure
  reduce object-store range requests
```

DataFusion supports projection/filter pushdown through its optimizer and file-source integrations where the file format supports it; its architecture documentation describes projection and filter pushdown as optimizer behavior before physical execution. ([Docs.rs][4])

---

## 27.6 Predicate pushdown

```rust
let df = ctx
    .read_parquet("s3://bucket/events/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
    .await?
    .filter(
        col("year").eq(lit(2026_i32))
            .and(col("month").eq(lit(5_i32)))
            .and(col("event_type").eq(lit("click")))
    )?;
```

```text
Predicate pushdown layers:
  partition pruning
  file pruning
  Parquet row-group pruning
  Parquet page/range pruning
  decode-time row filtering
  post-decode Arrow filter
```

DataFusion has Parquet pruning configuration, including `datafusion.execution.parquet.pruning`, and Parquet reader settings for predicate-cache sizing when pushed-down filters are enabled. ([datafusion.apache.org][3])

---

## 27.7 Parquet row-group sizing

```rust
use parquet::basic::{Compression, ZstdLevel};
use parquet::file::properties::{EnabledStatistics, WriterProperties};

let props = WriterProperties::builder()
    .set_compression(Compression::ZSTD(ZstdLevel::try_new(3)?))
    .set_max_row_group_row_count(1_000_000)
    .set_max_row_group_bytes(Some(256 * 1024 * 1024))
    .set_data_page_size_limit(1024 * 1024)
    .set_statistics_enabled(EnabledStatistics::Page)
    .build();
```

```text
Small row groups:
  more metadata
  more footer/statistics overhead
  more row-group pruning opportunities
  more files/ranges/operators
  worse compression ratio risk

Large row groups:
  better compression
  larger sequential reads
  fewer metadata entries
  higher writer buffering
  coarser pruning
  higher memory during scan/write

Typical data-lake starting point:
  128 MiB to 512 MiB encoded row-group target
  tune by selectivity, object-store latency, and writer memory
```

Rust Parquet `WriterPropertiesBuilder::set_max_row_group_bytes` sets a maximum encoded row-group size; if both byte and row-count limits are set, the smaller limit determines the produced row group. ([Apache Arrow][5]) Apache Parquet’s own configuration guidance recommends large row groups, noting that larger row groups enable larger sequential IO but require more write buffering. ([Parquet][6])

---

## 27.8 Parquet writer memory pressure

```rust
use parquet::arrow::ArrowWriter;

const MAX_ROW_GROUP_BUFFERED: usize = 256 * 1024 * 1024;

writer.write(&batch)?;

if writer.in_progress_size() > MAX_ROW_GROUP_BUFFERED {
    writer.flush()?;
}

eprintln!(
    "writer_memory={} in_progress_size={} in_progress_rows={}",
    writer.memory_size(),
    writer.in_progress_size(),
    writer.in_progress_rows(),
);
```

Parquet writing must buffer an entire row group before flushing; Rust `ArrowWriter` exposes `memory_size`, `in_progress_size`, `in_progress_rows`, and `flush` to monitor and control row-group buffering. ([Docs.rs][7]) Calling `flush` can control memory pressure, but smaller row groups may increase metadata overhead and worsen compression/query performance. ([Apache Arrow][8])

---

## 27.9 Cloud object-store range reads

```rust
use object_store::{ObjectStore, path::Path};
use std::sync::Arc;

let meta = store.head(&path).await?;
let footer_hint = 128 * 1024_u64;
let start = meta.size.saturating_sub(footer_hint);

let footer = store.get_range(&path, start..meta.size).await?;
```

### Vectored range reads

```rust
let ranges = vec![
    0..4096,
    8_388_608..8_454_144,
    16_777_216..16_842_752,
];

let chunks = store.get_ranges(&path, &ranges).await?;
```

`object_store::ObjectStore::get_ranges` is designed for structured-data workloads needing multiple non-contiguous byte ranges and can coalesce adjacent ranges into an appropriate number of parallel requests. ([Docs.rs][9])

### Parquet object reader path

```rust
use parquet::arrow::async_reader::store::ParquetObjectReader;
use parquet::arrow::async_reader::ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder;

let meta = store.head(&path).await?;

let reader = ParquetObjectReader::new(store.clone(), path.clone())
    .with_file_size(meta.size)
    .with_footer_size_hint(128 * 1024);

let mut stream = ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder::new(reader)
    .await?
    .with_batch_size(65_536)
    .build()?;
```

```text
Cloud read rules:
  use ParquetObjectReader for Parquet over object_store
  provide file_size from head()
  use footer_size_hint when known
  avoid fetching full object for footer
  bound concurrent range reads
  coalesce tiny adjacent ranges
  cache metadata for repeated scans
```

---

## 27.10 Avoid eager table materialization

```rust
// Bad for large outputs.
let batches: Vec<RecordBatch> = df.collect().await?;

// Good for service / large result.
let mut stream = df.execute_stream().await?;

while let Some(batch) = stream.next().await {
    let batch = batch?;
    // write / encode / send batch
}
```

DataFusion’s `collect` buffers all output batches in memory, while `execute_stream` returns a stream and avoids full-result buffering. ([Docs.rs][4])

```text
Collect only when:
  test
  preview
  bounded small result
  API explicitly requires Vec<RecordBatch>
  max rows/bytes enforced

Stream when:
  user query
  Flight/HTTP response
  large file scan
  object-store pipeline
  ETL transform
```

---

## 27.11 Tokio runtime separation for CPU/IO

```text
DataFusion uses Tokio runtime threads for query execution.
CPU-heavy query work inside async tasks can starve unrelated IO if the same runtime also serves latency-sensitive network traffic.
```

DataFusion docs describe using a Tokio runtime as a thread pool for query execution and note the runtime is used for CPU-intensive applications as well as async work. ([Docs.rs][4]) An Apache DataFusion issue explicitly documents the risk that CPU-bound work in async closures can starve IO on the same cooperative runtime. ([GitHub][10])

### Separate runtime skeleton

```rust
use tokio::runtime::Builder;

let query_runtime = Builder::new_multi_thread()
    .worker_threads(num_cpus::get())
    .thread_name("df-query")
    .enable_all()
    .build()?;

let api_runtime = Builder::new_multi_thread()
    .worker_threads(4)
    .thread_name("api-io")
    .enable_all()
    .build()?;
```

### Query execution on dedicated runtime

```rust
let handle = query_runtime.handle().clone();

let join = handle.spawn(async move {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();
    let df = ctx.sql("SELECT ...").await?;
    df.execute_stream().await
});
```

```text
One runtime is acceptable for:
  CLI
  batch job
  local-only ETL
  low-concurrency service

Separate query/runtime strategy is recommended for:
  API server + long queries
  object-store reads + CPU-heavy decode
  Flight SQL service with concurrent clients
  low-latency control plane
```

---

## 27.12 DataFusion memory pools

```rust
use datafusion::execution::memory_pool::{
    GreedyMemoryPool, FairSpillPool, TrackConsumersPool,
};
use datafusion::execution::runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder;
use std::sync::Arc;

let pool = Arc::new(TrackConsumersPool::new(
    Arc::new(GreedyMemoryPool::new(8 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024)),
    5,
));

let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_memory_pool(pool)
    .build_arc()?;
```

`RuntimeEnvBuilder::with_memory_limit` defaults to a `GreedyMemoryPool` wrapped in `TrackConsumersPool` and notes that DataFusion may not yet respect the memory limit in all cases. In DataFusion 54 the `MemoryPool` trait is `Any + Send + Sync + Debug + Display` — custom pools must be `'static` (own their state) and implement `Display`; see §16.13 for the full trait shape. ([Docs.rs][11])

### Pool selection

```text
UnboundedMemoryPool:
  tests
  local tools
  bounded trusted workloads

GreedyMemoryPool:
  simple service cap
  one dominant query
  low overhead

FairSpillPool:
  multiple spillable operators
  concurrent memory consumers
  fairness required

TrackConsumersPool:
  production diagnostics
  better memory-error messages
```

---

## 27.13 Disk manager and spill

```rust
let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_temp_file_path("/mnt/nvme/datafusion-spill")
    .with_max_temp_directory_size(512 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024)
    .build_arc()?;
```

DataFusion’s runtime environment includes a `DiskManager` for temporary files and spill files, and `RuntimeEnvBuilder` supports temp-file path and maximum temp-directory size configuration. ([Docs.rs][1])

```text
Spill path rules:
  use fast local disk
  avoid root filesystem
  avoid slow network filesystem
  set max temp directory size
  monitor spill bytes
  clean stale temp files on crash/restart if needed

Memory + spill:
  memory pool without spill => queries may fail under pressure
  spill path without memory limit => unbounded memory still possible
```

---

## 27.14 Target partitions and repartitioning

```rust
let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .set_usize("datafusion.execution.target_partitions", 32)
    .set_bool("datafusion.optimizer.repartition_joins", true)
    .set_bool("datafusion.optimizer.repartition_aggregations", true)
    .set_bool("datafusion.optimizer.repartition_sorts", true)
    .set_bool("datafusion.optimizer.repartition_windows", true)
    .with_batch_size(8192);

let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config(config);
```

DataFusion configuration includes target partitions, repartitioning settings for joins, aggregations, sorts, windows, and file scans, plus Parquet and explain-related settings. ([datafusion.apache.org][3])

```text
Increase target_partitions when:
  CPU underutilized
  enough files/row groups exist
  large joins/aggregations
  object-store concurrency bounded elsewhere

Decrease target_partitions when:
  tiny inputs
  object-store request explosion
  memory pressure
  scheduler overhead dominates
```

## 27.15 Projection/predicate pushdown validation

### EXPLAIN

```sql
EXPLAIN
SELECT user_id, amount
FROM events
WHERE year = 2026 AND amount > 100;
```

### DataFrame explain

```rust
let explained = df.explain(false, false)?;
explained.show().await?;
```

DataFusion `EXPLAIN` shows the logical and physical execution plan for a SQL statement; the user guide also notes you can see the plan through SQL `EXPLAIN` or DataFrame `explain`. ([datafusion.apache.org][12])

### Explain config

```sql
SET datafusion.explain.show_statistics = true;
SET datafusion.explain.show_sizes = true;
SET datafusion.explain.show_schema = true;
```

DataFusion explain configuration includes `show_statistics`, `show_sizes`, `show_schema`, `physical_plan_only`, and format options. ([datafusion.apache.org][3])

### Snapshot target

```text
Snapshot:
  optimized logical plan
  physical plan
  projection columns in scan
  pushed filters
  repartition nodes
  sort nodes
  join algorithm
  row-group pruning indicators
  expected limit/sort pushdown
```

## 27.16 Criterion benchmark: Arrow kernel

```rust
// benches/arrow_kernels.rs
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::{ArrayRef, BooleanArray, Int64Array, RecordBatch};
use arrow_ord::cmp::gt;
use arrow_select::filter::filter_record_batch;
use criterion::{black_box, criterion_group, criterion_main, Criterion};

fn make_batch(n: i64) -> RecordBatch {
    let ids = Int64Array::from_iter_values(0..n);
    let values = Int64Array::from_iter_values((0..n).map(|x| x * 2));

    RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
        ("id", Arc::new(ids) as ArrayRef),
        ("value", Arc::new(values) as ArrayRef),
    ])
    .unwrap()
}

fn bench_filter_record_batch(c: &mut Criterion) {
    let batch = make_batch(1_000_000);
    let id = batch.column_by_name("id").unwrap();
    let threshold = Int64Array::new_scalar(500_000);

    c.bench_function("filter_record_batch_1m", |b| {
        b.iter(|| {
            let mask = gt(black_box(id.as_ref()), black_box(&threshold)).unwrap();
            let out = filter_record_batch(black_box(&batch), black_box(&mask)).unwrap();
            black_box(out);
        })
    });
}

criterion_group!(benches, bench_filter_record_batch);
criterion_main!(benches);
```

`criterion_group!` and `criterion_main!` generate benchmark groups and executable benchmark entrypoints, and `black_box` is commonly used to prevent the compiler from optimizing away benchmark work. ([Bheisler][2])

---

## 27.17 Criterion benchmark: DataFusion query

```rust
// benches/datafusion_queries.rs
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::{ArrayRef, Int64Array, RecordBatch, StringArray};
use criterion::{criterion_group, criterion_main, Criterion};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

fn make_context() -> SessionContext {
    let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().unwrap();

    rt.block_on(async {
        let ctx = SessionContext::new();

        let n = 1_000_000;
        let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
            (
                "k",
                Arc::new(Int64Array::from_iter_values((0..n).map(|x| x % 1000))) as ArrayRef,
            ),
            (
                "v",
                Arc::new(Int64Array::from_iter_values(0..n)) as ArrayRef,
            ),
        ])
        .unwrap();

        ctx.register_batch("t", batch).unwrap();
        ctx
    })
}

fn bench_group_by(c: &mut Criterion) {
    let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().unwrap();

    c.bench_function("datafusion_group_by_1m", |b| {
        b.iter(|| {
            rt.block_on(async {
                let ctx = make_context();
                let df = ctx
                    .sql("SELECT k, SUM(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY k")
                    .await
                    .unwrap();

                let out = df.collect().await.unwrap();
                criterion::black_box(out);
            })
        })
    });
}

criterion_group!(benches, bench_group_by);
criterion_main!(benches);
```

```text
Benchmark caveat:
  context/table construction inside benchmark measures setup + query.
  move setup outside if measuring execution only.
  include both variants deliberately:
    end-to-end benchmark
    execution-only benchmark
```

---

## 27.18 Execution-only benchmark pattern

```rust
fn bench_query_execution_only(c: &mut Criterion) {
    let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().unwrap();

    let (ctx, sql) = rt.block_on(async {
        let ctx = make_context();
        (ctx, "SELECT k, SUM(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY k".to_string())
    });

    c.bench_function("df_query_execution_only", |b| {
        b.iter(|| {
            rt.block_on(async {
                let df = ctx.sql(&sql).await.unwrap();
                let out = df.collect().await.unwrap();
                criterion::black_box(out);
            })
        })
    });
}
```

```text
Benchmark dimensions:
  planning only
  optimization only
  physical planning only
  execution only
  end-to-end query
  cold cache
  warm cache
  object-store remote
  object-store local/in-memory
```

## 27.22 Production tuning workflow

```text
1. Establish baseline:
   representative data
   representative query
   fixed versions
   fixed hardware
   fixed object-store location

2. Capture plan:
   EXPLAIN
   optimized logical plan
   physical plan
   statistics/sizes/schema

3. Measure:
   elapsed
   CPU
   memory
   IO
   spill
   object-store requests
   output rows/batches

4. Apply one change:
   batch size
   projection
   predicate
   row-group size
   compression
   target_partitions
   runtime split
   memory pool
   spill path

5. Compare:
   Criterion for micro
   end-to-end harness for macro
   plan snapshot changes
   resource counters

6. Lock:
   config
   test
   benchmark guardrail
```

## 27.23 Deployment profiles

### CLI / local batch

```text
Batch size:
  32k–128k rows

Runtime:
  one Tokio runtime acceptable

Memory:
  unbounded or simple GreedyMemoryPool

Spill:
  OS temp or local configured path

Materialization:
  collect acceptable only for bounded output
```

### Data lake query service

```text
Batch size:
  8k–64k rows

Runtime:
  separate query runtime from API/runtime if latency matters

Memory:
  GreedyMemoryPool or FairSpillPool
  TrackConsumersPool for diagnostics

Spill:
  dedicated local NVMe path
  explicit max temp directory size

Object store:
  use range reads
  metadata caching
  bounded request concurrency

Output:
  execute_stream
  Flight/HTTP streaming
```

### Python extension

```text
Batch size:
  preserve incoming batches unless pathological

GIL:
  release around Rust compute / DataFusion execution

Output:
  PyRecordBatchReader for large data
  PyTable only for bounded output

Benchmark:
  include Python overhead separately from Rust kernel cost
```

## 27.24 Anti-pattern catalog

| Anti-pattern                             | Failure mode                   | Correct pattern                     |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- |
| one-row batches                          | dispatch overhead              | 8k–64k rows                         |
| collect unbounded query                  | memory blowup                  | `execute_stream`                    |
| concat chunks before every operation     | copy overhead                  | process batch-at-a-time             |
| tiny Parquet row groups                  | metadata/compression overhead  | row-group byte/row policy           |
| huge Parquet row groups                  | writer memory / coarse pruning | tune row count/bytes                |
| full object fetch for Parquet footer     | unnecessary cloud IO           | range reads / `ParquetObjectReader` |
| no projection pushdown                   | decoded unused columns         | select only needed columns          |
| no predicate pushdown                    | scanned unused row groups      | DataFusion filters before collect   |
| same runtime for API + heavy queries     | IO starvation / latency spikes | runtime separation                  |
| memory pool without spill path           | failures under pressure        | memory + disk config                |
| benchmark includes setup accidentally    | misleading results             | setup outside or label end-to-end   |
| plan snapshots compare raw unstable text | flaky tests                    | normalize and assert operators      |

## 27.26 Value case

```text
Batch sizing:
  value = amortize overhead while bounding memory and latency.

Zero-copy:
  value = avoid memory traffic; risk = retained backing buffers.

Compaction:
  value = release oversized parent buffers at ownership boundaries.

Projection pushdown:
  value = fewer columns decoded, transferred, and materialized.

Predicate pushdown:
  value = fewer files, row groups, pages, and rows decoded.

Parquet row-group sizing:
  value = compression/pruning/IO/memory tradeoff control.

Object-store range reads:
  value = avoid full-object reads and reduce cloud transfer/request waste.

Streaming:
  value = lower peak memory and lower first-result latency.

Tokio runtime separation:
  value = prevent CPU-heavy queries from starving latency-sensitive IO.

Memory pools:
  value = resource governance and failure predictability.

Disk manager/spill:
  value = execute larger-than-memory queries with controlled local storage.

Criterion:
  value = repeatable microbenchmarking and regression detection.

Plan snapshots:
  value = prevent accidental optimizer/pushdown/physical-plan regressions.
```

Final agent rule:

```text
Benchmark before tuning.
Stream by default.
Push projection and predicates before scan.
Size batches by rows and bytes.
Size Parquet row groups by encoded bytes and query selectivity.
Use object-store range reads for structured formats.
Separate CPU-heavy query execution from latency-sensitive IO when serving traffic.
Configure memory pool and spill path together.
Snapshot plans and benchmark outputs as part of CI.
```

# 28) Error handling, testing, and compatibility matrix

Style target: dense, syntax-first, agent-ready technical reference.

---

## 28.0 Error model

```text
Rust Arrow ecosystem error layers:

ArrowError:
  arrays, buffers, schemas, compute, IPC, CSV, JSON, FFI, Arrow-facing conversions

ParquetError:
  Parquet file/metadata/page/encoding/Arrow bridge errors

DataFusionError:
  SQL planning, schema resolution, optimizer, execution, datasource, Arrow, IO, object-store, resource errors

object_store::Error:
  local/S3/GCS/Azure/HTTP storage errors, conditional write errors, authz/authn, missing object, invalid config

ProductError:
  your crate's stable public error surface
```

`ArrowError` is the common Arrow Rust error type and includes variants such as `SchemaError`, `ComputeError`, `CastError`, `IpcError`, `JsonError`, `CsvError`, `ParquetError`, `CDataInterface`, `DivideByZero`, and `ArithmeticOverflow`. `ParquetError` is non-exhaustive and includes variants such as `General`, `NYI`, `EOF`, `ArrowError`, `IndexOutOfBound`, `External`, `NeedMoreData`, and `NeedMoreDataRange`. `object_store::Error` is also non-exhaustive and includes `NotFound`, `AlreadyExists`, `Precondition`, `NotModified`, `PermissionDenied`, `Unauthenticated`, `NotImplemented`, `NotSupported`, and `UnknownConfigurationKey`. ([Docs.rs][1])

## 28.2 Product error wrapper

```rust
use thiserror::Error;

#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum EngineError {
    #[error("arrow error: {0}")]
    Arrow(#[from] arrow_schema::ArrowError),

    #[error("parquet error: {0}")]
    Parquet(#[from] parquet::errors::ParquetError),

    #[error("datafusion error: {0}")]
    DataFusion(#[from] datafusion_common::DataFusionError),

    #[error("object-store error: {0}")]
    ObjectStore(#[from] object_store::Error),

    #[error("schema mismatch: expected={expected}, actual={actual}")]
    SchemaMismatch {
        expected: String,
        actual: String,
    },

    #[error("unsupported feature: {0}")]
    Unsupported(String),

    #[error("invalid input: {0}")]
    InvalidInput(String),

    #[error("resource exhausted: {0}")]
    ResourceExhausted(String),

    #[error("internal invariant violation: {0}")]
    Internal(String),
}

pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, EngineError>;
```

`thiserror` generates `Display`, `Error`, and `From` implementations while not appearing in the public API shape, so switching between handwritten implementations and `thiserror` is not a breaking API change. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 28.3 Error classification rules

```text
User/input errors:
  schema mismatch
  unsupported datatype
  invalid SQL
  invalid file path
  malformed JSON/CSV/IPC/Parquet
  missing object
  auth failure
  failed precondition

Runtime/resource errors:
  memory limit exceeded
  spill directory exhausted
  timeout
  cancellation
  object-store throttling
  transport failure

Internal errors:
  impossible datatype branch
  physical-plan invariant broken
  unexpected empty child plan
  mismatched batch schema after validated operator
```

DataFusion explicitly distinguishes expected errors, such as invalid caller operations, from unexpected `DataFusionError::Internal` errors that indicate internal invariants or potential bugs; its docs also recommend convenient macros for expected execution errors and assertion-style internal checks. ([Docs.rs][3])

---

## 28.4 Mapping lower-level errors to API boundaries

### gRPC / Flight / service boundary

```rust
fn to_tonic_status(err: EngineError) -> tonic::Status {
    match err {
        EngineError::SchemaMismatch { .. }
        | EngineError::InvalidInput(_)
        | EngineError::Arrow(arrow_schema::ArrowError::ParseError(_))
        | EngineError::Arrow(arrow_schema::ArrowError::CastError(_))
        | EngineError::Arrow(arrow_schema::ArrowError::SchemaError(_)) => {
            tonic::Status::invalid_argument(err.to_string())
        }

        EngineError::ObjectStore(object_store::Error::NotFound { .. }) => {
            tonic::Status::not_found(err.to_string())
        }

        EngineError::ObjectStore(object_store::Error::Unauthenticated { .. }) => {
            tonic::Status::unauthenticated(err.to_string())
        }

        EngineError::ObjectStore(object_store::Error::PermissionDenied { .. }) => {
            tonic::Status::permission_denied(err.to_string())
        }

        EngineError::ObjectStore(object_store::Error::Precondition { .. }) => {
            tonic::Status::failed_precondition(err.to_string())
        }

        EngineError::ResourceExhausted(_) => {
            tonic::Status::resource_exhausted(err.to_string())
        }

        EngineError::Unsupported(_) => {
            tonic::Status::unimplemented(err.to_string())
        }

        EngineError::Internal(_) => {
            tonic::Status::internal(err.to_string())
        }

        other => tonic::Status::internal(other.to_string()),
    }
}
```

### Python boundary

```rust
use pyo3::exceptions::{PyFileNotFoundError, PyPermissionError, PyRuntimeError, PyTypeError, PyValueError};
use pyo3::PyErr;

fn to_py_err(err: EngineError) -> PyErr {
    match err {
        EngineError::SchemaMismatch { .. } => PyTypeError::new_err(err.to_string()),
        EngineError::InvalidInput(_) => PyValueError::new_err(err.to_string()),
        EngineError::Unsupported(_) => PyNotImplementedError::new_err(err.to_string()),

        EngineError::ObjectStore(object_store::Error::NotFound { .. }) => {
            PyFileNotFoundError::new_err(err.to_string())
        }

        EngineError::ObjectStore(object_store::Error::PermissionDenied { .. })
        | EngineError::ObjectStore(object_store::Error::Unauthenticated { .. }) => {
            PyPermissionError::new_err(err.to_string())
        }

        _ => PyRuntimeError::new_err(err.to_string()),
    }
}
```

### CLI boundary

```rust
fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    if let Err(err) = run() {
        eprintln!("error: {err}");

        if std::env::var_os("RUST_BACKTRACE").is_some() {
            eprintln!("{err:?}");
        }

        std::process::exit(match err {
            EngineError::InvalidInput(_) | EngineError::SchemaMismatch { .. } => 2,
            EngineError::ObjectStore(object_store::Error::NotFound { .. }) => 3,
            EngineError::ObjectStore(object_store::Error::PermissionDenied { .. }) => 4,
            _ => 1,
        });
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

## 28.5 Non-exhaustive error matching

```rust
fn classify_object_store(err: &object_store::Error) -> &'static str {
    match err {
        object_store::Error::NotFound { .. } => "not_found",
        object_store::Error::AlreadyExists { .. } => "already_exists",
        object_store::Error::Precondition { .. } => "precondition",
        object_store::Error::NotModified { .. } => "not_modified",
        object_store::Error::PermissionDenied { .. } => "permission_denied",
        object_store::Error::Unauthenticated { .. } => "unauthenticated",
        object_store::Error::NotImplemented { .. } => "not_implemented",
        object_store::Error::NotSupported { .. } => "not_supported",
        object_store::Error::UnknownConfigurationKey { .. } => "bad_config",
        object_store::Error::InvalidPath { .. } => "invalid_path",
        object_store::Error::JoinError { .. } => "join_error",
        object_store::Error::Generic { .. } => "generic",
        _ => "unknown_future_variant",
    }
}
```

`object_store::Error` and `ParquetError` are non-exhaustive, so production code must include wildcard arms when matching. ([Docs.rs][4])

## 28.7 Golden IPC round-trip tests

```rust
use std::io::Cursor;
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::{ArrayRef, Int64Array, RecordBatch, StringArray};
use arrow_ipc::reader::FileReader;
use arrow_ipc::writer::FileWriter;

#[test]
fn ipc_file_round_trip_preserves_schema_and_values() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
        ("id", Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])) as ArrayRef),
        ("name", Arc::new(StringArray::from(vec![Some("a"), None, Some("c")])) as ArrayRef),
    ])?;

    let schema = batch.schema();
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();

    {
        let mut writer = FileWriter::try_new(&mut bytes, schema.as_ref())?;
        writer.write(&batch)?;
        writer.finish()?;
    }

    let mut reader = FileReader::try_new(Cursor::new(bytes), None)?;
    let out = reader.next().unwrap()?;

    assert_eq!(out.schema().as_ref(), schema.as_ref());
    assert_eq!(out.num_rows(), 3);
    assert_eq!(out.column(0).as_ref(), batch.column(0).as_ref());
    assert_eq!(out.column(1).as_ref(), batch.column(1).as_ref());

    Ok(())
}
```

### IPC stream round trip

```rust
use arrow_ipc::reader::StreamReader;
use arrow_ipc::writer::StreamWriter;

#[test]
fn ipc_stream_round_trip() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let batch = make_test_batch()?;
    let schema = batch.schema();

    let mut bytes = Vec::new();

    {
        let mut writer = StreamWriter::try_new(&mut bytes, schema.as_ref())?;
        writer.write(&batch)?;
        writer.finish()?;
    }

    let mut reader = StreamReader::try_new(Cursor::new(bytes), None)?;
    let out = reader.next().unwrap()?;

    assert_eq!(out.schema().as_ref(), schema.as_ref());
    assert_eq!(out.num_rows(), batch.num_rows());

    Ok(())
}
```

## 28.8 Golden Parquet round-trip tests

```rust
use bytes::Bytes;
use parquet::arrow::ArrowWriter;
use parquet::arrow::arrow_reader::ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder;

#[test]
fn parquet_round_trip_preserves_schema_and_values() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let batch = make_test_batch()?;
    let schema = batch.schema();

    let mut bytes = Vec::new();

    {
        let mut writer = ArrowWriter::try_new(&mut bytes, schema.clone(), None)?;
        writer.write(&batch)?;
        writer.close()?;
    }

    let reader = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(Bytes::from(bytes))?
        .with_batch_size(1024)
        .build()?;

    let out: Vec<RecordBatch> = reader.collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;

    assert_eq!(out.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(out[0].schema().as_ref(), schema.as_ref());
    assert_eq!(out[0].num_rows(), batch.num_rows());

    Ok(())
}
```

### Parquet projection test

```rust
#[test]
fn parquet_projection_reads_selected_columns() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let bytes = write_batch_to_parquet_bytes(make_test_batch()?)?;

    let builder = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(Bytes::from(bytes))?;
    let mask = parquet::arrow::arrow_reader::ProjectionMask::roots(
        builder.metadata().file_metadata().schema_descr(),
        [0],
    );

    let reader = builder.with_projection(mask).build()?;
    let batches: Vec<_> = reader.collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;

    assert_eq!(batches[0].num_columns(), 1);
    assert_eq!(batches[0].schema().field(0).name(), "id");

    Ok(())
}
```

## 28.10 SQL logic tests

### `.slt` file

```sql
# tests/sqllogictests/basic.slt

statement ok
CREATE TABLE t AS VALUES (1, 'a'), (2, 'b'), (3, 'c');

query IT
SELECT column1, column2 FROM t ORDER BY column1;
----
1 a
2 b
3 c

query I
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t;
----
3
```

### DataFusion-style commands

```bash
# Run all sqllogictests.
cargo test --profile=ci --test sqllogictests

# Run one file.
cargo test --profile=ci --test sqllogictests -- aggregate.slt

# Update expected output for one file.
cargo test --profile=ci --test sqllogictests -- aggregate.slt --complete
```

DataFusion uses sqllogictest files for SQL correctness testing, supports running all tests or individual `.slt` files, and supports a `--complete` mode to update expected outputs. DataFusion’s contributor guide says sqllogictests are easier to maintain because they avoid repeated Rust compile/link cycles and can be automatically updated. ([datafusion.apache.org][6])

### SQL logic test rules

```text
Use sqllogictest for:
  SQL parser behavior
  SQL planner behavior
  query result correctness
  optimizer regressions
  UDF/UDAF SQL behavior
  cross-engine SQL compatibility

Use Rust tests for:
  direct Arrow arrays
  error variants
  TableProvider internals
  ExecutionPlan internals
  object-store behavior
  Python extension bridge tests
```

## 28.11 DataFusion batch assertion macros

```rust
#[tokio::test]
async fn query_output_matches() -> datafusion_common::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
        ("id", Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![2, 1])) as ArrayRef),
    ])?;

    ctx.register_batch("t", batch)?;

    let out = ctx.sql("SELECT id FROM t ORDER BY id").await?
        .collect()
        .await?;

    datafusion::assert_batches_eq!(
        [
            "+----+",
            "| id |",
            "+----+",
            "| 1  |",
            "| 2  |",
            "+----+",
        ],
        &out
    );

    Ok(())
}
```

DataFusion’s testing guide documents assertion helpers such as `assert_batches_eq`, `assert_batches_sorted_eq`, `assert_contains`, and `assert_not_contains` for unit tests over `RecordBatch` outputs. ([datafusion.apache.org][6])

## 28.12 Snapshot tests

```rust
#[test]
fn logical_plan_snapshot() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let plan_text = build_plan()?.display_indent().to_string();
    insta::assert_snapshot!("optimized_plan", normalize_plan(&plan_text));
    Ok(())
}

fn normalize_plan(plan: &str) -> String {
    plan
        .replace("\\", "/")
        .replace("s3://secret-bucket", "s3://<bucket>")
}
```

DataFusion uses `insta` snapshot testing; its docs say snapshots are generated and compared on each test run, and `cargo insta review` can be used to review changes. ([datafusion.apache.org][6])

## 28.13 Fuzzing malformed IPC

### Fuzz target shape

```rust
// fuzz/fuzz_targets/ipc_file.rs

#![no_main]

use arrow_ipc::reader::FileReader;
use libfuzzer_sys::fuzz_target;
use std::io::Cursor;

fuzz_target!(|data: &[u8]| {
    let cursor = Cursor::new(data);

    if let Ok(mut reader) = FileReader::try_new(cursor, None) {
        while let Some(batch) = reader.next() {
            match batch {
                Ok(batch) => {
                    let _ = batch.validate();
                    let _ = batch.schema();
                    let _ = batch.num_rows();
                }
                Err(_) => break,
            }
        }
    }
});
```

Arrow’s security guidance recommends fuzzing IPC with binary payloads and, after decoding, validating the decoded Arrow data to strengthen both the IPC decoder and Arrow validation routines against invalid or malicious data. ([Apache Arrow][7])

---

## 28.14 Fuzzing malformed Parquet

```rust
// fuzz/fuzz_targets/parquet_reader.rs

#![no_main]

use bytes::Bytes;
use libfuzzer_sys::fuzz_target;
use parquet::arrow::arrow_reader::ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder;

fuzz_target!(|data: &[u8]| {
    let bytes = Bytes::copy_from_slice(data);

    if let Ok(reader) = ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(bytes) {
        if let Ok(mut reader) = reader.with_batch_size(1024).build() {
            while let Some(batch) = reader.next() {
                match batch {
                    Ok(batch) => {
                        let _ = batch.validate();
                    }
                    Err(_) => break,
                }
            }
        }
    }
});
```

Arrow C++ fuzzing coverage includes IPC stream/file readers, Parquet file reader, Parquet encoders/decoders, and CSV file reader, which is a useful scope model for Rust format-reader fuzzing even though the specific harnesses differ by language. ([Apache Arrow][8])

## 28.15 Fuzzing malformed JSON

```rust
// fuzz/fuzz_targets/json_reader.rs

#![no_main]

use std::io::Cursor;
use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_json::reader::ReaderBuilder;
use arrow_schema::{DataType, Field, Schema};
use libfuzzer_sys::fuzz_target;

fuzz_target!(|data: &[u8]| {
    let schema = Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![
        Field::new("a", DataType::Utf8, true),
        Field::new("b", DataType::Int64, true),
    ]));

    let cursor = Cursor::new(data);

    if let Ok(mut reader) = ReaderBuilder::new(schema)
        .with_batch_size(128)
        .with_ignore_type_conflicts(true)
        .build(cursor)
    {
        while let Some(batch) = reader.next() {
            match batch {
                Ok(batch) => {
                    let _ = batch.validate();
                }
                Err(_) => break,
            }
        }
    }
});
```

## 28.16 Fuzzing policy

```text
Fuzz targets:
  IPC stream reader
  IPC file reader
  Parquet file reader
  Parquet metadata/footer reader
  JSON reader
  CSV reader
  C Data / PyCapsule boundary if exposed
  schema parser / datatype parser
  Substrait plan decoder if exposed

Mutation classes:
  empty input
  truncated input
  random bytes
  valid file with one flipped bit
  valid file with truncated tail
  valid file with corrupted metadata
  oversized lengths
  deeply nested schemas
  invalid UTF-8
  invalid offsets
  invalid null counts
  invalid dictionary keys

Expected outcome:
  Ok(valid data)
  Err(parsed error)
  no panic
  no UB
  no infinite loop
  no memory explosion
```

## 28.18 Compatibility version matrix

As of **2026-07-14**, use this matrix as an explicit test target, not as an implicit guarantee:

| Component    |        Anchor | Test role                              |
| ------------ | ------------: | -------------------------------------- |
| Arrow Rust   |      `58.4.0` | arrays, schema, IPC, compute, FFI      |
| Parquet Rust |      `58.4.0` | Parquet read/write/interoperability    |
| DataFusion   |      `54.1.0` | SQL/DataFrame/query tests              |
| object_store |      `0.13.2` | local/S3/GCS/Azure/HTTP storage tests  |
| pyo3-arrow   |      `0.17.0` | Python Arrow PyCapsule interop         |
| Polars Rust  |      `0.53.0` | optional DataFrame interop tests       |
| PyArrow      |      `24.0.0` | Python IPC/Parquet/PyCapsule reference |
| Python       | `3.10`–`3.14` | wheel/import/interoperability matrix   |

The current docs.rs pages identify Arrow Rust `58.4.0`, DataFusion `54.1.0`, object_store `0.13.2`, pyo3-arrow `0.17.0`, and Polars `0.53.0`; PyArrow’s PyPI page shows `24.0.0`, and official PyArrow installation docs list Python 3.10–3.14 compatibility. ([Docs.rs][9])

## 28.19 Version-compatibility CI matrix

```yaml
name: compatibility

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  rust:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
        rust: [stable]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - run: cargo check --workspace --all-targets
      - run: cargo test --workspace --all-targets
      - run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - run: cargo tree -d

  python:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
        python: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13", "3.14"]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
      - run: python -m pip install -U pip maturin pytest pyarrow
      - run: maturin develop --release
      - run: pytest -q
```

PyO3’s build/distribution docs note that maturin can build manylinux-compliant wheels out of the box, while Python extension builds still require correct PyO3/maturin configuration and per-platform testing. ([pyo3.rs][10])

## 28.25 Rust SQL result tests

```rust
#[tokio::test]
async fn sql_result_is_stable() -> datafusion_common::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
        ("k", Arc::new(StringArray::from(vec!["a", "a", "b"])) as ArrayRef),
        ("v", Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![1, 2, 10])) as ArrayRef),
    ])?;

    ctx.register_batch("t", batch)?;

    let out = ctx.sql("SELECT k, SUM(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY k ORDER BY k")
        .await?
        .collect()
        .await?;

    datafusion::assert_batches_eq!(
        [
            "+---+----+",
            "| k | s  |",
            "+---+----+",
            "| a | 3  |",
            "| b | 10 |",
            "+---+----+",
        ],
        &out
    );

    Ok(())
}
```

## 28.26 Malformed-input tests

```rust
#[test]
fn malformed_ipc_returns_error_not_panic() {
    let bytes = b"not an arrow ipc file".to_vec();

    let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(|| {
        arrow_ipc::reader::FileReader::try_new(std::io::Cursor::new(bytes), None)
    });

    assert!(result.is_ok());
    assert!(result.unwrap().is_err());
}
```

```rust
#[test]
fn truncated_parquet_returns_error_not_panic() {
    let bytes = bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"PAR1bad");

    let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(|| {
        parquet::arrow::arrow_reader::ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(bytes)
    });

    assert!(result.is_ok());
    assert!(result.unwrap().is_err());
}
```

```rust
#[test]
fn malformed_json_returns_error_not_panic() {
    let schema = Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![
        Field::new("x", DataType::Int64, true),
    ]));

    let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(|| {
        arrow_json::reader::ReaderBuilder::new(schema)
            .build(std::io::Cursor::new(br#"{"x": "#))
    });

    assert!(result.is_ok());
}
```

## 28.27 Property tests

```rust
use proptest::prelude::*;

proptest! {
    #[test]
    fn int64_ipc_round_trip(values in proptest::collection::vec(any::<i64>(), 0..10_000)) {
        let batch = RecordBatch::try_from_iter(vec![
            ("x", Arc::new(Int64Array::from(values.clone())) as ArrayRef),
        ]).unwrap();

        let out = ipc_round_trip(batch.clone()).unwrap();

        prop_assert_eq!(out.num_rows(), batch.num_rows());
        prop_assert_eq!(out.schema().as_ref(), batch.schema().as_ref());
    }
}
```

## 28.28 Test matrix by boundary

| Boundary      | Required tests                                                          |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Arrow arrays  | constructors, nulls, slices, equality, schema, extension metadata       |
| Arrow compute | valid input, wrong type, length mismatch, null propagation, all-null    |
| IPC           | file, stream, projection, malformed, PyArrow interop                    |
| Parquet       | read, write, projection, row groups, compression, PyArrow interop       |
| JSON/CSV      | explicit schema, inference, malformed rows, null parsing, type conflict |
| object_store  | memory, local, cloud/emulator, range, conditional put, multipart        |
| DataFusion    | SQL, DataFrame, UDF, join, aggregate, window, explain snapshots         |
| Python        | PyArrow, arro3 if supported, pyo3-arrow, GIL release, wheel import      |
| Flight        | DoGet, DoPut, Flight SQL if used, TLS/auth, stream cancellation         |
| ADBC          | driver manager, native drivers, Arrow result streams, metadata          |
| Substrait     | SQL→Substrait→SQL equivalence, missing table/function errors            |

## 28.30 CI commands

```bash
# Rust correctness
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo test --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --doc

# Version graph
cargo tree -d
cargo tree -e features | rg 'arrow|parquet|datafusion|object_store|pyo3|polars'

# DataFusion SQL logic tests
cargo test --profile=ci --test sqllogictests

# Bench smoke
cargo bench --bench arrow_kernels -- --quick

# Python extension
python -m pip install -U maturin pytest pyarrow
maturin develop --release
pytest -q

# Fuzz local smoke
cargo fuzz run ipc_file -- -runs=10000
cargo fuzz run parquet_reader -- -runs=10000
cargo fuzz run json_reader -- -runs=10000
```

DataFusion’s testing guide documents Rust integration tests, doctests, sqllogictests, SQLancer-style SQL fuzz testing, snapshot testing with `insta`, and Criterion benchmarks as part of the project’s test methodology. ([datafusion.apache.org][6])

```text
Before release:
  cargo tree -d clean
  all Rust tests pass
  all Python wheel import tests pass
  PyArrow interop fixtures pass
  Parquet/IPC golden fixtures pass
  SQL logic tests pass
  fuzz smoke passes
  plan snapshots reviewed
  benchmark regression thresholds checked
  docs examples compile
  version matrix updated
  known compatibility gaps documented
```

## 28.32 Anti-pattern catalog

| Anti-pattern                                    | Failure mode                    | Correct pattern                     |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| expose raw `ArrowError` from public service API | unstable/internal error surface | domain error wrapper                |
| match non-exhaustive errors without wildcard    | future compile failure          | wildcard arm                        |
| assert SQL output order without `ORDER BY`      | flaky tests                     | explicit sort                       |
| use `Debug` strings as only data equality       | brittle                         | compare schema + arrays             |
| collect unbounded query in test helper          | OOM / slow CI                   | bounded collection                  |
| skip PyArrow interop tests                      | hidden cross-language break     | IPC/Parquet/PyCapsule fixtures      |
| fuzz decode without validating result           | misses invalid array bugs       | decode + validate                   |
| no malformed fixture tests                      | panic slips into release        | corrupted IPC/Parquet/JSON fixtures |
| allow duplicate Arrow major versions            | type mismatch                   | `cargo tree -d` gate                |
| build wheels only on developer OS               | broken distribution             | OS/Python matrix                    |

## 28.34 Value case

```text
Domain error wrapper:
  value = stable public API and clean service/Python/CLI mapping.

Schema mismatch tests:
  value = prevent silent type/nullability/metadata drift.

IPC golden tests:
  value = prove Arrow-native serialization compatibility.

Parquet golden tests:
  value = prove durable storage compatibility and PyArrow/Rust round trips.

PyArrow/Rust interop:
  value = cross-language correctness for real user workflows.

SQL logic tests:
  value = compact, maintainable SQL correctness regression suite.

Fuzzing:
  value = malformed-input hardening and panic/UB prevention.

Version matrix:
  value = reproducible compatibility claims.

cargo tree gates:
  value = prevent duplicate Arrow/DataFusion/PyO3 worlds.

Plan snapshots:
  value = detect optimizer/pushdown/physical-plan regressions.

Wheel matrix:
  value = prevent Python packaging/import failures across supported platforms.
```

Final agent rule:

```text
Wrap lower-level errors in a product error type.
Classify errors into invalid input, unsupported, not found, auth, resource, and internal.
Test schemas exactly and compatibly.
Round-trip IPC and Parquet through Rust and PyArrow.
Use sqllogictests for SQL semantics.
Fuzz all untrusted format readers.
Gate releases on cargo tree, wheel import, golden fixtures, and version matrix tests.
Never claim compatibility without an automated test that proves it.
```

### SMARTREF Arrow Boundary

Arrow/PyArrow surfaces move schemas, arrays, record batches, IPC payloads,
Flight rows, and PyCapsules. Durable schema identity is a SMARTREF schema
contract concern; Python helpers project contract-owned fingerprints and must
not introduce arbitrary schema authority.
